guides.title: Overhaul the 5.0L V8 engine
guides.summary: Remove, dismantle, measure, rebuild and reinstall the 5.0L engine, preserving its bearing selection, valve timing and transmission-specific requirements.
guides.introduction: The 5.0L V8 uses overhead camshafts with twin independent variable camshaft timing to control its valves. A crankshaft-driven oil pump supplies the bearings and lubrication system. An overhaul brings these assemblies apart for inspection and restores their fit, sealing and timing before the engine returns to the vehicle. This is specialist work involving engine lifting, precision measurement and staged torque-and-angle tightening.
guides.why: Bearing grades establish the crankshaft’s running clearance, while chain alignment establishes the relationship between pistons and valves. Incorrect selection or timing can cause serious damage. Clean passages, correctly matched components and carefully timed sealant application matter just as much as replacing worn parts.

when.summary: When established internal damage or measured wear requires engine removal and comprehensive rebuilding.
notes: Verify engine identification before ordering parts; revisions within the engine family can affect parts selection.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and precision equipment
prepare.detail: Provide a vehicle hoist, floor crane, engine stand, lifting bracket 303-F047 and support bar 303-F072. The work also needs crankshaft holding and seal tools, a three-leg puller, piston ring compressor, clearance-measuring equipment and torque-and-angle tools. Have an assistant available for engine installation and a diagnostic scan tool for final correction.

prepare.title: Plan replacement parts
prepare.detail: Renew discarded main-cap fasteners, connecting-rod bolts, head bolts, variable camshaft timing bolts, pulley bolt, crankshaft seals, timing oil filters, oil cooler, oil-pan baffle/gasket, specified O-rings and gaskets, and removed exhaust studs/nuts. Include a new steering shaft bolt and the applicable flywheel, flexplate, clutch pressure-plate or torque-converter fasteners.

prepare.title: Organize the bench
prepare.detail: Keep reusable caps, bearings, followers and adjusters identified by original position. Arrange clean storage and the specified sealing materials before assembly. Obtain the 5.0L specifications and piston subassembly procedure before making reuse decisions.

steps.title: Make the vehicle safe and open access
steps.body: Follow [engine removal](#/document/G1685335): place the vehicle in neutral on the hoist, release fuel pressure, disconnect both battery cables and drain coolant. Loosen the steering dash seal and hold the steering wheel straight ahead. Mark the hood position, then complete the listed intake, cooling, battery-tray and cowl access operations.

steps.title: Disconnect the underside and transmission interfaces
steps.body: Drain the oil, discard the filter and disconnect the cooler hoses, wiring and exhaust connections. Separate the steering shaft without hammering or prying; discard its bolt and secure the shaft. Follow the automatic branch for transmission wiring, cooling-tube brackets and discarded converter nuts, or the manual branch for the rear cover fasteners.

steps.title: Support and extract the engine
steps.body: Place support-bar feet on body structure, never the fenders. Raise the engine as directed, remove the mount brackets and left catalytic converter, and position the air-conditioning compressor aside. Transfer support to the crane; support the transmission at its bellhousing with the jack and wooden block, never its pan. Separate and lift the engine. Remove the applicable flexplate or clutch/flywheel assembly, marking a reusable pressure plate and discarding specified fasteners.

steps.title: Dismantle the upper engine in sequence
steps.body: Use [bench disassembly](#/document/G1685337). Remove the rear seal before mounting the engine on its stand, then strip wiring, covers and accessories. Remove right-hand timing components at the specified crankshaft position, followed by the left-hand components. Remove each front camshaft mega cap before the remaining caps. Keep reusable valve-train parts indexed. Remove the heads only when cool, and always before removing the crankshaft.

steps.title: Inspect the heads and dismantle the bottom end
steps.body: Check head and block mating surfaces for distortion. Protect exposed cavities and avoid scratching aluminum gasket faces. Remove the sump, pickup, pump and rear seal retainer. Inspect bore tops and perform the prescribed ridge/carbon preparation before withdrawing pistons upward. Preserve rod/cap orientation, then remove the main caps, crankshaft and cooling jets. Follow the separate piston procedure for subassembly work.

steps.title: Select bearings and build the rotating assembly
steps.body: Begin [engine assembly](#/document/G1685342) by recording block and crankshaft bearing codes. Use the chart for mains 1 and 5 separately from the chart for mains 2, 3 and 4; each result identifies upper/lower grades. Align oil passages and lubricate bearings. Install the thrust washer with its groove rearward and seat it as directed. Check end play and turning torque. Verify piston/ring clearances, then install pistons without contacting cooling jets or scratching journals. Refit matching cracked rod caps with new bolts.

steps.title: Restore lubrication and install the heads
steps.body: Prime the oil pump with 2 tablespoons of clean engine oil and rotate it by hand before installation. Follow the individual sealing and tightening sequences for the rear retainer, baffle, pickup and pan. Install the new oil cooler. Seat the crankshaft position sensor correctly and flush before bolting it down. Fit new head gaskets and head bolts using the complete staged tightening instructions.

steps.title: Time the left bank before the right bank
steps.body: Start left-hand assembly with the crankshaft keyway at 5 o’clock. Follow the illustrated camshaft positions and colored-link alignment, using new timing oil filters and timing-unit bolts. Release the installed tensioner’s holding pin. Rotate clockwise one complete revolution, then continue clockwise to the 12 o’clock keyway position before right-hand assembly. Follow only the instructed crankshaft movements; temporary guide/arm adjustments must return to the specified position.

steps.title: Close and dress the engine
steps.body: Fully depress the variable camshaft timing solenoid pins before installing the front cover. Follow each joint’s sealant deadline, fit new front and rear crankshaft seals with the specified installers, and install the pulley with a new bolt and original washer. Restore accessories, covers, coils, sensors, grounds and harness retainers. Confirm the oil-level tube locks in place. The rear seal is installed after lifting the engine off its stand.

steps.title: Refit the engine using the correct transmission branch
steps.body: Follow [engine installation](#/document/G1685344). For MT82, align the clutch with its tool, retain pressure-plate indexing or align new-part paint dots, and lubricate the input shaft. For 6R80, lubricate the converter pilot and align its marked relationship to the flexplate. Restore mounts, exhaust, steering, wiring and hoses; use the new steering bolt and perform the collapsed-column check. Install the new oil filter without lubricating its seal, fill engine oil, reconnect the battery, then fill and bleed cooling.

watchFor.title: Sealant deadlines differ
watchFor.body: The rear retainer has a 4-minute securing limit. Pan and front-cover work have 5-minute limits with specifically defined staged alternatives requiring final tightening within 1 hour. Pulley and valve-cover sealing also have 5-minute limits. Follow the exact fastener instructions; exceeded limits require removing sealant and cleaning.

watchFor.title: Protect sealing faces and friction-component handling
watchFor.body: Do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes or abrasive discs on head/block gasket faces. Do not breathe clutch dust or disperse it with compressed air; use the prescribed approved dust-removal methods.

notes: Replace spark-plug tube and variable camshaft timing solenoid seals only when damaged seals were removed.
Use this engine’s timing sequence exactly; an earlier engine’s alignment method is not interchangeable.

diagnostics.finding: Crankshaft turning torque exceeds 6 Nm (53 lb-in), or a measured clearance fails the 5.0L specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The rotating assembly has not met its assembly checks.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the fit or assembly problem before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: A lash adjuster or roller follower is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: Associated camshaft lobes and valves also require inspection.
diagnostics.next: Inspect those components and replace damaged parts.

diagnostics.finding: The crankshaft sensor ring was dropped or has visible damage.
diagnostics.meaning: It cannot be reused under the removal procedure.
diagnostics.next: Install a replacement sensor ring.

verification.title: Record internal assembly results
verification.body: Record bearing codes and selected grades, bearing-clearance checks, crankshaft end play and turning torque, piston/ring clearances, and head/block inspection results against the applicable specifications.

verification.title: Complete installed-engine checks
verification.body: Confirm the steering-column inspection, fluid filling and cooling-system bleeding are complete. Perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with a diagnostic scan tool, then road test the vehicle.

guides.title: Strip and reassemble a 5.0L cylinder head
guides.summary: Disassemble and rebuild the valves, springs, seals and head-mounted fittings of a prepared 5.0L cylinder head.
guides.introduction: The 5.0L V8 uses aluminum cylinder heads with intake and exhaust valves operated by overhead camshafts. Valve springs close the valves, while retainers and keys hold each spring assembly together. Valve-stem seals control oil at the guides. This bench operation services those parts and the head-mounted coolant outlets and sensors, with different fitting sequences for the left-hand and right-hand heads.
guides.why: Cleanliness is critical: debris entering oil passages, coolant passages or the oil pan can cause engine failure. Reused components must return to their original positions. Controlled spring compression is essential to removing and installing the retaining keys, and all specified discarded seals and sensors must be renewed.
searchTerms: left and right cylinder head assembly

when.summary: When a removed 5.0L cylinder head requires valve, valve-stem-seal or head-fitting service.
notes: Begin with the head prepared for bench disassembly. Vehicle removal, camshaft and timing work, and engine refitting are separate phases.

prepare.title: Arrange the spring-compressor equipment
prepare.detail: Use the specified compressor components: 303-300, 303-350, 303-1249 and 303-1418. This work requires the capability to control spring load and handle the small retaining keys.

prepare.title: Prepare a clean, organized bench
prepare.detail: Provide marked storage for components by original location, clean engine oil, and torque tools suitable for the listed fasteners. Keep cleaning debris away from all internal passages.

prepare.title: Gather the required new parts
prepare.detail: Have new valve-stem seals for either head, a new coolant-outlet gasket for the left head, and a new cylinder head temperature sensor and coolant-outlet O-ring for the right head. The outlet O-ring uses clean Motorcraft Orange coolant, VC-3-B, specification WSS-M97B44-D.

steps.title: Identify the head and mark reusable parts
steps.body: Establish whether the head is left-hand or right-hand before stripping its fittings. Mark components so anything reused returns to its original location. Keep this organization through both disassembly and assembly.

steps.title: Strip the left-hand head fittings
steps.body: For the left-hand head, remove the coolant-outlet bolts and outlet, then discard its gasket. Remove the bolts, camshaft position (CMP) sensors and radio interference capacitor.

steps.title: Strip the right-hand head fittings
steps.body: For the right-hand head, remove the CMP sensor and its bolt. Remove and discard the cylinder head temperature (CHT) sensor. Remove the coolant-outlet bolt and outlet, and discard the O-ring.

steps.title: Remove the plugs and valve assemblies
steps.body: On either head, remove the spark plugs. Use the specified compressor equipment to remove each valve's keys, retainer and spring. Remove and discard the valve-stem seal, then withdraw the valve. Repeat for the remaining valves while preserving their locations.

steps.title: Install new seals and return the valves
steps.body: Lubricate each new valve-stem seal and valve-guide bore with clean engine oil. Install the new seal, then install the valve into the head. Return reused valves to their original positions.

steps.title: Rebuild the spring assemblies
steps.body: Using the specified compressor equipment, install each spring, retainer and set of keys. Repeat for all remaining valves. Install the spark plugs and tighten them to 15 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the right-hand head fittings
steps.body: Install a new CHT sensor and tighten it to 11 Nm. Install the CMP sensor and bolt at 10 Nm. Lubricate a new coolant-outlet O-ring with the specified clean coolant, install the outlet pipe, and tighten its fastener to 10 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the left-hand head fittings
steps.body: Install the coolant outlet with a new gasket and tighten its bolts to 10 Nm. Refit the CMP sensors, radio interference capacitor and bolts, also tightening to 10 Nm.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled spring load
watchFor.body: Keep the spring controlled by the specified compressor while removing or installing its keys. Do not improvise around an inadequately supported spring.

watchFor.title: Mixed locations or reused discard parts
watchFor.body: Maintain component identification throughout the work. Renew every removed valve-stem seal and the head-specific discarded gasket, O-ring or CHT sensor.

notes: Use the engine identification information when selecting replacement parts; revisions can differ within the same engine family.

diagnostics.finding: Foreign material enters an oil or coolant passage during stripping or cleaning.
diagnostics.meaning: Contamination can cause engine failure after reassembly.
diagnostics.next: Restore cleanliness before continuing and prevent further debris from entering the passages.

verification.title: Account for every valve assembly
verification.body: Confirm that each valve has its new seal, spring, retainer and keys installed, and that reused components occupy their original locations.

verification.title: Record the completed head assembly
verification.body: Record the head side, required new parts and completed tightening checks for spark plugs, sensors and coolant outlet before the head proceeds to engine assembly.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L cylinder-head bench disassembly and assembly, including common valve work and separate left/right fitting sequences.

guides.title: Service the left-hand camshafts on the 5.0L and 5.2L V8
guides.summary: Remove and inspect the left-hand camshafts, followers and lash adjusters, then restore their positions with new variable-timing oil filters.
guides.introduction: The left-hand cylinder bank has separate intake and exhaust camshafts. Their lobes act through roller followers, while hydraulic lash adjusters take up valve-train clearance. Variable camshaft timing (VCT) changes valve timing to suit operating conditions. This job removes those camshafts and their associated followers and adjusters for inspection or replacement.
guides.why: The front bearing mega cap must come off before the other bearing caps to avoid engine damage. Reused components must return to their original positions, and the camshafts must be aligned as illustrated before fastening. Cleanliness protects the oil passages that serve the engine and its hydraulic components.

when.summary: When confirmed camshaft or valve-train damage, or another engine repair, requires left-bank camshaft removal.
notes: If both banks are being serviced, remove the right-hand camshafts first.
Early-build 5.2L engines do not have spring clips on the roller followers.

prepare.title: Plan the complete timing work
prepare.detail: Have the VCT-unit removal and installation procedure for the actual engine and the capability to complete its prerequisites. Provide suitable torque-and-angle tools and a clean way to retain each component's original position.

prepare.title: Gather new filters and assembly oil
prepare.detail: Obtain new VCT system oil filters. The 5.0L procedure calls for clean engine oil; the 5.2L specifies SAE 5W-50 oil meeting WSS-M2C931-E1 for the listed assembly lubrication.

steps.title: Remove the left-hand timing units
steps.body: Follow the [5.0L VCT-unit procedure](#/document/G1685333) or [5.2L VCT-unit procedure](#/document/G1800286). If both banks are involved, complete right-hand camshaft removal first. Remove and discard the VCT system oil filters.

steps.title: Release the bearing caps in the required order
steps.body: Remove the bolts and front camshaft bearing mega cap first. Then remove the remaining bearing caps and bolts, followed by the intake and exhaust camshafts. Preserve the original locations of all components that may be reused.

steps.title: Remove and inspect followers and adjusters
steps.body: Remove the roller followers and hydraulic lash adjusters. Where spring clips are fitted, separate the adjusters from those clips. Inspect the followers and adjusters for damage; any damage requires inspection of the associated camshaft lobes and valves as well.

steps.title: Reassemble and lubricate the valve-train parts
steps.body: Replace damaged components as necessary. Attach adjusters to follower spring clips where fitted, lubricate with the appropriate clean engine oil and reinstall the components. Return every reused component to its original location; follow the clip-free arrangement on early 5.2L engines.

steps.title: Position the camshafts accurately
steps.body: Lubricate the 5.0L camshafts before installation, or the journals and lobes specifically identified for the 5.2L. Install the intake and exhaust camshafts with their D-slots aligned exactly as shown in the selected engine procedure. The 5.0L instruction identifies this as the neutral position.

steps.title: Fit all caps before tightening
steps.body: Install the bearing caps and bolts without tightening, then install the front mega cap and its bolts, also loose. Only after all are positioned should the bolts be tightened through the stages in the applicable camshaft procedure.

steps.title: Restore the VCT system
steps.body: Install new VCT system oil filters into the camshafts. Reinstall the left-hand VCT units through the matching engine procedure, completing its timing and reassembly requirements before road testing.

watchFor.title: Clip-free 5.2L hardware
watchFor.body: Do not assume an early 5.2L follower is missing a part merely because it has no spring clip. Identify the actual arrangement before separating or assembling components.

watchFor.title: Contamination during open-engine work
watchFor.body: Keep cleaning debris and other foreign material out of oil passages, coolant passages and the oil pan; contamination can cause engine failure.

notes: The attached follower illustrations belong to the 5.0L procedure. Use each engine's own D-slot illustration for camshaft positioning.

diagnostics.finding: A hydraulic lash adjuster or roller follower is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The inspection must extend to the contacting camshaft lobes and valves.
diagnostics.next: Inspect those related parts and replace damaged components as necessary before reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm the assembly requirements
verification.body: Confirm reused parts returned to their original positions, the camshafts were aligned using the correct illustration, all cap-tightening stages were completed and new VCT oil filters were installed.

verification.title: Road test and record the result
verification.body: Road test the vehicle after completing the VCT-unit installation. Record the damaged parts found, components renewed and road-test outcome.

5.2L left-hand camshaft removal and installation, including early-build follower differences and specified lubrication.
Remove and reinstall the 5.0L left-hand VCT units and complete their timing-related prerequisites.
Remove and reinstall the 5.2L left-hand VCT units and complete their timing-related prerequisites.

guides.title: Remove and install the right-hand camshafts on 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Service the right-hand intake and exhaust camshafts while preserving component positions, bearing-cap order and engine-specific timing requirements.
guides.introduction: The right-hand cylinder head contains intake and exhaust camshafts whose lobes operate the valves through roller followers supported by hydraulic lash adjusters. The adjusters maintain the working relationship between these moving parts. Variable camshaft timing, or VCT, changes valve timing through units attached to the camshafts. This repair removes those units first, then exposes the camshafts and their supporting valve-train components.
guides.why: Clean oil passages and correctly assembled bearing supports are essential to engine survival. Debris introduced during repair can cause engine failure. The front bearing mega cap must come off before the other caps, reusable parts must return to their original positions, and the camshaft D-slots must match the engine-specific alignment illustration.

when.summary: When confirmed camshaft or related valve-train damage requires repair, or associated engine work requires camshaft removal.
notes: Use the engine identification information to select parts and the matching timing procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange internal-engine and timing capability
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment required by the matching VCT unit procedure before beginning. Its timing prerequisites remain part of this repair.

prepare.title: Organize a clean working area
prepare.detail: Keep removed caps, camshafts, followers and lash adjusters associated with their original locations. Prevent foreign material from entering oil passages, coolant passages or the oil pan.

prepare.title: Prepare lubrication and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have clean engine oil and new VCT system oil filters for the 5.0L. The 5.2L specifies Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil, XO-5W50-QGT, meeting WSS-M2C931-E1.

steps.title: Remove the right-hand timing units
steps.body: Complete the [5.0L VCT procedure](#/document/G1685333) or [5.2L VCT procedure](#/document/G1800286) through removal before working on the bearing caps. Remove the VCT oil filters from the camshafts; discard them on the 5.0L.

steps.title: Release the camshaft bearing supports
steps.body: Follow the [5.0L camshaft procedure](#/document/G1685314) or [5.2L camshaft procedure](#/document/G1800267). Remove the front mega-cap bolts and mega cap first, then the remaining bearing-cap bolts and caps. Remove the intake and exhaust camshafts.

steps.title: Remove and inspect the followers and adjusters
steps.body: Remove the roller followers and hydraulic lash adjusters. Separate adjusters from the follower spring clips where fitted. Early-build 5.2L engines do not have these clips. Inspect the followers and adjusters; damage requires inspection of the camshaft lobes and valves as well.

steps.title: Reassemble and lubricate the valve-train parts
steps.body: Replace damaged components as necessary. Assemble the adjusters onto the follower spring clips where fitted, lubricate with clean engine oil and reinstall. Return reusable components to their original positions, using the specified oil for the 5.2L.

steps.title: Position the camshafts
steps.body: Lubricate the camshafts before installation; the 5.2L specifically identifies the journals and lobes. Install the intake and exhaust camshafts with the D-slots aligned exactly as illustrated in the selected procedure. The 5.0L instruction identifies this as the neutral position.

steps.title: Install and tighten the bearing caps
steps.body: Install the individual bearing caps and bolts without tightening, then install the front mega cap and its bolts without tightening. Only then carry out the engine's specified staged tightening instructions. Do not tighten caps as each is placed.

steps.title: Restore the timing assemblies
steps.body: Install the VCT oil filters, using new filters on the 5.0L. Reinstall the right-hand VCT units through the matching timing procedure, completing its required operations before returning the vehicle to service.

watchFor.title: Mixed component locations
watchFor.body: Reusable parts must retain their original locations throughout removal, inspection and installation.

watchFor.title: Damage beyond the first failed part
watchFor.body: A damaged follower or adjuster calls for inspecting the associated camshaft lobes and valves before deciding the repair scope.

notes: The absence of follower spring clips on an early-build 5.2L is a documented construction difference.

diagnostics.finding: Damage to a hydraulic lash adjuster or roller follower
diagnostics.meaning: The repair may involve more than the initially removed component.
diagnostics.next: Inspect camshaft lobes and valves, then replace damaged parts as necessary.

verification.title: Complete the road test
verification.body: Both engine procedures finish with a road test after camshaft and VCT installation.

verification.title: Record the repair and result
verification.body: Record the damage found, parts replaced and road-test result against the original repair concern.

guides.title: Replace the 5.0L or 5.2L crankshaft rear seal and service its retainer
guides.summary: Renew the rear crankshaft sealing arrangement using the correct engine-specific retainer, sensor and seal-installation sequence.
guides.introduction: The rear crankshaft seal retains engine oil where the rotating crankshaft exits the back of the engine. Its retainer plate forms a separate sealed joint with the block, and the crankshaft position sensor sits nearby. This repair reaches the area behind the flywheel or flexplate. The 5.0L and 5.2L paths differ significantly: the 5.0L requires oil-pan removal, while the 5.2L procedure replaces the retainer plate and sensor and releases the pan-to-retainer attachments.
guides.why: A new seal cannot compensate for a poorly sealed retainer joint. Clean surfaces, the prescribed sealant working time and the proper installer all matter. The crankshaft sensor ring also needs careful handling: dropping it requires replacement even when damage is not obvious. The 5.2L adds a unique seal orientation and a separate sensor-bonding process.
searchTerms: 5.2L rear seal retainer and crankshaft sensor

when.summary: When repair of the rear crankshaft seal or retainer sealing joint is required.
notes: Oil near the engine-to-transmission joint should be traced before committing to this extensive access work.

prepare.title: Plan the access work
prepare.detail: Provide the capability and equipment required by the applicable flywheel or flexplate procedure. The 5.0L also requires its oil-pan removal and installation procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare tools and materials
prepare.detail: Both engines use seal installer 303-1250 and handle 205-153. The 5.0L additionally uses remover 303-519 with slide hammer 100-001. Have the specified Motorcraft TA-357 silicone; the 5.2L also requires Loctite 7649 Primer, Loctite 638 Sealer, a replacement retainer and replacement crankshaft position sensor.

steps.title: Expose and inspect the rear components
steps.body: Remove the 5.0L flexplate or flywheel, or the 5.2L flywheel, using the matching procedure. Remove the crankshaft sensor ring and engine-to-transmission spacer plate. Inspect the ring and discard it if dropped or visibly damaged.

steps.title: Follow the correct removal branch
steps.body: For the [5.0L](#/document/G1685317), extract and discard the seal with the specified remover and slide hammer, disconnect and remove the crankshaft position (CKP) sensor, remove the oil pan, then remove the retainer. For the [5.2L](#/document/G1800270), disconnect the sensor, remove the pan-to-retainer bolts, loosen the sensor bolt and remove the retainer bolts. Discard the retainer plate and CKP sensor.

steps.title: Prepare and seal the retainer joint
steps.body: Follow the [RTV surface-cleaning procedure](#/document/G1692003). On the 5.2L, prime the replacement retainer's sensor bore with Loctite 7649 and allow 2 minutes to dry without contamination. Apply the specified silicone bead to the block and secure the retainer within 4 minutes; if that time is exceeded, remove the sealant and clean again. Follow the staged tightening instructions. The 5.2L retainer is tilted up into position before its sequenced tightening and pan-to-retainer bolt installation.

steps.title: Install the new crankshaft seal
steps.body: Lubricate the seal bore and lips with clean engine oil; the 5.2L specifies Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 full synthetic oil meeting WSS-M2C931-E1. Position installer 303-1250 on the crankshaft, slide the new seal onto it and install with handle 205-153. For the 5.2L, follow its seal-orientation detail exactly; do not copy the orientation of an earlier V8 seal.

steps.title: Restore the sensor and surrounding assemblies
steps.body: Reinstall and reconnect the 5.0L CKP sensor, then reinstall its oil pan. For the new 5.2L sensor, apply a 2 mm bead of Loctite 638 around its barrel, 25 mm from the bottom end, before installation. Tighten and reconnect the sensor as specified. Restore the sensor ring and spacer plate, followed by the engine's appropriate flywheel or flexplate.

steps.title: Complete the road test
steps.body: After completing the linked installation procedures, road test the vehicle as required by both rear-seal procedures. Record the outcome against the concern that prompted the repair.

watchFor.title: Dropped sensor ring
watchFor.body: A ring that has been dropped must be discarded, even without visible damage.

watchFor.title: Mixing engine procedures
watchFor.body: The 5.2L replacement sensor, priming process and unique seal orientation are specific requirements, not optional additions to the 5.0L method.

notes: The 5.2L primer remains effective for up to 30 days after application, provided the primed surface is protected from other substances.
The 5.0L illustration of seal extraction should not be treated as the 5.2L seal-orientation instruction.

diagnostics.finding: The retainer was not secured within the sealant working time.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing process no longer meets the required installation condition.
diagnostics.next: Remove the sealant, clean the sealing area and repeat the application and installation.

verification.title: Check the engine-specific completion points
verification.body: Confirm the CKP connector is attached, the sensor ring passed inspection or was replaced, and the correct seal-installation branch was completed.

verification.title: Record the road-test result
verification.body: Record completion of the required road test and whether the original concern remains.

guides.title: Remove and refit the left cylinder head on the 5.0L V8
guides.summary: Remove the left cylinder head, inspect its mating surfaces and reinstall it with a new gasket and bolts before restoring timing, fluids and exhaust connections.
guides.introduction: The left-hand (LH) aluminum cylinder head carries the valves and overhead camshafts for one bank of the 5.0L engine. Its gasket seals the head-to-block joint around combustion chambers and fluid passages. Removing the head is a major repair involving camshaft work, exhaust access and temporary changes to engine support, followed by surface inspection and controlled bolt tightening.
guides.why: A new gasket depends on suitable mating surfaces and the correct clamping load. Scratches can form leak paths, trapped liquid or debris must be cleared from bolt holes, and torque-to-yield head bolts must be replaced. Camshaft and engine-support procedures are essential parts of the job.

when.summary: After diagnosis establishes a need to remove the LH cylinder head for repair or further inspection.
notes: Confirm engine identification when selecting replacement parts.

prepare.title: Arrange specialist engine capability
prepare.detail: Have a hoist, lifting bracket 303-050, support bar 303-F072, torque-and-angle tools, compressed air and oil-drain equipment. The work also requires fuel-pressure release, cooling-system service and camshaft-timing capability.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts and clean working conditions
prepare.detail: Obtain a new head gasket, new head bolts, a new oil filter and engine oil selected through the 5.0L specifications. Keep cleaning debris out of the exposed engine.

steps.title: Lift the vehicle and drain the cooling system
steps.body: Follow the [5.0L LH head procedure](#/document/G1685318). With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist at the specified lifting points. Release fuel-system pressure and drain the cooling system through their respective procedures.

steps.title: Remove the intake, camshaft and exhaust dependencies
steps.body: Disconnect the LH heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) and catalyst-monitor sensor connectors and release their harness retainers. Remove the intake manifold, LH camshaft and LH catalytic converter in that order, following each linked removal procedure and its prerequisites.

steps.title: Restore mount support before lifting off the head
steps.body: Install the LH engine-mount bracket, bolts and stud bolt. Use the support tools to lower the engine onto the LH mount, then remove the tools. Disconnect the camshaft position (CMP) sensors and ignition-interference capacitor, move the ground wire aside and detach the head harness retainer. Remove and discard the head bolts, lift off the head and discard its gasket.

steps.title: Clean and assess both mating surfaces
steps.body: Clean the head and block without metal scrapers, wire brushes, abrasive discs or other abrasive methods. Clear all coolant, oil and debris from the block's head-bolt holes using compressed air. Perform the separate cylinder-head and cylinder-block distortion checks before deciding the joint is ready for assembly.

steps.title: Install the gasket, head and new bolts
steps.body: Fit a new gasket and install the head with new torque-to-yield bolts. Follow the complete seven-stage 5.0L tightening instruction, including its intermediate 180° loosening stage. Do not reduce it to a single torque setting. Restore the head harness retainer, ground wire, CMP connectors and interference-capacitor connection.

steps.title: Reopen access and restore the removed assemblies
steps.body: Fit the lifting bracket and support bar with its legs on body structure, clear of the fenders. Raise the LH side of the engine 25 mm and remove the LH mount bracket. Install the LH catalytic converter, LH camshaft and intake manifold in that order using their complete installation procedures, including timing and support restoration.

steps.title: Reconnect the exhaust sensors and renew the oil
steps.body: Reconnect both LH exhaust-sensor connectors and retain their harnesses. Drain the engine oil and reinstall the drain plug. Discard the old oil filter and install a new one using its specified torque-and-angle stages without lubricating the O-ring. Fill with clean oil to the 5.0L specification.

steps.title: Fill, bleed and road test
steps.body: Complete the cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure, then road test the vehicle. This final operating check follows completion of the mechanical, electrical and fluid-restoration work.

watchFor.title: Damaged sealing faces
watchFor.body: Abrasive cleaning can scratch or gouge the head and block, creating leak paths beneath a new gasket.

watchFor.title: Unsafe vehicle support
watchFor.body: Use the marked lifting locations and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

notes: The exhaust-connector illustrations show an automatic transmission; the manual-transmission arrangement is similar.

diagnostics.finding: A mating surface does not satisfy its distortion check.
diagnostics.meaning: The joint has not been established as suitable for reassembly.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the condition using the applicable head or block inspection procedure before installing the gasket.

verification.title: Confirm assembly milestones
verification.body: Confirm completion of the head-bolt stages, camshaft installation, sensor reconnections, oil and filter renewal, and cooling-system bleeding.

verification.title: Record inspection and operating results
verification.body: Record the head and block inspection results and the road-test outcome, including any unresolved original concern.

guides.title: Remove and refit the right-hand cylinder head on the 5.0L V8
guides.summary: Remove the right-hand cylinder head, inspect its mating surfaces and reinstall it with a new gasket and bolts before renewing fluids.
guides.introduction: The right-hand cylinder head closes one bank of cylinders and carries its valves and overhead camshafts. Its gasket seals the joint to the cylinder block. Removing the head involves fuel-pressure release, cooling-system draining, camshaft work and a controlled transfer of engine support.
guides.why: A new gasket needs sound, clean mating surfaces and the correct bolt loading. Scratches can create leak paths, contamination can enter engine passages, and the torque-to-yield head bolts cannot be reused. The support sequence also matters: the engine must be carried by the prescribed mount or support equipment throughout the work.

when.summary: When a confirmed cylinder-head or gasket repair requires removal of the right-hand head.
notes: This removal procedure is not a diagnostic test proving a head or gasket fault.
Use the engine identification information when selecting replacement parts.

prepare.title: Provide lifting, support and timing capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the approved lifting points, engine lifting bracket 303-050 and support bar 303-F072. Have the capability and equipment required by the linked right-hand camshaft procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean assembly
prepare.detail: Have fuel-pressure-release and cooling-system service capability, oil drain equipment, compressed air and torque-and-angle tools. Obtain a new head gasket, new head bolts, a new oil filter and the specified refill fluids.

steps.title: Depressurize and drain before dismantling
steps.body: With the vehicle in Neutral, position it on the hoist. Follow [Fuel System Pressure Release](#/document/G1702146), then drain the cooling system through [the 5.0L cooling procedure](#/document/G1694583). Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

steps.title: Remove the connected assemblies
steps.body: Remove the [intake manifold](#/document/G1685326), [right-hand camshafts](#/document/G1685314) and [right-hand exhaust manifold](#/document/G1685323), in that order. Complete their access, timing and support requirements as part of this job.

steps.title: Transfer engine weight back to the mount
steps.body: Install the right-hand engine mount bracket, bolts and stud bolts, tightening them as specified. Use the lifting bracket and support bar to lower the engine onto the right-hand mount, then remove those special tools.

steps.title: Disconnect and lift off the head
steps.body: Disconnect the heater hose, camshaft position sensor connector and cylinder head temperature (CHT) sensor connector. Remove and discard the head bolts, remove the cylinder head, then discard the gasket.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the joint
steps.body: Clean and inspect both mating surfaces using the linked head and block distortion procedures. Do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes, power abrasive discs or other abrasive methods. Clear coolant, oil and foreign material from the block's head-bolt holes with compressed air while keeping debris out of engine passages.

steps.title: Install the gasket, head and new bolts
steps.body: Fit a new gasket, position the head and install new torque-to-yield bolts. Follow the numbered tightening illustration and every tightening, loosening and angle stage in [the head procedure](#/document/G1685319). Reconnect the heater hose and both sensor connectors.

steps.title: Restore access for reassembly
steps.body: Reinstall the lifting bracket and support bar, then raise the right-hand side of the engine 25 mm (1 inch). Remove the mount bracket, bolts and stud bolts. Reinstall the exhaust manifold, right-hand camshafts and intake manifold through their respective procedures, including their support and timing operations.

steps.title: Renew the oil and restore the cooling system
steps.body: Drain the engine oil and reinstall the drain plug to specification. Discard the old filter and install a new one without lubricating its O-ring; use this procedure's staged filter-tightening instruction. Fill with clean oil to [5.0L Specifications](#/document/G1685306), then fill and bleed the cooling system through the linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Support removed before the weight transfer
watchFor.body: The removal sequence lowers the engine onto the reinstalled mount before the special support tools are removed. Preserve that order.

watchFor.title: Abrasive damage to sealing faces
watchFor.body: Cleaning must not scratch or gouge the head or block. A damaged face can remain a leak path beneath a new gasket.

notes: The dry oil-filter O-ring instruction belongs to this 5.0L repair procedure; retain it during the final oil service.

diagnostics.finding: Head or block mating-surface inspection identifies distortion.
diagnostics.meaning: A new gasket alone does not establish a serviceable joint.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the finding using the applicable distortion procedure before committing to reassembly.

verification.title: Complete restoration and road testing
verification.body: Confirm the linked reassembly operations, oil refill and cooling-system filling and bleeding are complete, then road test the vehicle.

verification.title: Record the repair result
verification.body: Record the mating-surface inspection results, installation of new gasket and head bolts, completion of the tightening stages, and the road-test outcome.

guides.title: Replace the engine oil cooler — 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove, inspect and replace the oil cooler using the correct connections, access route and fluid checks for your engine.
guides.introduction: The oil cooler transfers heat away from engine oil, which supplies the engine’s bearings and oil galleries. The two engines use different arrangements: the 5.0L procedure disconnects coolant hoses and removes the oil filter, while the 5.2L procedure disconnects oil tubes and requires access through the left wheel area. Identify the engine before ordering parts or beginning work.
guides.why: Secure connections and correct fluid levels protect the lubrication system after reassembly. Metal inside a cooler is especially significant: replacing the cooler without correcting the underlying mechanical concern can lead to engine failure.

when.summary: When the oil cooler requires removal for inspection or replacement.
notes: Check engine identification information to obtain the correct parts.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the linked lifting procedure. Locate the lifting points by their stamped triangles and check adapter clearance. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the engine-specific supplies
prepare.detail: For the 5.0L, have hose locking pliers, a new cooler gasket and a new oil filter. Have suitable torque equipment and the specified replenishment fluids. The 5.2L also requires left wheel removal.

steps.title: Identify the branch and lift the vehicle
steps.body: Place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on the hoist. Follow only the cooler procedure matching the engine; the two access and connection sequences are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Remove the 5.0L cooler
steps.body: For either the shield alone or the bracket-and-shield assembly, loosen the two front bolts and remove the remaining bolts and assembly. Discard the oil filter. Clamp the coolant hoses with hose locking pliers, disconnect them, then remove the cooler retainer and cooler.

steps.title: Remove the 5.2L cooler
steps.body: Remove the underbody shielding and left wheel. Remove the bracket and air duct, then release the shield retainers and position the shield aside. Remove the retaining clips, disconnect the oil cooler tubes and remove the cooler fasteners and cooler.

steps.title: Inspect before installing another cooler
steps.body: Inspect the removed cooler and address any metal or aluminum contamination using the diagnostic decision below. On the 5.0L, remove and discard the cooler gasket.

steps.title: Reassemble the 5.0L arrangement
steps.body: Install a new gasket, cooler and retainer. Reconnect the coolant hoses and remove the locking pliers. Install a new filter without lubricating its O-ring, using the specified tightening stages. Refit the applicable shield assembly using its illustrated fastener groups and torque values.

steps.title: Reassemble the 5.2L arrangement
steps.body: Install the cooler, reconnect its tubes and install the retaining clips. Restore the shield, air duct and bracket. Apply the distinct bracket-to-cooler and bracket-to-frame tightening specifications, then reinstall the left wheel and underbody shielding.

steps.title: Restore the fluid levels
steps.body: Inspect and adjust engine oil level on either engine. On the 5.0L, also inspect and adjust coolant level in the degas bottle. Keep the fluid requirements specific to each engine.

watchFor.title: Hoses left clamped
watchFor.body: Remove the 5.0L hose locking pliers after reconnecting the coolant hoses.

watchFor.title: Different shield fasteners
watchFor.body: The 5.0L shield and bracket-and-shield arrangements have different tightening groups; use the matching illustration.

notes: 5.0L coolant: Motorcraft Orange Concentrated Antifreeze/Coolant, VC-3-B, specification WSS-M97B44-D.
5.2L oil: Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil, XO-5W50-QGT, specification WSS-M2C931-E1.

diagnostics.finding: Metal or aluminum material inside either cooler.
diagnostics.meaning: An underlying mechanical concern exists and can cause engine failure if left unresolved.
diagnostics.next: Complete the mechanical diagnosis directed to Section 303-00 before treating cooler replacement as the completed repair.

verification.title: Confirm the correct completion checks
verification.body: Verify the engine oil level on both engines and the degas-bottle coolant level on the 5.0L. Confirm the disturbed connections, retainers and shielding have been restored.

guides.title: Replace Secondary Timing Chain Tensioners on the 5.0L or 5.2L
guides.summary: Renew the secondary chain tensioner and shoe, restore camshaft timing-unit alignment and activate the replacement tensioner.
guides.introduction: Each secondary timing chain connects the intake and exhaust variable camshaft timing (VCT) assemblies on its cylinder bank. The hydraulic tensioner acts through a shoe to keep the chain tensioned. Replacement requires removing the VCT assemblies and restoring their precise relationship to the chain and camshafts.
guides.why: This is engine-timing work: correct seating, chain alignment and controlled tensioner release all matter. The replacement tensioner is shorter than the earlier design, so its appearance alone cannot establish whether it is fully installed.

when.summary: When secondary timing-chain tensioner renewal is required during engine repair.
notes: Identify the engine and serviced bank before selecting parts and procedures.

prepare.title: Arrange timing-work capability
prepare.detail: Have the engine-specific VCT and primary timing-chain procedures, camshaft counterholding wrench, torque-and-angle equipment and, for 5.2L installation, an assistant.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts and a clean work area
prepare.detail: Use replacement tensioners and shoes, with shipping clips retained until instructed. Have clean engine oil for the seals and bore. Keep debris out of oil passages, coolant passages and the oil pan.

steps.title: Remove the VCT assemblies in the required order
steps.body: Follow the [5.0L VCT procedure](#/document/G1685333) or [5.2L VCT procedure](#/document/G1800286). If servicing both banks, remove the right-hand secondary tensioner before the left-hand one.

steps.title: Discard the removed shoe and tensioner
steps.body: After removing that bank's VCT assemblies, remove and discard the shoe. Push the tensioner upward from beneath the camshaft mega cap—the cap containing its bore—and discard it too.

steps.title: Seat the replacement tensioner and shoe
steps.body: When servicing both banks, follow the left-hand installation phase first. Leave the shipping clip fitted. Oil the tensioner O-ring seals and mega-cap bore, then push the tensioner fully downward until it snaps into place. Install the replacement shoe; its tabs contact the front of the mega cap.

steps.title: Align the secondary chain and fit the VCT assemblies
steps.body: Place the intake timing mark between the two consecutive colored chain links and the exhaust mark at the single colored link. For the 5.0L, follow its illustrated installation position. For the 5.2L, position the exhaust mark approximately at 12 o'clock; have an assistant turn the intake camshaft counterclockwise using its flats until the locating pin engages, then slide both assemblies fully onto the camshafts.

steps.title: Secure the assemblies while counterholding
steps.body: Hold each camshaft with a wrench on its flats while installing the intake and exhaust VCT assembly bolts. Both engine procedures specify 15 Nm followed by 90°. Counterholding keeps tightening force from turning the camshaft.

steps.title: Release and activate the tensioner
steps.body: Remove and discard the shipping clip only now. Press the secondary chain and tensioner top shoe downward until the tensioner bottoms out, then release them. The tensioner should spring upward and tension the chain.

steps.title: Restore the primary timing drive
steps.body: Install the corresponding primary chain using the [5.0L timing-chain procedure](#/document/G1685330) or [5.2L timing-chain procedure](#/document/G1800283). When doing both banks, complete the left-hand chain installation before repeating the tensioner installation sequence on the right-hand side and installing its chain.

watchFor.title: Premature clip removal
watchFor.body: Keep the shipping clip fitted through tensioner seating, chain alignment and VCT bolt tightening.

watchFor.title: Contamination during cleaning
watchFor.body: Material scraped from gasket surfaces can enter engine passages and cause engine failure.

notes: The supplied tensioner-removal illustrations belong to the 5.0L procedure.
Use engine identification information when ordering parts; revisions can differ within an engine family.

diagnostics.finding: The replacement tensioner does not extend below the mega cap.
diagnostics.meaning: This is a feature of the revised, shorter design.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the snap-in seating and correct shoe-tab position.

verification.title: Confirm seating and timing
verification.body: Check full tensioner seating, shoe position, colored-link alignment and fully seated VCT assemblies before release.

verification.title: Confirm activation
verification.body: Verify that the tensioner springs upward and tensions the chain, then complete the engine-specific primary-chain installation.

guides.title: Remove, overhaul and reinstall the 5.2L V8 engine
guides.summary: Rebuild the 5.2L engine through controlled removal, inspection, bearing selection, valve timing, sealing and installation.
guides.introduction: The 5.2L engine combines a flat-plane crankshaft with double overhead camshafts and twin independent variable camshaft timing. Its bearings depend on pressurized oil, while its chains keep piston and valve movement synchronized. An overhaul opens these closely related systems, allowing damaged or worn components to be inspected and renewed before the engine is rebuilt and returned to the vehicle.
guides.why: Cleanliness, component identity and assembly order determine whether the rebuilt engine can survive. Debris can obstruct lubrication, mismatched connecting-rod caps can change bearing clearance, and incorrect camshaft phasing can cause serious internal damage. This is specialist engine work requiring measurement and controlled lifting, not simply replacement of visible worn parts.

when.summary: When established internal damage or measured wear requires engine removal and a full strip-down.
notes: Identify the engine build before ordering parts; components can differ within the same engine family.
Use measured condition to decide what needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and bench capability
prepare.detail: Provide a vehicle hoist, floor crane, engine stand, lifting bracket 303-F047, support bar 303-F072, and a trolley jack with wooden block. Support-bar feet belong on the body structure, and transmission support belongs under the bell housing.

prepare.title: Prepare measuring and assembly equipment
prepare.detail: Have clearance and end-play measuring capability, torque and angle tools, a piston ring compressor, clutch aligner, crankshaft holding tool and the specified seal installers and puller. An assistant is required during the camshaft/VCT operations.

prepare.title: Organize clean parts and replacements
prepare.detail: Keep reusable parts identified by original position. Prepare the specified engine oil, coolant, sealants and primer, plus every gasket, seal and fastener designated for replacement in the linked phases.

steps.title: Isolate the vehicle and clear access
steps.body: Follow the [removal phase](#/document/G1800288): place the vehicle in Neutral on the hoist, release fuel pressure, disconnect both battery cables and drain coolant. Loosen the steering-column dash seal and hold the steering wheel straight ahead. Index-mark the hood, then remove the prescribed intake, cooling, cowl, exhaust and starter components. Drain engine oil, discard the filter and disconnect the oil-cooler hoses.

steps.title: Separate and lift the engine
steps.body: Disconnect the steering shaft without hammering or prying; discard its bolt and secure the shaft to the frame rail. Use the support bar while removing mount brackets and positioning the air-conditioning compressor aside. Move transmission cooler tubes only if fitted. Transfer engine support to the crane, support the transmission beneath its bell housing, remove the remaining joining fasteners and lift the engine clear.

steps.title: Strip external components on the bench
steps.body: Begin the [disassembly phase](#/document/G1800290). Index-mark a reusable pressure plate and loosen its bolts evenly. Discard pressure-plate and flywheel bolts. Inspect the crankshaft sensor ring before mounting the engine on its stand. Remove the harness, covers, manifolds, pulley, coolant pump, oil pan and front cover in sequence. Retain the original pulley washer; renew discarded seals, gaskets and hardware.

steps.title: Remove timing components and heads in order
steps.body: Turn clockwise to the specified 9:30 crankshaft-keyway position and confirm the right-hand VCT timing mark is uppermost before dismantling that bank. An assistant must restrain the intake camshaft as the VCT assemblies come off. Remove each front camshaft mega cap before the remaining caps. Turn clockwise to 12:30 for the left-hand bank. Keep followers and lash adjusters identified. Remove the cylinder heads only when cool, and always before removing the crankshaft.

steps.title: Inspect and dismantle the bottom end
steps.body: Protect exposed passages and aluminum gasket faces. Check head and block distortion using their linked procedures. Remove the oil-filter adapter, discarded rear seal-retainer plate and crankshaft-position sensor, sprocket and pump. Inspect bore tops before withdrawing pistons. Preserve connecting-rod/cap orientation and avoid scratching journals or bores. Complete the [piston subassembly work](#/document/G1800293), then remove main caps, crankshaft, bearings and cooling jets.

steps.title: Select bearings and rebuild the rotating assembly
steps.body: Start the [assembly phase](#/document/G1800295) by recording block and crankshaft bearing codes. Use separate selection charts for mains 1 and 5 and for mains 2, 3 and 4. Install cooling jets and lubricated bearings with oil passages aligned. Orient the thrust-washer groove rearward, seat the washer as directed and install new discarded main-cap fasteners. Check end play and crankshaft turning torque before fitting pistons. Check piston and ring clearances, position ring gaps correctly, and install matched rod caps with new bolts.

steps.title: Restore lubrication and time the camshafts
steps.body: Prime the oil pump with 2 tablespoons of clean engine oil and rotate it by hand before installation. Refit the rear retainer and crankshaft-position sensor with their specified primer and sealant treatment. Install new head gaskets and head bolts. Assemble the left-hand camshafts and chains first at the specified 12:30 keyway position; then turn counterclockwise to 9:30 for the right-hand bank. Follow the illustrated D-slots, colored links and timing marks exactly, using new VCT bolts and the specified VCT filters.

steps.title: Seal and dress the engine
steps.body: Fully depress the VCT solenoid pins before fitting the front cover. Observe each joint's bead pattern and deadline: the rear retainer has a 4-minute securing window; the front cover, oil pan, pulley and valve covers have specified 5-minute requirements. The front-cover and oil-pan 1-hour alternatives apply only after their designated preliminary fasteners are tightened on time. Engage the pickup tube fully into its new seal. Refit accessories, new manifold studs and nuts, gaskets, covers and harness. Replace spark-plug-tube and VCT solenoid seals only where damaged seals were removed.

steps.title: Complete the rear seal and clutch assembly
steps.body: Transfer the engine to the crane for rear-seal installation, following the unique seal orientation shown in the assembly illustration. Refit the sensor ring, spacer and flywheel with new flywheel bolts. Align a reused pressure plate to its index marks; align replacement parts by their paint dots. Center the clutch disc and tighten new pressure-plate bolts progressively in the prescribed star pattern.

steps.title: Reinstall and recommission
steps.body: Follow the [installation phase](#/document/G1800297), including input-shaft lubrication, engine/transmission alignment and controlled support transfers. Restore mounts, grounds, hoses, wiring and removed components. Install a new steering-shaft bolt and perform the steering-column collapsed check before completing dash-seal installation. Use new cross-brace nuts and an oil filter, fill engine oil, reconnect the battery, and fill and bleed the cooling system. Complete the scan-tool misfire-profile routine before the road test.

watchFor.title: Contamination and damaged sealing faces
watchFor.body: Do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes or abrasive discs on head/block sealing faces. Protect openings during cleaning. Never blow clutch friction dust away with compressed air.

watchFor.title: Lost component identity
watchFor.body: Cracked connecting-rod caps must remain matched and correctly oriented. Reused valve-train components return to their original locations; early engines may lack follower spring clips.

watchFor.title: Expired sealant or incorrect timing
watchFor.body: Remove sealant and clean the joint if its permitted assembly window expires. Rotate the crankshaft only as directed during timing work.

notes: Use the linked 5.2L cooling procedure for draining, vacuum filling and bleeding; the installation phase contains a cooling cross-reference labeled 5.0L.
The detailed phases supply the tightening sequences, bearing charts and illustrations needed at the bench.

diagnostics.finding: A crankshaft sensor ring has been dropped or shows visible damage.
diagnostics.meaning: It is unsuitable for reuse.
diagnostics.next: Discard it and install a replacement.

diagnostics.finding: A roller follower or hydraulic lash adjuster is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: Related camshaft lobes and valves also require inspection.
diagnostics.next: Inspect those components and replace damaged parts before assembly.

verification.title: Record the mechanical results
verification.body: Record both bearing codes, selected grades, measured clearances and crankshaft end play against the 5.2L specifications. Crankshaft torque-to-turn must not exceed 6 Nm (53 lb-in) at the prescribed assembly check.

verification.title: Complete vehicle checks
verification.body: Confirm the steering-column collapsed check and prescribed fluid filling are complete. Perform the Powertrain Control Module Misfire Monitor Profile Correction routine with a diagnostic scan tool, then road test and record the result.

guides.title: Disassemble and rebuild a 5.2L cylinder head
guides.summary: Service the removed cylinder head's valves, springs, stem seals and bank-specific fittings while preserving reusable parts in their original locations.
guides.introduction: The 5.2L engine's aluminum cylinder heads carry the valves operated by its overhead camshafts. Valve springs close the valves, retainers and keys secure the springs, and stem seals control oil passing along the valve stems. This bench procedure dismantles and rebuilds those components, with different coolant fittings and sensors on the left and right heads.
guides.why: Reusable components must return to their original positions. Cleanliness protects the engine's oil and coolant passages, while the specified spring-compressor arrangement controls spring load during key removal and installation. The right-head temperature sensor also needs special attention: it must be replaced, and a broken tip must not remain in the head.
searchTerms: broken cylinder head temperature sensor tip

when.summary: When a removed 5.2L cylinder head requires valve, spring or valve-stem-seal service.
notes: This is the cylinder-head bench phase; engine removal, head installation and camshaft timing are separate operations.

prepare.title: Provide the spring-compressor arrangement
prepare.detail: Use tools 303-300, 303-350, 303-1249 and 303-1418 as illustrated. This work requires the ability to control loaded valve springs and handle their small retaining keys.

prepare.title: Prepare parts and assembly fluids
prepare.detail: Have new valve-stem seals. The left head needs a new coolant-outlet gasket; the right needs a new outlet O-ring and cylinder head temperature sensor. Use Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil and the specified Motorcraft Orange coolant for their respective lubrication steps.

prepare.title: Organize a clean bench
prepare.detail: Identify the head and replacement parts from the engine identification information. Mark reusable components so each returns to its original location.

steps.title: Strip the left-head fittings when applicable
steps.body: Remove the coolant-outlet bolts and outlet, discarding its gasket. Remove the heat shield and fasteners, then the intake and exhaust camshaft position (CMP) sensors, radio interference capacitor and their fasteners.

steps.title: Strip the right-head fittings when applicable
steps.body: Remove the CMP sensor and its bolt, then remove the cylinder head temperature (CHT) sensor. Inspect its tip before discarding the sensor. Remove any broken tip from the head bore before a replacement is installed. Remove the coolant-outlet bolt and outlet, and discard the O-ring.

steps.title: Release the first valve spring
steps.body: For either head, remove the spark plugs. Fit the specified compressor tools as shown in the [disassembly procedure](#/document/G1800292), then remove the valve keys, retainer and spring. Keep the parts identified by valve position.

steps.title: Remove the seal and valve
steps.body: Remove and discard the valve-stem seal, then remove the valve from the head. Repeat the spring, seal and valve removal sequence for the remaining valves while maintaining the original-location identification.

steps.title: Install new stem seals and the valves
steps.body: Lubricate each new stem seal and its valve-guide bore with clean specified engine oil. Install the new seal first, then install the valve into the head. This preserves the stated assembly order and supplies lubrication at the guide and seal.

steps.title: Reassemble each spring
steps.body: Use the specified compressor arrangement to install the spring, retainer and keys. Return reusable parts to their marked positions and repeat for the remaining valves. Install the spark plugs using the tightening value in the assembly procedure.

steps.title: Complete the right head
steps.body: Install a new CHT sensor, then the CMP sensor and its bolt. Lubricate the new coolant-outlet O-ring with clean specified engine coolant before installing the outlet pipe. Use the separate sensor and outlet tightening specifications.

steps.title: Complete the left head
steps.body: Install the heat shield, intake and exhaust CMP sensors, and radio interference capacitor with their fasteners. Install the coolant outlet with a new gasket. Follow the [assembly phase](#/document/G1800292) for the attachment tightening values.

watchFor.title: Spring load during key handling
watchFor.body: Keep the spring controlled by the specified tools while removing or installing its retaining parts.

watchFor.title: Mixed valve positions
watchFor.body: Preserve the identification throughout cleaning and assembly so reused parts return to their original locations.

notes: The left outlet uses a gasket; the right outlet uses a coolant-lubricated O-ring. Obtain the parts for the correct bank.

diagnostics.finding: The removed right-head CHT sensor has a missing tip.
diagnostics.meaning: A broken portion may remain in the cylinder-head bore.
diagnostics.next: Remove the fragment before fitting the new sensor. Replace the sensor even when its removed tip is intact.

verification.title: Account for each valve assembly
verification.body: Confirm each valve has its new stem seal, spring, retainer and keys, and that reusable components occupy their marked locations.

verification.title: Record bank-specific completion
verification.body: Record the right-head sensor-tip inspection and sensor replacement when applicable. Confirm the correct new outlet seal, fittings and spark plugs are installed and tightened.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L cylinder-head bench disassembly and assembly, including left/right fittings and valve-spring tooling.

guides.title: Change the engine oil and filter on the 5.2L V8
guides.summary: Drain the engine oil, renew the fitted filter type and refill using the 5.2L engine specification.
guides.introduction: The lubrication system supplies pressurized oil to the crankshaft bearings, connecting rod bearings and oil galleries. An oil change renews that lubricant and the filter that removes contamination from circulation. This engine has separate procedures for spin-on and cartridge filters, so identify the fitted arrangement before gathering parts.
guides.why: The filter seals and drain plug keep the lubrication system closed. Reusing cartridge housing seals can cause leakage, while overtightening the hand-operated drain plug can damage both the plug and oil pan. Correct parts and controlled installation matter as much as draining the old oil.

when.summary: When an oil-and-filter change is required, or engine work requires draining and renewing the oil.
notes: Identify the engine and fitted filter arrangement before ordering parts.
Obtain the oil specification and filling quantity from the linked 5.2L Specifications article before draining.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the lifting points identified by stamped triangles. Check hoist and underbody clearance. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this job.

prepare.title: Gather the correct service materials
prepare.detail: Prepare oil drain equipment, clean engine oil, the correct new filter, a torque wrench and suitable filter tooling. Cartridge service also requires new housing O-rings and a clean lint-free cloth.

steps.title: Open the service access
steps.body: With the transmission in Neutral, position the vehicle on the hoist using the lifting procedure. Remove the retainer and access cover to expose the service area.

steps.title: Drain and remove the fitted filter
steps.body: For a spin-on filter, remove and discard the filter over the drain equipment. For a cartridge filter, loosen the housing and allow its oil to drain before removing it. Discard the element and O-rings, making sure no element components remain in either the housing or adapter.

steps.title: Drain the oil pan by hand
steps.body: Turn the drain plug counterclockwise 120 degrees by hand, then pull it out. After draining, push it back into the pan and turn it clockwise 120 degrees by hand. Do not use tools or add extra tightening force.

steps.title: Install the appropriate new filter
steps.body: For a spin-on filter, lubricate its O-ring with clean engine oil and tighten the new filter with a cap wrench and torque wrench to 23 Nm. For a cartridge filter, wipe the threads and sealing surfaces, inspect the housing and stem, then install and lubricate new housing O-rings. The smallest O-ring supplied with the filter is not used here. Fit the new element and tighten the housing to 24 Nm.

steps.title: Close the access and refill
steps.body: Install the access cover and retainer, then fill with clean engine oil using the [5.2L Specifications](#/document/G1800259). Use that specification for oil selection and quantity.

watchFor.title: Old cartridge parts left behind
watchFor.body: Check both the housing and adapter before fitting the new element; removing the main filter body does not establish that every component came out.

watchFor.title: Damaged drain hardware
watchFor.body: The drain plug is designed for hand operation. Tool-assisted tightening risks damaging its engagement with the pan.

notes: The filter tightening values belong to their respective filter arrangements and are not interchangeable.

diagnostics.finding: The cartridge housing or stem is cracked, damaged or separating.
diagnostics.meaning: Renewing the element and seals alone will not correct the damaged housing.
diagnostics.next: Install a new oil filter housing assembly.

verification.title: Confirm service closure
verification.body: Confirm the plug was locked by hand, the correct new filter and seals were installed, and the access cover and retainer are secured.

verification.title: Record the refill
verification.body: Record the fitted filter type and the oil specification and quantity used from the 5.2L Specifications article.

procedures.purpose: Complete 5.2L oil draining and filling procedure, including both filter arrangements.
Identify safe lifting points and hoist-clearance precautions.
Select the specified 5.2L engine oil and filling quantity.

guides.title: Remove and refit the 5.2L left cylinder head
guides.summary: Remove the left cylinder head, inspect its sealing joint and reinstall it with a new gasket and new torque-to-yield bolts.
guides.introduction: The left-hand cylinder head closes one bank of cylinders and carries the valves and overhead camshafts. Its joint with the block must contain combustion pressure while keeping oil and coolant in their intended passages. This repair opens that joint and includes the surrounding intake, camshaft, exhaust and engine-support work needed to reach it.
guides.why: Debris entering an engine passage can cause engine failure, while scratches across a sealing face can become leak paths. The head bolts stretch during tightening and must be replaced. Engine support also changes during this procedure, so the mount and support-bar sequence matters as much as the head installation.

when.summary: When diagnosis or planned engine repair requires removal of the 5.2L left cylinder head.
notes: Confirm engine identification before obtaining replacement parts.
Plan for camshaft and timing work through the dedicated left-camshaft procedure.

prepare.title: Provide lifting and engine support
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist, engine lifting bracket 303-050 and support bar 303-F072. Follow the marked lifting points; never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare for engine repair
prepare.detail: Have new head bolts and a new head gasket, torque-and-angle tightening equipment, compressed air for bolt-hole cleaning, and the capability to release fuel pressure and vacuum-fill and bleed the cooling system.

steps.title: Make the vehicle and fluid systems ready
steps.body: Place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on the hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Complete the [5.2L fuel-pressure release](#/document/G1794916), then drain the cooling system using its [draining, vacuum-filling and bleeding procedure](#/document/G1807369).

steps.title: Remove the assemblies above and beside the head
steps.body: Remove the [intake manifold](#/document/G1800279), [left camshaft assembly](#/document/G1800266) and [left exhaust manifold](#/document/G1800276), in that order. Follow each complete procedure, including the camshaft timing requirements; these are substantial access phases.

steps.title: Return the engine to its left mount
steps.body: Install the left engine-mount bracket, bolts and stud bolt, tightening them to 55 Nm. Use the lifting bracket and support bar to lower the engine onto the left mount, then remove those special tools. This restores mount support before the head is detached.

steps.title: Disconnect and lift off the head
steps.body: Remove the ground-strap nut and move the strap aside. Disconnect the camshaft position (CMP) sensors and ignition interference capacitor, then detach the harness retainer. Remove and discard the cylinder-head bolts, remove the head and discard its gasket.

steps.title: Prepare and assess the sealing joint
steps.body: Clean the head and block mating faces without metal scrapers, wire brushes, power abrasive discs or other abrasive methods. Clear coolant, oil and debris from the block's head-bolt holes with compressed air. Inspect both faces using [Cylinder Head Distortion](#/document/G1661748) and [Cylinder Block Distortion](#/document/G1661746) before proceeding.

steps.title: Install the head with new fastening parts
steps.body: Fit the new gasket, head and new bolts using the [head installation procedure](#/document/G1800271). Its tightening stages are 30 Nm, 50 Nm, then an additional 90° and another 90°. Restore the harness retainer, sensor and capacitor connectors, and ground strap; tighten the ground-strap nut to 9 Nm.

steps.title: Restore access assemblies and cooling
steps.body: Refit the lifting bracket and support bar with the bar's legs on body structure. Raise the left side of the engine 25 mm, then remove the mount-bracket bolts, stud bolt and bracket. Reinstall the left exhaust manifold, left camshaft assembly and intake manifold through their complete procedures. Fill and bleed the cooling system, then road test.

watchFor.title: Support-bar feet on the fenders
watchFor.body: The fenders are not the specified support surface. Position the legs on body structure to prevent damage.

watchFor.title: Contaminated bolt holes or sealing faces
watchFor.body: Clear trapped fluids and debris before assembly, and prevent cleaning residue from entering oil or coolant passages.

notes: This procedure applies to the left head of the 5.2L engine. Use its dedicated intake, camshaft and exhaust procedures throughout.

diagnostics.finding: The head or block mating face fails its distortion inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing joint requires further evaluation before reassembly.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable distortion procedure's limits and decisions before fitting the new gasket.

verification.title: Confirm assembly prerequisites
verification.body: Confirm new head bolts and gasket were used, all tightening stages were completed, electrical connections were restored and cooling-system filling and bleeding are complete.

verification.title: Record the road-test result
verification.body: Carry out the required road test and record the result, including any remaining concern.
