guides.title: Remove and refit the right cylinder head on the 5.2L V8
guides.summary: Remove the right cylinder head, inspect the head and block surfaces and rebuild the joint with a new gasket and torque-to-yield bolts.
guides.introduction: The right-hand (RH) cylinder head houses the valves and overhead camshafts for one bank of the 5.2L V8. Its gasket seals the combustion chambers and fluid passages where the aluminum head meets the block. This job combines intake, camshaft and exhaust-manifold removal with head inspection, staged bolt tightening and restoration of the heater and sensor connections.
guides.why: Correct gasket sealing depends on surface condition and controlled bolt loading. Reusing torque-to-yield bolts or damaging the mating faces undermines that repair. Because the camshafts are chain driven, their removal and installation require the complete timing procedure as part of the head work.

when.summary: After diagnosis establishes that the RH cylinder head must be removed for repair or inspection.
notes: Use the engine identification information to select the correct replacement parts.

prepare.title: Arrange engine and timing capability
prepare.detail: Have a vehicle hoist, lifting bracket 303-050, support bar 303-F072, torque-and-angle tools and compressed air. The job requires fuel-pressure release, cooling-system service and the complete RH camshaft procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare the sealing parts
prepare.detail: Obtain a new head gasket and new head bolts. Provide clean working conditions so dismantling and surface preparation cannot introduce debris into oil or coolant passages.

steps.title: Prepare the vehicle and fluid systems
steps.body: Follow the [5.2L RH head procedure](#/document/G1800272). Position the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist using the marked lifting points. Release fuel-system pressure and drain the cooling system through the 5.2L procedures before dismantling.

steps.title: Remove the assemblies above and beside the head
steps.body: Remove the intake manifold, RH camshaft and RH exhaust manifold in that order. Follow each linked removal procedure, including its access and timing prerequisites. These are substantial phases of the repair and must be completed before proceeding to the head.

steps.title: Settle the engine onto its mount
steps.body: Install the RH engine-mount bracket, bolts and stud bolts. Using the lifting bracket and support bar, lower the engine onto the RH mount, then remove the support tools. This restores the prescribed support arrangement before the cylinder head is removed.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the head
steps.body: Disconnect the heater hose, camshaft-position sensor connector and cylinder-head-temperature (CHT) connector. Remove and discard the head bolts, lift off the head and discard the gasket. Keep debris out of the newly exposed engine passages.

steps.title: Inspect the joint before reassembly
steps.body: Clean the head and block mating surfaces without metal scrapers, wire brushes, power abrasive discs or other abrasive methods. Clear coolant, oil and foreign material from the block's head-bolt holes with compressed air. Apply the separate head and block distortion procedures to establish whether both faces are suitable for assembly.

steps.title: Install the new gasket and bolts
steps.body: Position the new gasket and head, then install new torque-to-yield bolts. Follow the illustrated bolt order through all tightening stages: 30 Nm, 50 Nm, an additional 90°, then another 90°. The torque settings and angle stages together establish the specified clamping load; old bolts must not be reused.

steps.title: Reconnect and rebuild the surrounding assemblies
steps.body: Reconnect the heater hose, camshaft-position sensor and CHT connector. Reinstall the support tools, raise the RH side of the engine 25 mm and remove the RH mount bracket. Install the RH exhaust manifold, RH camshaft and intake manifold in that order, completing their timing, support and installation requirements.

steps.title: Restore coolant circulation and test
steps.body: Fill and bleed the cooling system using the 5.2L procedure, then road test the vehicle. Complete the filling and bleeding operation before the final operating assessment.

watchFor.title: Scratched or gouged mating faces
watchFor.body: Damage from abrasive cleaning can create a leak path even with a new gasket.

watchFor.title: Liquid or debris in bolt holes
watchFor.body: The holes must be cleared before new bolts are fitted; do not assemble over retained coolant, oil or foreign material.

watchFor.title: Vehicle lifting errors
watchFor.body: Check lifting-point and adapter placement, and never work beneath jack-only support.

notes: Keep the tightening illustration in its shown orientation when identifying bolt positions.

diagnostics.finding: Head or block distortion does not meet the applicable inspection requirements.
diagnostics.meaning: Gasket replacement alone has not established a suitable sealing joint.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the surface condition through the relevant inspection procedure before reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm the rebuild
verification.body: Confirm all head-bolt stages, camshaft installation, heater-hose and sensor connections, and cooling-system filling and bleeding are complete.

verification.title: Record the final results
verification.body: Record head and block inspection results, completion of the tightening sequence and the road-test outcome.

Drain, vacuum-fill and bleed the 5.2L cooling system.
Remove and install the 5.2L intake manifold.
Complete 5.2L RH camshaft removal and installation with its timing prerequisites.
Remove and install the 5.2L RH exhaust manifold.

Assess cylinder-block distortion before reassembly.

guides.title: Replace the 5.2L primary timing chain tensioners
guides.summary: Replace the applicable primary chain tensioner while preserving the chain’s original alignment with the crankshaft sprocket and variable camshaft timing unit.
guides.introduction: The 5.2L engine uses chain-driven camshafts and hydraulic timing chain tensioners. Its variable camshaft timing (VCT) system changes valve timing during operation. This repair replaces a right-hand or left-hand primary tensioner while retaining the chain’s existing engagement with its sprockets.
guides.why: Removing a tensioner takes away chain support. The chain must remain in its original position at both the crankshaft sprocket and VCT unit; incorrect indexing can cause valve and piston damage. Cleanliness is equally important because debris entering engine passages or the oil pan can cause engine failure.

when.summary: When repair requires replacement of a 5.2L right-hand or left-hand primary timing chain tensioner.
notes: This operation preserves existing chain timing; it is not a substitute for establishing correct timing after chain displacement.

prepare.title: Confirm parts and engine identity
prepare.detail: Use the engine identification information when obtaining replacement parts. Engine displacement alone does not identify every part revision.

prepare.title: Prepare for internal engine work
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment required by the engine-front-cover procedure, a clean work area, a vise, a suitable tensioner holding pin, a torque wrench and an angle-measuring tool.

steps.title: Remove the front cover
steps.body: Complete the [5.2L engine front cover removal](#/document/G1800273). Keep foreign material, including debris from gasket-surface cleaning, out of oil passages, coolant passages and the oil pan throughout the repair.

steps.title: Mark and remove the right-hand tensioner
steps.body: If servicing the right-hand side, scribe matching location marks on its chain and VCT unit, then on its chain and crankshaft sprocket assembly. Preserve both relationships while removing the primary tensioner bolts and tensioner.

steps.title: Mark and remove the left-hand tensioner
steps.body: If servicing the left-hand side, make the corresponding chain-to-VCT and chain-to-crankshaft scribe marks before removing its tensioner. Each side needs its own identifiable marks; do not rely on the opposite side’s alignment.

steps.title: Install the left-hand tensioner
steps.body: For the left-hand installation, compress the plunger using an edge of a vise and insert a suitable pin into the housing hole. Verify the crankshaft-to-chain marks, then the VCT-to-chain marks. Install the tensioner and tighten its bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm), followed by 25°. Remove the holding pin.

steps.title: Install the right-hand tensioner
steps.body: Repeat the compression and pinning method for the right-hand tensioner. Verify its crankshaft and VCT scribe-mark alignments before installation. Tighten its bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm), followed by 25°, then remove its holding pin. When both sides are serviced, the installation sequence is left-hand followed by right-hand.

steps.title: Reinstall the front cover
steps.body: After completing the applicable branches of the [tensioner procedure](#/document/G2051731), reinstall the engine front cover through its dedicated procedure. Maintain the same contamination control during closing work.

watchFor.title: Displaced chain marks
watchFor.body: Do not continue tensioner installation if either required pair of scribe marks no longer aligns. Valve and piston damage can result from a changed chain position.

watchFor.title: A holding pin left installed
watchFor.body: Remove each tensioner’s holding pin after its mounting bolts have received both tightening stages.

notes: Only carry out the side-specific branches needed for the tensioner being serviced.

diagnostics.finding: The chain’s scribe marks do not align with the crankshaft sprocket or VCT unit before installation.
diagnostics.meaning: The required check that original chain indexing has been preserved has failed.
diagnostics.next: Stop and establish correct chain alignment before proceeding; installing a tensioner does not correct displaced timing.

verification.title: Record alignment for each serviced side
verification.body: Record confirmation of both chain-to-crankshaft and chain-to-VCT alignment separately for the right-hand and left-hand sides that were serviced.

verification.title: Confirm tensioner and cover completion
verification.body: Confirm completion of both bolt-tightening stages, removal of every installed holding pin and completion of the engine-front-cover installation.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L right-hand and left-hand primary timing chain tensioner removal and installation.
5.2L engine front cover removal prerequisite and final reinstallation.

guides.title: Flush cooling-system contamination — 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove cooling-system deposits using aluminum-safe cleaner and the correct radiator and engine backflushing route for each engine.
guides.introduction: Coolant carries engine heat to the radiator, where it passes to the outside air. Rust, sludge and other deposits reduce cooling efficiency. Flushing combines chemical cleaning with water flow through the radiator and engine to loosen and remove this material. The hose connections and thermostat arrangements differ between engines, so selecting the correct route matters as much as selecting the cleaner.
guides.why: Reversed or pulsating flow loosens sediment more effectively than steady flow in the normal direction. However, flushing pressure can damage the radiator, and opening a hot system can release scalding coolant. Water left after flushing also affects the final coolant mixture; the 5.0L procedure specifically requires a concentration measurement and correction.

when.summary: When rust, sludge or other foreign material requires removal from the cooling system.
notes: Overheating alone does not establish that contamination is the cause.
This is condition-based cleaning, not a stated periodic service interval.

prepare.title: Cool the system before opening it
prepare.detail: Never loosen the pressure cap while the engine is running or the cooling system is hot. Allow it to cool again if the cleaner’s operating instructions have heated it.

prepare.title: Control pressure and collect waste
prepare.detail: Keep radiator internal pressure at or below 138 kPa (20 psi). Collect used coolant and flushing water containing antifreeze or cleaner for disposal under applicable requirements.

steps.title: Apply cleaner and drain
steps.body: Use the specified Motorcraft cleaner, which is suitable for aluminum radiators, and follow its package directions. Then drain through the engine-specific cooling-system procedure. Choose the complete flushing route for the [2.3L](#/document/G1673125), [3.7L](#/document/G1694550), [5.0L](#/document/G1694584) or [5.2L](#/document/G1807370).

steps.title: Backflush the radiator through the correct opening
steps.body: For the 2.3L and both V8s, disconnect the upper and lower radiator hoses and introduce flushing water through the lower radiator opening. The 3.7L instead requires radiator removal: orient it with the upper hose connection at the top and flush through that upper connection. Maintain the radiator pressure limit throughout.

steps.title: Open the engine flushing route
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the thermostat housing; its thermostat and housing are serviced together. On the 3.7L and 5.2L, remove the thermostat and reinstall the coolant inlet connection without it before flushing. On the 5.0L, remove the thermostat and coolant inlet connection, leaving the connection off for the engine flush.

steps.title: Backflush the engine
steps.body: Introduce water through the lower radiator hose on the 2.3L. Use the upper radiator hose on the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L. These routes are engine-specific. After flushing the 5.0L, reinstall its coolant inlet connection without the thermostat as directed before proceeding to thermostat installation.

steps.title: Restore the cooling circuit
steps.body: Reinstall the 2.3L thermostat housing assembly or the separate thermostat on the other engines using the applicable removal-and-installation procedure. Reinstall the 3.7L radiator. Reconnect the radiator hoses on the other engines, then complete the correct engine-specific filling and bleeding procedure to restore coolant circulation.

steps.title: Measure and correct the 5.0L mixture
steps.body: Compensate for flushing water remaining in the system. Idle the engine for 5 minutes to mix coolant and water, then measure concentration with a coolant/battery refractometer or similar instrument. Observe the cool-system opening precaution when sampling or adjusting. Use concentrated coolant to reach the specified concentration; do not substitute an assumed mixture.

watchFor.title: Persistent heavy deposits
watchFor.body: Severe contamination may need a cooling-system pressure flusher when solvent cleaning is insufficient. This does not remove the radiator pressure limit.

watchFor.title: Premature conclusions during V8 warm-up
watchFor.body: The 5.0L and 5.2L cold-side thermostats can open and close repeatedly during warm-up before remaining open. That behavior alone does not establish a blockage.

notes: The 5.0L concentration check is an explicit final phase of its flushing procedure; no concentration percentage is supplied here.

diagnostics.finding: Chemical cleaning does not remove severe contamination effectively.
diagnostics.meaning: Solvent treatment alone is insufficient.
diagnostics.next: Use the specified pressure-flushing method with suitable equipment and controlled radiator pressure.

diagnostics.finding: The 5.0L mixture is too dilute after flushing.
diagnostics.meaning: Residual flushing water has affected coolant concentration.
diagnostics.next: Adjust with concentrated coolant to the engine’s specified concentration.

verification.title: Confirm the circuit is restored
verification.body: Confirm thermostat or housing installation, radiator and hose reconnection, and completion of the applicable filling and bleeding procedure.

verification.title: Record the measured 5.0L result
verification.body: Record the refractometer concentration and any correction made, separately from noting that filling and bleeding are complete.

guides.title: Backflush the Heater Core and Restore the Cooling System
guides.summary: Clean the heater core with the specified cooling-system flush, rinse thoroughly and complete the engine-specific filling and bleeding procedure.
guides.introduction: The heater core transfers heat from engine coolant to cabin air. Coolant must circulate through its passages for that heat transfer to work. Backflushing cleans those passages against the normal direction of flow, after which the cooling system must be rinsed, refilled and cleared of air.
guides.why: The cleaning chemical, water rinse and final coolant fill are separate stages. Leaving out the rinse leaves cleaning material in the circuit; leaving out bleeding can leave air where coolant needs to circulate. Opening a hot system also exposes you to pressurized steam and coolant.

when.summary: When heater-core cleaning is indicated during investigation or repair of a coolant-flow concern.
notes: Weak cabin heat alone does not establish that the heater core is restricted.

prepare.title: Let the engine cool
prepare.detail: Do not open the pressure relief cap while the engine is running or the cooling system is hot.

prepare.title: Arrange the complete cooling-system service
prepare.detail: Have Premium Cooling System Flush, water for thorough rinsing, and the equipment and refill materials required by the fitted engine's draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure.

steps.title: Partially drain the cooled system
steps.body: Follow the appropriate draining procedure for the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L. Establish this access before introducing cleaner; the job begins with a partial cooling-system drain.

steps.title: Select and use the specified flush
steps.body: Backflush the heater core with Premium Cooling System Flush, following its package directions. The 3.7L and 5.2L procedures explicitly name Motorcraft Premium Cooling System Flush VC-1. The 2.3L and 5.0L procedures direct product selection through their engine cooling specifications.

steps.title: Rinse thoroughly with water
steps.body: After the chemical cleaning stage, thoroughly flush with water before refilling. This removes the cleaning material from the core and completes the required preparation for the final coolant fill.

steps.title: Fill and bleed for the fitted engine
steps.body: Complete the matching Engine Cooling System Draining, Vacuum Filling and Bleeding procedure. Treat air removal as part of the repair, because filling the reservoir alone does not establish that the coolant circuit has been properly filled.

watchFor.title: Hot, pressurized coolant
watchFor.body: Even slight loosening of a hot pressure cap can release steam and liquid forcefully.

watchFor.title: An incomplete rinse
watchFor.body: Do not proceed to the final coolant fill before the thorough water-flushing stage is complete.

notes: On the 5.0L and 5.2L, the cold-side thermostat can cycle during warm-up. Early warm-up behavior alone is not evidence of a restricted heater core.

verification.title: Confirm the cleaning sequence
verification.body: Confirm that package-directed chemical cleaning was followed by a thorough water rinse.

verification.title: Confirm cooling-system restoration
verification.body: Complete all filling and bleeding requirements in the corresponding engine procedure.

guides.title: Replace the engine block heater on the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L
guides.summary: Drain the correct cooling system, replace the block heater and restore its protected wiring route before filling and bleeding.
guides.introduction: The block heater uses electrical heat to warm the engine through its coolant. Removing it opens the cooling system, so the repair includes coolant draining and a complete filling and bleeding stage. The 2.3L additionally requires starter motor removal for access; the 3.7L and 5.0L procedures proceed directly to the heater after draining.
guides.why: The heater must be tightened correctly at its coolant connection, and its wiring must remain secured away from hot or rotating components. Correct filling and bleeding restores the cooling circuit after the opening has admitted air. A nearby coolant leak should be located accurately before assuming the heater is responsible.

when.summary: When a block-heater fault has been established or heater removal is required for related repair work.
notes: Select coolant-service instructions by engine, even though the heater tightening specification is shared.

prepare.title: Prepare for coolant service
prepare.detail: Have the matching engine’s draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure available, together with its required equipment and coolant specifications. Follow its precautions before opening the cooling system.

prepare.title: Prepare electrical and access work
prepare.detail: Ensure the heater is disconnected from its power supply. For the 2.3L, follow the starter procedure’s preparation requirements before removing the starter; this prerequisite is part of the access work.

steps.title: Drain the matching cooling system
steps.body: Use the coolant procedure for the [2.3L](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L](#/document/G1694549) or [5.0L](#/document/G1694583). Complete draining before disconnecting and removing the heater.

steps.title: Create access on the 2.3L
steps.body: Remove the starter motor using the [2.3L starter procedure](#/document/G1673178), including its prerequisites. The 3.7L and 5.0L heater procedures do not specify starter removal.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the heater
steps.body: Observe how the heater wiring is routed and secured, then disconnect its electrical connector. Remove the block heater using the correct engine procedure. Use the illustration for your selected engine to identify the connector and heater location.

steps.title: Install the heater and restore its wiring
steps.body: Install the heater and tighten it to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm), as specified for each of these engines. Reconnect the electrical connector and secure the wiring away from rotating or hot components. Reinstall the starter on the 2.3L by reversing its removal procedure.

steps.title: Fill and bleed the system
steps.body: Complete the engine-specific filling and bleeding procedure after reassembly. Follow that procedure’s full sequence so the cooling system is restored after heater removal.

watchFor.title: Wiring exposed to heat or movement
watchFor.body: A connected plug is not enough: the heater wiring must also be routed and secured away from hot and rotating parts.

watchFor.title: A different leak source on the 3.7L
watchFor.body: Oil or coolant at the front-left weep hole behind the generator points to the channel cover plate’s sealing system, not automatically to the block heater.

notes: The replacement sequence does not establish an electrical diagnosis; heater performance testing requires the applicable diagnostic information.

diagnostics.finding: Oil or coolant leaks from the 3.7L weep hole behind the generator.
diagnostics.meaning: The cooling-system description identifies a failed channel cover plate gasket and requires replacement of the plate.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable engine repair path for the channel cover plate instead of treating this location as evidence for heater replacement.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical and wiring completion
verification.body: Verify the heater was tightened to specification, its connector is attached and its wiring is secured clear of the stated hazards. Confirm starter reinstallation on the 2.3L.

verification.title: Record coolant-service completion
verification.body: Record the engine variant and completion of its filling and bleeding procedure, keeping that result distinct from any separate heater electrical test.

3.7L block heater removal and installation.
5.0L block heater removal and installation.
2.3L cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding before and after heater replacement.
Required 2.3L starter motor removal and installation for heater access.
3.7L cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.
5.0L cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.

applicability.equipment: Block-heater access and torque tools; engine-specific cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding equipment. The 2.3L also requires the capability and prerequisites for starter motor removal.

guides.title: Replace the cooling fan motor and shroud using the correct engine procedure
guides.summary: Remove and refit the fan assembly with engine-specific intake access and the additional coolant work required on the 2.3L.
guides.introduction: The electric cooling fan moves air through the radiator, and its shroud directs that airflow. The motor and shroud are removed together after clearing intake components and the coolant degas bottle. Access differs between engines: the 2.3L procedure also opens the upper radiator hose and requires draining, filling and bleeding the cooling system.
guides.why: Choosing the correct engine sequence avoids unnecessary coolant disturbance and ensures enough access to remove the assembly. Harness retainers are equally important: they keep the wiring in its intended position around the fans. An overheating complaint alone does not establish that the fan assembly needs replacement.
searchTerms: cooling fan motor and shroud replacement

when.summary: When fan assembly replacement has been justified or the motor and shroud must be removed for related access.
notes: Identify the engine before selecting the intake-removal and coolant-service instructions.

prepare.title: Select the access route
prepare.detail: Use the separate fan procedure for the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L. The 5.2L begins with the outlet pipe; the other procedures begin intake removal with the air cleaner.

prepare.title: Plan the 2.3L coolant work
prepare.detail: Have the complete draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure available before opening the system, including its equipment and handling precautions.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Engine-specific intake and fan access; torque tools. The 2.3L additionally requires a hose clamp remover/installer and the equipment specified for cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.

steps.title: Drain first where required
steps.body: On the 2.3L, drain the cooling system through [the applicable coolant procedure](#/document/G1673124) before removing intake components. The supplied 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L fan-removal sequences do not call for draining.

steps.title: Clear the intake components
steps.body: On the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, remove the air cleaner followed by its outlet pipe, using the matching engine references. On the 5.2L, remove the outlet pipe first and then the air cleaner; follow the outlet-pipe reference within that engine’s fan procedure.

steps.title: Move the bottle and release the harness
steps.body: Remove the degas bottle bolts and position the bottle aside. Disconnect the fan electrical connectors and detach the wiring harness retainers so the assembly can be removed without pulling on its wiring.

steps.title: Release and remove the fan assembly
steps.body: On the 2.3L, use a hose clamp remover/installer to release the clamp and disconnect the upper radiator hose. For every engine, remove the fan mounting bolts and then remove the cooling fan motor and shroud.

steps.title: Reinstall in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the assembly and tighten the mounting bolts to the applicable specification. Restore the upper radiator hose on the 2.3L, reconnect the fan wiring and secure its retainers. Refit the degas bottle and intake components in reverse removal order.

steps.title: Complete the coolant stage
steps.body: On the 2.3L, fill and bleed the cooling system using the same engine-specific coolant procedure. This is a required completion stage after the radiator hose has been opened.

watchFor.title: Loose fan wiring
watchFor.body: Restore the harness retainers as well as the electrical connectors; the illustrated routing belongs to the 2.3L procedure.

watchFor.title: Escalating overheat warnings
watchFor.body: On the 5.0L and 5.2L, the described fail-safe strategy can progress from warnings to cylinder deactivation and engine shutdown. Stop rather than continuing to run an overheating engine.

notes: Positioning the degas bottle aside is common to all four procedures; disconnecting the upper radiator hose is specified only in the 2.3L sequence.

diagnostics.finding: P0125 or P0128 on the described 5.0L or 5.2L cooling system.
diagnostics.meaning: These diagnostic trouble codes concern thermostat monitoring, not direct confirmation of a failed fan.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the indicated cooling-system concern before authorizing fan replacement.

diagnostics.finding: P1285 or P1299 on the described 5.0L or 5.2L system.
diagnostics.meaning: Overheating or fail-safe operation has been detected; the code does not identify the fan as the cause.
diagnostics.next: Address the overheating cause and rectify the fault before clearing the diagnostic trouble code.

verification.title: Check restored connections
verification.body: Confirm the fan and bottle fasteners are tightened, electrical connectors and harness retainers are restored, and the intake components are installed.

verification.title: Record engine-specific completion
verification.body: Record the engine variant and, for the 2.3L, completion of radiator-hose reconnection and the full filling and bleeding procedure.

guides.title: Drain, refill and bleed the 5.2L engine cooling system
guides.summary: Recover the coolant, refill with the correct mixture and complete the air-purging sequence using either vacuum or conventional filling.
guides.introduction: Coolant carries heat from the engine to the radiator and also supplies the heater core. The degas bottle provides expansion space, separates air and serves as the filling point. This job restores the coolant supply after draining or repairs, with a controlled bleeding sequence to remove trapped air.
guides.why: The 5.2L engine has a cold-side thermostat that can open and close repeatedly during warm-up before remaining open. Filling the bottle alone does not establish that coolant has circulated throughout the system. Correct concentration, sufficient warm-up and the prescribed purge cycles all contribute to engine protection.

when.summary: After cooling-system draining or repairs, or when contaminated coolant requires replacement.
notes: Clear coolant changing from orange to pink or light red does not, by itself, require replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange safe access and collection
prepare.detail: Use a hoist, drain hose, clean fluid container and thick cloth for the pressure cap. Follow the marked lifting points and clearance precautions; never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the filling equipment
prepare.detail: Have the ROB75240 coolant/battery refractometer and, for vacuum filling, a cooling-system vacuum tester and refiller. Use the specified Motorcraft Orange coolant and distilled water as required.

steps.title: Cool, lift and drain
steps.body: Allow the engine to cool before opening the system. Cover the expansion-tank cap with a thick cloth while releasing pressure. Put the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on the hoist. Remove whichever illustrated underbody shields are fitted, then drain through a hose at the radiator drain valve into a clean container.

steps.title: Establish the correct mixture
steps.body: Measure concentration before adjusting it. The normal target is 48/52 to 50/50 coolant to distilled water. Use VC-3DIL-B prediluted coolant, specification WSS-M97B44-D2, to maintain that range; use VC-3-B concentrate, specification WSS-M97B44-D, and/or distilled water for other corrections. After flushing, prepare the mixture from concentrate and distilled water.

steps.title: Choose one filling route
steps.body: Close the radiator drain valve. For vacuum filling, reinstall the shields and follow the filler manufacturer's instructions to fill and bleed. Without a vacuum filler, disconnect the heater inlet hose and fill the degas bottle until coolant emerges from the heater inlet tube. Reconnect the hose, reinstall the shields and fill the bottle to MAX FILL.

steps.title: Perform the initial purge
steps.body: Tighten the degas-bottle cap to its hard stop and switch the climate control off. Run the engine at 3,500 rpm for 30 seconds, then switch it off and wait 1 minute to allow large air pockets to purge.

steps.title: Check the initial level safely
steps.body: Allow cooling before opening the cap; the timed pause does not make a hot system safe to open. The initial level instruction uses the top of MAX FILL when warm or the top of MIN FILL LEVEL when cold. Adjust as necessary and secure the cap before running again.

steps.title: Warm through and complete the purge cycles
steps.body: Idle until normal operating temperature and until the cooling fan has cycled on at least once, the specified indication of a fully open thermostat. Complete five cycles consisting of 3,500 rpm for 30 seconds, idle for 30 seconds, then engine off for 1 minute.

steps.title: Finish the refill
steps.body: Allow the engine to cool before reopening the system. Complete the final level check, topping up to MAX FILL if necessary, and reinstall the pressure-relief cap.

watchFor.title: Concentration outside the permitted limits
watchFor.body: Extreme-climate adjustments must remain between 40% and 60% coolant. Too much reduces overheat protection; too little reduces freeze and corrosion protection.

watchFor.title: Temperature continuing to rise
watchFor.body: An overheating warning calls for stopping the engine, not continuing the purge sequence.

notes: Do not mix coolant types or add alcohol, methanol or brine. Ford does not recommend recycled coolant for this system; clean recovered coolant is a separate reuse provision.
An in-vehicle drain recovers less than 80% of system capacity, so concentration must be measured rather than assumed.

diagnostics.finding: Coolant is dirty, rusty or contaminated.
diagnostics.meaning: It is unsuitable for reuse.
diagnostics.next: Replace it and recycle or dispose of the recovered fluid correctly.

diagnostics.finding: A non-specified coolant has been used.
diagnostics.meaning: Correct corrosion protection cannot be assumed.
diagnostics.next: Carry out the required chemical flushing procedure before refilling.

verification.title: Confirm circulation and final fill
verification.body: Confirm the fan-cycle indication, completed purge cycles, final level and secure cap.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record measured concentration and the temperature condition associated with the level check.

procedures.purpose: Complete 5.2L draining procedure, coolant selection, and both vacuum and conventional filling/bleeding branches.
Correct lifting points and hoist-clearance precautions for drain access.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger oil return tube
guides.summary: Move the air-conditioning compressor aside, renew the turbocharger drain-tube sealing connection and restore the engine oil level.
guides.introduction: Engine oil lubricates the turbocharger bearings and helps cool its center housing. The return tube carries that oil back to the sump. This job restores the drain connection and its sealing surfaces; access requires removing the air-conditioning compressor belt and supporting the compressor aside.
guides.why: Old O-ring residue or damage at a sealing port can cause another leak after reassembly. The tube must also be fully seated before its bolts are tightened, so the fasteners secure an already positioned connection rather than draw it into place.
searchTerms: oil leak at turbo drain tube

when.summary: When a confirmed drain-tube or sealing defect requires repair, or the tube must be removed for service.
notes: Oil around the turbocharger does not by itself identify the return tube as the leaking connection.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underbody access
prepare.detail: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, use a hoist following the lifting procedure. Identify the marked lifting points and check adapter and underbody clearances. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare parts, oil and support
prepare.detail: Have new drain-tube bolts, a new O-ring seal, suitable compressor support and a torque wrench. Use clean SAE 5W-30 synthetic blend engine oil, XO-5W30-Q1SP meeting WSS-M2C946-B1, for seal lubrication and any required top-up.

steps.title: Lift the vehicle and remove the belt
steps.body: Follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631), then remove the compressor belt using the [2.3L belt procedure](#/document/G1688221). Correct access lets the compressor be moved without working around its installed drive belt.

steps.title: Move and support the compressor
steps.body: Disconnect the air-conditioning compressor electrical connectors and release the wiring-harness retainers. Remove its mounting bolts, then position and support the compressor aside to expose the oil return tube.

steps.title: Remove the drain tube and inspect its ports
steps.body: Remove and discard the drain-tube bolts, then remove the tube. Clean the sealing ports completely of O-ring residue and inspect the sealing surfaces and line for damage. Follow the [tube procedure](#/document/G1689384) for the connection arrangement.

steps.title: Lubricate, seat and secure the tube
steps.body: Lubricate the new O-ring with clean specified engine oil. Install the tube and make sure it is fully seated before running down the new bolts. Tighten the drain-tube bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the compressor and oil level
steps.body: Position the compressor and tighten its mounting bolts to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm). Reconnect its electrical connectors and harness retainers, reinstall the belt through its dedicated procedure, then check and top off the engine oil as necessary.

watchFor.title: A tube that will not seat
watchFor.body: Do not use bolt tightening to pull an unseated tube into its sealing port. Establish correct seating before fastener rundown.

watchFor.title: Contamination or damaged sealing surfaces
watchFor.body: Pay particular attention to oil-feed, drain and coolant sealing ports encountered during turbocharger work. Residue and damage can cause leaks and repeat repairs.

notes: If turbocharger air-intake components are opened during associated work, cover their ports to keep debris away from the compressor vanes.

diagnostics.finding: O-ring residue or damage is present at a drain-tube sealing port.
diagnostics.meaning: The connection cannot be relied on to seal correctly in that condition.
diagnostics.next: Remove residue and resolve sealing-surface or line damage before installing the tube.

verification.title: Confirm the restored connections
verification.body: Confirm full tube seating, installation of new bolts, correct fastener tightening and restoration of the compressor, belt, connectors and wiring retainers.

verification.title: Confirm engine oil level
verification.body: Check the engine oil after reassembly and top off as necessary with the specified oil.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger oil return tube removal, sealing and installation.
Lifting-point identification and safe hoist positioning.
2.3L air-conditioning compressor belt removal and installation.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger oil supply tube
guides.summary: Replace the turbocharger oil supply tube and its oil filter while protecting the intake and restoring clean, fully seated oil connections.
guides.introduction: The turbocharger uses exhaust energy to compress incoming air. Engine oil lubricates its sleeve bearings and helps cool the center housing before returning to the sump. The supply tube carries that oil into the turbocharger. Replacing it involves opening both the oil connection and nearby intake plumbing, so the job combines careful sealing work with strict protection against foreign material.
guides.why: Small particles entering the intake can damage the compressor vanes. Residue or damage at an oil connection can prevent sealing and cause another leak. The replacement tube must also be fully seated before its fasteners are tightened: the bolts secure the connection, rather than pull a poorly aligned tube into place.

when.summary: When the turbocharger oil supply tube has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Oil near the turbocharger calls for locating the leak; it does not by itself identify the supply tube as the cause.

prepare.title: Have both replacement parts ready
prepare.detail: Obtain a new oil supply tube assembly and a new turbocharger oil filter. Both removed items must be discarded.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean assembly
prepare.detail: Have clean engine oil, protection for open intake ports and suitable fastener tools. Use the 2.3L engine specifications for oil selection and topping up.

steps.title: Open the intake access
steps.body: Remove the [air cleaner outlet pipe](#/document/G1675706). Cover exposed intake openings as components come off so dirt cannot reach the compressor.

steps.title: Move the outlet plumbing clear
steps.body: Disconnect the turbocharger bypass-valve electrical connector and detach its harness retainers. Loosen the turbocharger outlet-pipe clamps and remove the pipe, following the [tube replacement procedure](#/document/G1689385).

steps.title: Remove the old tube and filter
steps.body: Remove the oil supply tube retaining bolts, then remove and discard the complete tube assembly. Remove and discard the turbocharger oil filter as well; reusing it is specifically prohibited.

steps.title: Inspect the sealing connections
steps.body: Make sure the exposed sealing ports are completely clean, free from O-ring residue and undamaged. Inspect and clean removed intake components as necessary before reassembly. A damaged sealing surface must be addressed rather than concealed by tightening the connection harder.

steps.title: Install and seat the replacement parts
steps.body: Install the new turbocharger oil filter and lubricate the O-ring seal with clean engine oil. Fully seat the new supply tube and start its retaining bolts finger tight. Tighten the bolts in the procedure's stated order, using the separate specification assigned to each fastener.

steps.title: Restore the intake and oil level
steps.body: Install the turbocharger outlet pipe and tighten its clamps. Reconnect the bypass valve and secure the harness retainers, then reinstall the air cleaner outlet pipe. Check and top off the engine oil using the [2.3L specifications](#/document/G1660452).

watchFor.title: Debris in open ports
watchFor.body: Even small intake debris can damage the compressor. Keep openings protected throughout the repair.

watchFor.title: A tube that will not seat
watchFor.body: Stop and correct alignment or sealing interference before fastener rundown.

notes: The two supply-tube retaining bolts have different tightening specifications; do not treat them as interchangeable.

diagnostics.finding: O-ring residue or damage at an exposed sealing port.
diagnostics.meaning: The connection may not seal reliably after assembly.
diagnostics.next: Remove residue and resolve sealing-surface damage before installing the replacement tube.

verification.title: Confirm reconnection
verification.body: Check that the outlet pipe, clamps, bypass-valve connector and harness retainers have all been restored.

verification.title: Record the oil-level check
verification.body: Record the final engine-oil level and any oil added after assembly.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger oil supply tube and filter removal and installation, including fastener-specific tightening.
2.3L air cleaner outlet-pipe removal and installation for access.
2.3L engine oil specifications used for lubrication and the final oil-level correction.

guides.title: Replace ignition coils on the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Remove and inspect coil-on-plug units, replace damaged assemblies or boots as specified, and restore the correct engine-specific connections and tightening.
guides.introduction: A coil-on-plug unit supplies ignition voltage directly to its spark plug through an insulated boot. This job removes the unit and inspects it for physical damage before refitting or replacement. The engines share that basic arrangement, but their access requirements, replacement instructions and mounting-bolt tightening differ.
guides.why: Cleaning around a seated coil keeps loose material from falling into the opening during removal. A slight twist releases the boot seal without forcing it straight upward. Correct tightening matters because the mounting instructions range from a fixed torque to torque followed by an additional angle.

when.summary: When a coil requires removal or replacement, or inspection reveals cracks, rips or tears.
notes: Select the engine procedure before starting; the 3.7L right-hand coils require upper intake-manifold removal.

prepare.title: Match tools to the engine branch
prepare.detail: Provide compressed air for cleaning, suitable hand tools and a torque wrench. The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L also require controlled angle tightening. Right-hand access on the 3.7L requires the capability and prerequisites in the upper intake-manifold procedure.

steps.title: Expose the coils on the 2.3L or 3.7L
steps.body: On the [2.3L](#/document/G1673188), disconnect the battery through the linked procedure, then remove the appearance-cover nuts, bolts and cover. On the [3.7L](#/document/G1675558), remove the upper intake manifold for right-hand access. That manifold-removal instruction applies to the right-hand bank.

steps.title: Expose the coils on the V8 engines
steps.body: On the [5.0L](#/document/G1675574), remove the appearance cover, release the positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve coupling and crankcase ventilation tube coupling, and move them aside before removing the coil covers. On the [5.2L](#/document/G1805373), release the PCV hose couplings, position the hoses out of the way and remove the coil covers.

steps.title: Disconnect, clean and lift out the coils
steps.body: Follow the selected procedure's connector and cleaning sequence. On the 2.3L, release the harness retainers and slide back any cover over a connector locking tab before depressing it. Use compressed air around the coils while they are still seated; the 3.7L places this cleaning before connector disconnection. Remove the mounting bolts, then use a slight twisting motion to release each coil's seal and lift it out.

steps.title: Inspect the specified replaceable part
steps.body: For the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L, inspect the coil-on-plug assembly for cracks, rips or tears and replace damaged assemblies. The 3.7L instruction specifically calls for replacing rubber boots with this damage. Use that distinction when deciding which part needs renewal.

steps.title: Install and tighten for the exact engine
steps.body: Install the coils and mounting bolts. The 2.3L requires 89 lb.in (10 Nm). The 3.7L requires 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then 50°. Both V8 procedures require 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then 45°. Reconnect the electrical connectors; on the 2.3L, secure the locking tabs and harness retainers.

steps.title: Restore the access components
steps.body: Refit the 3.7L upper intake manifold if removed. On the V8s, refit the coil covers and reconnect the ventilation couplings. Before fitting the 5.0L appearance cover, move any grommets retained in the cover back onto the intake manifold. On the 2.3L, refit the appearance cover, tighten its fasteners to 80 lb.in (9 Nm) and reconnect the battery through its procedure.

watchFor.title: Connector locks and seals
watchFor.body: Release the locking tab rather than pulling against it. Use the specified slight twist when lifting a coil whose boot seal remains attached.

notes: Use the procedure and illustration for your selected engine to identify the coils and their access requirements.

diagnostics.finding: Cracks, rips or tears are visible.
diagnostics.meaning: The assembly or rubber boot has physical damage requiring the engine-specific replacement action.
diagnostics.next: Replace the damaged assembly on the 2.3L, 5.0L or 5.2L; renew the damaged rubber boot on the 3.7L.

verification.title: Confirm tightening and restoration
verification.body: Check that the selected engine's torque and angle were completed, connectors are secured, and disturbed retainers, ventilation couplings and covers are restored. Confirm battery reconnection on the 2.3L and manifold installation where required on the 3.7L.

guides.title: Remove and refit the 2.3L EcoBoost crankcase oil separator
guides.summary: Remove the intake manifold to access the crankcase oil separator, inspect its gasket and restore both assemblies correctly.
guides.introduction: The crankcase vent oil separator helps separate carried oil from crankcase ventilation gases. On this engine, the intake manifold must come off to reach it. The work involves removing the separator housing, checking its sealing joint and refitting it with a serviceable gasket or a replacement where needed.
guides.why: The housing depends on clean mating faces and a sound gasket to seal properly. Much of this job concerns access: the intake manifold carries electrical connections, ventilation couplings and tube retainers that must all be restored.

when.summary: When the separator requires removal or replacement, or its gasket needs renewal.
notes: Gasket replacement depends on inspection; removal alone does not require a new gasket.

prepare.title: Provide intake-manifold access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist with the vehicle in NEUTRAL as directed by the intake-manifold procedure. Have suitable hand tools, a torque wrench and the capability to release the specified hose couplings without damaging them.

steps.title: Remove the intake manifold
steps.body: Follow [intake manifold removal](#/document/G1660523). Remove the appearance cover, release the evaporative-emissions purge connections and retainers, and move the purge valve aside. Disconnect the sensor and throttle wiring, move the charge-air cooler outlet tube aside and release the rear vacuum coupling. Free the coolant-tube attachment, move the manifold back, then disconnect the positive crankcase ventilation tube and knock-sensor connector retainers.

steps.title: Remove and examine the separator
steps.body: Follow the [separator procedure](#/document/G1673197) to remove its bolts and housing. Inspect the gasket around the mating perimeter. Replace it as necessary; retain it only if serviceable. Make both mating faces clean and free of corrosion and foreign material before refitting.

steps.title: Refit the housing and manifold
steps.body: Install the separator and tighten its bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). Inspect the intake-manifold gaskets for nicks, cuts and abrasions before reuse. Reconnect the ventilation coupling and knock-sensor retainers as the manifold is positioned. Ensure the coolant tube is correctly located and the manifold fits onto its stud before tightening the manifold and tube attachments to their respective specifications.

steps.title: Restore the remaining connections
steps.body: Complete the manifold installation sequence: reconnect the rear vacuum tube, charge-air outlet, throttle and sensor wiring, purge valve and its couplings. Secure the fuel and evaporative-emissions tubes in their retainer, then refit the appearance cover.

watchFor.title: Coolant-tube positioning
watchFor.body: The coolant tube must be in position when the intake manifold is installed; confirm alignment before tightening.

notes: If this work accompanies upper-engine failure, inspect the intake manifold for metal debris and replace the manifold if debris is found.

diagnostics.finding: The separator gasket is damaged or unserviceable.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing joint needs attention; this finding alone does not establish an internal separator fault.
diagnostics.next: Renew the gasket and prepare the mating faces before assembly.

verification.title: Check the restored assembly
verification.body: Confirm separator bolt tightening, manifold and coolant-tube positioning, and reconnection of all disturbed couplings, electrical connectors and retainers.

verification.title: Complete the conditional road test
verification.body: If a new intake manifold was installed, road-test the vehicle.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L crankcase vent oil separator removal, gasket inspection and installation.
Required 2.3L intake-manifold access, gasket inspection and restoration.

guides.title: Replace the PCV valve on a 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine
guides.summary: Renew the positive crankcase ventilation valve using the correct engine access sequence and a lubricated new valve seal.
guides.introduction: The positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve forms part of the route carrying crankcase vapors into the intake system. A tube connects to the valve through a quick-release coupling, while an O-ring seals the valve into its mounting. The three engines share the replacement principle, but their cover-removal steps differ.
guides.why: Removing this valve damages its locking mechanism, so it must be replaced even if removal was only intended for inspection. Lubricating the new O-ring with clean engine oil helps it seat during installation. Correct coupling release also avoids forcing the attached ventilation tube.

when.summary: When PCV valve replacement is indicated, or whenever the installed valve has been removed.

prepare.title: Identify the engine and connection
prepare.detail: Select the matching valve and quick-release coupling procedures. Be able to release the tube coupling without forcing it.

prepare.title: Have the replacement ready
prepare.detail: Obtain the correct new PCV valve and clean engine oil for its O-ring. Plan to discard the removed valve.

steps.title: Open the appropriate access
steps.body: On the 5.0L, remove the engine appearance cover first. If its rubber grommets remain in the cover, remove them and return them to the intake manifold before later refitting the cover. The 3.7L and 5.2L procedures begin at the tube connection.

steps.title: Release the tube and remaining cover
steps.body: Disconnect the ventilation tube-to-valve quick-release coupling using the engine-specific coupling procedure. On the 5.0L and 5.2L, then remove the right-hand spark plug cover. The 3.7L procedure does not require that cover-removal step.

steps.title: Remove and discard the valve
steps.body: Rotate the valve counterclockwise and remove it. Discard it immediately so the damaged locking mechanism cannot be mistaken for a reusable part.

steps.title: Fit the new valve and restore access parts
steps.body: Lubricate the new valve's O-ring with clean engine oil. Install by reversing the applicable removal sequence: refit the valve, the right-hand spark plug cover where applicable, and the tube connection. Finish the 5.0L by refitting its appearance cover over the correctly positioned grommets.

watchFor.title: Reusing a removed valve
watchFor.body: An apparently intact valve still requires replacement after removal because its locking mechanism is damaged.

notes: The illustrated valve location is for the 3.7L. Use the matching V8 procedure for 5.0L or 5.2L access.

diagnostics.finding: The valve has already been removed.
diagnostics.meaning: It is no longer suitable for reinstallation, regardless of the original reason for removal.
diagnostics.next: Fit a new valve with its O-ring lubricated.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Confirm that a new valve was fitted, the tube coupling is reconnected, and all applicable covers and grommets have been restored.

procedures.purpose: 3.7L PCV valve removal and installation.
5.0L PCV valve replacement, including appearance-cover grommets and spark plug cover.
5.2L PCV valve replacement and right-hand spark plug cover access.
3.7L quick-release coupling procedure referenced for the ventilation tube.
5.0L quick-release coupling procedure referenced for the ventilation tube.
5.2L quick-release coupling procedure referenced for the ventilation tube.

guides.title: Replace Mustang camshaft position sensors by engine
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the appropriate intake or exhaust camshaft position sensor using the access route and seal lubricant specified for the engine.
guides.introduction: A camshaft position (CMP) sensor provides the engine controls with information about camshaft position. Intake and exhaust sensors are separate components, and the larger engines have sensors on both cylinder banks. Replacement involves electrical disconnection, removal of the sensor retainer and careful installation of the oil-sealed sensor.
guides.why: The sensor attachment is straightforward, but access differs substantially between engines and banks. Following the correct branch avoids unnecessary dismantling. Lubricating the O-ring with the specified clean engine oil helps it seat as the sensor is installed.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that a particular CMP sensor requires replacement, or removal is needed for other repairs.
notes: Identify the engine, cylinder bank where applicable, and intake or exhaust sensor before dismantling.

prepare.title: Plan the access work
prepare.detail: Have tools for sensor retainers and a suitable low-range torque wrench. Manifold removal capability is required for the 3.7L right-hand sensors and all 5.0L and 5.2L sensors.

prepare.title: Match the seal lubricant
prepare.detail: Use the matched procedure's clean engine oil: SAE 5W-30 synthetic blend for 2.3L, SAE 5W-20 synthetic blend for 3.7L, SAE 5W-20 full synthetic for 5.0L, or SAE 5W-50 full synthetic for 5.2L.

steps.title: Select the correct sensor branch
steps.body: Use the engine-specific procedure linked below. Right-hand and left-hand banks have different access sequences; the intake and exhaust sensor instructions should not be treated as interchangeable locations.

steps.title: Prepare access on the 2.3L EcoBoost
steps.body: Remove the appearance-cover nuts and cover. Disconnect the low-pressure fuel sensor electrical connector and detach the fuel supply tube retainer from the valve-cover stud. These are connector and retainer operations; the CMP procedure does not call for opening a fuel connection.

steps.title: Prepare access on the 3.7L
steps.body: For the right-hand sensors, remove the [upper intake manifold](#/document/G1681529), then follow the intake-sensor and exhaust-sensor operations. The left-hand branch proceeds directly to the exhaust sensor followed by the intake sensor; the manifold-removal requirement belongs to the right-hand branch.

steps.title: Prepare access on the 5.0L or 5.2L
steps.body: Remove the intake manifold using the [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1685326) or [5.2L procedure](#/document/G1800279). Both engines list intake then exhaust sensor operations on each bank. On the left bank, move the radio ignition interference capacitor aside before removing the exhaust sensor.

steps.title: Remove the sensor being serviced
steps.body: Disconnect its electrical connector, remove its retainer and withdraw the sensor using the selected engine and bank procedure. On the 2.3L, the intake sensor operation precedes the exhaust sensor operation. Keep track of which connector and retainer belong to the serviced location.

steps.title: Lubricate, install and restore access
steps.body: Lubricate the sensor O-ring with the specified clean engine oil before installation. Reverse the applicable removal sequence and tighten the sensor retaining fastener to 10 Nm. Restore any displaced capacitor, tube retainer and electrical connections, and reinstall the applicable manifold. On the 2.3L, tighten the appearance-cover nuts to 9 Nm.

watchFor.title: Different oils despite similar sensors
watchFor.body: The seal-lubrication materials differ by engine. Use the specification in the matching sensor procedure.

watchFor.title: Left-bank exhaust access on the V8 engines
watchFor.body: The interference capacitor must be moved aside for access and restored during reassembly.

notes: These removal and installation procedures do not establish a sensor failure from a symptom or fault code.

verification.title: Confirm installation details
verification.body: Check that the lubricated sensor is installed, its retaining fastener is tightened and its electrical connector is reconnected.

verification.title: Confirm the access route is restored
verification.body: Account for the components removed on the selected branch, including manifold installation, the V8 capacitor or the 2.3L fuel-sensor connector and tube retainer.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost intake and exhaust CMP sensor removal and installation, including appearance-cover and fuel-tube-retainer access.
3.7L intake and exhaust CMP sensor removal and installation on both banks, with upper-manifold removal for the right bank.
5.0L CMP sensor removal and installation on both banks, including manifold access and left exhaust sensor capacitor clearance.
5.2L CMP sensor removal and installation on both banks using the specified 5W-50 seal lubricant.
3.7L upper intake manifold removal and installation for right-hand sensor access.
5.0L intake manifold removal and installation for sensor access.
5.2L intake manifold removal and installation for sensor access.

guides.title: Replace the clutch pedal position switch
guides.summary: Disconnect the clutch pedal position switch, remove it from its bracket and install the replacement in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The clutch pedal position (CPP) switch provides an electrical indication of clutch-pedal position. Its bracket locates it at the pedal, and its connector joins it to the vehicle wiring. Replacement is a short operation once the faulty component has been identified. The 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures all use the same disconnect, remove and reverse-install sequence.
guides.why: Both interfaces matter: the bracket holds the switch in its working position, while the connector carries its electrical connection. Fitting a replacement without fully restoring either interface leaves the repair incomplete. The removal operation itself does not establish why a pedal-related complaint occurred.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the clutch pedal position switch as requiring replacement.
notes: Select the procedure matching the engine before working at the pedal bracket.

prepare.title: Identify the mounting and connector
prepare.detail: Locate the CPP switch at its bracket and examine the matching procedure’s illustration. Be able to reach the electrical connector and bracket retention without pulling on the wiring.

steps.title: Confirm the switch to be removed
steps.body: Match the switch, connector and bracket to the applicable engine procedure. This establishes the component and mounting interface before anything is disconnected.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body: Release and unplug the switch connector. Handle the connector body rather than using the wires to pull it free, then keep it clear of the switch removal path.

steps.title: Remove the switch from the bracket
steps.body: Remove the CPP switch using the bracket engagement shown in the applicable procedure. Note how it sits in the bracket so the replacement can return to the correct mounting position.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Fit the replacement switch into the bracket, then reconnect the electrical connector. Complete the mounting before reconnecting the wiring, following the reverse of the removal sequence.

watchFor.title: Incomplete bracket engagement
watchFor.body: A switch that is not properly retained has not been fully installed, even if its connector is attached.

watchFor.title: An unsecured connector
watchFor.body: Confirm the connector is fully engaged after the switch is mounted.

notes: No switch adjustment or electronic relearn is specified within this replacement operation.
The selected illustration shows the 2.3L installation.

verification.title: Confirm completed reassembly
verification.body: Check that the bracket retains the switch and the electrical connector is secured. These checks confirm assembly; they do not independently prove that the original electrical complaint has been resolved.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L CPP switch removal and reverse-order installation.
3.7L CPP switch removal and reverse-order installation.
5.0L CPP switch removal and reverse-order installation.
5.2L CPP switch removal and reverse-order installation.

applicability.equipment: Vehicles fitted with a clutch pedal; engine-specific procedures cover 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L.

guides.title: Replace the crankshaft position sensor by engine variant
guides.summary: Follow the correct engine-specific sensor access and installation route, then complete the scan-tool Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction.
guides.introduction: The crankshaft position (CKP) sensor supplies crankshaft-position information to the engine controls. Its replacement method differs considerably between these engines: the 2.3L needs mechanical alignment, the 3.7L uses bell-housing access, the 5.0L requires intake-manifold removal, and the 5.2L sensor is replaced with the rear-seal retainer kit.
guides.why: Correct installation includes both physical positioning and the specified scan-tool learning step. On the 2.3L, loosening the crankshaft pulley bolt can also release the unkeyed timing sprocket because the assembly relies on friction and diamond washers. That makes an unnecessary pulley-bolt disturbance a serious timing risk.

when.summary: After diagnosis calls for CKP sensor replacement and the engine-specific access route is confirmed.
notes: Complete only the applicable engine branch, followed by the common scan-tool correction.
The replacement procedures do not establish a sensor fault from a symptom alone.

prepare.title: Arrange installation and learning equipment
prepare.detail: Have a scan tool capable of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction. The 2.3L also requires timing peg 303-507, alignment tool 303-1521 and the equipment specified for its stretchy A/C belt.

prepare.title: Plan the access work
prepare.detail: Provide hoist access for the 3.7L. The 5.0L manifold operation requires fuel-pressure release, battery ground and positive cable disconnection, and new manifold gaskets. Obtain the complete rear-seal-with-retainer-plate kit for the 5.2L.

steps.title: 2.3L: expose and remove the sensor
steps.body: Follow [A/C Compressor Belt](#/document/G1688221) to remove the belt. Disconnect the compressor connectors and harness retainers, remove its bolts and support the compressor aside as illustrated. Remove the CKP sensor bolts, disconnect its connector and remove the sensor. Maintain engine-repair cleanliness.

steps.title: 2.3L: establish position and align the replacement
steps.body: Follow [the 2.3L sensor procedure](#/document/G1692140). Turn the crankshaft clockwise until the first piston is 45° before top dead center, using the front-cover and pulley guide holes. Remove the engine plug bolt, install timing peg 303-507 and rotate clockwise until the crankshaft contacts it. Connect and fit the sensor with finger-tight bolts. Fit alignment tool 303-1521 to the sensor and trigger-wheel tooth, then tighten the sensor bolts to 7 Nm.

steps.title: 3.7L: use the bell-housing access
steps.body: Place the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist. Remove the heat-shield nut, bolt and shield, then move the access plug aside. Withdraw the sensor and its bolt from the bell housing before disconnecting the electrical connector, preventing the sensor from falling inside. Connect and install the replacement using [the 3.7L procedure](#/document/G1692248).

steps.title: 5.0L: reach the sensor through manifold removal
steps.body: Complete [Intake Manifold removal](#/document/G1685326), including pressure release, battery disconnection and the fuel, hose and rear-wiring access steps. The fuel rail can remain with the manifold assembly. Discard the manifold gaskets. Disconnect the CKP connector and remove the sensor bolt and sensor, then fit the replacement using [the 5.0L procedure](#/document/G1692276).

steps.title: 5.2L: replace the sensor with its retainer kit
steps.body: The sensor and crankshaft rear-seal retainer plate must be removed and discarded together. Follow [Crankshaft Rear Seal with Retainer Plate](#/document/G1800270) and install the sensor as part of that kit, as required by [the 5.2L sensor procedure](#/document/G1802182).

steps.title: Restore the applicable access assemblies
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove both special tools, install the engine plug bolt, and restore the compressor, connectors, retainers and belt. Follow the belt procedure's seating checks for both drive belts. On the 3.7L, restore the access plug and heat shield. On the 5.0L, reinstall the manifold with new gaskets and complete all reconnections through its installation procedure.

steps.title: Complete the common learning procedure
steps.body: For every engine, use the scan tool to perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction and follow its on-screen instructions. Treat this as part of sensor installation, after the applicable mechanical work is complete.

watchFor.title: 2.3L pulley-bolt disturbance
watchFor.body: Do not loosen the pulley bolt during this access work. Any repair requiring its loosening needs the specified crankshaft and camshaft locking procedure first.

watchFor.title: The timing peg is a one-direction stop
watchFor.body: The 2.3L crankshaft can still turn counterclockwise with the peg installed. Maintain the required top-dead-center position during alignment.

notes: If the 5.0L manifold operation follows upper-engine failure, inspect the manifold for metal debris. Replace it if debris is found; a newly installed manifold also requires the stated road test.

verification.title: Check the applicable physical installation
verification.body: Confirm sensor fastening and access reassembly against the engine-specific procedure. For the 2.3L, specifically confirm both special tools are removed and both belts are seated correctly.

verification.title: Record the learning result
verification.body: Record successful completion of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction, or the scan tool's reported reason it could not complete.

3.7L CKP bell-housing access, installation and scan-tool correction.

5.2L CKP replacement as part of the rear-seal retainer kit and scan-tool correction.
2.3L A/C compressor-belt removal, installation and belt-seating checks.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost engine coolant temperature sensor
guides.summary: Replace the coolant temperature sensor using its specified tightening stages, then refill and bleed the 2.3L cooling system.
guides.introduction: The engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor supplies a temperature input to the electronic engine controls. The powertrain control module combines sensor information with its programmed strategy to control engine operation. Replacing this sensor opens a coolant passage as well as disconnecting an electrical input, so the job includes cooling-system draining and restoration.
guides.why: Draining the system reduces coolant loss, but fluid can still escape at the sensor opening. Having the replacement ready helps control that loss. Correct tightening secures the new sensor, and completing the filling and bleeding procedure restores coolant circulation without leaving trapped air.

when.summary: When replacement of the 2.3L engine coolant temperature sensor has been established as necessary.
notes: This is the replacement path; it does not establish the cause of an incorrect temperature signal.

prepare.title: Prepare for coolant handling
prepare.detail: Have the replacement sensor and a shop towel ready, together with the equipment required for the 2.3L cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Provide safe access and controlled tightening
prepare.detail: Use a vehicle hoist, suitable sensor-removal tools and torque-and-angle capability. Identify the marked lifting points and check that hoist adapters clear suspension and underbody components.

steps.title: Drain the cooling system
steps.body: Begin the [sensor replacement procedure](#/document/G1692142) by completing the [2.3L cooling-system draining procedure](#/document/G1673124). Follow its handling precautions before opening the sensor's coolant passage.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and stage the replacement
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on the hoist using the triangle-marked lifting points. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Keep the new sensor and shop towel close to the work area before removing the old component.

steps.title: Disconnect and exchange the sensor
steps.body: Disconnect the sensor's electrical connector, then remove the sensor, capturing escaping coolant with the towel. Install the replacement using both tightening stages: first 16 Nm, then an additional 180°. The angle stage is part of the installation requirement.

steps.title: Reconnect and restore the cooling system
steps.body: Reconnect the electrical connector as part of reversing removal. Fill and bleed the cooling system using the linked 2.3L procedure, including its specified filling method. Finish that procedure before treating the sensor replacement as complete.

watchFor.title: Residual coolant at the opening
watchFor.body: System draining does not eliminate the need to catch escaping fluid when the sensor is removed.

watchFor.title: Incomplete installation
watchFor.body: Both the electrical reconnection and cooling-system filling and bleeding are required after installing the sensor.

notes: Use the 2.3L cooling procedure for the applicable coolant requirements and filling sequence.

verification.title: Confirm sensor installation
verification.body: Confirm completion of both tightening stages and reconnection of the sensor electrical connector.

verification.title: Record coolant restoration
verification.body: Record that the cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure has been completed, rather than recording only the sensor exchange.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost ECT sensor removal, replacement and two-stage installation tightening.
Required 2.3L cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.
Correct vehicle lifting points and safe hoist positioning.

guides.title: Replace the engine mount control solenoid on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Replace the engine mount control solenoid and restore its vacuum connections, electrical connector and mounting retainer.
guides.introduction: The engine mount control solenoid is an electrically operated valve in the mount's vacuum-control plumbing. It connects an electrical command to the vacuum side of the system. This job replaces that external valve assembly, making the electrical connector, vacuum hose connections and mounting retainer the main points of attention.
guides.why: Correct hose connections are necessary for the valve to control the intended vacuum path. The electrical connector supplies the command side, while the retainer secures the assembly. Replacing the valve without restoring all these connections would leave the repair incomplete.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the engine mount control solenoid requires replacement.
notes: A mount-related concern by itself does not establish that the solenoid has failed.

prepare.title: Identify the connections
prepare.detail: Use the component illustration to distinguish the electrical connector, vacuum hose connectors and mounting retainer. Note the existing hose-to-port arrangement before disconnecting it.

prepare.title: Prepare the replacement and tools
prepare.detail: Have the correct replacement solenoid, suitable hand tools and a torque wrench for the 11 Nm retaining-fastener specification.

steps.title: Disconnect the control connections
steps.body: Follow the [replacement procedure](#/document/G1817827). Disconnect the electrical connector and the vacuum hose connectors from the solenoid assembly, keeping their original destinations identifiable for installation.

steps.title: Remove the solenoid
steps.body: Remove the mounting retainer and take out the engine mount control solenoid. This releases the valve assembly after its attached wiring and hoses have been disconnected.

steps.title: Mount the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to position the replacement solenoid and install its retainer. Tighten the retaining fastener to 11 Nm so the assembly is secured as specified.

steps.title: Restore the vacuum and electrical paths
steps.body: Reconnect the vacuum hoses to their original connections and reconnect the electrical connector. Compare the finished arrangement with the illustrated assembly and the positions noted before removal.

watchFor.title: A missed vacuum connection
watchFor.body: The assembly has several hose connections. Check each connection individually rather than judging completion from the mounted solenoid alone.

watchFor.title: Confusing replacement with diagnosis
watchFor.body: A successful physical installation does not establish the cause of an unresolved mount-control complaint.

notes: The tightening value applies to the mounting retainer; the electrical and vacuum connectors are reconnected through the reverse installation sequence.

verification.title: Check reassembly
verification.body: Confirm that the solenoid is retained at the specified torque, the electrical connector is reconnected and every disconnected vacuum hose is restored to its original connection.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L engine mount control solenoid removal and installation, including electrical/vacuum disconnection and retainer tightening.

applicability.equipment: 2.3L EcoBoost engine mount control solenoid with the illustrated electrical and vacuum connections.

guides.title: Replace the oil-pressure sensor — 5.0L Performance Package or 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the oil-pressure sensing component using its engine-specific connector access, sealing condition and tightening method.
guides.introduction: The engine oil-pressure sensing component provides an electrical indication related to the lubrication system’s pressure. Its threaded connection must seal against oil leakage, while its connector carries the electrical signal. The 5.0L procedure calls the component a switch and applies only to Performance Package vehicles; the 5.2L procedure calls it a sensor and includes a protective cover.
guides.why: The two components have different installation tightening instructions despite their similar purpose. The 5.0L uses torque followed by an additional angle, while the 5.2L uses a single torque value. Sealant is specifically required when reusing the removed component. Replacing the sensing component does not itself correct a mechanical oil-pressure problem.

when.summary: When the applicable oil-pressure switch or sensor requires replacement or removal and refitting.
