steps.body: During charging, inject the calculated allowance through the low-side service port. The chart also permits direct inlet-port addition for the condenser, condenser with drier element, and evaporator. Use the applicable method once for the calculated dose.

steps.title: Use the injector-set operating sequence when applicable
steps.body: With the engine off and cool, system pressure should be 413–551 kPa at 24°C. Fill and adjust the injector, then connect it to the low-side service valve. Clear every hose and tool from the cooling fan and drive belt before starting the engine. Switch A/C on and turn the injector piston clockwise to deliver the oil.

watchFor.title: Pulley rotation without shaft rotation
watchFor.body: For the rotating-drain methods, turning only the pulley will not satisfy the draining instruction.

watchFor.title: Different drain-bolt specifications
watchFor.body: Types 1, 2 and 3 have different drain-bolt tightening values. Use the identified type's instructions.

notes: Factory fluorescent dye normally makes additional dye unnecessary before leak diagnosis, even after substantial refrigerant removal.

Replacement receiver driers and elements contain a dye wafer that dissolves after approximately 30 minutes of continuous A/C operation. Additional dye is unnecessary after flushing when the prescribed new desiccant component is installed.

diagnostics.finding: Excessive oil escaped through a ruptured or separated hose or other damage.
diagnostics.meaning: The ordinary component allowance does not cover this loss.
diagnostics.next: Replace the receiver drier and follow the total-system-oil-capacity branch, establishing the vehicle's specified capacity before filling.

verification.title: Record the oil balance
verification.body: Record recovered oil, old-compressor drain quantity when applicable, the repair allowance and the amount delivered.

verification.title: Confirm branch completion
verification.body: Check that applicable drain bolts, port caps, clutch and field coil have been restored according to the selected compressor procedure.

procedures.purpose: Complete component oil allowances, compressor-type balancing, service-unit filling and injector-set procedure.

guides.title: Replace the A/C compressor pressure-relief valve on the 3.7L or 5.0L
guides.summary: Recover the refrigerant, replace the compressor pressure-relief valve and restore the system through controlled oil accounting, evacuation and charging.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning compressor's pressure-relief valve provides a release path for excessive refrigerant pressure. It is part of the sealed refrigerant circuit, so replacing it requires recovery equipment before the valve is disturbed. The 3.7L and 5.0L procedures share the same basic repair sequence, but their illustrations locate the valve on the respective compressor installations.
guides.why: The small amount of mechanical work should not obscure the system-service requirements. Refrigerant must be identified before recovery to protect the service equipment from contamination. Oil removed during recovery must be accounted for because the compressor relies on oil circulating with the refrigerant. Evacuation and its vacuum-hold check are required before the correct charge is restored.
searchTerms: A/C compressor pressure relief valve replacement

when.summary: When the compressor pressure-relief valve has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: A cooling complaint alone does not establish that this valve is defective.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant-service capability
prepare.detail: Use refrigerant identification equipment and Ford-approved R134a recovery, evacuation and charging equipment, following the equipment manufacturer's instructions.

prepare.title: Prepare oil accounting
prepare.detail: Provide a way to record oil collected during recovery. Use only clean, new Motorcraft PAG Refrigerant Compressor Oil YN-12-D, with the appropriate service unit or oil injector.

steps.title: Identify and recover the refrigerant
steps.body: Follow [recovery, evacuation and charging](#/document/G1912323). Analyze the refrigerant before recovery, then connect to both service ports; low-side-only recovery is prohibited. Record any oil removed. After recovery, allow the system to stand and confirm the vacuum remains stable for 2 minutes, repeating the prescribed recovery sequence if it does not.

steps.title: Replace the correct compressor valve
steps.body: Use the [3.7L valve procedure](#/document/G1701608) or [5.0L valve procedure](#/document/G1701616) to identify the component. Remove the valve only after recovery is complete. Install the replacement by reversing the removal operation and tighten it to 10 Nm.

steps.title: Account for refrigerant oil
steps.body: Use the [oil-adding procedure](#/document/G1912330) to restore the correct oil amount, including oil collected during recovery. Its table does not assign a separate extra allowance to pressure-relief-valve replacement. Do not substitute the allowance for a hose, compressor or O-ring repair.

steps.title: Evacuate and confirm the vacuum holds
steps.body: Evacuate to at least 99.4 kPa of vacuum, as close to 101.1 kPa as possible, and continue pumping for at least 45 minutes. Turn the pump off and observe the gauge for 10 minutes to confirm the vacuum is held.

steps.title: Restore the specified charge
steps.body: Set the applicable refrigerant charge amount and charge through the service equipment following its instructions. If the oil-injector method is used, follow its prescribed low-side connection and operating conditions, and keep all hoses and tools clear of the cooling fan and drive belt.

watchFor.title: Contaminated refrigerant
watchFor.body: Do not put it into normal recovery equipment. Follow the prescribed referral or use equipment designated for contaminated refrigerant and the required disposal process.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled oil addition
watchFor.body: Adding an arbitrary quantity can upset the system oil balance. Compressor-replacement oil-matching routines are not automatically part of valve replacement.

notes: Factory-added fluorescent dye supports leak diagnosis; adding more dye is not normally necessary before diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Vacuum is lost during the post-recovery observation.
diagnostics.meaning: The recovery completion condition has not been met.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the specified recovery steps until vacuum remains stable for 2 minutes.

diagnostics.finding: Vacuum is not held during the post-evacuation observation.
diagnostics.meaning: The required pre-charge check has not passed.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the failed hold condition before completing charging.

verification.title: Confirm service completion
verification.body: Confirm valve tightening, the evacuation period, vacuum-hold observation and specified refrigerant charge are complete.

verification.title: Record the service quantities
verification.body: Record refrigerant identification, oil recovered and added, the vacuum-hold result and the charge amount used.

procedures.purpose: 3.7L compressor pressure-relief-valve removal and installation.
5.0L compressor pressure-relief-valve removal and installation.
Refrigerant identification, complete recovery, evacuation, vacuum-hold checks and charging.
Correct PAG oil selection, recovery-oil compensation and oil-injection methods.

guides.title: Replace the A/C expansion valve on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L models
guides.summary: Recover the refrigerant, replace the thermostatic expansion valve using the correct engine access sequence, and complete oil replenishment and refrigerant servicing.
guides.introduction: The thermostatic expansion valve (TXV) meters refrigerant entering the air-conditioning evaporator, where the system absorbs heat from cabin air. Air conditioning (A/C) also reduces cabin humidity. Replacement opens the refrigerant circuit, regardless of whether the vehicle has manual or dual automatic temperature control.
guides.why: Open refrigerant connections need immediate protection from dirt. Seal lubricant and refrigerant-oil replenishment have specific requirements. Access also changes with the engine: the V8 procedures include battery and brace work that is absent from the listed 2.3L and 3.7L sequences.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established a need to replace the thermostatic expansion valve.
notes: A cooling complaint alone does not establish that the valve requires replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant-service capability
prepare.detail: Have equipment and capability for the applicable recovery, evacuation and charging procedure before opening any connection. Obtain the required refrigerant-oil amount through the oil-adding procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare clean connections and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have suitable caps or other port protection, the specified seal lubricant and required seals. The 5.2L branch also requires replacement strut-tower cross-brace nuts.

steps.title: Recover the refrigerant
steps.body: Begin with the applicable [recovery procedure](#/document/G1912323). Complete recovery before loosening the valve connections; removing the valve is only one part of servicing the opened refrigerant circuit.

steps.title: Follow the engine-specific access branch
steps.body: On 5.0L vehicles, disconnect the battery ground and positive cables; if a cross brace is fitted, detach its battery-cable retainer and remove the brace nuts and brace. On 5.2L vehicles, disconnect the battery, detach the harness retainer, discard the brace nuts and remove the strut-tower cross brace. Use the [battery procedure](#/document/G1692356).

steps.title: Disconnect and protect the lines
steps.body: The 2.3L and 3.7L sequences proceed from recovery to the valve connections. Remove the retaining nut and TXV bracket, then disconnect the condenser outlet and evaporator outlet lines. Protect every exposed port and fitting against contamination.

steps.title: Replace the valve and reconnect
steps.body: Remove the valve bolts and TXV, then follow the applicable installation sequence in reverse. The 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures explicitly require new O-rings lubricated only with the specified material. Tighten valve bolts to 62 lb.in (7 Nm) and the line-bracket nut to 133 lb.in (15 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the engine-specific access components
steps.body: Refit the brace and retainers where removed, using new cross-brace nuts on the 5.2L. Complete battery reconnection through its dedicated procedure. Follow the 5.0L procedure’s own brace installation details when that optional brace is fitted.

steps.title: Complete oil and refrigerant servicing
steps.body: All engine branches require the correct amount of clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) oil through [Refrigerant Oil Adding](#/document/G1912330). Complete evacuation and charging through the applicable refrigerant-service procedure. Obtain quantities from those procedures rather than assuming they are shared between variants.

watchFor.title: Port protection left in place
watchFor.body: Remove caps, tape and other protective materials before reconnecting the valve and lines.

watchFor.title: Confusing oil replenishment with seal lubrication
watchFor.body: The instruction to add PAG oil does not replace the requirement to use the specified seal-lubricating material.

notes: The illustrations show the 2.3L valve connections; follow the appropriate engine procedure for surrounding access.
The 3.7L installation instruction specifies reverse-order reassembly and correct PAG-oil replenishment; retain that branch’s own requirements.

verification.title: Confirm connection and access restoration
verification.body: Confirm that protective materials are removed, joints are reassembled, required new seals are installed and all removed battery, brace and retainer components are restored.

verification.title: Record the refrigerant-service completion
verification.body: Record the applicable oil amount used and the completion results required by the recovery, evacuation and charging procedure.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost TXV removal, installation and new O-ring requirements.
3.7L Duratec TXV removal, installation and oil replenishment.
5.0L TXV replacement, battery disconnection and optional cross-brace access.
5.2L TXV replacement, battery access and cross-brace removal with discarded nuts.
A/C refrigerant recovery, evacuation and charging.
Determine and add the correct refrigerant-oil amount.
Battery disconnection and reconnection for the V8 access branches.

guides.title: Diagnose perimeter alarm failures and unwanted activations
guides.summary: Use alarm history, switch inputs and directed circuit tests to distinguish arming, hood-switch, intrusion-sensor and alarm-output faults.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) coordinates the perimeter alarm, using entry-point switches, key information and the intrusion/inclination sensor to recognize unauthorized access. It then operates the horn and lamps. Diagnosis separates a missing input, failed output, wiring problem and incorrect operating condition before selecting a repair.
guides.why: An alarm that stays silent may never have armed, may not detect the entry, or may have an output fault. Unwanted activation requires identifying the recorded trigger. These distinctions prevent a working sensor or BCM from being replaced for a fault elsewhere.

when.summary: When the alarm fails to arm or respond, activates unexpectedly, or stores a relevant BCM fault code.
notes: Replacement decisions in pinpoint tests require the stated concern to be present; use recorded history to investigate intermittent complaints.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%, inspect previous repairs, wiring and connectors, and retrieve related module codes. Diagnose circuit faults before system-performance faults.

prepare.title: Prepare for circuit testing
prepare.detail: Use the Diagnostic Methods procedure, correct probe adapters and Wiring Diagrams Cell 117. Follow each test's ignition and connector-isolation instructions. Use fused jumpers only where directed.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Ford-capable diagnostic scan tool; digital multimeter; correct terminal probe adapters; fused jumper wires; applicable wiring diagrams and Ford diagnostic capability.

steps.title: Identify the complaint and recorded trigger
steps.body: Disarm the alarm before attempting BCM communication. Retrieve codes and, for unwanted activation, record ALARM_EVT_1 through ALARM_EVT_4. Route the complaint through the diagnostic findings below before choosing a pinpoint test.

steps.title: Test A: hood opening does not trigger the alarm
steps.body: Inspect the hood latch for damage. Monitor the hood-switch parameter identification (PID), HOOD_SW, while disconnecting the switch. An AJAR reading directs latch replacement. Otherwise, test the input for a short to ground; repair a failed circuit or proceed to the BCM connection check.

steps.title: Test B: intrusion sensing does not trigger the alarm
steps.body: Inspect BCM fuse 18 (5A), then test sensor supply and ground. Missing supply with a sound fuse requires a supply-wire continuity check; a sound wire directs BCM assessment. With supply and ground satisfactory, test the LIN circuit for shorts to voltage, shorts to ground and an open. Inspect the overhead-console harness before replacing the sensor. Repair harness faults or replace the console as directed. Initialize a replacement sensor, retest, and proceed to BCM assessment if the concern remains.

steps.title: Test C: no arming or turn-signal confirmation
steps.body: Close the hood before the BCM self-test and resolve retrieved codes first. Then check closed-door and closed-luggage-lid indications, hazard-lamp operation and remote keyless entry (RKE) lock/unlock operation in order. Follow the corresponding lighting, instrumentation or entry-system diagnostic branch when a check fails. If these checks pass, assess BCM connections.

steps.title: Test D: investigate B1305:01
steps.body: Follow the specified fused-jumper tests for the hood switch. If substituting the closed switch clears the code, replace the latch. If grounding the input clears it, repair the switch ground circuit. Remove each jumper after its self-test. If the code persists, test input-wire continuity before proceeding to BCM assessment.

steps.title: Resolve the common BCM branch
steps.body: Inspect BCM connectors for corrosion, bent or damaged terminals and pushed-out pins; repair them as directed and reconnect securely. Retest the concern. If it remains, check applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS; follow a relevant bulletin or the vehicle-identification-number-specific guided BCM routine. If reconnection resolves it, still correct the underlying connector fault.

watchFor.title: Testing an armed vehicle
watchFor.body: An attempted scan-tool session can trigger the alarm and temporarily block BCM diagnostics.

watchFor.title: An open hood during self-test
watchFor.body: B1305:01 can set simply because the hood is open; close it before the arming diagnostic self-test.

notes: A replacement intrusion/inclination sensor requires LIN New Module Initialization.
If directed BCM replacement becomes necessary, it requires programmable module installation, at least 2 programmed keys and a parameter reset.

diagnostics.meaning: These distinguish a LIN short to ground, communication faults or a reported sensor obstruction.
diagnostics.next: Use Test B. A code is not sufficient evidence to replace the sensor.

diagnostics.meaning: B109F:49 identifies internal sensor failure; B109F:55 identifies missing configuration.
diagnostics.next: For B109F:49, install and initialize a new sensor. For B109F:55, perform LIN New Module Initialization. Route other unlisted codes to BCM diagnostics.

diagnostics.finding: Recorded unwanted-alarm event.
diagnostics.meaning: Panic indicates commanded operation; Door Ajar, Interior Motion Detected, Tilt Detected and Hood Ajar identify different inputs.
diagnostics.next: Explain panic-button operation for Panic; diagnose door switches for Door Ajar, use Test B for motion/tilt, and Test D for Hood Ajar. A RUN transition without a valid passive anti-theft key read is another listed possible cause.

diagnostics.finding: Only a door, luggage-lid or horn response is missing.
diagnostics.meaning: The complaint belongs to a particular input or output path.
diagnostics.next: For door entry, diagnose courtesy lamps failing to illuminate with the door open. For luggage entry, diagnose the incorrect lid-ajar indication. For absent horn output, use horn diagnostics.

verification.title: Repeat the original operating condition
verification.body: After repair, test normal operation with the relevant entry point closed through its 20-second arming countdown. Allow for the driver-door's 12-second activation delay when applicable. Confirm the repaired input and required alarm outputs.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record initial codes, alarm-event history, failed circuit checks, repairs and the repeat-test outcome. Confirm required sensor initialization is complete and distinguish historical triggers from a newly reproduced event.

procedures.purpose: Complete code and symptom charts, Pinpoint Tests A–D, connections and pass/fail limits.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites, probing, meter use and fused-jumper methods.
Arming conditions, alarm delays, scan-access protection and sensor initialization requirements.
BCM diagnosis for other codes and directed module assessment.
Door-ajar and courtesy-lamp diagnostic branches.
Incorrect luggage-compartment-lid ajar indication.
Absent horn output during alarm activation.
Hood latch replacement when Test A or D directs it.
Overhead-console removal and replacement when Test B directs it.
Turn-signal or hazard-output faults found in Test C.
RKE lock/unlock faults found in Test C.

guides.title: Replace the fuel filler door spring
guides.summary: Release the spring's retaining tab with a screwdriver and fit the replacement into the fuel filler door assembly.
guides.introduction: The fuel filler door spring provides spring force for the exterior flap's operation. A retaining tab secures the small spring component in the door assembly. Replacement is a short mechanical job carried out with the filler door open: release the tab, withdraw the component and install its replacement.
guides.why: The retaining tab is the key to removal. Pressing it releases the spring from its mounting, allowing the component to move out along the illustrated path. Locating that release point first keeps the work focused on the part designed to disengage.
searchTerms: fuel filler door spring retaining tab

when.summary: When the fuel filler door spring itself requires replacement.
notes: The procedure begins with the fuel filler door open.

prepare.title: Prepare the component and tool
prepare.detail: Have the replacement spring and a screwdriver ready. Use the release-tab illustration to identify the screwdriver contact point before applying pressure.

steps.title: Open the door and identify the spring
steps.body: Open the fuel filler door. Locate the spring component beside the filler opening and identify its retaining tab using the [replacement illustration](#/document/G1693226). Note how the component sits in its mounting so the replacement can follow the same arrangement.

steps.title: Press the retaining tab and remove the spring
steps.body: Use the screwdriver to press the indicated tab. With the tab released, withdraw the spring from the fuel filler door assembly in the illustrated direction. The image separates these actions: release the tab first, then move the component out.

steps.title: Install the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to return the replacement spring to the mounting position. Restore the retaining-tab engagement that secured the original component, and confirm the spring is seated in the assembly.

watchFor.title: Resistance before tab release
watchFor.body: If the spring remains retained, check that the screwdriver is pressing the indicated tab before continuing withdrawal.

watchFor.title: Incomplete retention
watchFor.body: A replacement placed in the opening still needs its retaining tab engaged to complete installation.

notes: The close-up illustration shows the release tab more clearly than the overall view of the open door.

verification.title: Confirm seating and retention
verification.body: Check that the replacement occupies the original mounting position and is secured by its retaining tab.

procedures.purpose: Fuel filler door spring release-tab removal and reverse-sequence installation.

guides.title: Remove and refit a front door trim panel
guides.summary: Release the concealed fasteners and staged retainers, lift the panel off the door, then disconnect and reconnect its wiring and latch cable.
guides.introduction: The front door trim panel forms the interior door surface and surrounds the window switch and inside release handle. Bolts, clips and pin-type retainers secure it to the door. Even after these attachments are released, electrical connections and the latch cable can still tether the panel. Removal provides access behind the trim or allows the panel itself to be replaced.
guides.why: The panel releases in stages and then lifts upward and outward from the door. Following that sequence avoids pulling against an attachment that is still engaged. The upper and center bolts also use a different tightening specification from the lower retainers, so installation requires more than simply tightening every fastener alike.

when.summary: When replacing the front door trim panel or gaining access to components behind it.
notes: The right door is illustrated; the left door follows a similar procedure.
Retain installation information shown alongside the removal steps.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and fastener work
prepare.detail: Have suitable trim-release and fastener tools, plus a torque tool capable of the specified low tightening values.

prepare.title: Plan switch removal and panel support
prepare.detail: Have the front door window control switch procedure available. Support the panel during final separation so its electrical connections and latch cable remain accessible.

steps.title: Expose the upper fastening
steps.body: Remove the small cover and upper trim-panel bolt shown in [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600). The cover conceals an attachment that must be released before moving the panel.

steps.title: Remove the switch and remaining threaded attachments
steps.body: Remove the window switch using [Front Door Window Control Switch](#/document/G1695936). Then remove the center trim-panel bolt and lower retainers.

steps.title: Release the rear upper area
steps.body: Position the rear upper portion away from the door. Release the clip, followed by the pin-type retainers, in the illustrated sequence.

steps.title: Continue around the rear and lower portions
steps.body: Position the rear and lower portions away, releasing the indicated pin-type retainer and then the clip. Move the panel farther away and release the remaining pin-type retainers in their illustrated order.

steps.title: Lift off and disconnect
steps.body: Lift the panel upward and outward to release it from the door. Disconnect electrical connectors where fitted, then release the latch cable. Keep supporting the panel until these remaining connections are free.

steps.title: Transfer parts and reinstall
steps.body: Transfer parts as necessary and reverse the removal sequence. Reconnect the latch cable and applicable electrical connectors, engage the panel and retainers, and reinstall the switch and fasteners. Tighten the upper and center bolts to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm); tighten the lower retainers to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm).

watchFor.title: A section remains firmly attached
watchFor.body: Recheck the fasteners and the illustrated retainer sequence before pulling farther.

watchFor.title: The panel is loose but still tethered
watchFor.body: Electrical connectors and the latch cable are disconnected after lifting the panel free. Do not let its weight pull on them.

notes: The final release is upward and outward; pulling the whole panel straight away does not follow the specified removal sequence.

verification.title: Confirm connections and seating
verification.body: Confirm the latch cable and fitted electrical connectors are reattached, the upper panel mounting is engaged, and the clips and pin-type retainers are seated.

verification.title: Confirm fastener installation
verification.body: Check that the upper and center bolts received their specified torque and the lower retainers received their separate lower torque. Confirm transferred parts, the switch and the fastening cover are installed.

procedures.purpose: Front door trim-panel removal and installation, including staged clip release, connections and fastener torques.
Remove and reinstall the front door window control switch during trim-panel access.

applicability.equipment: Either front door; left-hand-drive arrangement illustrated, with right-hand drive similar.

guides.title: Remove and Refit the Rear Spoiler
guides.summary: Remove the rear spoiler, clean its mounting surface and restore its nut and double-sided tape attachments.
guides.introduction: The rear spoiler shapes airflow over the rear of the car and attaches to the luggage-compartment lid through both threaded fasteners and double-sided adhesive tape. This job releases both attachments, prepares the lid surface and reinstalls the spoiler with the specified tightening and bonding pressure.
guides.why: Removing the nuts does not release the tape bond. During installation, a clean surface allows the tape to contact the lid properly, while the specified pressure establishes adhesion along the spoiler's length. Nut tightening and tape bonding are separate parts of securing the assembly.

when.summary: When the rear spoiler requires replacement or removal for luggage-compartment lid work.

prepare.title: Prepare for interior access
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the luggage-compartment lid trim, rubber grommets and spoiler nuts, plus a torque wrench capable of the specified low tightening value.

prepare.title: Plan the adhesive attachment
prepare.detail: Allow for cleaning residual adhesive and dirt from the lid, and for restoring the double-sided tape attachment during installation.

steps.title: Expose the spoiler fasteners
steps.body: Remove the luggage-compartment lid trim panel, then remove the rubber grommets. This opens access to the spoiler's retaining nuts without disturbing the external attachment first.

steps.title: Remove the nuts and release the spoiler
steps.body: Remove the retaining nuts. Lift the spoiler to detach its double-sided tape from the lid. Expect the adhesive to continue holding the spoiler after the threaded fasteners have been removed.

steps.title: Clean the mounting surface
steps.body: Remove residual adhesive and dirt from the luggage-compartment lid. Complete this preparation before positioning the spoiler so residue does not interfere with contact between the tape and lid.

steps.title: Restore both attachments
steps.body: Refit the spoiler with its double-sided tape attachment in place. Apply approximately 15 lbs. of pressure along its length to ensure adhesion. Install the retaining nuts and tighten them to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), then reinstall the rubber grommets and lid trim panel.

watchFor.title: Incomplete tape adhesion
watchFor.body: Secured nuts alone do not establish that the adhesive has bonded along the spoiler.

watchFor.title: Overlooking the installation torque
watchFor.body: Use the specified low nut torque when reversing the removal sequence.

notes: The procedure illustrates a single-wing spoiler; other spoiler styles are described as similar.

verification.title: Confirm attachment and access restoration
verification.body: Confirm that the prescribed pressure was applied along the spoiler, the tape adhered, the nuts were tightened to specification, and all grommets and trim were reinstalled.

procedures.purpose: Rear spoiler removal, mounting-surface cleaning and installation with specified torque and bonding pressure.

guides.title: Replace a Recaro front-seat backrest cover
guides.summary: Remove the seat, trim attachments and side airbag to replace the Recaro backrest cover while preserving its foam attachments and airbag deployment path.
guides.introduction: The backrest cover is secured over the foam by clips, hooks and hook-and-loop strips. On a seat with a side airbag, the cover also forms part of the intended deployment arrangement. This job replaces the upholstery or removes it for backrest access; it includes separate finishing branches for Recaro and GT 350 Recaro seats.
guides.why: A damaged side-airbag seat cover must be replaced rather than repaired because alterations can affect airbag deployment. Careful separation of the cover also protects attachment strips and hooks embedded in the foam. Pulling too hard can turn a cover job into additional foam damage.

when.summary: When a Recaro backrest cover is damaged or must be removed for backrest service.
notes: Cleaning is permitted; repairing a trim cover on a seat equipped with a side airbag is prohibited.
The left-hand-drive driver seat is illustrated; other seating positions are similar.

prepare.title: Arrange seat and airbag service capability
prepare.detail: Have the complete front-seat and Recaro side-airbag procedures available. Airbag removal requires the relevant supplemental restraint system service capability and the safety prerequisites in that procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare trim tools and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Prepare tools for the guide bolt and trim attachments. Have a new cover when replacing damaged upholstery; inspect bezels before deciding whether they can be reused.

steps.title: Remove the front seat
steps.body: Follow [Front Seat](#/document/G1695491) to remove the assembly. This establishes access for the backrest work.

steps.title: Remove the guide and surrounding bezels
steps.body: If fitted, remove the safety-belt guide by removing its cover and bolt. Remove the front pass-through bezels, then the rear bezels, inspecting both sets for damage and replacing them as necessary. Remove the backrest release-handle bezel.

steps.title: Remove the side airbag
steps.body: Follow [Recaro Seat Side Airbag](#/document/G1709237) before releasing the upholstery. Use that procedure for the airbag's safety requirements, removal and later installation.

steps.title: Free the lower cover attachments
steps.body: Detach the J-clip from the backrest frame and release the cover from the carrier hooks. Carefully release the hook-and-loop strips and hook-and-arrow attachments, then position the cover upward. Avoid pulling their anchors out of the foam.

steps.title: Follow the correct Recaro finishing branch
steps.body: Use the Recaro or GT 350 Recaro branch in [Backrest Cover Removal and Installation](#/document/G1695529). Each requires careful release of the remaining hook-and-loop strips before removing the cover. Remove the backrest carrier only if required.

steps.title: Inspect the airbag deployment area
steps.body: Before installation, inspect the side airbag, its cavity, mounting surface and deployment chute. Remove all foreign material. Replace a damaged airbag or damaged deployment chute rather than reinstalling it.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the carrier if removed, secure the cover attachments, and reinstall the airbag through its dedicated procedure. Refit the bezels, release-handle trim and safety-belt guide where fitted, then reinstall the seat through the front-seat procedure.

watchFor.title: Foam attachments beginning to lift
watchFor.body: Take care during separation: hook-and-loop strips and hook-and-arrow anchors can tear out of the foam pad.

watchFor.title: Damaged or contaminated deployment area
watchFor.body: Resolve damage and remove foreign material before closing the backrest; either can interfere with side-airbag deployment.

notes: Use the seat-specific branch. General information about power, memory or climate-controlled seats does not establish that those features are fitted to a Recaro seat.

verification.title: Confirm deployment-area condition
verification.body: Confirm that the airbag, cavity, mounting surface and chute passed inspection, foreign material was removed, and damaged components were replaced.

verification.title: Confirm trim and seat reassembly
verification.body: Check that the cover attachments and bezels are engaged without torn foam anchors, and that the airbag and seat installation procedures are complete.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the backrest cover using the Recaro or GT 350 Recaro branch.
Remove the complete front seat before upholstery work and reinstall it afterward.
Safely remove and reinstall the side airbag fitted to Recaro seats.

applicability.equipment: Recaro and GT 350 Recaro front seats; seat side-airbag removal is required.

guides.title: Adjust Convertible Door Glass for Correct Seal Fit
guides.summary: Set door-glass height, fore/aft position and inward/outward alignment against the convertible roof seals and rear quarter glass.
guides.introduction: The door glass must meet both the convertible-top weatherstrips and the rear quarter glass. Its clamps establish height and fore/aft position, while the regulator rails control inward/outward alignment. This adjustment restores those relationships through measured changes.
guides.why: A misaligned door or rear quarter window can make correctly positioned front glass appear wrong. Establishing those references first avoids compensating at the wrong component, while equal rail movement prevents binding.

when.summary: When measurements show incorrect door-glass engagement or spacing, including during wind-noise or water-leak investigation.
notes: Check door alignment first if the door has been removed or replaced.

prepare.title: Prepare for measured adjustment
prepare.detail: Have marking tape, a measuring scale, suitable access tools and a torque wrench capable of the specified low tightening values.

prepare.title: Arrange access and initialization
prepare.detail: Use the applicable speaker removal procedure and have the named Power Door Window Initialization procedure available for completion.

steps.title: Establish the surrounding alignment
steps.body: For wind noise or water entry, check and correct rear quarter glass alignment first. If the door was removed or replaced, check front-door alignment before adjusting the glass.

steps.title: Expose the adjustment points
steps.body: Open the door and remove its speaker. Position the passenger front door module aside as directed, then remove the grommets, adhesive tapes and lower watershield. Install the window control switch, raise the door glass fully and close the door.

steps.title: Measure seal engagement
steps.body: Place tape at the A-pillar position 245 mm from the outer belt moulding base and at the roof-line position 230 mm forward from the glass rear edge. With the door open, record tape-to-glass-top distances. Close it and record tape-to-seal-retainer-bottom distances. Subtract the closed-door readings from the open-door readings.

steps.title: Correct height and fore/aft position
steps.body: Open the door, loosen both glass clamps and reposition the glass. Tighten the clamps to 9 Nm, then repeat the measurements. Required engagement is 4 mm ±2 mm at the A-pillar and 8 mm ±2.5 mm at the rear roof-line location.

steps.title: Check the quarter-window gap
steps.body: Measure the gap at positions 75 mm above the outer belt moulding base and 75 mm below the glass top. Each gap should be 9.8 mm ±1.5 mm, with top-to-bottom variation within ±1.0 mm. Record both readings.

steps.title: Set inward/outward engagement
steps.body: Lower the rear quarter glass and cycle the door glass against the top weatherstrips. Open the door, loosen the fore/aft run nuts and lower regulator nuts, and move both rails equally. Close and cycle again; repeat as needed. Open the door and lower its glass before tightening the regulator-rail nuts, lower run bolt/nuts and upper run nuts to 11 Nm without shifting the runs. Raise both windows and close the door.

steps.title: Repeat the checks and restore the door
steps.body: Repeat the taped engagement measurements and the in/out cycling check with the quarter glass lowered. Correct any remaining error, raise the quarter glass and close the door. Remove the tape, reinstall removed components and carry out Power Door Window Initialization.

watchFor.title: Binding during travel
watchFor.body: Unequal front and rear rail adjustments can bind the glass.

watchFor.title: Movement during tightening
watchFor.body: Keep the glass runs stationary while securing their fasteners.

notes: The right-hand side is illustrated; the left-hand procedure is similar.
Convertibles lack one-touch up and bounce-back features. Rear quarter window motors do not require initialization.

diagnostics.finding: Front engagement is correct, but quarter-window spacing or parallelism is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The remaining correction belongs at the rear quarter glass.
diagnostics.next: Follow Rear Quarter Window Glass Adjustment - Convertible.

verification.title: Record the final geometry
verification.body: Retain final engagement readings, both quarter-window gaps and their difference.

verification.title: Confirm operating engagement
verification.body: Complete the repeated weatherstrip-engagement check and required door-window initialization.

procedures.purpose: Complete convertible door-glass measurement, adjustment, reassembly and initialization reference.
Check or correct convertible rear quarter glass alignment.
Establish front-door alignment after door removal or replacement.
Right-hand speaker removal and installation for the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 access branch.

guides.title: Repair a broken rear-window defroster grid line
guides.summary: Restore a confirmed break in a rear-window heater or antenna grid line with a carefully prepared conductive repair.
guides.introduction: The rear-window defroster passes electricity through narrow conductive lines to warm the glass and improve rearward visibility. These lines are baked onto the glass surface, so scraping can remove them. Repair builds a conductive bridge across a localized break; the same method also applies to the antenna grid lines.
guides.why: A repair must have enough conductive material to carry current properly. Too few coats or insufficient drying between applications can leave excessive resistance, causing weak defrosting and concentrated heating at the repair. Surface preparation and careful masking also protect the surrounding grid.
searchTerms: rear window defroster line not heating

when.summary: When electrical testing confirms a break in a rear-window heater or antenna grid line.
notes: Appearance alone cannot establish whether a line still conducts electricity.

prepare.title: Confirm the break
prepare.detail: Have a voltmeter or 12V test lamp and the capability to diagnose the affected line. Residue can make a scraped-off conductor look intact.

prepare.title: Gather the repair materials
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner, 0000 steel wool, polypropylene film fine line tape and the Mopar Rear Window Defogger Repair Kit. Have the specified Motorcraft lacquer touch-up paint available if the brown layer is missing.

prepare.title: Prepare a safe working area
prepare.detail: Follow the linked health precautions, including disabling remote start, wearing eye and ear protection, and using gloves for sharp-edge handling. Consult the materials' safety information and keep solvents away from ignition sources.

steps.title: Warm and clean the repair area
steps.body: Bring the vehicle to at least 16°C (60.8°F). Clean the entire repair area with the specified glass cleaner and 0000 steel wool to remove dirt, wax, grease, oil and other contamination.

steps.title: Mark and mask the break
steps.body: Mark the break on the outside of the glass. On the repair side, place fine line tape immediately above and below the conductor, with the break centered. Extend the masking 26 mm beyond the affected area in both directions.

steps.title: Restore the brown layer only where needed
steps.body: If the brown layer remains intact, use only silver repair compound. If both layers are missing, apply lacquer touch-up paint across the break first, without overlapping the surviving silver conductor. Additional paint applications may be needed for a color match.

steps.title: Build the conductive bridge
steps.body: Apply silver repair compound in smooth, continuous strokes, overlapping sound conductor by at least 6.35 mm on each side. Apply a minimum of 6 applications. Allow at least 5 minutes between applications of either paint or silver coating.

steps.title: Remove the masking and excess coating
steps.body: Although the coating air-dries in approximately one minute, allow the repair to dry completely before removing the mask. Carefully remove excess compound above or below the line with a razor blade, avoiding the conductor itself.

steps.title: Check operation after drying
steps.body: Allow at least 5 minutes before energizing the repair, then test the system for normal operation. Optimum adhesion develops after approximately 24 hours.

watchFor.title: Damage from cleaning tools
watchFor.body: Do not use scrapers, sharp instruments or abrasive cleaners for routine interior glass cleaning. The specified repair preparation and controlled trimming require particular care around intact lines.

watchFor.title: A thin or rushed repair
watchFor.body: Poor defrosting or excessive localized heating can result from insufficient coating thickness or inadequate drying between coats.

notes: The finished repair initially looks bright silver. It will tarnish over time toward the gold or brown appearance of the surrounding grid.

diagnostics.finding: A line looks intact but feels smooth where it was scraped.
diagnostics.meaning: Visible residue may remain after the raised conductive material has been removed.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the electrical break with a voltmeter or 12V test lamp before coating.

verification.title: Confirm normal operation
verification.body: Check the repaired system after the permitted drying period and confirm the original concern is resolved.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the repaired line locations and the outcome of the normal-operation check.

procedures.purpose: Complete heater and antenna grid repair, including materials, masking, coating, drying and operation check.
General service, sharp-edge and chemical-handling precautions required before repair.

guides.title: Initialize the front door window motor
guides.summary: Teach the door-window motor its travel limits and lower soft stop, then verify the automatic functions fitted to the vehicle.
guides.introduction: The door-window regulator motor contains electronics that control automatic travel and the short drop used to clear the door weatherstrip. Initialization establishes the window’s travel limits and lower soft stop. It is needed when fitting a new door-window motor or restoring lost initialization. Convertible equipment needs care: it has no one-touch up or bounce-back feature, and its rear quarter-window motors do not require initialization.
guides.why: The motor must reach both ends of travel and complete the final cycle to establish the required positions. The door must remain closed. During initialization, the glass closes with high force and cannot detect an obstruction, so normal obstacle protection must not be relied upon.

when.summary: After door-window motor replacement or loss of initialization, including power interruption while the glass is moving.
notes: An existing motor must first be de-initialized; a new motor skips that operation.

prepare.title: Make the glass path safe
prepare.detail: Review the health and safety precautions in Section 100-00. Keep all objects and body parts clear of the glass throughout the procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange operating access
prepare.detail: Use the window control switch with the door closed and window power available. For an existing motor, arrange access to the battery cable or window motor fuse for the required interruption while the window is moving.

steps.title: De-initialize an existing motor
steps.body: For an existing motor, disconnect the battery cable or window motor fuse while the window is operating. Reconnect the cable or fuse before continuing. If a new motor has been installed, skip this step.

steps.title: Establish the upper travel limit
steps.body: With the door closed and window fully open, pull and hold the switch UP at its second detent. Continue holding until the glass has stalled against the top run for at least 2 seconds, then release the switch.

steps.title: Establish the lower travel limit
steps.body: Press and hold the switch DOWN at its second detent. Keep holding until the glass has stalled at the bottom of travel for at least 2 seconds. Reaching the bottom without the required hold does not complete this step.

steps.title: Set the lower soft stop
steps.body: Cycle the glass up and down once more. This additional cycle sets the soft stop for downward travel and completes the learning sequence before the operational checks.

watchFor.title: An open door
watchFor.body: The door-window motor will not initialize with the door open.

watchFor.title: An obstruction during learning
watchFor.body: Do not place an object or body part in the opening to test reversal during initialization; obstacle detection is unavailable.

notes: The second detent is the switch position used to request automatic window travel.
Short-drop operation is fitted to both coupe and convertible door windows.

diagnostics.finding: One-touch up and obstacle detection stopped after power was disconnected while a door window was moving.
diagnostics.meaning: That interruption disables these functions where fitted; it does not by itself establish motor failure.
diagnostics.next: Carry out the applicable initialization sequence and check operation.

diagnostics.finding: A convertible has no one-touch up or bounce-back response.
diagnostics.meaning: These features are not fitted to the convertible.
diagnostics.next: Assess only the functions fitted to that vehicle; do not use this absence to condemn the motor.

verification.title: Test the fitted automatic functions
verification.body: Check one-touch down on the door window and one-touch up where fitted. Convertible rear quarter windows are excluded from this initialization and one-touch test.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Note which door was initialized, whether the motor was new or existing, and whether each applicable one-touch function operated correctly.

procedures.purpose: Door-window motor de-initialization, travel-limit learning, soft-stop setting and operational verification.
Door-motor operation, effects of interrupted power and convertible feature exceptions.

applicability.equipment: Front power door windows; distinguish coupe functions from convertible equipment.

guides.title: Adjust convertible rear quarter window glass
guides.summary: Set the rear quarter glass height, spacing and inward or outward pitch so it meets the door glass and convertible-top seals correctly.
guides.introduction: The convertible rear quarter glass must meet both the front door glass and the roof seals. Its mounting bolts control height and fore/aft position, while the regulator assembly's jack screws control inward or outward pitch. Adjustment corrects this geometry without replacing the glass or regulator.
guides.why: A gap can look acceptable at one end while the glass is tilted at the other. Recorded measurements establish alignment; a separate roof-seal check establishes engagement. Both must remain correct after the fasteners are tightened.
searchTerms: uneven gap between door and quarter glass
rear quarter window clips door glass

when.summary: When measured glass spacing or height is outside specification, or the division-bar seal fails to engage correctly.
notes: The right-hand procedure is illustrated; the left-hand side is similar.

prepare.title: Measurement and fastening
prepare.detail: Have suitable millimetre measuring equipment, a way to record readings and torque tools for the glass, regulator and speaker-bracket fasteners.

prepare.title: Access
prepare.detail: Be prepared to remove the rear quarter speaker, its bracket and, if equipped, the radio transceiver module (RTM), following their linked procedures.

steps.title: Expose the adjustment area
steps.body: Open the door, lower the roof and raise all windows fully. Remove the RTM if equipped, then the speaker and access plug. Remove the bracket nuts and stud bolt, release the wiring retainers and move the harness aside before removing the bracket. Close the door for the dimensional checks.

steps.title: Record the starting geometry
steps.body: Measure the inter-glass gap at the rear edge of the door glass, 7.5 mm from the base of the outer belt moulding and 7.5 mm from the top of the door glass. Each gap must be 9.8 mm ± 1.5 mm, with a top-to-bottom difference within ± 1.0 mm. The quarter glass must be level with, or up to 1 mm higher than, the door glass.

steps.title: Correct height and fore/aft position
steps.body: Loosen the glass bolts only enough to permit movement. Adjust the glass and repeat the height and gap measurements. Once correct, tighten the glass bolts to 11 Nm without shifting the glass.

steps.title: Check engagement with the roof
steps.body: Close the roof, raise all windows fully and open the door. Check that the division-bar seal enters the roof seals completely and engages the door glass without clipping. This checks a different aspect of alignment from the measured gap.

steps.title: Adjust inward or outward pitch
steps.body: Lower the roof, close the door and raise all windows fully. Loosen the appropriate regulator assembly nuts and adjust the jack screws: two control pitch near the quarter panel, and one controls pitch at the roof. Repeat the roof-closed engagement check, then tighten the assembly nuts to 20 Nm without moving the glass.

steps.title: Repeat both checks and restore access components
steps.body: With the roof lowered, door closed and windows fully raised, repeat and record all height and gap measurements. Then close the roof, raise the windows and open the door to recheck seal engagement. Repeat the relevant adjustment until both checks pass. Refit removed components; speaker-bracket nuts tighten to 8 Nm and the stud bolt to 11 Nm.

watchFor.title: Movement during tightening
watchFor.body: Holding the correct position matters: tightening can disturb an otherwise satisfactory adjustment.

watchFor.title: Clipping at the division bar
watchFor.body: Correct measured spacing does not excuse incomplete roof-seal entry or contact that clips the door glass.

notes: Rear quarter window motors do not require initialization; they have no one-touch up or down function.

diagnostics.finding: Gap, height or top-to-bottom difference is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The quarter glass requires positional adjustment.
diagnostics.next: Use the glass-bolt adjustment and repeat the recorded measurements.

diagnostics.finding: The division-bar seal does not engage completely or clips the door glass.
diagnostics.meaning: Inward or outward pitch needs correction.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the regulator jack screws and repeat both alignment checks.

verification.title: Record the final result
verification.body: Retain the final upper gap, lower gap, their difference and relative glass height after tightening.

verification.title: Confirm seal engagement
verification.body: With the roof closed and windows fully raised, confirm complete division-bar seal entry and engagement without clipping.

procedures.purpose: Complete convertible rear quarter glass adjustment, including access, dimensional checks, pitch adjustment and final verification.
Remove and reinstall the radio transceiver module when equipped.
Remove and reinstall the rear quarter panel speaker for adjustment access.

guides.title: Replace a front door window control switch
guides.summary: Remove the switch and bezel together, separate the switch using the correct driver or passenger retention method, and restore its electrical connection.
guides.introduction: The door switch requests window movement; electronics in the window motor or door modules carry out that request. The driver’s master switch controls both front windows and, on convertibles, the rear quarter windows. The passenger switch controls its own door glass. This job changes the switch while retaining the bezel, unless the complete assembly is simply being removed and refitted.
guides.why: The bezel and switch have separate retention points. Removing the complete assembly first exposes the connector and the correct switch attachments without forcing the visible trim. Driver and passenger switches separate differently, and memory-seat equipment changes the electrical command path, so an unresponsive window does not by itself identify a failed switch.

when.summary: When a front window switch needs replacement or its switch-and-bezel assembly must be removed for access.
notes: Select the driver or passenger branch by function, rather than assuming the driver is always on the left.
Left-hand-drive illustrations also guide the similar right-hand-drive operation.

prepare.title: Identify the switch and equipment
prepare.detail: Confirm which door is being serviced and whether the vehicle has memory driver-seat equipment. With memory equipment, switch requests pass through door modules; without it, the switches provide low-current commands to the window motors.

prepare.title: Locate the retention points
prepare.detail: Use the illustrations in the switch procedure to identify the bezel clips and driver-switch retainers before applying force.

steps.title: Lift out the switch and bezel together
steps.body: Following the [switch removal procedure](#/document/G1695936), use the illustrated trim lever to release the bezel from the door trim and remove the switch-and-bezel assembly. The same overall method applies to both front doors.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body: Disconnect the switch connector once the assembly is accessible. This frees the assembly from the door wiring before any work on the switch-to-bezel attachment.

steps.title: Separate the switch only when replacing it
steps.body: For the driver switch, remove the retainers and lift the switch out of the bezel. For the passenger switch, release its retaining tab and remove the switch. If the existing assembly is only being removed for access, this separation is unnecessary.

steps.title: Install the switch and restore the bezel
steps.body: Reverse the appropriate branch: secure the replacement switch in the bezel with its retainers or tab, reconnect the electrical connector, and reinstall the assembly into the door trim. Check that the switch is retained before seating the bezel.

watchFor.title: Convertible feature differences
watchFor.body: Convertibles do not have one-touch up or bounce-back. Their absence must not be treated as evidence that the replacement switch has failed.

watchFor.title: Conditional initialization
watchFor.body: If the battery was disconnected while a door window was moving, one-touch up and obstacle detection can be disabled. Follow Power Door Window Initialization when that condition applies; switch replacement alone is not stated to require initialization.

notes: The short-drop movement that clears the door weatherstrip is controlled by window-motor electronics responding to the door-ajar signal.

diagnostics.finding: A window does not respond to the switch.
diagnostics.meaning: The missing response could involve the switch command path, door module where fitted, or window motor.
diagnostics.next: Establish the fault before treating switch replacement as the remedy.

diagnostics.finding: A window without memory-seat equipment ignores an unusually quick second-detent command.
diagnostics.meaning: The motor may not have received enough separation between signals to determine the requested direction.
diagnostics.next: Release and operate the switch again before concluding that it is defective.

verification.title: Check the applicable window functions
verification.body: With delayed accessory power active, confirm up and down commands from the serviced switch. Check equipped one-touch functions, respecting the convertible exceptions. At the master switch, check both front-window commands.

verification.title: Record the original complaint result
verification.body: Record which switch and window were affected and whether the same command now works. Note any remaining feature issue separately from the completed switch installation.

procedures.purpose: Both-door switch-and-bezel removal, driver/passenger switch separation and reverse-order installation.
Window command paths, normal operating behavior and the conditional initialization reference.

applicability.equipment: Trim-removal lever as illustrated, suitable tools for the driver-switch retainers, and a replacement switch matching the door and vehicle equipment.

guides.title: Replace and align the front door window glass on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Release the door glass from its clips, reinstall it, then complete body-style-specific adjustment and power window initialization.
guides.introduction: The front door glass is carried by the powered window mechanism and seats into the surrounding weatherstrip. On both coupe and convertible models, the short-drop function lowers it slightly when the door opens and raises it again when the door closes. Glass replacement therefore includes mechanical alignment and power window initialization as well as removal and refitting.
guides.why: The glass is retained by bolts and clips whose tangs must be released from the outboard side with a non-marring tool. Forcing the glass before those attachments release risks damage. Adjustment establishes its relationship to the seals, while the required initialization completes the power window setup after the repair.

when.summary: When front door glass requires replacement or removal, followed by adjustment and initialization.
notes: The procedure illustrates the left-hand door; the right-hand side is similar.

prepare.title: Plan the access and glass handling
prepare.detail: Follow the front door speaker removal procedure for access. Have the non-marring tool ready and maintain control of the glass as its attachments are released.

prepare.title: Prepare both finishing procedures
prepare.detail: Select coupe or convertible glass adjustment before starting. Also obtain Power Door Window Initialization through the reference in the glass procedure; it remains a required installation step.

steps.title: Remove the speaker
steps.body: Remove the front door speaker using the [linked speaker procedure](#/document/G1694049). Complete that access work before reaching the glass through the door openings.

steps.title: Remove the watershields
steps.body: Remove the lower watershield followed by the upper watershield, as illustrated. These covers must be restored during reassembly to re-establish the door’s internal water barriers.

steps.title: Position the glass fully up
steps.body: Remove the adhesive access covers, install the front door window control switch and raise the glass to its full-up position. Establish this position before releasing the glass fasteners.

steps.title: Release the glass attachments
steps.body: Remove the glass bolts. From the outboard side of the glass, use a non-marring trim tool to pry back the tang on each clip. Release the clip retention and remove the glass, keeping it controlled as the final attachment releases.

steps.title: Reinstall the glass and access parts
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure, ensuring the glass clips engage. Tighten the glass bolts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Restore the adhesive covers, watershields, speaker and other components disturbed during access.

steps.title: Adjust for the body style
steps.body: Carry out [coupe glass adjustment](#/document/G1697266) or [convertible glass adjustment](#/document/G1725016), as applicable. Use the correct procedure to establish the installed glass position.

steps.title: Initialize the door window
steps.body: Carry out Power Door Window Initialization using the reference within the [glass replacement procedure](#/document/G1695937). Do not substitute a guessed switch-hold sequence for that procedure.

watchFor.title: Prying against the glass
watchFor.body: Direct the non-marring tool at the retaining-clip tang from the specified outboard side.

watchFor.title: Incorrect feature expectations
watchFor.body: Convertible models do not have one-touch up or bounce-back. Their absence is not evidence that the glass repair failed.

notes: Body style determines the adjustment procedure. The short-drop function applies to both coupe and convertible.

diagnostics.finding: One-touch up and obstacle detection are disabled after the battery was disconnected while a suitably equipped door window was moving.
diagnostics.meaning: The window may require initialization; this condition alone does not identify damaged glass or a failed motor.
diagnostics.next: Complete the applicable power door window initialization and reassess operation.

diagnostics.finding: Glass does not clear or reseat into the weatherstrip during door operation.
diagnostics.meaning: Both body styles depend on short-drop movement and correct glass positioning.
diagnostics.next: Revisit the applicable adjustment and initialization procedures before considering the repair complete.

verification.title: Check seating and movement
verification.body: Confirm normal powered movement and that the glass lowers slightly as the door opens, then rises to seat when it closes. Assess one-touch features only where equipped.

verification.title: Record both finishing stages
verification.body: Record the body-style adjustment used, completion of door window initialization and the observed short-drop and closing results.

procedures.purpose: Front door glass removal and installation, including clip release and the required initialization reference.
Front door speaker removal and installation for access; the supplied reference describes the left-hand speaker.
Required front door glass adjustment for coupe models after installation.
Required front door glass adjustment for convertible models after installation.

applicability.equipment: Front door glass handling and regulator access; non-marring trim tool, torque tool, window control switch and access to the applicable glass-adjustment and initialization procedures.

guides.title: Replace a front door window regulator motor
guides.summary: Remove the regulator to replace its motor, then adjust the door glass and complete power-window initialization.
guides.introduction: The window regulator motor drives the mechanism that raises and lowers the door glass. Its integral electronics also control the short drop that clears the weatherstrip when the door opens, together with automatic window functions where fitted. Replacing this motor therefore involves both mechanical installation and restoring the glass position and electronic operation.
guides.why: The glass must clear the grooved weatherstrip during door opening and seat correctly after closing. Glass adjustment establishes its physical fit; initialization is a separate required operation. Skipping either can leave a newly installed motor with an unresolved window concern.

when.summary: When diagnosis has identified the front door window regulator motor as requiring replacement.
notes: A window that does not move is not, by itself, proof of a failed motor.
The left side is illustrated; the right side uses a similar procedure.

prepare.title: Plan the complete access work
prepare.detail: Have the front door regulator removal and installation procedure available. This motor procedure begins with the regulator removed.

prepare.title: Prepare for adjustment and initialization
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and the correct coupe or convertible glass-adjustment procedure ready, together with Power Door Window Initialization. These finishing operations are part of the repair.

steps.title: Remove the window regulator
steps.body: Follow [Front Door Window Regulator](#/document/G1695938) to remove the assembly. Complete its access and removal sequence before separating the motor.

steps.title: Separate the motor
steps.body: Remove the motor retainers shown in [Front Door Window Regulator Motor](#/document/G1695939), then lift the motor away as illustrated. The image identifies the motor attachments on the removed regulator.

steps.title: Install the replacement and refit the regulator
steps.body: Reverse the motor removal sequence, then reinstall the regulator using its complete procedure. Finish the mechanical assembly before moving on to glass adjustment.

steps.title: Adjust the door glass
steps.body: Carry out [Coupe Door Window Glass Adjustment](#/document/G1697266) or [Convertible Door Window Glass Adjustment](#/document/G1725016), according to body style. Correct positioning allows the glass to meet the weatherstrip properly.

steps.title: Initialize the front door window
steps.body: Carry out Power Door Window Initialization as referenced in the motor procedure. Follow that exact sequence rather than substituting an assumed switch routine. The exception for convertible rear quarter motors does not remove this front-door requirement.

watchFor.title: Glass does not clear or seat in the weatherstrip
watchFor.body: Recheck glass adjustment and short-drop operation before treating the replacement as complete.

watchFor.title: Expectations differ by body style
watchFor.body: Convertibles do not have one-touch up or bounce-back operation; do not use those features as convertible acceptance checks.

notes: Memory-seat equipment changes the command path through the driver and passenger door modules. It does not change the motor procedure's requirement for adjustment and initialization.

diagnostics.finding: The window does not respond to a switch.
diagnostics.meaning: The command path includes switches and, with memory-seat equipment, door modules.
diagnostics.next: Establish the motor fault before replacement; this removal procedure does not isolate an electrical failure.

diagnostics.finding: One-touch up was lost after battery disconnection during window movement.
diagnostics.meaning: That event disables one-touch up and obstacle detection where fitted.
diagnostics.next: Address initialization before assuming another motor is needed.

verification.title: Check movement and short drop
verification.body: Confirm raising and lowering from the applicable controls. Opening the door should lower the glass slightly; closing it should return the glass into the weatherstrip.

verification.title: Confirm the finishing operations
verification.body: Confirm that the correct body-style glass adjustment and front door window initialization were completed, and check the automatic functions fitted to the vehicle.

applicability.equipment: Coupe or convertible front door windows, with or without a memory driver seat.

guides.title: Replace the front door window regulator on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Remove the window glass and regulator, install the mechanism in its marked position, then adjust and initialize the door window.
guides.introduction: The regulator carries the door glass and converts the motor's movement into window travel. Its mounting position affects how the glass meets the weatherstrip. The motor also contains electronics for features such as the short drop when a door opens, so a regulator repair includes mechanical alignment and the required window initialization.
guides.why: Marking the mountings preserves a useful starting position, but it does not replace the final glass adjustment. Correct positioning lets the glass clear the weatherstrip when the door opens and seat again when it closes. Coupe and convertible adjustment procedures differ.

when.summary: When diagnosis confirms a regulator fault or the mechanism must be removed for door repairs.
notes: The left-hand side is illustrated; the right-hand procedure is similar.
Convertibles do not have one-touch up or bounce-back features.

prepare.title: Plan the glass work
prepare.detail: Have the front door glass removal procedure and the adjustment procedure for the actual body style available. This job requires removing and handling the glass before releasing the regulator.

prepare.title: Prepare to preserve alignment
prepare.detail: Provide a marker and suitable fastener tools, including controlled tightening capability. Have the regulator-motor procedure ready if installing a new regulator, and obtain the named Power Door Window Initialization procedure before dismantling.

steps.title: Remove the door glass
steps.body: Follow [Front Door Window Glass](#/document/G1695937) to remove the glass first. This separates the glass from the mechanism before the regulator mountings are released.

steps.title: Disconnect and mark the regulator
steps.body: Remove the adhesive tapes, disconnect the regulator electrical connector and move the wiring harness aside. Mark the nut positions before removing the nuts so the regulator can return to its previous mounting position.

steps.title: Rotate the mechanism out of the door
steps.body: Rotate the front half of the regulator rearward, then rotate its rear half forward and remove it. Follow the illustrated movement sequence to bring the mechanism through the door openings.

steps.title: Transfer the motor when installing a new regulator
steps.body: Motor removal is necessary only when installing a new component. Use [Front Door Window Regulator Motor](#/document/G1695939) for removal and subsequent installation instead of treating the motor and regulator as an inseparable assembly.

steps.title: Refit at the recorded positions
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure, aligning the regulator with the marks made before dismantling. Restore its fasteners, electrical connection, harness position and tapes, and reinstall the glass through its own procedure.

steps.title: Adjust and initialize the window
steps.body: Carry out [coupe glass adjustment](#/document/G1697266) or [convertible glass adjustment](#/document/G1725016), as applicable. Then perform Power Door Window Initialization. Mounting marks guide assembly; these final operations establish the finished window setup.

watchFor.title: Mounting positions lost during removal
watchFor.body: Mark before loosening the nuts. Once the mechanism moves, its previous position is no longer a reliable visual reference.

watchFor.title: Harness caught during extraction
watchFor.body: Keep the disconnected harness aside while rotating the regulator through the openings, then restore its original routing during installation.

notes: Short-drop operation is fitted to both body styles. The lack of initialization for convertible rear-quarter motors does not cancel the front door window procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The window does not respond to a switch command.
diagnostics.meaning: Operation also depends on the motor, control signals and, with memory seats, the door modules; this alone does not establish regulator failure.
diagnostics.next: Establish whether the fault is mechanical or in the control/motor system before replacing the regulator.

diagnostics.finding: A coupe loses one-touch up after battery disconnection while the window was moving.
diagnostics.meaning: One-touch up and obstacle detection can be disabled by that interruption.
diagnostics.next: Complete the required initialization before treating the lost feature as a mechanical defect.

verification.title: Check travel and weatherstrip seating
verification.body: Confirm the adjusted glass travels correctly and performs its short drop when the door opens, then returns into the weatherstrip when the door closes. Check one-touch operation only as fitted.

verification.title: Record the completed setup
verification.body: Record the body style, completed glass adjustment and initialization, and the final travel and short-drop results.

procedures.purpose: Complete front door regulator removal and installation, including extraction movements and final setup requirements.
Remove and reinstall the front door glass.
Remove and reinstall the motor when fitting a new regulator.
