verification.body: Record the headlamp optical-center-to-ground measurement used to establish the reference line.

procedures.purpose: Headlamp bulb removal and installation through the cover, electrical connector and spring retainers.
Headlamp assembly removal and installation, including bumper-cover access and mounting requirements.
Post-installation vertical aiming, including entry conditions, height-dependent reference lines and VOL/VOR branches.

guides.title: Remove and refit the convertible loadspace trim panels
guides.summary: Remove the upper, middle and lower loadspace trim in sequence, then refit it without trapping the roof flap or seatbelts.
guides.introduction: The convertible's loadspace trim covers the side area around the rear seating and roof opening. The upper panel meets a seatbelt guide and convertible flap, while the middle panel must clear the front and rear safety belts. Removal provides access behind the panels or allows trim replacement; correct refitting preserves belt access and the flap's position.
guides.why: These panels use clips, and the middle panel also has a rear locating tab. Their release sequence matters because simply pulling every panel outward does not follow all its attachments. During installation, trapped roof material or twisted belts can remain hidden behind trim that appears fitted.

when.summary: When convertible loadspace trim needs replacement or removal for access behind the panels.
notes: The illustrated right side is representative of the left; left-hand-drive and right-hand-drive operations are similar.

prepare.title: Arrange roof and seat access
prepare.detail: Fully open the convertible top and have the equipment required for rear seat backrest removal. Allow room to move the panels while keeping the safety belts clear.

prepare.title: Understand the attachments
prepare.detail: Review the upper-panel clip illustration and the middle-panel rear-tab release direction before pulling on the trim.

steps.title: Remove the rear backrest
steps.body: With the roof fully open, follow [Rear Seat Backrest — Convertible](#/document/G1709034) to remove the backrest and gain access to the loadspace trim.

steps.title: Release the upper and middle panels
steps.body: Following [Loadspace Trim Panel — Convertible](#/document/G1692610), move the seatbelt guide aside, release the clips and remove the upper panel. Release the middle-panel clips, then pull forward and outward to free its rear tab. Move the front and rear safety belts aside and remove the middle panel.

steps.title: Remove the remaining trim
steps.body: Release the scuff plate clips and remove that panel. Then release the clips holding the lower loadspace panel and remove it, completing the prescribed removal sequence.

steps.title: Refit with the flap and belts clear
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Before installing the upper panel, inspect the convertible flap and move it aside if necessary so it cannot become trapped underneath. Install the upper panel and restore the seatbelt guide. Refit the backrest through its linked procedure, ensuring belt webbing is untwisted and belts and buckles remain accessible.

watchFor.title: Middle-panel rear tab
watchFor.body: Release it with the specified forward-and-outward movement after releasing the clips.

watchFor.title: Concealed belts
watchFor.body: Keep both front and rear belts clear while positioning the middle panel.

notes: Upper-panel installation includes a specific flap inspection; reversing removal alone does not replace that check.

diagnostics.finding: The convertible flap lies beneath the upper panel.
diagnostics.meaning: The flap is caught in the trim installation.
diagnostics.next: Reposition the flap clear before completing upper-panel installation.

verification.title: Inspect flap and guide
verification.body: Confirm the convertible flap is not trapped and the seatbelt guide is back in position.

verification.title: Check occupant belt access
verification.body: Visually confirm untwisted webbing and accessible belts and buckles after all trim and the backrest are installed.

procedures.purpose: Convertible upper, middle, scuff plate and lower loadspace-trim removal and installation, including flap and belt positioning.
Convertible rear seat backrest removal for trim access and subsequent installation.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost high-pressure fuel pump
guides.summary: Replace the high-pressure fuel pump while inspecting its drive tappet and renewing the required seal, bolts and fuel tube.
guides.introduction: The high-pressure fuel pump raises fuel pressure for the engine's fuel system. A cam-driven tappet transfers mechanical movement into the pump. Replacement therefore involves both fuel connections and the pump's drive interface: tappet condition, cam-lobe position and controlled bolt tightening all matter to the installation.
guides.why: Fuel pressure must be released before opening the system, and residual pressure in the high-pressure tube needs separate containment. The pump must be installed with its drive lobe at bottom dead center. Required new parts and staged tightening are integral to the repair.

when.summary: When pump replacement is justified, or tappet wear requires inspection of the pump and its drive lobe.
notes: This mechanical replacement procedure does not establish a pump fault from an engine symptom.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped for high-pressure fuel work, battery isolation, controlled engine rotation and torque-angle tightening. Have shop towels, clean engine oil and the torque equipment needed for the flare nuts, including adapter-setting calculations.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement items
prepare.detail: Have a new high-pressure fuel tube, pump mounting bolts and pump O-ring seal. If a strut tower cross brace is fitted, its removed nuts must also be replaced.

steps.title: Release pressure and disconnect the battery
steps.body: Complete [Fuel System Pressure Release](#/document/G1671508), then disconnect both battery cables through [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Do not loosen fittings or plugs on the pump body; follow the specified hose and tube disconnections.

steps.title: Clear the pump access
steps.body: If a cross brace is fitted, detach the harness retainer, move the positive cable aside, and remove the brace, discarding its nuts. Remove the engine appearance cover, disconnect the pump connector and remove its noise insulator, spreading the openings to reduce damage. Disconnect the supply hose using [Quick Release Coupling](#/document/G1671510).

steps.title: Remove insulation and the high-pressure tube
steps.body: Detach the heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) connector retainer from the pump bracket. Remove the pump-drive and brake-vacuum-pump insulation and their retainers, including the harness retainer. Wrap the pump-end flare nut with a shop towel to absorb residual fuel during loosening. Remove the tube securing nut and bolt, disconnect the flare nuts, and discard the tube.

steps.title: Remove the pump and inspect its drive
steps.body: Remove the pump bracket. Alternately loosen the pump bolts one complete revolution at a time, then discard them and remove the pump. Discard its O-ring and remove the drive tappet. Inspect for flat spots or scoring; if present, inspect the pump and tappet drive lobe and replace components as necessary.

steps.title: Position and lubricate the drive
steps.body: Following [pump installation](#/document/G1689353), turn the crankshaft only clockwise to place the pump cam lobe at bottom dead center (BDC). Lubricate the tappet and drive-unit bore with clean engine oil. Align the tappet notch with the bore groove during installation, then fit and oil a new pump O-ring.

steps.title: Seat the pump evenly
steps.body: Install the pump with new bolts loosely fitted. Alternately tighten each bolt one complete revolution until seated, then apply the specified two-stage torque-and-angle sequence. Reinstall and tighten the pump bracket.

steps.title: Fit the new high-pressure tube
steps.body: Install the new tube with its flare nuts, bracket bolt and bracket nut finger-tight. Calculate the correct torque-wrench setting using the adapter formulas specified in [the pump procedure](#/document/G1689353). Apply its three-stage flare-nut tightening sequence, then tighten the bracket nut and bolt to their respective specifications.

steps.title: Restore insulation and connections
steps.body: Refit both drive-area insulators and their retainers, the harness retainer and HO2S connector retainer. Reconnect the supply hose through the coupling procedure. Refit the pump insulator, spreading its openings, then reconnect the pump connector and install the appearance cover. If fitted, install the cross brace with new nuts and restore the positive cable and harness retainer.

steps.title: Reconnect and pressurize
steps.body: Reconnect both battery cables through the battery procedure. Complete fuel-system pressurization using [Fuel System Pressure Release](#/document/G1671508); this is the final specified service operation.

watchFor.title: Incorrect installation position
watchFor.body: The pump drive lobe must be at BDC before pump installation. Do not turn the crankshaft counterclockwise.

watchFor.title: Reusing discarded items
watchFor.body: The removed tube, pump bolts, O-ring and any removed cross-brace nuts are not installation parts.

notes: Use the tightening stages and adapter calculations in the 2.3L pump procedure; bracket fasteners and flare nuts have separate requirements.

diagnostics.finding: The drive tappet has flat spots or scoring.
diagnostics.meaning: The pump and tappet drive lobe also require inspection.
diagnostics.next: Inspect both and install new components as necessary before reassembly.

verification.title: Record the inspection outcome
verification.body: Record the tappet findings and any resulting pump or drive-lobe replacement.

verification.title: Confirm completion
verification.body: Confirm required new parts, staged tightening, restored connections and insulation, battery reconnection and prescribed fuel-system pressurization.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost pump removal and installation, tappet inspection, cam positioning, mandatory replacement parts and staged tightening.
2.3L fuel-system pressure release before opening connections and pressurization after assembly.
Battery cable disconnection before pump work and reconnection after installation.
2.3L fuel-supply quick-release coupling disconnection and reconnection.

guides.title: Replace a rear suspension upper arm
guides.summary: Replace the rear upper arm with new attachment hardware, tighten it with the suspension loaded, and check rear camber.
guides.introduction: The rear upper arm connects the chassis to the wheel knuckle and works with the lower arm to locate the wheel as the suspension moves. Each rear wheel can respond independently to road irregularities. Replacing the upper arm disturbs these locating attachments, so the job includes controlled suspension support and a rear camber check.
guides.why: The bushings must be secured with the suspension loaded or the vehicle resting on its wheels. Tightening with the suspension hanging can produce incorrect clamp load and damage the bushings. Both attachment bolt-and-nut sets are discarded during removal, and their replacements must meet the specified quality and tightening requirements.

when.summary: When rear upper-arm replacement is required and loaded tightening plus a rear camber check can be completed.
notes: Have access to the Rear Camber Adjustment procedure in section 204-00 before beginning.

prepare.title: Provide controlled suspension support
prepare.detail: Have suitable vehicle lifting equipment, support for holding the suspension at curb height, and a torque wrench. Follow the wheel-and-tire procedure for access.

prepare.title: Obtain the required hardware
prepare.detail: Prepare a new upper-arm-to-knuckle bolt and nut and a new upper-arm-to-frame flag-bolt and nut. Use the same or equivalent quality and design, never a lesser substitute.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and support the suspension
steps.body: Follow [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) to remove the wheel. Support the suspension at curb height before disturbing the upper-arm attachments.

steps.title: Remove the upper arm
steps.body: Follow [Upper Arm removal](#/document/G1686656). Remove and discard the upper-arm-to-wheel-knuckle bolt and nut first. Then remove and discard the frame flag-bolt and nut and remove the arm.

steps.title: Install with new fasteners
steps.body: Reverse removal using new attachment hardware. Tighten the bushing fasteners only with the suspension loaded or vehicle weight on the wheels. The knuckle attachment requires 76 lb.ft (103 Nm); the frame attachment requires 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Keep these two specifications associated with their respective joints.

steps.title: Restore the wheel and check camber
steps.body: Complete wheel installation through its procedure. Check rear camber and adjust if necessary using Rear Camber Adjustment, section 204-00. This establishes whether wheel inclination needs correction after the arm has been replaced.

watchFor.title: Tightening at full droop
watchFor.body: Do not perform final bushing-fastener tightening with the suspension hanging unloaded.

watchFor.title: Old hardware returning to service
watchFor.body: Both removed bolt-and-nut sets must be discarded, including the frame flag-bolt.

notes: Curb-height support is a required working condition, not an instruction to estimate an arbitrary suspension position.

diagnostics.finding: Rear camber requires correction after installation.
diagnostics.meaning: Replacing the arm has not completed the wheel-alignment requirement.
diagnostics.next: Carry out the specified rear camber adjustment.

verification.title: Confirm attachment conditions
verification.body: Confirm new hardware was used and both attachments received their specified torque with the suspension loaded.

verification.title: Record the camber result
verification.body: Record the rear camber check and whether adjustment was necessary, including the final result if adjusted.

procedures.purpose: Rear upper-arm removal and installation, discarded hardware, loaded bushing tightening and required rear camber check.
Wheel-and-tire removal for rear upper-arm access and installation afterward.

guides.title: Replace a convertible top motor and initialize the roof
guides.summary: Access the roof motor through the rear speaker area, replace it, and complete the required closing and opening initialization.
guides.introduction: The convertible roof uses two electric motors with integrated control electronics. They share movement and position information so both sides work together. Replacing a motor therefore involves both mechanical access and a final initialization cycle. The rear quarter speakers, their brackets and the motor guards must be moved before the motors can be reached.
guides.why: A roof that will not move does not automatically have a failed motor. Roof movement depends on operating conditions and confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully lowered. Establishing the reason for the fault first avoids replacing a motor when an interlock is correctly preventing operation.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a convertible top motor that requires replacement.
notes: Confirm the roof operating conditions and window status before treating non-operation as a motor fault.

prepare.title: Plan access for the fitted audio system
prepare.detail: Use the rear quarter speaker procedure for SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3, as fitted. Speakers and speaker brackets are removed on both sides.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled reassembly
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools and a torque wrench covering the small bracket fasteners and motor attachments. Keep the different fasteners identified.

steps.title: Remove the rear quarter speakers
steps.body: Remove both speakers using the appropriate audio-system procedure. Begin the remaining access work with the [motor removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1708675), which distinguishes the shared operations from the extra work on the right.

steps.title: Move the right-side module assembly aside
steps.body: On the right side only, release the module wiring-harness clips from the speaker bracket. Remove the module bracket nut and bolt, then position the module and bracket assembly aside.

steps.title: Clear the speaker brackets and wiring
steps.body: On both sides, remove the speaker bracket stud, bracket nuts and bracket. Disconnect the indicated harness connectors and move the harness aside to expose the motor area.

steps.title: Remove the motor
steps.body: Remove the motor guard bracket retainers and position the guard aside. Remove the convertible top motor, following the appropriate side illustration. The motor mounting torque for installation is 106 lb.in (12 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the access components
steps.body: Reverse removal, restoring the motor guard, harness connections, speaker brackets, right-side module assembly and speakers. Use the individual fastener specifications in the procedure; these attachments have different tightening requirements.

steps.title: Initialize the motors
steps.body: Fully close and latch the convertible top, then release the latch and reopen it fully. Hold the roof switch throughout each movement. Remove any fitted tonneau covers before raising the roof and perform the cycle with the vehicle stationary and accessory operation available.

watchFor.title: Missing rear-window confirmation
watchFor.body: The roof remains inhibited if either rear quarter window fails to report its fully lowered position.

watchFor.title: An incomplete initialization cycle
watchFor.body: Partial roof movement does not complete the specified fully closed, latched and fully reopened sequence.

notes: Brief audio muting when the roof is latched or unlatched is normal.

diagnostics.finding: The display requests cover removal or reduced speed.
diagnostics.meaning: An operating condition is preventing roof movement; the message does not establish motor failure.
diagnostics.next: Correct the indicated condition before reassessing operation.

diagnostics.finding: The roof still does not operate with the required conditions satisfied.
diagnostics.meaning: Roof or body control modules can store diagnostic trouble codes even without a dedicated warning indicator.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the stored faults and window-status inputs before authorizing motor replacement.

verification.title: Record the initialization result
verification.body: Confirm and record that the roof reached fully closed and latched, then fully open after reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm access work is complete
verification.body: Check that disconnected harness connectors and clips, guards, brackets and both speakers have been restored.

procedures.purpose: Convertible top motor removal, installation and motor initialization.
Rear quarter speaker removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Rear quarter speaker removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC.
Explain roof synchronization, window interlocks and roof-status messages.

guides.title: Replace an SVT Performance Package front wheel knuckle
guides.summary: Remove and refit the front wheel knuckle with new specified fasteners, then check camber and calibrate dynamic suspension if fitted.
guides.introduction: The front wheel knuckle carries the wheel hub and connects it to the strut, lower suspension arms and steering tie rod. Its position helps establish wheel geometry while allowing the wheel to steer. This job separates those connections, so correct joint handling, replacement fasteners and final suspension setup are central to a successful repair.
guides.why: Hammering or using a separator fork can damage the knuckle, ball joints or protective seals. Suspension fasteners are critical parts and must match the specified quality and design. A dynamic-suspension height sensor also needs protection during disassembly and calibration afterward.
searchTerms: SVT Performance Package front wheel knuckle

when.summary: When a confirmed repair requires removal or replacement of the front wheel knuckle.
notes: Identify whether dynamic suspension is fitted before beginning.

prepare.title: Arrange suspension-service capability
prepare.detail: Use appropriate vehicle lifting and support, a tie rod end remover, lower-arm ball-joint separator 204-592 and suitable torque equipment. Have access to the brake disc shield and front camber procedures called up by the knuckle procedure.

prepare.title: Obtain the required new fasteners
prepare.detail: Prepare a new tie rod end nut, front and rear lower-arm outboard nuts, and both strut-to-knuckle bolts and nuts. Use the same or equivalent quality and design.

prepare.title: Plan the dynamic-suspension branch
prepare.detail: If fitted, a scan tool capable of running Ride Height Calibration is needed to finish the job.

steps.title: Isolate power and clear the hub area
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground cable using its procedure; the steering-service notice identifies a risk to the steering gear's internal power relay. Remove the SVT Performance Package front hub assembly and brake disc shield. Remove the wheel speed sensor bolt and position the sensor aside.

steps.title: Separate the steering connection
steps.body: Remove and discard the tie rod end nut. Use the tie rod end remover to separate the joint without striking the knuckle. Position the remover carefully so it does not damage the joint boot.

steps.title: Release the lower suspension arms
steps.body: If dynamic suspension is fitted, remove the height-sensor arm bracket bolt and move the bracket aside before disturbing the lower arms. Discard the front lower-arm outboard nut and separate its joint with tool 204-592, then repeat for the rear lower arm. Do not insert a pry tool or fork between a ball joint and knuckle; any pry-bar use is confined to the lower-arm body opening.

steps.title: Remove the knuckle
steps.body: Control the arms as they settle so their ball-joint seals are not damaged. Remove and discard both strut-to-knuckle bolts and nuts, then remove the knuckle.

steps.title: Rebuild the structural connections
steps.body: Position the knuckle and install new strut bolts and nuts. Reconnect the rear lower arm, followed by the front lower arm, using new outboard nuts. Tighten each connection to its specification in the [knuckle procedure](#/document/G1692539).

steps.title: Restore sensors, steering and hub components
steps.body: Refit the height-sensor arm bracket if equipped. Reconnect the tie rod with a new nut, reinstall the wheel speed sensor, then restore the brake disc shield and hub assembly. Reconnect the battery ground cable.

steps.title: Complete suspension setup
steps.body: Check front camber and adjust it if necessary using Front Camber Adjustment. For dynamic suspension, connect the scan tool and complete Ride Height Calibration following its directions.

watchFor.title: Seal damage during separation
watchFor.body: Care is needed both while applying the separator and while lowering the released arm into its resting position.

watchFor.title: Reused discarded hardware
watchFor.body: The specified nuts and strut fasteners must be replaced, even if they appear serviceable.

notes: The height-sensor disconnection and calibration requirements apply only when dynamic suspension is fitted.

verification.title: Verify mechanical completion
verification.body: Confirm all required new fasteners are installed and tightened, and that the sensor, shield and hub installation steps are complete.

verification.title: Record the setup results
verification.body: Record the front camber check and any adjustment. Where applicable, also record successful completion of Ride Height Calibration.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L SVT Performance Package front knuckle removal, installation, fastener requirements and final suspension setup.
Battery ground disconnection and reconnection for the steering and suspension repair.
SVT Performance Package front wheel bearing and hub removal and installation.

guides.title: Replace the convertible B-pillar and inner reinforcement
guides.summary: Replace the convertible B-pillar structure at its factory joints, then restore its welded connections, foam, sealing and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The B-pillar assembly and its inner reinforcement form part of the convertible's body structure and connect to the rear floor crossmember. Replacement is a structural body repair involving welded panels, not simply a trim or bolt-on panel change. The reinforcement is boron steel, and the repair must retain the factory-joint replacement approach.
guides.why: Correct body dimensions provide the reference for installing the replacement structure. Welding new parts into a distorted opening would preserve that distortion. The completed repair also needs its noise-control foam, seam sealing and corrosion protection restored; sound welds alone do not finish the job.

when.summary: When structural damage requires replacement of the convertible B-pillar assembly and reinforcement.
notes: Boron-steel reinforcement components cannot be sectioned; replacement must use factory joints.

prepare.title: Use a structural body-repair facility
prepare.detail: The work requires body measurement and restoration capability, resistance spotwelding, and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment.

prepare.title: Prepare removal and panel-fitting equipment
prepare.detail: Have an air body saw, spot-weld drill bit, 8 mm drill bit and locking pliers, together with the specified seam sealer and flexible foam repair material.

prepare.title: Plan the surrounding repairs
prepare.detail: Rear seat cushion and convertible quarter-panel removal are prerequisites. Include their reinstatement and the corrosion-prevention procedure in the repair plan.

steps.title: Establish the body dimensions
steps.body: Assess the structure against [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516). If required, restore the vehicle to its pre-accident dimensions before removing the pillar. Use the applicable convertible measurements where body-style-specific information is provided.

steps.title: Expose the repair area
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion and convertible quarter panel using their procedures. Position the carpeting and wiring harness away from the repair area so they are clear of the removal and joining work.

steps.title: Release the crossmember and remove the foam
steps.body: Remove the rear floor crossmember-to-B-pillar bolts. Remove the noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) foam at the pillar base using the specified air body saw operation. This does not authorize cutting a section from the boron reinforcement.

steps.title: Separate the factory-welded assemblies
steps.body: Drill out the spot welds and remove the B-pillar assembly. Then drill out the inner reinforcement's spot welds and remove the reinforcement. Preserve this sequence and the factory-joint boundaries in the [replacement procedure](#/document/G1687553).

steps.title: Prepare and weld the replacement structure
steps.body: Drill the specified 8 mm plug-welding holes in the replacement panel. Clamp and resistance-spot-weld the inner reinforcement first, followed by the B-pillar assembly. Complete the specified MIG welding of the B-pillar panel.

steps.title: Restore the foam and crossmember attachment
steps.body: Apply the specified expanding NVH foam. Reinstall the rear floor crossmember bolts and tighten them to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm), restoring the bolted connection after the welded structure is installed.

steps.title: Finish, seal and protect the repair
steps.body: Metal-finish the repair area. Seal all affected areas to production level with the specified seam sealer, then restore corrosion protection using [Corrosion Prevention](#/document/G1687508).

steps.title: Restore the surrounding components
steps.body: Reposition the carpeting and wiring harness. Reinstall the rear seat cushion and convertible quarter panel using their respective procedures.

watchFor.title: A proposed partial reinforcement repair
watchFor.body: Do not substitute a cut-and-splice section for factory-joint replacement of the boron reinforcement.

watchFor.title: Unfinished seams or exposed repaired metal
watchFor.body: Sealing and corrosion protection remain required after the metal finishing is complete.

notes: The illustrated left-side sequence applies similarly to the right side.

diagnostics.finding: The body is dimensionally displaced from its pre-accident condition.
diagnostics.meaning: The existing structure is not yet a suitable positioning reference for replacement parts.
diagnostics.next: Complete the required dimensional restoration before pillar replacement.

verification.title: Record dimensional restoration
verification.body: Document the applicable body measurements and any restoration performed against the Body and Frame references.

verification.title: Confirm every repair layer is restored
verification.body: Check completion of the specified welded joints, crossmember bolts, expanding foam, production-level seam sealing and corrosion protection before closing out the repair.

procedures.purpose: Convertible B-pillar and inner reinforcement removal and installation at factory joints.
Body construction information and applicable dimensional references for structural restoration.
Rear seat cushion removal and installation for access.
Convertible quarter-panel removal and installation surrounding the B-pillar repair.
Restore corrosion protection after welding and finishing.

guides.title: Replace knock sensors on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Follow the engine-specific access route, replace the knock sensors in their required positions, and restore all disturbed intake connections.
guides.introduction: Knock sensors detect engine vibration associated with abnormal combustion and provide an input to engine control. Their attachment to the engine matters because it couples that vibration into the sensor. The sensor replacement itself is brief, but access differs substantially: the 2.3L uses a lifted-vehicle access route, while the other listed engines require intake-manifold removal.
guides.why: Correct positioning and tightening preserve the intended sensor mounting. Manifold access adds separate fuel, electrical and sometimes cooling-system work. Cleanliness is especially important around exposed engine passages, where debris introduced during repair can cause engine damage.

when.summary: When diagnosis or an established engine repair requires knock sensor removal or replacement.
notes: Choose the procedure by engine before dismantling; the access operations are not interchangeable.

prepare.title: Match capability to the access route
prepare.detail: Prepare suitable torque equipment and vehicle-hoist capability where required. Manifold removal requires fuel-pressure release and battery isolation; the 3.7L also requires cooling-system draining, filling and bleeding.

prepare.title: Prepare for manifold reassembly
prepare.detail: Have new intake-manifold gaskets for the manifold being removed. Plan to keep exposed passages clean and to restore the electrical, fuel and hose connections using the full intake procedure.

steps.title: Use the 2.3L access sequence
steps.body: For the [2.3L](#/document/G1692146), remove the appearance-cover nuts and cover. With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist using the lifting procedure. Detach the knock-sensor connector retainers from the intake manifold and disconnect the connectors. Note component positions before removal.

steps.title: Prepare the 3.7L lower-intake access
steps.body: For the [3.7L](#/document/G1692252), disconnect the knock-sensor connector, then follow the lower-intake procedure. It requires hoisting in NEUTRAL, releasing fuel pressure, disconnecting the battery ground cable and draining coolant. Remove the upper intake and complete the specified fuel, thermostat, injector and coolant-connection work before lifting off the lower manifold. Discard its gaskets.

steps.title: Follow the appropriate V8 procedure
steps.body: For the [5.0L](#/document/G1692281), remove the intake manifold using its linked procedure. The [5.2L sensor procedure](#/document/G1991989) explicitly directs intake removal to that same 5.0L-titled article. Its access work includes fuel-pressure release, both battery cables, the brace if fitted, cowl and intake components, and connected hoses and wiring. Discard the removed manifold gaskets. Note sensor positions, then disconnect their connectors.

steps.title: Replace and secure the sensors
steps.body: Remove the sensor bolts and sensors using the selected engine procedure. Reinstall and tighten the sensor bolts to 177 lb.in (20 Nm), a specification given for each listed engine. On the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L, restore the component positions noted before removal.

steps.title: Reassemble the intake where removed
steps.body: Clean and inspect the sealing surfaces and install new gaskets. Reverse the relevant manifold-removal sequence, following its own tightening instructions. Both supplied manifold procedures allow the fuel rail to remain with the manifold assembly; rail removal is not automatically required.

steps.title: Restore connections and finish the access work
steps.body: Reconnect the sensor wiring and any detached retainers. Restore all engine-specific fuel, electrical, hose, cover and access components. On the 3.7L, complete cooling-system filling and bleeding. On the V8 intake route, restore the appearance-cover grommets to the manifold if they remained in the cover, and reinstall the brace if fitted.

watchFor.title: Misreading the 3.7L illustration
watchFor.body: Its cylinder heads are removed for clarity. Cylinder-head removal is not a knock-sensor access step.

watchFor.title: Contamination during manifold work
watchFor.body: Keep cleaning residue and other foreign material out of engine passages.

notes: Use the selected engine's intake procedure for its fastener sequence and specifications.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris is found in the intake manifold after upper-engine failure involving valve or piston damage.
diagnostics.meaning: The manifold can retain material capable of causing further engine damage.
diagnostics.next: For the supplied manifold procedures, install a new manifold when this conditional inspection finds metal debris.

verification.title: Confirm installation details
verification.body: Check sensor positioning, specified bolt tightening, connector engagement and restoration of disturbed intake components.

verification.title: Record the applicable completion work
verification.body: Record cooling-system refill and bleeding for the 3.7L. If a new intake manifold was installed, complete and record the road test required by the manifold procedure.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost knock-sensor removal and installation, including lifted access and retained component orientation.
3.7L Duratec knock-sensor removal and installation after lower-intake removal.
5.0L knock-sensor removal and installation beneath the intake manifold.
5.2L knock-sensor removal and installation, including its explicit intake-procedure cross-reference.
Vehicle lifting prerequisites for the applicable engine access routes.
3.7L lower-intake removal and refitting, including fuel isolation, coolant work and new gaskets.
5.0L intake removal and refitting, also explicitly referenced by the 5.2L sensor procedure.

guides.title: Remove and refit the coupe rear quarter trim panel
guides.summary: Release the surrounding trim, seatbelt guide and garment hook to remove the rear quarter panel trim and restore it correctly.
guides.introduction: The rear quarter trim finishes the interior beside the rear seating area. Removing it provides access behind the panel or allows a damaged panel to be replaced. The access sequence also involves the C-pillar trim and the seatbelt's upper D-ring guide, so the job includes more than releasing the visible panel clips.
guides.why: Several different attachments hold the surrounding parts: clips, a tether, cover tabs, a garment-hook retainer and the seatbelt guide bolt. Releasing them in order prevents an overlooked attachment from resisting removal. During refitting, correct belt routing matters as much as the appearance of the trim.

when.summary: When the rear quarter trim needs replacement or must be removed for access behind it.
notes: This sequence begins with the coupe loadspace-trim procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and belt-guide work
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools for the retainers and D-ring bolt, plus a torque wrench for reinstalling the seatbelt guide. Keep the covers and retainers identified for refitting.

prepare.title: Use the correct access sequence
prepare.detail: Review the loadspace-trim removal procedure before starting; that panel is removed before the C-pillar trim.

steps.title: Remove the surrounding upper trim
steps.body: Remove the [coupe loadspace trim](#/document/G1692601). Release the C-pillar trim clips, disconnect its tether clip and remove the C-pillar panel. The tether is a separate attachment and must be released before the panel is removed.

steps.title: Move the seatbelt guide aside
steps.body: Release the tabs and remove the D-ring retainer cover. Remove the D-ring bolt and position the seatbelt aside, keeping track of its routing for reassembly.

steps.title: Release the quarter trim
steps.body: Open the garment-hook retainer cover. Remove the retainer and garment hook, then release the rear quarter panel clips and remove the trim. Follow the [complete trim procedure](#/document/G1692603) for this attachment sequence.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Reinstall the quarter trim and garment hook, then restore the seatbelt guide. Tighten its bolt to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm) and refit the cover. Reconnect the C-pillar tether and clips, and restore the loadspace trim.

watchFor.title: Twisted or concealed belt webbing
watchFor.body: During installation, make sure the webbing is not twisted and that the belts and buckles remain accessible to occupants.

notes: The illustrated left-hand-drive, right-side sequence applies similarly to right-hand-drive vehicles and the opposite side.

verification.title: Check the trim attachments
verification.body: Confirm the clips, tether, garment hook and covers have all been restored.

verification.title: Check restraint access
verification.body: Confirm the D-ring bolt is tightened and the seatbelt webbing lies untwisted, with belts and buckles accessible from the seats.

procedures.purpose: Rear quarter trim removal and installation, including C-pillar trim, garment hook and seatbelt guide.
Coupe loadspace-trim removal and installation for initial access.

guides.title: Remove, replace and align the hood
guides.summary: Disconnect the hood attachments, remove it with an assistant, transfer components when replacing it, and check alignment after refitting.
guides.introduction: The hood provides opening access to the engine compartment and carries insulation, washer-hose attachments and, when fitted, a scoop. Its hinges establish its position while the hood-mounted striker engages the latch. Removal for access and replacement with a new hood share the main sequence, but component-transfer work is only needed for replacement.
guides.why: The hood is awkward to control once its hinge nuts are removed, so an assistant is required. Marking the hinge positions gives a useful starting reference for installation. Those marks do not replace the final alignment check, especially when a new panel has been installed.

when.summary: When the hood requires replacement or removal for access to other work.
notes: Scoop, striker and hood-pad removal are conditional operations for fitting a new component.

prepare.title: Arrange assistance
prepare.detail: Have an assistant available to control the hood during removal and refitting.

prepare.title: Prepare the fastener and alignment work
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools, a torque wrench and a way to index-mark the hinge locations. Keep the Hood Alignment procedure available for the final fit check.

steps.title: Disconnect the attached insulation and washer hose
steps.body: Remove the hood-insulation retainers and insulation. Detach the windshield washer hose retainers and couplings so the hose no longer connects the hood to the surrounding installation.

steps.title: Remove transfer components only when required
steps.body: When fitting a new hood, remove the scoop nuts, brackets and scoop if equipped. For a new hood on all vehicles, remove the striker-to-hood bolts and striker, then the retainers and hood pad assembly. These operations are unnecessary for simply removing and reinstalling the existing hood.

steps.title: Mark and remove the hood
steps.body: Index-mark the hinge locations before loosening their attachments. With the assistant controlling the panel, remove the hinge nuts and hood. Use the [hood procedure](#/document/G1693249) for the attachment locations.

steps.title: Install and restore the attachments
steps.body: Reverse removal, using the hinge marks as the initial positioning reference. Tighten the hood hinge nuts to 17 lb.ft (23 Nm). Where components were transferred, tighten the striker bolts to 106 lb.in (12 Nm) and scoop bracket nuts to 27 lb.in (3 Nm). Restore the pad, washer hose couplings and retainers, and insulation.

steps.title: Check the final panel position
steps.body: Check hood alignment and adjust it as necessary using [Hood Alignment](#/document/G1693220). Complete this step even when the original hinge marks appear to line up.

watchFor.title: A remaining washer-hose connection
watchFor.body: Confirm the couplings and retainers have been detached before attempting to move the hood away.

notes: The hinge operation is illustrated on the right side; the left side is similar.

diagnostics.finding: The hood does not align correctly after refitting.
diagnostics.meaning: The initial hinge position needs further adjustment.
diagnostics.next: Follow Hood Alignment to establish the final fit.

verification.title: Confirm restored attachments
verification.body: Check completion of the hinge fastening, washer-hose connections and insulation installation, plus any striker, scoop or pad transfers.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record that hood alignment was checked and whether adjustment was necessary.

procedures.purpose: Hood removal and installation, including replacement-only transfers and the optional scoop branch.
Check and correct hood alignment after installation.

guides.title: Remove and refit the cowl panel grille
guides.summary: Remove the windshield-base grille by releasing its fasteners, then restore the wiper arms to their correct parked positions.
guides.introduction: The cowl panel grille is the broad cover across the bottom of the windshield, beneath the wiper arms. This job removes the grille for replacement or access underneath it. The work involves both clipped body trim and wiper-arm installation, so correct reassembly includes restoring the blade positions.
guides.why: The grille must be released from its clips before it is lifted and pulled out. The wiper motor must also be parked before the arms are installed; otherwise, aligning the blades by appearance alone can leave their positions incorrect.

when.summary: When the cowl grille requires replacement or must be removed for access beneath the windshield.
notes: The illustrated procedure shows left-hand drive; right-hand drive is similar.

prepare.title: Wiper-arm tools
prepare.detail: Have a two-leg puller and a torque wrench available. The puller is specified for removing the arms from their pivots.

prepare.title: Fastener access
prepare.detail: Identify the battery-cover retainers and the grille retainers and clips in the removal procedure before attempting to move the panel.

steps.title: Remove the wiper arms
steps.body: Follow the [wiper pivot-arm removal procedure](#/document/G1694632). Remove the nut covers and nuts, then use the two-leg puller to remove the arms. This clears the components that sit over the grille.

steps.title: Release the cover and grille fasteners
steps.body: Remove the battery-cover retainers and lift away the cover. Next remove the grille retainers, then depress and remove its clips. Depressing the clips releases their locking action before the panel is moved.

steps.title: Lift out and refit the grille
steps.body: Following the [cowl procedure](#/document/G1693246), lift the grille upward first, then pull it out. Install the grille by reversing that sequence, restore its clips and retainers, and reinstall the battery cover and its retainers.

steps.title: Park the motor and install the arms
steps.body: Before installing the arms, turn the ignition ON and command one complete wiper cycle to establish the motor's PARK position. Install the arms with the blades inside the windshield marks. Tighten the arm nuts to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm), turn the ignition off, and install the nut covers.

watchFor.title: Resistance at a clip
watchFor.body: Check that the clips have been depressed and removed before continuing the upward-and-outward removal movement.

watchFor.title: Incorrect blade alignment
watchFor.body: Use both the motor's PARK position and the windshield marks when installing the arms.

notes: The wiper-arm illustrations omit the hood for clarity; hood removal is not a listed step.

verification.title: Restored attachments
verification.body: Confirm that the grille clips, grille retainers and battery-cover retainers have been reinstalled.

verification.title: Wiper installation
verification.body: Confirm that the parked blades are inside the windshield marks, the arm nuts are tightened, and the nut covers are fitted.

procedures.purpose: Complete cowl panel grille removal and reverse-order installation.
Prerequisite wiper-arm removal and final installation, including motor parking, blade alignment and nut tightening.

guides.title: Neutralize the powertrain and drivetrain mounts
guides.summary: Allow the installed powertrain and drivetrain mounts to settle through a prescribed vehicle movement before securing their fasteners.
guides.introduction: The mounts support the engine and drivetrain while accommodating movement between these assemblies and the vehicle. Neutralizing adjusts their installed position so they are not held twisted or strained. The mounts remain installed: their fasteners are loosened, the vehicle moves a short distance forward and backward, and the fasteners are tightened again.
guides.why: A mount can be damaged if the adjustment twists or strains it. The controlled movement provides the settling action, while the mount-specific fastening instructions determine how to loosen and secure the assembly correctly for the particular engine and drivetrain.

when.summary: When the repair being performed calls for neutralizing the installed powertrain or drivetrain mounts.
notes: This adjustment provides no stand-alone diagnosis of a failed mount.

prepare.title: Mount-specific instructions
prepare.detail: Have the correct loosening and tightening instructions for the fitted engine, drivetrain and mounts available before beginning. They govern any special fastening requirements.

prepare.title: Access and controlled movement
prepare.detail: Arrange the fastening tools and access required by those instructions, together with a clear area in which the vehicle can travel the prescribed distance in both directions.

steps.title: Loosen the specified mount fasteners
steps.body: Use the [neutralizing procedure](#/document/G1661756) together with the applicable mount instructions. Loosen the powertrain and drivetrain mount fasteners, but do not remove them. Retaining the fasteners is an explicit condition of this adjustment.

steps.title: Let the assemblies settle
steps.body: Start the vehicle and move forward 0.6–1.2 m. Then reverse the same distance. Throughout this movement, avoid twisting or straining the mounts; the purpose is to settle their installed position without damaging them.

steps.title: Secure the mounts
steps.body: Tighten the powertrain and drivetrain mount fasteners using the instructions for the actual mounts fitted. Complete the prescribed fastening before proceeding to the normal-operation test.

steps.title: Test normal operation
steps.body: Test the system for normal operation after tightening. Assess the result of the adjustment rather than assuming that completing the forward-and-reverse movement has resolved the reason for the work.

watchFor.title: Mount distortion
watchFor.body: Do not continue an adjustment that twists or strains a mount; the procedure specifically warns that this can cause damage.

watchFor.title: Unspecified fastening details
watchFor.body: The general neutralizing procedure supplies no universal mount torque. Use the engine- and mount-specific instructions.

verification.title: Fastening complete
verification.body: Confirm that every loosened mount fastener has been tightened according to its applicable procedure.

verification.title: Record the operating result
verification.body: Record whether normal operation was restored and whether the concern that prompted the adjustment remains.

procedures.purpose: General mount-neutralizing adjustment, including the movement sequence and requirement for mount-specific fastening instructions.

guides.title: Repair a detached heated rear-window terminal
guides.summary: Solder a replacement lead terminal onto sound rear-window bus-bar material and verify heated-glass operation after cooling.
guides.introduction: The heated rear window uses an electrical grid to warm the glass and improve rearward visibility. Its bus bar is the conductive strip that distributes current to the grid, and the lead terminal connects that strip to the wiring. This repair restores a detached terminal where enough sound conductive material remains for the replacement terminal's contact areas.
guides.why: Successful attachment depends on both clean conductive material and controlled heating. The replacement terminal's temperature-sensitive paint indicates when its pre-applied solder is ready. Keeping the terminal still through heating and cooling prevents it from shifting before the joint has set.
searchTerms: heated rear window wire tab repair

when.summary: When a rear-window lead terminal has detached and sound conductive bus-bar material remains for attachment.
notes: A rear window that does not heat needs diagnosis; that symptom alone does not establish a terminal fault.

prepare.title: Temperature and repair materials
prepare.detail: Bring the vehicle to at least 60.8 °F (16 °C). Use Back Glass Terminal Kit 4F1Z-14421-AA, a grey scuff pad of 600 to 1000 grit, and Motorcraft Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner ZC-23 meeting ESR-M14P5-A.

prepare.title: Controlled soldering capability
prepare.detail: Use an electric soldering gun rated at 100 watts or more, rosin-core solder for tinning its tip, and a regular lead pencil to hold the terminal. Have a way to follow the specified heating and cooling periods.

steps.title: Establish a sound attachment area
steps.body: Locate intact conductive material for the replacement type A terminal. The terminal normally covers the original location, but its contact feet must sit on good conductive material. Space or pillar trim may require positioning above or below the original tab.

steps.title: Clean the bus bar
steps.body: Clean the repair area with the specified grey scuff pad, then the specified glass cleaner. Remove dirt, wax, grease, oil and other contamination so the terminal can attach to the conductive base.

steps.title: Prepare and hold the terminal
steps.body: Follow the [terminal repair procedure](#/document/G1695934). Melt a small amount of rosin-core solder onto the gun tip to improve heat transfer. Position the terminal and hold it with the pencil at 90 degrees; an angled hold can let it slip when the solder melts.

steps.title: Heat until the indicator changes
steps.body: Place the gun tip on top of the terminal, away from its painted areas, and energize it. The terminal already carries solder, flux and temperature-sensitive paint. The paint should liquefy and change color in approximately 25–45 seconds. As soon as the color completely changes on either side, de-energize the gun.

steps.title: Hold the joint and allow it to cool
steps.body: Keep the terminal stationary with the gun and pencil for an additional 30 seconds. Remove both tools, then allow another 2 minutes of cooling before attaching the wiring lead.

steps.title: Reconnect and check heating
steps.body: Attach the electrical lead, turn on the heated rear window and verify operation. Make this check after the full cooling period so reconnecting the lead does not disturb the newly formed joint.

watchFor.title: Unsuitable heat source
watchFor.body: Do not use a flame torch or flame-heated soldering gun. These provide inadequate tip heating, and their exhaust heat can damage nearby plastic trim.

watchFor.title: Missing conductive coating
watchFor.body: Do not place a terminal foot on the original attachment area where conductive material is missing.

diagnostics.finding: No sound conductive base is available for the terminal feet.
diagnostics.meaning: The required attachment condition has not been met.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the bus-bar condition before attempting this terminal repair.

diagnostics.finding: Heating remains absent after reconnection.
diagnostics.meaning: The terminal repair has not established normal system operation. Defrost supply also depends on relay control and can end through timing, ignition state or low-voltage load management.
diagnostics.next: Continue rear-window-defrost diagnosis rather than assuming another terminal is needed.

verification.title: Record the heating result
verification.body: Record whether heated rear-window operation was restored after the specified cooling period and lead reconnection.

procedures.purpose: Complete terminal preparation, soldering, cooling, reconnection and operating check.
Rear-window-defrost relay operation and control conditions relevant to interpreting the final heating check.

guides.title: Repair paint contamination, etching and delamination
guides.summary: Choose environmental decontamination and controlled surface correction or manufacturing-damage refinishing according to the paint defect.
guides.introduction: Paint defects can involve contamination on the finish, etching into its surface, or failure of the coating itself. These conditions require different work. Environmental treatment removes contamination before polishing is considered; manufacturing-damage repair removes failed coating and rebuilds the finish, with clear coat applied across the affected panel.
guides.why: Iron particles left beneath new paint can produce rust spots again. Cleaning products must remain wet to avoid paint failure, and abrasive correction must stay within the permitted paint-film removal limit. Delamination requires complete removal of the failed coating.

when.summary: When environmental contamination, acid-rain etching or manufacturing-related paint delamination needs correction.
notes: Choose the repair branch according to the defect; refinishing is conditional on the condition of the finish.

prepare.title: Chemical and sanding precautions
prepare.detail: Review the [body repair precautions](#/document/G1693182) and chemical safety data. Wear the specified chemical protection; sanding or grinding requires eye protection with side shields and a dust mask.

prepare.title: Cleaning and finishing capability
prepare.detail: Provide cold-water rinsing, separate clean mitts for each product, Valugard Acid Neutralizer VG-A100G and Alkaline Neutralizer VG-B102G. Abrasive correction and refinishing require control of film removal and the product manufacturer's equipment, pads, speeds and application sequence.

steps.title: Environmental damage: rinse and prepare the first wash
steps.body: Follow the environmental branch of the [paint repair procedure](#/document/G1687576). Flush dust, dirt and foreign material away with cold water. Mix 8 parts water with 1 part acid neutralizer in a bucket.

steps.title: Apply and rinse the acid neutralizer
steps.body: Work quickly from the top toward the sides with a clean twisted lambs wool mitt. Keep the whole vehicle wet and lightly agitate for 5–7 minutes, making 4–5 circuits; severe conditions allow up to 8 minutes. Rinse the mitt frequently. Rinse the vehicle completely with cold water, then dry only horizontal surfaces, leaving the glass undried.

steps.title: Apply the alkaline neutralizer
steps.body: Use this product undiluted. Dispense it from a squirt bottle onto a separate clean closed-loop mitt. Do not apply it directly to plastic trim. Keep the treatment wet and lightly agitate for 5–7 minutes, or up to 8 minutes for severe conditions, then rinse completely with cold water.

steps.title: Shampoo and inspect for remaining particles
steps.body: Shampoo the entire exterior with car wash soap and a clean closed-loop mitt. Rinse with cold water and dry completely. Inspect for remaining ferrous metal particles and repeat the decontamination procedure as necessary before proceeding.

steps.title: Correct remaining surface damage
steps.body: Use one manufacturer's buffing products in its prescribed sequence: rubbing compound, then machine glaze. Acid-rain etching may also require color sanding. Clean corrected areas with a 1-to-1 alcohol-and-water mixture and verify scratch and swirl removal before final polish. Apply final polish by hand, with a dual-action sander and foam pad, or an orbital polisher with the appropriate bonnet. Wash and dry afterward.

steps.title: Manufacturing damage: remove failed coating
steps.body: For the manufacturing-damage branch, wash the repair area with pH-neutral soap and water, then remove trim, emblems and hardware. Sand or media blast the damaged surface, keeping the repair area as small as possible while removing all delamination.

steps.title: Prepare the exposed surface
steps.body: Treat bare metal to prevent flash corrosion. Prime and block sand as necessary before refinishing, then mask adjacent panels against overspray.

steps.title: Restore the coating and fittings
steps.body: Following the paint manufacturer's procedures, spot repair the base coat where needed and apply clear coat to the entire panel. Reinstall the trim, emblems and hardware removed from the repair area.

watchFor.title: Products drying on the finish
watchFor.body: Neither neutralizer may dry on the vehicle; drying can cause paint failure.

watchFor.title: Excessive abrasive correction
watchFor.body: Do not remove more than 0.3 mil of paint film through buffing, polishing or color sanding. Exceeding this limit requires refinishing.

notes: Never paint over iron particles. Complete the specified decontamination first.

diagnostics.finding: Acid-rain discoloration or etching remains after surface correction.
diagnostics.meaning: The damage may be beyond what the permitted correction can restore.
diagnostics.next: Proceed to refinishing when the correction procedure cannot restore the finish.

diagnostics.finding: Coating is delaminating.
diagnostics.meaning: The failed coating must be removed completely.
diagnostics.next: Use the manufacturing-damage preparation and refinishing branch.

verification.title: Environmental repair checks
verification.body: Verify that no ferrous particles remain and that scratches and swirls are removed before final polish.

verification.title: Refinishing completion
verification.body: Confirm that all delamination was removed, the panel received clear coat, and removed fittings were restored.

procedures.purpose: Both repair branches: environmental decontamination and finish correction, and manufacturing-damage preparation and refinishing.
Required body repair precautions, including chemical handling and sanding protection.

guides.title: Replace the convertible top front panel
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the roof's front panel while preserving shims, fabric attachments and weatherstrip positions, then set alignment with the top latched.
guides.introduction: The convertible top front panel carries the front attachments for the roof material, headliner and side weatherstrips and forms the roof's front latching area. Replacing it requires carefully releasing these layers, the tension cables and the riveted stay pads. Reassembly preserves their original positions and establishes panel-to-frame alignment before final tightening.
guides.why: Partially opening the roof gives the fabric and connected parts enough slack for service. Marks and retained shims preserve the original installation references. The panel-to-frame fasteners remain loose until the roof is closed and latched, allowing alignment to be established in that position.

when.summary: When the convertible top front panel needs replacement or removal for an identified repair.
notes: Service views show a closed roof, but the working position is approximately 25–50 percent open to provide slack.

prepare.title: Tools, materials and assistance
prepare.detail: Arrange an assistant, an electric drill, a rivet gun, stay-pad rivets, double-sided tape and tools capable of the specified fastener torques. Preserve shims and mark bracket positions during removal.

prepare.title: Roof operation
prepare.detail: Keep the vehicle stationary and ensure accessory delay is active for roof movement. Release the latch before opening and remove fitted tonneau covers before raising. Roof movement also depends on confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully lowered.

steps.title: Release the roof and remove the front trim
steps.body: Begin the [front-panel removal procedure](#/document/G1708671). Lower the latch handle and turn it clockwise to release the roof. Open the top approximately 25 percent and remove the handle. Remove the front trim retainers, release the clips beneath its rear edge and remove the trim.

steps.title: Free the headliner and side weatherstrips
steps.body: Remove the headliner push pins along the panel's rear edge. On both sides, detach the headliner tension brackets from the panel; they may remain attached to the headliner. Mark the side weatherstrip brackets at their retainers, note any shim positions, and remove both weatherstrip-and-bracket assemblies.

steps.title: Release and fold back the roof material
steps.body: Remove the material's rear push pins. Across the front, pull the material backward and downward off the panel clips, then release it from the double-sided tape on both sides. Roll it forward and upward over the panel, then fold it back to the first crossbow to expose the tension-cable ends and stay-pad rivets.

steps.title: Disconnect the remaining attachments and remove the panel
steps.body: Disconnect both tension cables. Drill out the stay-pad rivets and remove every rivet shaving from the vehicle and roof assembly. Slide each stay pad toward the panel's center to disengage it. With an assistant, remove the panel-to-frame retainers and the panel, keeping any shims in their original side positions.

steps.title: Install the panel loosely and restore the stay pads
steps.body: Follow the [installation phase](#/document/G1708671). With an assistant, position the panel and restore the frame shims as removed. Loosely install the frame retainers for later alignment. Slide each stay pad outward into position, install its rivets with the rivet gun, and reconnect both tension cables.

steps.title: Reattach the roof material
steps.body: Fold the material over the panel's front. Apply double-sided tape on both sides in the original positions. Roll the material downward and rearward while engaging it over the front clips, then install the push pins along the panel's rear edge.

steps.title: Restore weatherstrips and headliner
steps.body: Refit the side weatherstrip assemblies using the marks and recorded shim positions, and tighten their retainers to specification. Install the headliner tension brackets, aligning them with the headliner's rear push-pin positions before tightening. Reposition the headliner and install its push pins.

steps.title: Set alignment with the roof latched
steps.body: Close the roof and temporarily install the latch handle and retainer; the handle retainer need not yet be tightened. Pull the roof downward to position the latch, then turn the handle counterclockwise to secure it fully. With the roof latched, tighten the panel-to-frame bracket nuts on both sides to the specified torque.

steps.title: Finish the trim installation
steps.body: Turn the handle clockwise to release the roof and open it approximately 25 percent. Remove the handle, engage the front trim's rear clips, and install and tighten its front retainers. Reinstall the latch handle and tighten its retainer. Use the separate trim and handle torque specifications in the installation procedure.

watchFor.title: Lost installation references
watchFor.body: Weatherstrip bracket marks and shims preserve distinct mounting positions. Keep those references with their original sides.

watchFor.title: Roof refuses to move
watchFor.body: Latch, tonneau-cover and rear-window conditions can inhibit operation. Failure to move does not by itself identify a defective front panel.

notes: Perform the paired cable, stay-pad, weatherstrip and bracket operations on both sides, even where a procedure view shows only one side.

verification.title: Alignment sequence completed
verification.body: Confirm that the panel-to-frame nuts were tightened only after the roof was closed and fully latched.

verification.title: Attachments and cleanliness
verification.body: Confirm that shims, rivets, cables, fabric clips, push pins, weatherstrip brackets and trim have been restored, all specified fasteners tightened, and all rivet shavings removed.

procedures.purpose: Complete front-panel removal and installation, including fabric handling, riveting, shims, closed-roof alignment and individual fastener torques.
Roof operating conditions and window, latch and tonneau-cover interlocks relevant to positioning the top.

guides.title: Start an IDS session when vehicle communication fails
guides.summary: Use manual vehicle identification when IDS cannot establish its initial session, then follow network diagnosis if the powertrain control module remains unresponsive.
guides.introduction: The Integrated Diagnostic System (IDS) first tries to communicate with the powertrain control module (PCM). Once that connection is established, it attempts communication with the other vehicle modules. A failure at this first stage can prevent automatic session setup. This procedure supplies vehicle identification manually so the diagnostic process can continue.
guides.why: The message about missing PCM communication describes a failed connection, not a confirmed defective module. Manual identification separates the session-identification step from the remaining communication problem and provides a clear point at which to continue with network diagnosis.

when.summary: When IDS cannot establish a vehicle session and reports no communication with the powertrain control module.
notes: For push-button-start vehicles, use the Push Button Ignition Switch procedure in section 211-05 to establish the required ignition state.

prepare.title: Scan equipment and identification access
prepare.detail: Have IDS available and access to the PCM label or the vehicle's Detailed Vehicle Specification on the service-information screen. The diagnostic connector is beneath the instrument panel.

prepare.title: Service precautions
prepare.detail: Review the [general health and safety precautions](#/document/G1693189). Disable remote start before work around the vehicle and use the specified eye and ear protection. If accessing the PCM label requires work near cooling fans, follow the fan precautions before approaching them.

steps.title: Attempt the normal session
steps.body: Connect the diagnostic equipment and turn the ignition to RUN, following the applicable ignition-switch procedure. Begin the [IDS session procedure](#/document/G1693129) and allow its initial attempt to communicate with the PCM.

steps.title: Recognize the failed initial connection
steps.body: If a session cannot be established, IDS may report that no communication can be established with the PCM. Remember that the normal attempt to contact other modules follows successful PCM communication.

steps.title: Choose manual identification
steps.body: When IDS asks whether to retry communication, select NO. This moves the process toward entering the vehicle's identifying information manually.

steps.title: Enter a valid PCM identifier
steps.body: Enter a PCM part number, tear tag or calibration number to identify the vehicle and start a session. The PCM label carries its part number and four-character tear tag. If those cannot be found, double-click the vehicle identification number at the upper left of the PTS service-information screen and obtain the tear tag from Detailed Vehicle Specification.

steps.title: Follow the remaining communication fault
steps.body: If communication is still unavailable after manually entering the PCM part number, follow the [Communications Network diagnosis](#/document/G1813071) for a PCM that does not respond to the scan tool. Complete that diagnostic path before making a component-replacement decision.

watchFor.title: Session opening versus communication
watchFor.body: Entering identification and opening a session does not, by itself, demonstrate that PCM or other module communication has been restored.

diagnostics.finding: IDS cannot establish its initial PCM connection.
diagnostics.meaning: Automatic session setup has failed; the message alone does not identify the cause.
diagnostics.next: Select NO at the retry prompt and enter a supported vehicle identifier.

diagnostics.finding: The PCM remains unresponsive after manual identification.
diagnostics.meaning: The communication concern remains beyond the identification step.
diagnostics.next: Continue with the PCM-no-response path in Communications Network diagnosis.

verification.title: Check session and communication separately
verification.body: Confirm whether the vehicle session opens and whether PCM communication is actually available.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the identifier used, the session outcome and any remaining communication message so the next diagnostic phase starts from an established result.

procedures.purpose: IDS session recovery through manual PCM identification when automatic communication fails.
Required general service precautions before diagnostic work.
Follow-on network diagnosis when the PCM still does not respond after manual identification.

guides.title: Remove and refit the coupe loadspace trim panel
guides.summary: Remove the surrounding trim and rear seat cushion to release the coupe’s loadspace side panel, then restore its clips and safety-belt routing.
guides.introduction: The loadspace trim panel forms the finished interior surface beside the coupe’s rear seating and loadspace. Clips hold it against the body, while the surrounding trim and safety-belt guide affect how it comes away. This job removes the panel for replacement or access behind it, then restores the interior with the belts correctly positioned.
guides.why: The panel needs to be released in sequence because the scuff plate, seat cushion and belt guide are involved in gaining access. Pulling the panel before releasing these items can load its attachments unnecessarily. During refitting, belt routing deserves particular attention: a seated panel is not a finished repair if it leaves twisted webbing or inaccessible buckles.

when.summary: When the coupe’s loadspace side trim needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: The illustrated procedure shows a left-hand-drive vehicle and the right-hand panel; the opposite configurations are similar.

prepare.title: Plan the adjoining seat work
prepare.detail: Have the rear seat cushion removal and installation procedure available. Cushion removal is a required access step.

prepare.title: Identify the panel attachments
prepare.detail: Review the illustrated clip locations and belt-guide relationship before releasing the panel. The work requires controlled handling of clipped interior trim.

steps.title: Clear the doorway trim
steps.body: Following the [panel procedure](#/document/G1692601), position the door weatherstrip aside. Release the clips and remove the scuff plate trim panel to clear the adjoining trim.

steps.title: Open access beside the rear seat
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion using the [rear seat cushion procedure](#/document/G1692168). Then release the backrest latch and lower the backrest, following the stated access sequence.

steps.title: Release the loadspace panel
steps.body: Position the safety-belt guide aside, release the panel clips and remove the loadspace trim panel. Use the illustration to locate the attachments rather than treating the whole panel as a single pull-off piece.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Install the panel and return the belt guide, backrest, cushion, scuff plate and weatherstrip in the reverse sequence. As the trim goes back, make sure the belt webbing remains untwisted and the belts and buckles remain accessible to occupants.

watchFor.title: Belt webbing caught by the refitted trim
watchFor.body: Check belt routing while positioning the panel, before the surrounding parts conceal the area.

notes: Use the same overall sequence for the opposite side while following that side’s actual clip and belt-guide positions.

verification.title: Interior restored
verification.body: Confirm the panel and scuff plate clips are engaged, the weatherstrip is restored and the rear seat components are refitted.

verification.title: Belts ready for occupants
verification.body: Confirm the safety-belt webbing is not twisted and every affected belt and buckle is accessible.

procedures.purpose: Coupe loadspace trim panel removal and installation, including clip locations and belt-routing precautions.
Required rear seat cushion removal and subsequent installation.

guides.title: Replace and configure the body control module
guides.summary: Remove the body control module and complete the key programming, configuration and equipment-dependent initialization required for a replacement.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) receives switch, sensor and network information and controls functions including lighting, locks, wipers, battery-saving features and vehicle security. Replacing it changes both an electrical component and the vehicle’s stored configuration. The physical exchange is only one part of the repair; a new module also needs security setup and the applicable learning procedures.
guides.why: A disabled output does not automatically mean the BCM has failed. Its field-effect transistor (FET) protection can switch off an overloaded circuit to protect the module. Resolve the underlying circuit fault before deciding on replacement. Once replacement is justified, the programming sequence matters because normal ignition operation depends on programmed keys and a completed security parameter reset.

when.summary: When diagnosis confirms BCM replacement is required, or the module must be removed and refitted.
notes: The extended programming sequence applies to a new BCM.
Parking aid, video rear parking aid and electronic steering-column lock steps apply only when fitted.

prepare.title: Programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of programmable module installation (PMI), security parameter reset and the listed configuration functions. Have two keys available.

prepare.title: Diagnostic access and trim tools
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover. Preserve the scan-tool session; if needed, a session can be started using the powertrain control module (PCM) part number or tear tag number on the PCM.

steps.title: Begin the module transfer
steps.body: Start BCM PMI as directed in the [replacement procedure](#/document/G1694185). If the old BCM does not communicate, replacement may require As-Built configuration data. When replacing the BCM, also begin PMI for the integral parking aid module (PAM), if equipped.

steps.title: Remove the trim and module
steps.body: Release the right-hand scuff plate clips with the trim remover, then remove the lower right-hand cowl trim. Release the harness retainer and move the harness aside. Remove the retaining nut and BCM, and disconnect its electrical connectors.

steps.title: Install and maintain diagnostic communication
steps.body: Reverse removal, tightening the retaining nut to 71 lb.in (8 Nm). For a new BCM, continue the remaining steps: normal ignition operation is unavailable until two keys are programmed and the parameter reset is complete. The BCM still communicates with the scan tool with ignition off.

steps.title: Program the keys using the button sequence
steps.body: Do not use the scan tool for this particular key-programming step. Put the first key in the [backup starting location](#/document/G1694657), press START/STOP and wait approximately 6 seconds. Press START/STOP again and remove that key. Place the second key in the backup location and press START/STOP.

steps.title: Prepare and complete BCM programming
steps.body: Before running the BCM PMI installation, use the center display to ensure valet mode is off. A new BCM may arrive in factory mode; perform [factory mode deactivation](#/document/G1766370) if necessary. Complete BCM PMI following the scan-tool instructions.

steps.title: Complete security and system initialization
steps.body: Perform the [security parameter reset](#/document/G1672905), followed by Configuration Engine Immobilizer (CEI) configuration and the battery monitor sensor reset. If video rear parking aid is fitted, carry out its new-module initialization using the scan tool.

steps.title: Restore fitted equipment and preferences
steps.body: If fitted, perform BCM-to-electronic steering column lock (ESCL) configuration/training through the [security programming procedure](#/document/G1672905). Configure the [customer preference parameters](#/document/G1813073), then [train the tire-pressure sensors](#/document/G1686523).

steps.title: Test the BCM and finish parking-aid programming
steps.body: Carry out the BCM self-test, including an on-demand self-test, and repeat the self-test to confirm all diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) have cleared. If PAM is fitted, complete its PMI process afterward.

watchFor.title: Valet mode interrupts programming
watchFor.body: Leaving valet mode active before BCM PMI installation can cause the process to fail.

watchFor.title: Replacement without circuit repair
watchFor.body: An unresolved excessive-current fault can expose the replacement module to the same damaging condition.

notes: The BCM-B is a separate body module; this procedure concerns the BCM.
