Clearing FET-related codes does not reset the accumulated fault-event counter.

diagnostics.finding: A protected output shuts down with a short-circuit DTC, possibly accompanied by U1000:00.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM may be protecting an overloaded circuit rather than suffering an internal failure.
diagnostics.next: Correct the circuit fault. Where protection requires a service reset, run the on-demand self-test and clear codes once the test confirms the fault is corrected.

diagnostics.finding: U1000:00 and U3000:49 occur with the associated short-circuit DTC under the FET protection strategy.
diagnostics.meaning: The final fault-tolerance level has been reached; U3000:49 cannot be cleared.
diagnostics.next: Repair the circuit fault, then replace and configure the affected module.

verification.title: Configuration completed
verification.body: Confirm both keys, the parameter reset and every applicable initialization, preference and sensor-training operation are complete.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the initial and repeated BCM self-test results, including the on-demand test, and confirmation that all DTCs cleared. Record PAM PMI completion when applicable.

procedures.purpose: BCM removal, installation and complete replacement configuration sequence.
Explain BCM operation and distinguish recoverable FET output protection from a replacement-required fault state.
Locate the passive key backup starting position for the prescribed key-programming sequence.
Deactivate factory mode if present in the replacement BCM.
Perform the security parameter reset and conditional BCM-to-ESCL configuration/training.
Restore customer preference programmable parameters.
Train tire-pressure sensor locations after BCM replacement.

guides.title: Check driveshaft runout and balance on the 5.2L
guides.summary: Trace a road-speed-related driveline vibration through inspection, runout measurement and the appropriate driveshaft balancing method.
guides.introduction: The driveshaft carries rotation from the transmission toward the rear axle. A shaft that runs eccentrically or has an uneven mass distribution can produce a floorpan tremor or a rumble, hum or boom. Runout measures how far the rotating shaft departs from a true path; balancing corrects uneven mass distribution. These checks therefore answer different questions.
guides.why: Balancing comes after inspection and runout checks because added weight cannot correct a damaged shaft or an out-of-true mounting flange. Keeping the original tire pressures and vehicle load preserves the baseline complaint. Supporting the driveline near its normal curb-weight position also matters: changing its operating angle can change the condition being investigated.

when.summary: When a repeatable road-speed-related vibration requires driveshaft inspection, runout checking or balancing.
notes: Driveline vibration has a higher frequency and lower amplitude than high-speed shake.
The concern should relate to road speed rather than acceleration or deceleration; it may diminish while coasting in NEUTRAL.

prepare.title: Safe access and measurement
prepare.detail: Use the specified lifting points and a twin-post hoist or frame hoist with jackstands, keeping the shaft near its curb-weight angle. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Have holding fixture and dial indicator 100-002 (TOOL-4201-C).

prepare.title: Choose the balancing capability
prepare.detail: Instrumented balancing requires a Vehicle Communication and Measurement Module (VCMM), Vehicle Measurement System (VMS), accelerometer, reflective tape, photo-tachometer and suitable weights. The alternative method uses hose clamps. Obtain the applicable runout limits through the Specifications reference in the complete procedure.

steps.title: Establish the unchanged baseline
steps.body: Visually inspect the vehicle and reproduce the complaint on a road test before making adjustments. Do not change tire pressures or vehicle load. Note the road speed and character of the vibration for later comparisons.

steps.title: Inspect the shaft and joints
steps.body: Following the [lifting guidance](#/document/G1663631), inspect for damage, undercoating and incorrectly seated universal joints (U-joints). Rotate the shaft slowly by hand, feeling for joint binding or end play. Remove the shaft to inspect slip-yoke splines for galling, dirt, rust or incorrect lubrication. Clean it or replace U-joints as necessary; replace a damaged shaft. Road-test after corrections.

steps.title: Measure persistent vibration concerns
steps.body: Use the [runout procedure](#/document/G2214730) and dial indicator, turning the shaft through the axle. Measure front, center and rear; measure those locations on every section of a multiple-piece shaft. Excessive front or center runout requires shaft replacement. If only rear runout is excessive, mark its high point and continue with indexing.

steps.title: Separate shaft eccentricity from flange effects
steps.body: Mark the shaft-to-pinion-flange relationship, disconnect it, rotate it 180 degrees and reconnect. Recheck rear runout. If still excessive, mark the new high point and compare the marks using the decisions below. If runout becomes acceptable, road-test again. With acceptable shaft, flange and pinion runout but persistent vibration, proceed to balancing.

steps.title: Set up instrumented balancing
steps.body: For the VCMM/VMS method, mount an accelerometer near the transmission or differential end. Clean the shaft for reflective tape and position the photo-tachometer approximately 20 degrees from perpendicular to the tape surface. Keep the sensor fixed throughout testing. Run the first balance test with the shaft unmodified.

steps.title: Apply the correct test-weight branch
steps.body: For tapped pinion flanges, number the holes in the direction of rotation, starting with the top hole. Run the second test with the specified test-weight set screw in hole No. 1, remove it, then install the directed weight combination. For untapped flanges, use the shaft-size-appropriate test weight secured by a metal band near the tube-to-yoke weld. Mark its location and run the second test. Remove that weight and secure the recommended correction weight at the directed position using a metal band and epoxy. Results are referenced to the test-weight location.

steps.title: Verify the instrumented correction
steps.body: After either flange branch, run the third VCMM/VMS test to verify the repair. Keep the measurement setup unchanged so the result can be compared with the earlier tests.

steps.title: Use the hose-clamp method as an alternative
steps.body: Mark four approximately equal sectors near the shaft rear. Test one clamp head at each position at the complaint road speed, choosing the least vibration; equal adjacent results call for a position between them. If vibration persists, add a second clamp at that position. If there is no improvement, move the heads equal distances in opposite directions, initially separating them about 13 mm (1/2 in). Increase separation and retest until the best combination or acceptable vibration is reached. Tighten the clamps in their final positions; they remain installed.

watchFor.title: Restricted indexing positions
watchFor.body: Circular flanges permit quarter-turn positions, half-round flanges only two positions, and six-bolt constant-velocity joint flanges sixth-turn positions.

watchFor.title: Changing measurement conditions
watchFor.body: A moved photo-tachometer or changed test-weight reference undermines the comparison between balance runs.

notes: The full procedure gives test-weight selection details for each flange and shaft-size branch. Aftermarket test weights and clamps are permitted.

diagnostics.finding: The two rear runout high-point marks are within 25 mm (1 in) of each other.
diagnostics.meaning: The driveshaft itself is eccentric.
diagnostics.next: Install a new driveshaft.

diagnostics.finding: The high-point marks are on opposite sides, 180 degrees apart.
diagnostics.meaning: The slip yoke or pinion flange is responsible for the runout pattern.
diagnostics.next: Check pinion-flange runout. Excessive flange runout indicates a bent pinion. If flange and pinion runouts are acceptable, road-test and balance only if vibration persists.

verification.title: Repeat the complaint condition
verification.body: Recheck at the original road-test speed after corrections. Confirm instrumented repairs with the third balance test, or confirm the best hose-clamp result with the clamps securely tightened.

verification.title: Record the comparison
verification.body: Record runout at each measured location, indexing results, balance-test results or final clamp positions, and the vibration observed at the original road speed.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L driveshaft inspection, runout decisions, flange indexing, instrumented balancing and hose-clamp balancing.
Identify approved lifting points and safe vehicle support for underbody inspection and measurement.

guides.title: Disconnect and reconnect the battery on the 5.2L
guides.summary: Interrupt vehicle electrical power at the negative battery connection, then reconnect the disturbed cables and restore their covers.
guides.introduction: The maintenance-free battery supplies direct-current power and helps stabilize voltage in the vehicle’s negative-ground electrical system. Disconnecting its negative cable opens the normal electrical return path. This job provides that power interruption and restores the connection afterward; positive-cable removal is an additional branch when the work requires it.
guides.why: The important distinction is whether you need to interrupt vehicle power or disconnect both cables. Negative-cable disconnection alone provides the stated power interruption, so the positive terminal need not be disturbed for that purpose. Reconnection also affects learned operating behavior: the powertrain control module (PCM) may need driving time to relearn its adaptive strategy.

when.summary: When repair work requires battery power to be interrupted and subsequently restored.
notes: Disconnecting the positive cable is unnecessary when the purpose is only to interrupt vehicle electrical power.

prepare.title: Access and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have tools for the battery-cover retainers and terminal nuts, with torque control suitable for 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Identify which cable connections the intended work requires.

steps.title: Remove the battery cover
steps.body: Remove the retainers and lift away the battery cover as shown in the [disconnect and connect procedure](#/document/G1692356). This exposes the cable connections.

steps.title: Disconnect the negative cable
steps.body: Loosen the negative-terminal nut and position the negative cable aside so it remains disconnected. Together with cover removal, this completes the prescribed steps for interrupting vehicle electrical power.

steps.title: Disconnect the positive cable only if required
steps.body: If the work also requires positive-cable removal, position its protective cover aside, loosen the terminal nut and move the cable aside. Preserve the negative-first disconnection sequence.

steps.title: Reconnect in reverse order
steps.body: If both cables were removed, reconnect the positive cable and restore its cover before reconnecting the negative cable. If only the negative cable was removed, reconnect that connection. Tighten each disturbed terminal nut to 44 lb.in (5 Nm), then refit the battery cover and retainers.

watchFor.title: Adaptive behavior after reconnection
watchFor.body: Some abnormal driving symptoms can occur while adaptive values are relearned. Their appearance immediately after reconnection does not by itself establish a separate component failure.

notes: The cable system incorporates battery-current and generator-current sensors.

diagnostics.finding: Drive behavior changes after battery disconnection and reconnection.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM may still be relearning its adaptive strategy.
diagnostics.next: The vehicle may need to be driven to allow relearning; no fixed driving duration or distance is specified.

verification.title: Connections and covers restored
verification.body: Confirm every disturbed terminal nut is tightened to specification and the positive-terminal cover, if moved, and battery cover are back in place.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L battery power interruption, optional positive-cable disconnection and reverse-order reconnection.

guides.title: Replace the MT82 transmission support insulator
guides.summary: Support and strap the installed MT82 transmission while removing its support insulator, then refit the assembly with the specified bolt and nut torques.
guides.introduction: The transmission support insulator forms part of the mounting for the MT82 six-speed manual gearbox. It carries support loads while limiting direct vibration transfer into the vehicle structure. This repair exchanges the external support component while a transmission jack controls the gearbox during removal and refitting.
guides.why: Removing a support changes how the transmission is held. The transmission jack carries the assembly during the relevant stage, and the retaining strap secures it to the jack. The insulator’s bolts and nuts have different tightening specifications, so identifying the two fastener groups is part of completing the job correctly.

when.summary: When the MT82 support insulator requires replacement or removal during an established repair.
notes: Confirm the vehicle has the MT82 transmission before using this procedure.

prepare.title: Lifting and transmission support
prepare.detail: Provide a vehicle hoist, transmission jack and retaining strap. The work requires competence in lifting the vehicle and securing the transmission while its support is removed.

prepare.title: Fastener access and torque control
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the insulator nuts and bolts and a torque wrench capable of both installation settings. Keep the two fastener groups identifiable.

steps.title: Position the vehicle on the hoist
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist. Follow the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631), using the marked lifting points and checking that hoist adapters clear suspension components and mounting brackets.

steps.title: Remove the nuts and secure the gearbox
steps.body: Follow the [insulator procedure](#/document/G1687338): remove the transmission support insulator nuts, then support the transmission with the transmission jack. Secure the transmission to the jack with the retaining strap before removing the insulator bolts.

steps.title: Remove the insulator
steps.body: With the transmission supported and strapped, remove the support insulator bolts and the insulator. Maintain controlled support while the mounting component is absent.

steps.title: Install and tighten the support
steps.body: Install the insulator and its bolts, tightening the bolts to 76 lb.ft (103 Nm). Then install the insulator nuts and tighten them to 52 lb.ft (70 Nm). Complete both fastening stages before withdrawing temporary transmission support.

watchFor.title: Inadequate support
watchFor.body: The required transmission jack and retaining strap work together. Never get beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the vehicle’s emergency jack is unsuitable for this repair.

notes: Removal releases the nuts before the supported bolt-removal stage. Installation secures the bolts before the nuts.

verification.title: Both fastener groups completed
verification.body: Confirm the bolts received 76 lb.ft (103 Nm) and the nuts received 52 lb.ft (70 Nm), and that the installed support is secure before removing the jack and strap.

procedures.purpose: MT82 transmission support insulator removal and installation for the supplied 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
Approved lifting points, hoist positioning and vehicle-support precautions.

guides.title: Section and refinish a damaged outer body-side panel
guides.summary: Plan a permitted localized body-side repair, join the replacement section and restore the joint finish, sealing and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: Body-side sectioning replaces a damaged portion of the outer panel while retaining suitable surrounding material. The repair involves more than cutting and welding: the replacement panel determines what can be fitted, the joint construction supports the repair, and sealing and refinishing protect it from moisture. This is specialist collision-repair work with strict limits around structural anchoring areas.
guides.why: Choosing the smallest permitted repair area limits unnecessary removal, but attachment points take priority over convenience. Sectioning near door, belt or striker anchors can affect structural integrity. Horizontal joints also need deliberate sealing because water migrates toward them, making them particularly vulnerable to corrosion.

when.summary: When localized outer body-side damage can be repaired within the permitted sectioning areas.
notes: The left side is illustrated; the right side is similar.
Body-side replacement panels are supplied as two-part panels.

prepare.title: Have the replacement panel first
prepare.detail: Do not begin removing the vehicle body side until the replacement panel is available for reference. Use it when planning the smallest practical repair area.

prepare.title: Establish the prohibited areas
prepare.detail: Do not section at door-hinge, safety-belt or striker anchoring points. Welding within 50 mm (1.96 in) of door-hinge or striker locations may compromise collision integrity. Sectioning in the A-pillar door-hinge portion, B-pillar or quarter-panel dog leg is not approved.

prepare.title: Provide body-repair equipment and materials
prepare.detail: The procedure lists an air body saw, plasma cutter, spherical cutter and spot-weld drill bit, plus resistance spotwelding and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment. Have high-quality weld-through primer, fibre-based and conventional fillers, a specified seam sealer and a Ford-approved paint system.

steps.title: Plan the section against the replacement
steps.body: Use the [sectioning procedure](#/document/G1687519) to choose cut points that minimize the repair area while respecting every anchoring and sectioning exclusion. Remove only as much outer body-side material as necessary.

steps.title: Expose and release the damaged area
steps.body: Remove trim as necessary and drill out the spot welds in the damaged area. Use the appropriate listed cutting equipment to remove the planned section, keeping the actual replacement panel available as the reference.

steps.title: Prepare the joint
steps.body: Where possible, form a lap-joint backer plate from a portion of the old panel to strengthen the joint. Before welding overlapping surfaces or substrates, apply high-quality weld-through primer between them.

steps.title: Weld the replacement section
steps.body: Use resistance spotwelding wherever possible; the procedure identifies it as producing a higher-quality repair. Use the listed MIG/MAG equipment as required for the repair, maintaining the planned joint arrangement and prohibited-area boundaries.

steps.title: Finish and seal the joints
steps.body: Rough-finish sectioning joints with fibre-based body filler. Final-finish the sectioning joints and plug welds with conventional body filler. Properly seal every horizontal joint using a seam sealer listed in the procedure to prevent moisture intrusion.

steps.title: Refinish and restore the trim
steps.body: Refinish with a Ford-approved paint system following its manufacturer’s recommendations. Complete the applicable [corrosion-prevention work](#/document/G1687508), then reinstall the removed vehicle trim.

watchFor.title: A convenient cut through a prohibited area
watchFor.body: The aim of a small repair does not authorize sectioning through an anchoring point or an excluded pillar or dog-leg area. Revise the repair approach before cutting.

watchFor.title: Unsealed horizontal joints
watchFor.body: A finished-looking surface can still admit moisture if the underlying horizontal joint has not been properly sealed.

notes: Select the seam sealer from the products specified in the linked sectioning procedure.
Apply weld-through primer before joining overlapping surfaces, while those surfaces remain accessible.

verification.title: Joint finishing complete
verification.body: Confirm sectioning joints received the specified rough and final finishing, plug welds were final-finished and horizontal joints were properly sealed.

verification.title: Protection and interior restored
verification.body: Confirm refinishing and corrosion prevention are complete and all trim removed for access has been reinstalled.

procedures.purpose: Outer body-side sectioning limits, equipment, joint preparation, welding, filling, sealing and refinishing sequence.
Corrosion-prevention treatment associated with the completed body-panel repair.

guides.title: Replace the rear wheel bearing and hub
guides.summary: Replace the rear bearing-and-hub assembly using new mounting bolts and a new spindle nut tightened in the prescribed sequence.
guides.introduction: The rear hub carries the wheel, while its bearing lets the wheel rotate within the suspension knuckle. The halfshaft passes through the hub to transmit drive. This job removes the complete bearing-and-hub assembly after separating the halfshaft and removing the rear brake disc; it does not involve dismantling the bearing itself.
guides.why: The hub mounting bolts and spindle nut secure heavily loaded connections. Their replacement and tightening requirements are part of the repair, not optional finishing details. The spindle nut uses a staged tightening sequence that includes loosening, so simply tightening it to a single final torque would not reproduce the specified installation.

when.summary: When replacement of the rear bearing-and-hub assembly has been established as necessary.
notes: Use the rear brake-disc procedure appropriate to the fitted brakes, including the separate SVT Performance Package procedure where applicable.
The replacement procedure does not establish the cause of a wheel or suspension complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange wheel and brake access
prepare.detail: Be equipped to support the vehicle and complete the linked wheel-and-tire and rear brake-disc procedures before starting hub removal.

prepare.title: Have the specified remover and tightening equipment
prepare.detail: Use hub remover 205-D070 (D93P-1175-B) to press the halfshaft from the hub. Have torque and angle-measuring equipment suitable for the prescribed installation sequence.

prepare.title: Obtain replacement fasteners
prepare.detail: Have a new spindle nut and four new bearing-and-hub bolts ready. Suspension fasteners must be the same or equivalent quality and design.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and release the halfshaft
steps.body: Follow the wheel-and-tire procedure. Remove and discard the spindle nut, then use the specified remover to press the halfshaft from the hub. This separates the drive connection before the hub assembly is released.

steps.title: Remove the brake disc
steps.body: Follow the applicable rear brake-disc procedure. The standard rear disc and SVT Performance Package disc have separate instructions; complete the correct access procedure before reaching the hub mounting bolts.

steps.title: Remove the bearing-and-hub assembly
steps.body: Remove and discard all four mounting bolts, then remove the assembly from the knuckle. The illustration identifies these bolts behind the hub and marks them for disposal.

steps.title: Mount the replacement hub
steps.body: Position the bearing-and-hub assembly and install four new bolts. Tighten them in a cross pattern to 98 lb.ft (133 Nm), then reinstall the brake disc using its applicable procedure.

steps.title: Complete the drive connection and wheel installation
steps.body: Apply the brake to prevent halfshaft rotation and install a new spindle nut. Tighten to 184 lb.ft (250 Nm), loosen 90°, tighten to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm), then tighten a further 30°. Complete every stage in order, then reinstall the wheel and tire.

watchFor.title: Reused retaining hardware
watchFor.body: The removed spindle nut and all four hub bolts are discarded parts. Do not return them to service.

watchFor.title: Incomplete spindle-nut sequence
watchFor.body: The loosening stage is intentional. A torque-only installation omits part of the specified fastening process.

notes: Although the specified tool is named a front wheel hub remover, this rear-hub procedure expressly calls for it.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Check that the hub has four new mounting bolts, the correct brake-disc installation is complete, and the wheel-and-tire procedure has been completed.

verification.title: Record the critical tightening
verification.body: Record completion of the cross-pattern hub tightening and every stage of the new spindle-nut sequence.

procedures.purpose: Rear wheel bearing-and-hub removal and installation, including the specified remover, discarded fasteners and staged spindle-nut tightening.
Wheel-and-tire removal for access and installation after hub replacement.
Standard rear brake-disc removal and installation for the listed 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
Rear brake-disc removal and installation for the listed 5.2L application with SVT Performance Package.

guides.title: Replace and calibrate the vehicle dynamics control module
guides.summary: Remove the vehicle dynamics control module through the load-space trim, program a new module and complete ride-height calibration.
guides.introduction: The vehicle dynamics control module (VDM) controls the firmness of the adaptive suspension dampers. It combines suspension-height measurements with information about braking, steering and vehicle movement, then varies electrical current to each damper. That current changes a magnetic field inside the damper, restricting fluid flow to adjust damping. Replacement therefore involves both fitting the module and preparing its electronic control system for the vehicle.
guides.why: A new module needs the correct vehicle information, and calibration teaches the system its reference suspension position. These are different tasks. Calibration with the suspension hanging, freshly lowered or carrying passengers or cargo can establish an unsuitable reference. Static electrical discharge can also damage the module during handling.

when.summary: When VDM replacement is justified by diagnosis, or the module must be removed and refitted.
notes: Calibration is required after VDM removal or disconnection as well as replacement.
A firm ride or suspension message does not, by itself, identify a failed VDM.

prepare.title: Provide electronic service capability
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of new-module programming and the Ride Height Calibration routine. Follow its instructions for both operations.

prepare.title: Protect the module
prepare.detail: Use handling precautions that prevent static electrical charges from reaching the module.

prepare.title: Plan access and calibration conditions
prepare.detail: Access is through the load-space floor, rear trim and right-hand side trim. Arrange a level calibration location and a short drive to settle the suspension beforehand.

steps.title: Expose the module
steps.body: Remove the load-space floor panel and rear trim panel, then position the right-hand load-space trim aside. This provides access to the electrical connector and module retainers.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the VDM
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector, remove the retainers and remove the module. Maintain static-discharge precautions while handling the exposed unit.

steps.title: Install the module and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Secure the VDM retainers to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm), reconnect the electrical connector and restore the displaced and removed load-space panels.

steps.title: Program a new module
steps.body: When fitting a new VDM, use the diagnostic scan tool to program the correct vehicle information. Follow all tool directions; ride-height calibration does not replace this configuration step.

steps.title: Settle the suspension
steps.body: Before calibration, neutralize the suspension by driving a short distance, such as around a parking lot. Do not calibrate with the vehicle raised or immediately after lowering it.

steps.title: Carry out ride-height calibration
steps.body: Place the vehicle stationary on a level surface with no passengers or cargo. Connect the scan tool and run Ride Height Calibration, following its directions through completion.

watchFor.title: Incorrect calibration conditions
watchFor.body: Suspension position must be neutral before the system learns its reference. Lifting history, vehicle movement or an added load can interfere with that condition.

watchFor.title: Skipped programming
watchFor.body: A physically installed new module still requires the correct vehicle information for proper suspension operation.

notes: The VDM also monitors height-sensor and damper-coil circuits during its initial electrical check when the ignition is switched on.

diagnostics.finding: A suspension message appears and the ride becomes firm.
diagnostics.meaning: A detected system fault may cause the VDM to deactivate dynamic suspension. Sensors, damper coils and their circuits are among the monitored parts; this response does not prove a module defect.
diagnostics.next: Use the diagnostic trouble codes and appropriate system diagnosis to establish the repair before replacing the VDM.

verification.title: Confirm electronic completion
verification.body: Record successful new-module programming when applicable and the scan tool's completed Ride Height Calibration result.

verification.title: Confirm physical completion
verification.body: Check that the connector is reconnected, module retainers are tightened and the load-space trim and floor panel are restored.

procedures.purpose: VDM access, removal, installation, retainer tightening and required Ride Height Calibration.
Dynamic-suspension operation, new-VDM programming requirements and the conditions required for valid ride-height calibration.

guides.title: Replace the A/C receiver drier using the correct engine access route
guides.summary: Replace the receiver drier through the engine-specific access route, then restore the refrigerant system's oil balance, vacuum and charge.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning (A/C) receiver drier helps manage liquid refrigerant and moisture within the refrigerant circuit. Replacing it opens that circuit, so removing the small component is only part of the job. Refrigerant must first be identified and recovered, and the completed system must be evacuated and charged. Access differs significantly: the 2.3L requires condenser removal, while the other listed engines use underbody access.
guides.why: Contamination can enter through an open connection, and contaminated refrigerant can spoil recovery equipment's stored supply. Oil removed during recovery also needs to be accounted for. Correct access, sealing and refrigerant servicing are therefore as important as securing the replacement drier.

when.summary: When receiver-drier replacement has been established as part of a refrigerant-system repair.
notes: Select the procedure by engine before dismantling; the access and seal instructions are not identical.
These replacement procedures do not diagnose poor cooling.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant-service capability
prepare.detail: Use refrigerant identification equipment and the Ford-approved R134A management equipment specified in the recovery procedure, following equipment instructions.

prepare.title: Prepare lifting and service materials
prepare.detail: Provide hoist access using the lifting procedure, with the transmission in NEUTRAL. Obtain the applicable charge, oil and seal-lubrication specifications before opening the system.

prepare.title: Plan the required seals
prepare.detail: The 2.3L condenser procedure and the 5.2L drier procedure require new O-ring seals lubricated only with the specified material. Protect exposed openings against contamination.

steps.title: Identify and recover the refrigerant
steps.body: Check purity before recovery. Connect to both high- and low-side service ports; low-side-only recovery is prohibited. Record any oil recovered. After recovery, confirm the vacuum remains stable for about 2 minutes, repeating the recovery sequence if it does not.

steps.title: Follow the correct access branch
steps.body: For the 2.3L, follow the condenser procedure: remove the required shields and intake components, disconnect and cover refrigerant ports, reposition the degas bottle and cooling assembly, then release the condenser. For the 3.7L and 5.0L, remove the underbody shield bolts and retainers. For the 5.2L, complete both specified underbody-shield removal operations.

steps.title: Remove the receiver drier
steps.body: Remove the air deflector, then the drier attachment bolts, retainer and drier. On the 2.3L this follows condenser removal. Keep the engine-specific illustrations and instructions with the work so access details are not transferred between variants.

steps.title: Install and close the system
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal sequence. The drier attachment bolts are tightened to 80 lb.in (9 Nm) in all four procedures. Fit the required new O-rings for the 2.3L condenser connections and 5.2L drier, using the specified lubricant. Remove temporary port protection when reconnecting.

steps.title: Restore the correct oil quantity
steps.body: Follow Refrigerant Oil Adding for the correct amount of clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) oil. Account for the oil recovered, which must be replaced, alongside the applicable component-replacement requirements. Do not guess an oil quantity or transfer one between engines.

steps.title: Evacuate and charge
steps.body: Evacuate to at least 99.4 kPa (29.5 in-Hg) of vacuum, as close to 101.1 kPa (30 in-Hg) as possible, and continue pumping for at least 45 minutes. Stop the pump and observe vacuum retention for 10 minutes. Set the correct refrigerant charge amount and charge according to the service-unit instructions.

watchFor.title: Contaminated refrigerant
watchFor.body: Do not recover it into the normal bulk supply. Follow the contamination route, including dedicated contaminated-refrigerant recovery equipment and the specified disposal requirements.

watchFor.title: Misread access illustration
watchFor.body: The 2.3L condenser illustration notes that the bumper is removed for clarity; that note is not an instruction to remove it.

notes: The selected drier illustration shows the 2.3L arrangement.
The 3.7L and 5.0L underbody-shield fasteners have their own installation setting; do not use the drier-bolt setting for them.

diagnostics.finding: Vacuum is lost during the post-recovery observation.
diagnostics.meaning: The recovery procedure has not reached its required stable-vacuum condition.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the prescribed recovery sequence until vacuum remains stable for 2 minutes.

verification.title: Confirm evacuation completion
verification.body: Verify the specified evacuation and vacuum-hold stages before completing charging.

verification.title: Record the service result
verification.body: Record recovered oil, oil added, the vacuum-hold result and the refrigerant charge used for the vehicle.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost receiver-drier removal and installation after condenser removal.
3.7L Duratec receiver-drier removal through underbody access, installation and oil-restoration requirement.
5.0L receiver-drier removal through underbody access, installation and oil-restoration requirement.
5.2L receiver-drier replacement, including shield access, contamination protection, new O-rings and oil restoration.
Required 2.3L condenser removal and installation, including access components and new connection seals.
Refrigerant identification, recovery, evacuation, vacuum observation and charging.
Vehicle lifting requirements for hoist access.
Determine and add the appropriate refrigerant-system oil quantity.

guides.title: Replace the door lock control switch
guides.summary: Remove the front door trim panel, release the lock switch's retaining clips and restore the panel's electrical and latch connections.
guides.introduction: The door lock control switch lets an occupant request powered locking or unlocking. It is one of several ways to request that action: passive entry and the remote keyless entry transmitter can also operate the locks. This job changes the switch in the door trim, rather than the door latch. Most of the work lies in removing and reinstalling the trim panel carefully.
guides.why: The panel is secured by bolts, retainers and clips, then remains connected by wiring where fitted and the latch cable. Following the release sequence gives access to the switch without treating the panel as a loose cover. The switch itself is clip-retained, so its clips must be released before removal.

when.summary: When the door lock control switch has been identified for replacement.
notes: An unanswered lock request alone does not establish that the switch is defective.
The switch procedure shows left-hand drive and the left side; right-hand drive and the opposite side are similar.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim removal
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the panel fasteners and the ability to release trim retainers and switch clips carefully.

prepare.title: Include the window-switch prerequisite
prepare.detail: Follow the front door trim procedure, including its front door window-control-switch removal requirement.

steps.title: Remove the panel fasteners
steps.body: Remove the cover and upper trim-panel bolt, the front door window control switch, the center bolt and the lower retainers in the trim procedure's order.

steps.title: Release and lift off the trim
steps.body: Release the clips and pin-type retainers progressively at the rear upper, rear/lower and front portions. Lift the panel up and out, disconnect electrical connectors where equipped, and release the latch cable.

steps.title: Exchange the lock switch
steps.body: With the panel removed, release the door lock control switch's retaining clips and remove the switch. Install the replacement by reversing those actions so the clips retain it in the panel.

steps.title: Restore the door trim
steps.body: Transfer panel parts as necessary and reverse the trim-removal sequence, reconnecting the latch cable and fitted electrical connectors. Observe the separate tightening specifications for the upper and center bolts and the lower retainers.

watchFor.title: Connections still attached
watchFor.body: Do not pull the released panel away while its latch cable or fitted electrical connectors remain attached.

watchFor.title: Unreleased switch clips
watchFor.body: Release the retaining clips before withdrawing the switch; pulling against them can damage its mounting.

notes: The illustration shows panel removal and its connections; use the switch procedure for the switch's clip-release step.

verification.title: Confirm switch retention
verification.body: Check that the replacement switch is held by its retaining clips.

verification.title: Confirm panel reassembly
verification.body: Verify the latch cable and applicable connectors are reattached and the trim clips, retainers and fasteners are restored.

procedures.purpose: Door lock control switch clip release, removal and installation, with side and steering-position applicability notes.
Required front door trim removal and installation, including fasteners, retainers, electrical connections and latch cable.

guides.title: Replace the passenger-side temperature door actuator
guides.summary: Unload the temperature door where possible, disconnect and replace its passenger-side actuator, then restore its mounting and electrical connection.
guides.introduction: The temperature door actuator moves a door in the heating and air-conditioning unit to regulate delivered air temperature. This job replaces the passenger-side actuator and reconnects its electrical supply. On vehicles with Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC), the passenger can select a temperature independently of the driver. The repair concerns temperature-door movement; blower speed and air-distribution selections are separate functions.
guides.why: The procedure recommends placing the temperature door at its mid-position, if possible, before removing the actuator. This unloads tension on the door and makes actuator replacement easier. Treat that as a helpful preparation condition: an actuator that cannot move may prevent it, and the instruction does not make mid-position an absolute prerequisite.
searchTerms: passenger side temperature door actuator replacement

when.summary: When the passenger-side temperature door actuator has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: A temperature complaint alone does not establish an actuator failure.
Identify the fitted temperature-control arrangement; independent passenger temperature selection applies to DATC.

prepare.title: Identify the actuator and its attachments
prepare.detail: Use the component illustration to identify the passenger-side actuator, electrical connector and retainers. Have tools suited to the actual retainers and access to the unit.

prepare.title: Reduce door tension where possible
prepare.detail: Arrange the temperature door in its mid-position before disconnecting the actuator, if its condition allows.

steps.title: Prepare the door position
steps.body: If possible, place the temperature door at mid-position. This reduces the tension acting through the actuator connection during removal.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body: Disconnect the passenger-side temperature door actuator connector before removing its mounting retainers.

steps.title: Remove the actuator
steps.body: Remove the retainers and withdraw the passenger-side actuator. The illustration identifies the actuator and its mounting points; the replacement sequence does not call for dismantling the actuator.

steps.title: Install the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: position the replacement actuator, install its retainers and reconnect the electrical connector. Restore both its mechanical attachment and electrical connection.

watchFor.title: Tension during removal
watchFor.body: If mid-position could not be achieved, the tension-reducing preparation has not been completed; keep that condition in mind while removing the actuator.

notes: With Electronic Manual Temperature Control, the temperature setting determines outlet temperature; with DATC, it represents the desired cabin temperature.

verification.title: Confirm installation completion
verification.body: Check that the replacement passenger-side actuator is mounted with its retainers installed and its electrical connector reconnected.

procedures.purpose: Passenger-side temperature door actuator removal and installation, including the conditional mid-position preparation.

guides.title: Identify A/C refrigerant before recovery or charging
guides.summary: Test refrigerant composition before service to identify contamination and keep unsuitable refrigerant out of normal recovery equipment.
guides.introduction: Air conditioning cools cabin air and reduces its humidity. Before recovering refrigerant from the vehicle or charging it from a storage container, identification testing establishes what the refrigerant actually contains. This is a service decision point: a contaminated sample requires a different recovery route, while air in an otherwise pure sample has its own interpretation.
guides.why: Contaminated refrigerant can spoil the recovered refrigerant supply and damage recovery equipment. Air also affects A/C performance, but the identifier excludes air when calculating refrigerant purity. Understanding that distinction prevents a green purity result from being mistaken for confirmation that the sample contains no air.

when.summary: Before recovering or charging refrigerant, including refrigerant supplied from a storage container.
notes: The stated purity thresholds describe R-134a results; do not apply them automatically to R-1234yf.

prepare.title: Arrange suitable identification equipment
prepare.detail: Use refrigerant identification equipment conforming to SAE J1771 for R-134a, or equipment conforming to SAE J2912 that identifies R-134a and R-1234yf. Have its operating instructions available.

prepare.title: Prepare for a contamination finding
prepare.detail: The workshop must be able to arrange dedicated recovery-only equipment for contaminated refrigerant and follow the applicable A/C flushing procedure if contamination is confirmed.

steps.title: Sample the actual refrigerant source
steps.body: Take the sample directly from the vehicle refrigeration system or storage container, following the identifier manufacturer's sampling instructions. Sampling precedes recovery or charging so an unsuitable supply is recognized before it enters service equipment.

steps.title: Read composition alongside the indicator
steps.body: Use the result distinctions below and the complete [identification procedure](#/document/G1912329). The display reports the weight concentrations of R-134a, R-12, R-22 and hydrocarbons. Air content is displayed when the R-134a purity requirement is met.

steps.title: Verify an apparent contamination result
steps.body: Repeat the identification test whenever contaminated refrigerant is detected. This establishes whether the contamination finding is repeatable before the workshop proceeds with the contaminated-refrigerant recovery route.

steps.title: Keep confirmed contamination isolated
steps.body: Do not recover contaminated refrigerant into R-134a recovery/recycling equipment. Use recovery-only equipment specifically designed to capture and store contaminated refrigerant, protecting both the normal recovered supply and the recycling equipment.

steps.title: Correct the original concern and complete follow-on work
steps.body: Determine and correct the customer's initial concern, then follow Air Conditioning (A/C) System Flushing in Group 412. Replace the suction accumulator, receiver drier or receiver drier element as that procedure directs. Dispose of contaminated refrigerant according to applicable federal, state and local regulations.

watchFor.title: Hazard alarms
watchFor.body: A red failure indication and audible alarm require attention to the reported composition, especially a Hydrocarbon High message.

watchFor.title: A purity pass with air present
watchFor.body: Air is excluded from the refrigerant purity calculation, so a passing result does not establish that air content is acceptable.

notes: Sampling and any offered air-purge operation remain subject to the identification equipment's instructions.

diagnostics.finding: R-134a purity is 98% or greater by weight.
diagnostics.meaning: The green PASS indicator confirms the specified refrigerant purity threshold.
diagnostics.next: Review the displayed air content before continuing refrigerant service.

diagnostics.finding: R-134a purity is below 98% by weight.
diagnostics.meaning: The red FAIL indicator and alarm identify a sample that does not meet the purity requirement.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the identification test; confirmed contamination requires dedicated recovery-only equipment.

diagnostics.finding: Hydrocarbons are 2% or greater by weight.
diagnostics.meaning: The identifier reports Hydrocarbon High, illuminates FAIL and sounds an alarm for potential hazards.
diagnostics.next: Verify the result by repeating the test and keep confirmed contaminated refrigerant out of normal recovery/recycling equipment.

diagnostics.finding: R-134a purity passes and air is 2% or greater by weight.
diagnostics.meaning: The identifier offers an air purge; the air has not caused the refrigerant purity calculation to fail.
diagnostics.next: Respond to the purge prompt according to the equipment instructions.

verification.title: Record the identification result
verification.body: Record the sampled source, indicated composition, pass/fail result and any repeated contamination result so the subsequent service route is traceable.

verification.title: Confirm the correct recovery route
verification.body: For confirmed contamination, verify dedicated recovery was used and that flushing-related component replacement and disposal requirements were addressed.

procedures.purpose: Refrigerant sampling, R-134a result interpretation, repeat testing and the confirmed-contamination recovery pathway.

guides.title: Replace the A/C compressor inlet line on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Recover the refrigerant, exchange the engine-specific compressor inlet line and restore its sealed connections with the specified lubrication.
guides.introduction: The air conditioning compressor inlet line carries refrigerant back to the compressor. Its fittings must retain refrigerant while keeping the circuit clean. Replacing the line means opening that circuit, renewing the specified seals and restoring the correct refrigerant-oil provision. The four engine versions share this overall sequence, but their line routing and lubricant instructions must be followed individually.
guides.why: Recovery must precede opening either fitting. Once disconnected, uncovered ports provide a route for dirt to enter the system. Seal condition and the correct lubricant matter during reassembly because the joints must close without damaging their new seals. Oil quantity is determined through the refrigerant-oil procedure, not by guessing from the removed line.

when.summary: When a confirmed repair requires removal or replacement of the A/C compressor inlet line.
notes: A cooling complaint alone does not establish that this line needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant service
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment to perform the applicable recovery, evacuation and charging procedure, together with Refrigerant Oil Adding.

prepare.title: Prepare clean connections
prepare.detail: Have suitable port protection, new O-ring seals, the required sealing parts and a torque wrench. Keep all open connections protected throughout removal.

prepare.title: Confirm the engine-specific lubricant
prepare.detail: The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L procedures specify Motorcraft PAG refrigerant compressor oil YN-12-D, specification WSH-M1C231-B. For the 5.2L, obtain the applicable Group 412 seal-lubricant specification. PAG means polyalkylene glycol.

steps.title: Choose the matching line procedure
steps.body: Identify both connections and the line routing using the correct engine procedure: [2.3L EcoBoost](#/document/G1874213), [3.7L Duratec](#/document/G1874215), [5.0L](#/document/G1874217) or [5.2L](#/document/G1874219). The illustrations show different installed arrangements.

steps.title: Recover the refrigerant
steps.body: Perform the applicable A/C recovery procedure before loosening a line connection. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L instructions refer to Air Conditioning (A/C) System Recovery, Evacuation and Charging; the 5.2L directs recovery through Group 412.

steps.title: Disconnect the first fitting
steps.body: Remove the inlet-line nut and separate the fitting, immediately protecting the exposed openings. On the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, discard both the O-ring seal and gasket seal from this connection.

steps.title: Release the remaining connection and remove the line
steps.body: Remove the second nut, disconnect the fitting and lift out the inlet line. Protect the remaining ports. Again, the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L require the removed O-ring and gasket seal to be discarded.

steps.title: Install the line with new seals
steps.body: Reverse the engine-specific removal sequence, removing protective materials as connections are assembled. Install new O-rings using only the specified seal lubricant; do not reuse discarded seals. Both inlet-line connection nuts are specified at 18 Nm in each of these procedures.

steps.title: Restore the required oil and refrigerant service
steps.body: Use Refrigerant Oil Adding to establish the correct amount of clean PAG oil. Complete the applicable evacuation and charging work through the refrigerant-service procedure; these line instructions do not provide an oil quantity or refrigerant charge.

watchFor.title: Open or forgotten protected ports
watchFor.body: Keep openings sealed during the job, then remove every cap, tape piece or other protective material before making the relevant connection.

watchFor.title: Lubricant transferred between variants
watchFor.body: The 5.2L instructions require its applicable specifications. Do not assume the lubricant named for the other engines also applies.

notes: The selected illustration shows the 2.3L connection; use the other linked procedures for their respective engine layouts.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Check that both fittings are connected, their nuts have been tightened as specified, new O-rings were installed and no discarded seals were reused.

verification.title: Record service completion
verification.body: Record the engine variant, lubricant used and oil added under Refrigerant Oil Adding, together with completion of the applicable refrigerant-service procedure.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost inlet-line removal and installation, discarded seals, connection torque and specified seal lubricant.
3.7L Duratec inlet-line removal and installation, discarded seals, connection torque and specified seal lubricant.
5.0L inlet-line removal and installation, discarded seals, connection torque and specified seal lubricant.
5.2L inlet-line removal and installation, port protection, new O-rings and references to its applicable lubricant specifications.

guides.title: Adjust convertible-top tension belt buckles
guides.summary: Adjust both roof tension buckles equally, checking top operation and latching effort after each secured adjustment.
guides.introduction: The convertible top's tension belt buckles provide a mechanical adjustment to roof tension. Tightening their screws adds tension; loosening them reduces it. Because this also changes latching effort, the job is a controlled adjustment-and-test process. The roof's electric motors move the top, but buckle adjustment addresses mechanical tension rather than electronic operating faults.
guides.why: Partially opening the roof unloads the buckles before they are released. Matching the screw positions from side to side preserves equal adjustment, while recording the starting positions provides a way back if the change is unsuitable. Both buckles must be secured to the body before each operational test so the result reflects their installed condition.

when.summary: When convertible-top tension or latching effort needs correction through the tension belt buckles.
notes: Adjustments made on one side must also be made on the other.
A top that will not move requires its operating conditions to be checked before tension is altered.

prepare.title: Provide access and measurement
prepare.detail: Arrange access from both sides of the luggage compartment, a suitable means of measuring the screw positions and tools for the adjusters. Remove the subwoofer speaker if fitted, following its removal procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare to operate the top
prepare.detail: Keep the vehicle stationary with accessory delay active. Opening requires the top latch to be released; closing requires any tonneau covers to be removed. The roof switch must be held during movement.

steps.title: Relieve belt tension
steps.body: After any required subwoofer removal, partially open the top as shown in the [buckle adjustment procedure](#/document/G2401442). This removes tension from the buckles before their brackets are disconnected.

steps.title: Release both adjuster brackets
steps.body: Work from the luggage compartment on both sides. Push inward on the rear of each tension belt adjuster to release its locking tabs, then pull its rear downward to disconnect the bracket from the body.

steps.title: Record the starting screw positions
steps.body: Measure and note each screw's initial position before turning it. Check the relationship between the two sides: their positions should match. These measurements allow the adjustment to be returned to its starting setting if needed.

steps.title: Make equal changes and test
steps.body: Turn both buckle screws equally in the direction required: tighten to increase tension or loosen to reduce it. Resecure both buckles to the vehicle after every adjustment, then retest roof operation and latching effort before deciding on another change.

steps.title: Finish at the intended tension
steps.body: Continue the equal-adjustment and secured-test sequence until the intended roof tension is achieved. The fully tightened and maximum-travel loosened illustrations explain the adjustment's endpoints; neither is a prescribed target. Reinstall everything removed for access.

watchFor.title: Unequal screw positions
watchFor.body: Do not make a one-sided correction and leave the opposite buckle unchanged; the procedure requires identical positions and equal adjustments.

watchFor.title: Testing with a buckle released
watchFor.body: Reconnect both buckles to the body before operating the top after an adjustment.

notes: The right-hand side is illustrated; the left-hand side follows the same process.

diagnostics.finding: The top will not raise or lower.
diagnostics.meaning: Roof movement depends on operating permissions and confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully down; refusal to move does not establish incorrect belt tension.
diagnostics.next: Check the opening or closing prerequisites and window-down operation before continuing buckle adjustment.

diagnostics.finding: An adjustment changes latching effort.
diagnostics.meaning: Buckle screw position directly changes roof tension and therefore affects the effort needed to latch it.
diagnostics.next: Assess the result with both buckles secured, then make another equal adjustment or return to the recorded starting positions.

verification.title: Confirm the installed result
verification.body: Verify equal screw positions, secure engagement of both brackets and satisfactory top operation after the final adjustment.

verification.title: Record the adjustment
verification.body: Keep the initial and final screw-position measurements with the observed change in roof tension and latching effort.

procedures.purpose: Convertible-top buckle access, release, equal adjustment, repeated operational testing and reassembly.

guides.title: Replace the floor-console audio input jack on a SYNC system
guides.summary: Remove the console jack bezel, disconnect its wiring and release the retaining tabs to exchange the audio input jack.
guides.introduction: The audio input jack provides a connection for an external audio source within the SYNC entertainment system. It sits in a bezel accessed beneath the floor-console lid. This job separates the jack from that surrounding trim and replaces it while retaining the rest of the console arrangement.
guides.why: The bezel, electrical connectors and jack-retaining tabs are separate stages of removal. Following that order gives access to the jack's retention without pulling on the connected wiring. The illustration identifies the tabs that must release before the jack can leave its housing.

when.summary: When the audio input jack requires replacement or removal for an established repair.
notes: An audio-input complaint alone does not identify the jack as the failed component.

prepare.title: Arrange console access
prepare.detail: Clear access to the floor-console lid and jack bezel. The work requires careful handling of trim, electrical connectors and the jack's retaining tabs.

prepare.title: Identify the retaining features
prepare.detail: Use the jack illustration to distinguish its retaining tabs from the surrounding bezel. Avoid assuming that pulling the visible socket will release the assembly.

steps.title: Open the lid and remove the bezel
steps.body: Open the floor-console lid, then remove the audio input jack bezel following the [removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1704850). The bezel must come free before the electrical connectors are disconnected.

steps.title: Disconnect the wiring
steps.body: Support the released bezel and disconnect the electrical connectors. This separates the jack assembly from the vehicle wiring before its retaining tabs are released; do not use the wiring to carry the assembly.

steps.title: Release and remove the jack
steps.body: Release the retaining tabs shown at the upper and lower sides of the jack in the illustration, then remove the jack from the bezel. If it remains retained, check the tabs rather than increasing the pulling force.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Install the replacement jack into the bezel, allowing its retaining tabs to engage. Reconnect the electrical connectors and reinstall the bezel. Reversing the removal sequence restores both the mechanical retention and the electrical connection.

watchFor.title: A jack that remains loose
watchFor.body: Recheck retaining-tab engagement before treating the bezel installation as complete.

watchFor.title: Wiring under load
watchFor.body: Keep the bezel supported while unplugging or reconnecting it so the connectors are not carrying its weight.

notes: The system also has separately identified USB ports; this removal path is specifically for the audio input jack.

verification.title: Check retention and reconnection
verification.body: Confirm the jack is retained by its tabs, the electrical connectors are reconnected and the bezel is seated in the console.

procedures.purpose: SYNC audio input jack bezel removal, electrical disconnection, tab release and reverse-order installation.

guides.title: Remove and refit the steering-column shrouds
guides.summary: Release the gap trim, wheel-accessed tabs and outer clips before removing the upper and lower steering-column covers.
guides.introduction: The steering-column shrouds form the upper and lower trim enclosure around the column. A separate upper gap hider closes the visible transition to the surrounding trim. Removing these pieces provides access around the column or allows damaged covers to be replaced. The upper cover uses tabs and clips, while screws secure the lower cover.
guides.why: The upper shroud has several retaining points that become accessible in sequence. Turning the steering wheel exposes tabs that can otherwise keep the cover attached. Releasing those tabs and the outer clips before lifting the cover avoids trying to overcome its retention by bending the trim.

when.summary: When the steering-column covers need replacement or removal to provide repair access.
notes: The illustrated layout is left-hand drive; the right-hand-drive procedure is similar.

prepare.title: Have the specified trim tools
prepare.detail: Prepare an interior trim remover and a flat-bladed screwdriver. Each has a different role: the trim remover releases the gap hider, while the screwdriver releases the wheel-accessed shroud tabs.

prepare.title: Allow column and wheel movement
prepare.detail: The column must be fully extended and lowered, and the steering wheel must be turned to expose the retaining tabs.

steps.title: Position the column and free the gap hider
steps.body: Fully extend and lower the steering column. Using the interior trim remover, release the tabs connecting the upper gap hider to the upper shroud, then position the gap hider aside.

steps.title: Release the wheel-accessed tabs
steps.body: Following the [shroud procedure](#/document/G1692617), rotate the steering wheel 90 degrees and release the exposed shroud tab with the flat-bladed screwdriver. Then rotate the wheel 180 degrees and release the other tab.

steps.title: Remove the upper shroud
steps.body: Release the outer clips on each side and remove the upper cover. The illustration shows the cover lifting away after these clips have been released; that lifting action follows the earlier tab-release work.

steps.title: Remove the lower shroud
steps.body: Remove the lower cover's screws, then remove the lower shroud. Keep the screw-fastened lower section distinct from the clipped upper section when identifying what still holds a cover in place.

steps.title: Restore the trim enclosure
steps.body: Install the parts in reverse order: refit the lower shroud and its screws, reinstall the upper shroud with its clips and tabs engaged, then reconnect the upper gap hider.

watchFor.title: Resistance from an unreleased retainer
watchFor.body: If the upper cover resists removal, recheck the wheel-accessed tabs and both sets of outer clips before applying more force.

watchFor.title: Gap trim left disconnected
watchFor.body: The upper gap hider is a separate attachment and must be reconnected after the shrouds are installed.

notes: The steering wheel is rotated for access; its removal is not part of this shroud procedure.

verification.title: Check each fastening method
verification.body: Confirm the lower screws are installed, the upper tabs and outer clips are engaged, and the gap hider is attached without an unseated edge.

procedures.purpose: Upper gap-hider release, steering-wheel positioning for shroud tabs, upper and lower cover removal and reverse-order installation.

guides.title: Repair an exterior mirror assembly, glass, motor or fitted lamp
guides.summary: Choose the required mirror repair branch, preserve its option-specific wiring and reassemble the serviced components in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The exterior mirror combines a housing with electrically adjustable glass. Depending on equipment, it can also contain glass heating, position memory, a turn signal, a puddle or projection lamp and a blind-spot indicator. Repair may involve the whole door-mounted assembly or an individual component. These are alternative access paths: removing the complete mirror is not listed as a prerequisite for every internal repair.
guides.why: The assembly-removal sequence changes the door-glass position as access requirements change. The mirror must be supported when its mounting hardware is removed to protect both it and the door. Internal connectors vary with fitted options, and an electrical complaint may come from the integral jumper harness rather than the motor or complete mirror.

when.summary: When damage or a diagnosed fault requires repair of the exterior mirror or one of its serviceable components.
notes: Identify the fitted options and required repair branch before dismantling.
Inspect the jumper harness before replacing a mirror or motor for an electrical concern.

prepare.title: Arrange the appropriate access
prepare.detail: Whole-assembly work requires the front door trim-panel and appropriate speaker procedures. Speaker references are identified for SYNC 2/SYNC 3; follow the equipment applicable to the vehicle.

prepare.title: Prepare for glass and wiring work
prepare.detail: Have a flat-bladed screwdriver for releasing the glass and the capability to handle small screws, tabs and option-specific connectors. Electrical fault assessment must include the mirror jumper harness.

steps.title: Select the repair branch
steps.body: Use the complete [exterior mirror procedure](#/document/G1945075) to choose assembly, glass, motor, cover, turn-signal or puddle-lamp work. For electrical concerns, first inspect the integral jumper harness for open or shorted circuits and damaged or pushed-out pins; attempt harness repair where a harness concern exists.

steps.title: For assembly removal, open the door access
steps.body: Raise the window fully. Remove the [door trim panel](#/document/G1692600) and the appropriate [left](#/document/G1693897) or [right](#/document/G1693898) front door speaker. Remove the door-mounted tweeter if fitted. Remove the rectangular tape cover and, on vehicles without door-mounted tweeters, the additional tape cover specified by the procedure.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the complete mirror
steps.body: Through the lower speaker opening, disconnect the mirror electrical connection and separate the wiring harness guide. Reconnect the window switch and lower the glass fully. Support the mirror while removing its mounting nut and bolts, then remove the assembly.

steps.title: For glass service, release the glass from the motor
steps.body: Position the mirror glass fully inward and upward. Insert a flat-bladed screwdriver between the glass and motor, twist to release the glass and position it aside. Disconnect its electrical connectors, whose number and location depend on fitted options.

steps.title: For motor service, remove the bezel
steps.body: With the glass removed, remove the bezel screws and release its tabs. Remove the motor screws and position the motor aside, then disconnect its electrical connectors and remove it.

steps.title: For cover or turn-signal service, work through the motor branch
steps.body: Remove the motor first. Disconnect the mirror-mounted side turn signal if fitted, then remove the cover screw, release the tabs and remove the cover. With the cover removed, the mirror-mounted turn signal can be removed.

steps.title: For puddle-lamp service, work through the glass opening
steps.body: Remove the mirror glass, press the puddle-lamp retaining tab and lower the lamp. Disconnect its electrical connectors to release it. This branch calls for glass removal rather than the motor-and-cover sequence.

steps.title: Reassemble the branch used
steps.body: Reverse the relevant removal sequence, reconnecting every fitted connector and engaging the screws and tabs disturbed. For whole-assembly work, support the mirror until secured and restore the harness guide, tape covers, speakers, any removed tweeter and door trim.

watchFor.title: Unsupported assembly
watchFor.body: Removing the mounting hardware without supporting the mirror risks damage to the mirror or door surface.

watchFor.title: Different glass connections
watchFor.body: Do not assume both mirrors or replacement assemblies have identical connector arrangements; options determine the connections present.

notes: Memory-equipped mirrors use door-module control and position feedback; non-memory mirrors receive motor voltage and ground from the mirror control switch.

diagnostics.finding: The mirror does not respond to adjustment.
diagnostics.meaning: A wiring defect can interrupt motor operation; the symptom alone does not condemn the motor.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the integral jumper harness and its pins before deciding on motor or assembly replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Heated glass is inactive while rear-window defrost is off.
diagnostics.meaning: Mirror heating operates only while the rear-window defrost system is active.
diagnostics.next: Assess heating with rear defrost active before treating the glass as faulty.

diagnostics.finding: Memory recall stops when the mirror or driver-seat control is operated.
diagnostics.meaning: Manual control input cancels an active memory recall.
diagnostics.next: Distinguish normal cancellation from a recall fault before replacing components.

verification.title: Check the repaired functions and attachments
verification.body: Confirm secure mounting or component retention and complete electrical reconnection. Check glass adjustment; assess fitted memory, heating and any serviced lamp under their normal operating conditions.

verification.title: Record the repair result
verification.body: Record the component serviced, harness findings and results for the affected fitted features, including any unresolved complaint.

procedures.purpose: Exterior mirror assembly removal and the separate glass, motor, cover, turn-signal and puddle-lamp service branches.
Front door trim-panel removal and installation for complete mirror assembly access.
Left-hand front door speaker access procedure for applicable SYNC 2/SYNC 3 equipment.
Right-hand front door speaker access procedure for applicable SYNC 2/SYNC 3 equipment.
Mirror jumper-harness inspection guidance and distinctions between power, memory and heated-mirror operation.

applicability.equipment: Power exterior mirrors; memory, heating and mirror lamps as equipped

guides.title: Replace a front door check arm
guides.summary: Remove the door trim and watershield to replace the check arm, then restore its mountings and the door's interior connections.
guides.introduction: The check arm restrains the front door as it opens and helps control its travel. Its attachment inside the door means replacement involves both mechanical fasteners and interior trim. The door panel must be released carefully because wiring and the interior latch cable remain connected behind it.
guides.why: Once disconnected, the arm cannot restrain door movement. Controlling the door protects nearby panels, while supporting the trim prevents its remaining cable and electrical connections from carrying the panel's weight.

when.summary: When a front door check arm requires removal or replacement.
notes: A door movement complaint alone does not establish that the check arm needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange controlled access
prepare.detail: Allow room to hold the door steady and support the trim panel during disconnection.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening tools
prepare.detail: Use hand tools and torque equipment suitable for the check-arm hardware and the smaller trim-panel fasteners.

steps.title: Release the external attachment
steps.body: Follow the [check-arm procedure](#/document/G1693222). Control the door and remove the check-arm bolt. Its installation torque differs from that of the nuts inside the door.

steps.title: Remove the door trim
steps.body: Follow [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600): remove the upper bolt cover and bolt, the window control switch through its referenced procedure, the center bolt and lower retainers. Release the clips and pin retainers in the specified rear-upper, rear/lower and remaining-panel sequence. Lift the panel up and out, then disconnect electrical connectors where fitted and release the latch cable.

steps.title: Withdraw the check arm
steps.body: Remove the check-arm nuts, then the front watershield. Remove the check-arm assembly through the resulting access. Preserve this sequence so the shield and surrounding trim do not obstruct withdrawal.

steps.title: Restore the arm and trim
steps.body: Reverse removal. Refit the arm and watershield, tightening the nuts to 106 lb.in (12 Nm). Reconnect the latch cable and applicable connectors before seating the trim; transfer trim parts as necessary. Follow the panel procedure's individual fastening torques. Install the check-arm bolt to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm).

watchFor.title: Attached trim
watchFor.body: Do not pull a partly released panel away while its retainers, latch cable or electrical connections still hold it.

notes: The check-arm procedure shows the left side; the right is similar. Trim instructions show a right-hand door on a left-hand-drive vehicle, with opposite arrangements similar.

verification.title: Confirm fastening and reconnection
verification.body: Check the arm bolt and nuts against their separate torque settings, and confirm the watershield, latch cable, applicable connectors and panel retainers are restored.

procedures.purpose: Front door check-arm removal and installation, including mounting torques.
Door-trim access, staged retainer release, cable disconnection and trim refitting.

guides.title: Replace a front seat backrest cover
guides.summary: Replace the backrest upholstery while preserving its foam attachments, wiring and side-airbag deployment path.
guides.introduction: The backrest cover fits over the foam and is secured by several different attachments, including hook-and-loop strips, J-shaped clips and hog rings. It also surrounds the side-airbag deployment chute. Where climate-controlled seating is fitted, blower components and cover straps add another layer of routing to preserve during removal.
guides.why: This is upholstery work with a restraint-system consequence. A damaged cover on a seat equipped with a side airbag must be replaced, not repaired; cleaning is permissible. Incorrect cover or chute work can interfere with airbag deployment. Pulling aggressively at hook-and-loop attachments can also tear their mating strips from the foam.

when.summary: When the backrest cover needs replacement or removal for access beneath the upholstery.
notes: Safety-belt guides, belt straps and blower-snorkel operations apply only where those parts are fitted.

prepare.title: Complete the seat-removal prerequisite
prepare.detail: Arrange removal and refitting through [Front Seat](#/document/G1695491), following its complete prerequisites. This work requires competence around seat side airbags; upholstery instructions are not an electrical-disconnection shortcut.

prepare.title: Prepare upholstery and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have hog ring pliers and suitable torque equipment available. Use a new cover when replacement is required, and be prepared to replace any damaged side airbag or deployment chute discovered during inspection.

steps.title: Remove the seat and guide sleeves
steps.body: Remove the front seat through its linked procedure, then remove the [head restraint guide sleeves](#/document/G1695520). Continue with the [backrest-cover procedure](#/document/G1702539) once those access operations are complete.

steps.title: Clear the belt guides and release-handle trim
steps.body: Remove the inner safety-belt guide if fitted. For an outer guide, remove its cover and front and rear bolts; both bolts have an installation torque of 106 lb.in (12 Nm). Remove the seat release-handle bezel.

steps.title: Free the wiring, straps and insert
steps.body: Release the electrical-connector retainers and move the harnesses aside. Position the cover to detach its straps, routing them out through the blower snorkel if fitted. Move the cover aside, release the insert's pin retainers and position the cover upward. Move the snorkel aside where present.

steps.title: Release the lower cover attachment
steps.body: Release the J-clip and draw the cover out from between the seat cushion and backrest cushion. Carefully separate the hook-and-loop strips and move the cover upward without pulling the foam-mounted strips loose.

steps.title: Free the deployment chute and remaining retainers
steps.body: Detach the side-airbag deployment-chute retainers and pull the chute through the backrest foam. Release the cover J-clips, move the cover upward, release the J-clip from the frame and remove the hog rings.

steps.title: Remove the cover from the foam
steps.body: Position the safety-belt strap as needed where fitted. Carefully separate the remaining hook-and-loop attachment and remove the cover, keeping the foam's attachment strips intact.

steps.title: Inspect and reassemble
steps.body: Inspect the side airbag, its cavity, mounting surface and deployment chute. Remove all foreign material; replace a damaged airbag or damaged chute.
