steps.body: Check dimensional accuracy before welding. Clamp and weld the outer member, then the inner member, with MIG/MAG equipment as directed. Complete the specified resistance spot welds in the frame-member assembly.

steps.title: Install the apron panels
steps.body: Drill the specified plug-weld holes in the replacement panel with the 8 mm bit. Follow each illustrated apron reinforcement installation and welding stage, using the specified clamps and welding method. The battery-tray reinforcement operation belongs only to the right-hand side.

steps.title: Finish and protect the welded structure
steps.body: Install and resistance-spot-weld the fender apron bracket. Metal-finish the sectioning seams, seal all repaired areas to production level, restore corrosion protection and refinish with the approved paint system.

steps.title: Reassemble the vehicle
steps.body: Install the bracket and tighten its fasteners to 14 Nm. Refit the fender apron panel reinforcement and the removed mechanical components, following the applicable installation procedures rather than treating engine variants as interchangeable.

watchFor.title: Replacement weld locations
watchFor.body: Replacement resistance welds must sit adjacent to the original locations and match their quantity. MAG plug welds must match both the original locations and quantity.

watchFor.title: Misalignment before welding
watchFor.body: Resolve dimensional errors before permanent joining; panel fit alone does not replace the specified body measurements.

notes: The left-hand side is illustrated. Right-hand similarities do not make the right-hand-only battery-tray operation part of this repair.

verification.title: Record dimensional results
verification.body: Record the relevant body measurements and their comparison with Body and Frame specifications before welding.

verification.title: Confirm joint and finish completion
verification.body: Check weld quantity and placement, completed sectioning seams, production-level sealing, restored corrosion protection and completion of the referenced reassembly procedures.

guides.title: Replace the MT82 manual transmission output shaft seal
guides.summary: Replace the rear output seal by removing the driveshaft and flange, then reinstall the flange with its prescribed tooling and bolt-tightening sequence.
guides.introduction: The MT82 output shaft delivers transmission torque through the rear flange to the driveshaft. A seal in the rear transmission case retains lubricant around this rotating connection. Access requires removing the flange and temporarily removing the transmission crossmember, while leaving the internal gears assembled. The job is therefore as much about secure support and correct flange installation as it is about replacing the seal.
guides.why: Once the crossmember is removed, the transmission needs a strapped transmission jack to carry and stabilize it. Dedicated installers control placement of the new seal and flange. The flange bolt also has a specific tighten–loosen–retighten sequence and thread-locking preparation; simply tightening it once to a final value does not complete the prescribed installation.

when.summary: When the MT82 output shaft seal has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Fluid near the rear flange warrants identifying its origin before selecting this repair.
This procedure applies to the MT82 installation covered for 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines.

prepare.title: Provide supported underbody access
prepare.detail: Arrange safe vehicle access for driveshaft removal and a transmission jack with a safety strap. Have the separate driveshaft procedure available.

prepare.title: Gather the removal and installation tools
prepare.detail: Use a two-leg puller for flange removal; handle 205-153 with rear-seal installer 308-811; flange installers 308-808 and 308-809; and companion-flange tool 308-938 for the flange bolt.

prepare.title: Prepare the replacement seal and fastener supplies
prepare.detail: Have a new output shaft seal, suitable torque equipment and the thread-locking adhesive specified through the primary procedure's Specifications reference. The removed seal must be discarded.

steps.title: Remove the driveshaft
steps.body: Follow the [driveshaft removal procedure](#/document/G2214904) to expose the transmission output flange. Its separate installation requirements remain part of completing this repair.

steps.title: Support the transmission before removing its mounting
steps.body: Place the transmission on the transmission jack and secure it with the safety strap. Remove the bolts, transmission support insulator and crossmember only after this support is established.

steps.title: Remove the flange and old seal
steps.body: Remove the output shaft flange bolt, then withdraw the flange with the two-leg puller. Remove and discard the output shaft seal, following the [seal procedure](#/document/G1687337).

steps.title: Install the new seal and flange
steps.body: Place the new seal on handle 205-153 and installer 308-811, then install it with those tools. Install the output shaft flange using tools 308-808 and 308-809. The seal and flange use different installation arrangements.

steps.title: Prepare and tighten the flange bolt
steps.body: Fit tool 308-938. Clean the output shaft bolt threads and apply one dot of the specified thread-locking adhesive to their lower end. Tighten to 200 Nm, loosen five turns, then tighten to 180 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the mounting and driveshaft
steps.body: Install the support insulator and crossmember. Use the primary procedure's illustrated fastener locations to apply the correct torque to each bolt group. Reinstall the driveshaft using its linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Support interrupted during the repair
watchFor.body: Keep the transmission supported and strapped while its normal crossmember support is removed.

watchFor.title: Fastener groups confused
watchFor.body: The support mounting has separate torque callouts. Identify their illustrated positions rather than applying one value to every bolt.

notes: Tool 308-809 is named a synchronizer gear-pack installer, but this operation uses it for flange installation; internal gear disassembly is not part of the sequence.

verification.title: Record the flange-bolt installation
verification.body: Record completion of thread preparation, adhesive application and all three tightening stages.

verification.title: Confirm restored support and driveline attachment
verification.body: Confirm the support insulator and crossmember fasteners were tightened at their correct locations and driveshaft installation is complete.

procedures.purpose: MT82 output shaft seal removal and installation, including flange tooling and staged bolt tightening.
Driveshaft removal for seal access and installation after transmission support is restored.

guides.title: Remove and refit the air cleaner outlet pipe: 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L
guides.summary: Remove the intake outlet pipe using the correct engine-specific tube connections, then restore the pipe, clamps and attached hoses.
guides.introduction: The air cleaner outlet pipe carries filtered air onward through the engine intake and provides connections for other tubes. Its removal is straightforward, but the attached tubes differ substantially between engines. On the 2.3L EcoBoost, keeping debris out is especially important because particles entering the intake can damage the turbocharger compressor vanes.
guides.why: Disconnecting every attached tube before moving the pipe avoids pulling on connections that are still secured. Correct reassembly restores the intended air path and each associated connection. Cleanliness on the turbocharged engine is a component-protection requirement, even when the pipe is only being removed temporarily.

when.summary: When the outlet pipe needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: Select the procedure by engine; the hose arrangements and number of pipe clamps differ.

prepare.title: Prepare for clamps and tube connections
prepare.detail: Have tools suitable for the fitted clamps and a torque wrench capable of their specified tightening value. Identify the engine before disconnecting anything.

prepare.title: Protect the 2.3L intake
prepare.detail: Keep debris from entering any opened turbocharger or engine intake component. Arrange a clean working area before exposing the pipe connections.

steps.title: Identify the connections and gain access
steps.body: Use the matching engine illustration to identify the outlet pipe and its attached tubes. On the 5.0L, remove the engine appearance cover first.

steps.title: Disconnect the engine-specific tubes
steps.body: For the [2.3L](#/document/G1675706), loosen the clamp and move aside the charge air cooler (CAC) bypass-valve inlet tube, then disconnect the crankcase ventilation tube. For the [3.7L](#/document/G1675695), disconnect the brake booster and crankcase ventilation tubes. For the [5.0L](#/document/G1675684), disconnect both brake booster tubes, the crankcase ventilation tube and the resonator air inlet tube.

steps.title: Release and remove the outlet pipe
steps.body: Loosen the three specified pipe clamps on the 2.3L, or the two pipe clamps on the 3.7L and 5.0L, and remove the pipe. Keep the disconnected tubes positioned aside and maintain debris protection at the open intake.

steps.title: Inspect where required and reverse the removal
steps.body: On the 2.3L, inspect the turbocharger or engine intake components and clean them if necessary before installation. Refit in reverse order. Tighten the outlet-pipe clamps identified in each procedure to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), restore the tube connections and reinstall the 5.0L appearance cover.

watchFor.title: Turbocharger contamination
watchFor.body: Even very small particles can damage compressor vanes; do not leave contamination in the opened 2.3L intake.

watchFor.title: Clamp specification applied too broadly
watchFor.body: The stated torque accompanies the outlet-pipe clamp operation. Do not assume it specifies every other clamp on the attached tubing.

notes: On the 3.7L and 5.0L, a restricted air cleaner element can reduce performance and fuel economy. That condition alone does not establish a need to replace the outlet pipe.

verification.title: Confirm the air path is reassembled
verification.body: Check that the pipe is seated, its specified clamps are tightened and every tube disconnected for the selected engine is reconnected.

verification.title: Complete variant-specific work
verification.body: Confirm the 2.3L intake inspection and any necessary cleaning are complete, and the 5.0L appearance cover is restored.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost outlet-pipe removal and installation, including bypass tubing and intake cleanliness.
3.7L outlet-pipe removal and installation with brake booster and crankcase ventilation connections.
5.0L outlet-pipe removal and installation, including appearance cover and additional tube connections.

guides.title: Replace the in-tank fuel pump and sender unit
guides.summary: Release fuel pressure, lower the tank level and replace the pump-and-sender assembly through the rear-seat access opening with a new seal.
guides.introduction: The tank-mounted assembly supplies pressurized fuel and carries the sender that reports fuel level. Replacement involves connections both above the tank and inside it. Access is through an opening beneath the rear seat cushion, but the tank must first be prepared so fuel sits below the unit's mounting flange. The four engine procedures share this access sequence while retaining engine-specific pressure-release and coupling instructions.
guides.why: Fuel pressure can remain after pump operation stops, so pressure release must precede disconnection. Lowering the fuel level addresses a separate problem: fuel reaching the open mounting flange. During installation, a new O-ring and correctly engaged alignment tabs establish the prescribed seal and unit position before the lock ring is tightened.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for replacement of the tank-mounted fuel pump and sender assembly.
notes: The removal sequence does not diagnose a fuel-pressure or gauge complaint.
Use the matching 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L procedure and replacement assembly.

prepare.title: Arrange controlled fuel recovery
prepare.detail: Provide fuel tanker 292-00004, the supplemental refueling adapter from the luggage compartment, and a 6 ft. length of 5/8 in. semi-rigid fuel drain tube.

prepare.title: Prepare access and sealing parts
prepare.detail: Have lock-ring tool 310-123 and a new pump-and-sender O-ring seal. Provide access to the rear seat cushion and the engine-matched pressure-release and quick-coupling procedures.

prepare.title: Respect the capless filler
prepare.detail: Use the supplemental adapter for drain-tube entry. The Easy Fuel capless filler assembly must not be modified.

steps.title: Release pressure, then disconnect the battery
steps.body: Complete the fuel-pressure release procedure for the fitted engine. Next, disconnect the battery ground cable using [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Do not substitute battery disconnection for pressure release.

steps.title: Drain below the mounting flange
steps.body: Insert the supplemental adapter and specified drain tube through the capless filler until the tube enters the tank. Connect the fuel tanker and remove as much fuel as possible. This removes fuel from the filler pipe and lowers the tank level below the pump mounting flange.

steps.title: Open the rear-seat access
steps.body: Remove the [rear seat cushion](#/document/G1692168), then remove and position aside the pump-and-sender access cover. This exposes the external electrical and fuel connections.

steps.title: Disconnect the external connections
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector and external fuel-tube quick-release coupling. Use the coupling procedure for the fitted engine so the connector is released by its intended mechanism.

steps.title: Unlock and disconnect the assembly
steps.body: Remove the lock ring with tool 310-123. Following the engine-specific removal procedure, disconnect the internal fuel-tube quick coupling and remove the pump-and-sender unit. The internal connection must be released before the assembly is fully removed.

steps.title: Refit with a new seal and correct alignment
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the internal connection and installing a new O-ring seal. Ensure the alignment tabs on the unit and fuel tank meet before tightening the lock ring.

steps.title: Restore the external connections and access
steps.body: Reconnect the external fuel coupling and electrical connector, restore the access cover and rear seat cushion, and complete battery reconnection through its procedure. Follow the applicable coupling instructions during reconnection as well as removal.

watchFor.title: Fuel still at the flange
watchFor.body: For a completely full tank, the procedure describes removing approximately 3 gallons to lower the level. The operative requirement is fuel below the mounting flange.

watchFor.title: Tabs not aligned
watchFor.body: Establish the specified alignment before tightening the lock ring; tightening is not a substitute for positioning the assembly.

notes: The 5.2L assembly contains two electric pumps. Its internal equipment should not be inferred from the other engine variants.
The 5.0L and 5.2L descriptions identify a separately serviceable level sender, so a fuel-level complaint alone does not justify complete assembly replacement.

diagnostics.finding: A 5.0L or 5.2L vehicle stopped after a collision.
diagnostics.meaning: Its collision-triggered pump shut-off feature may explain pump inactivity.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable shut-off and diagnostic guidance before treating inactivity as proof of pump failure.

verification.title: Confirm sealing before closing access
verification.body: Confirm a new O-ring was installed and the tank and unit alignment tabs met before lock-ring tightening.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Confirm both internal and external fuel couplings, the electrical connection, access cover, rear seat cushion and battery reconnection are complete.

guides.title: Minimize wheel-to-hub runout on the 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Position the measured wheel-and-tire high spot at the bottom, then tighten the wheel under light suspension loading to use available hub clearance.
guides.introduction: A wheel can have a small amount of clearance around the hub before its nuts are fully tightened. This procedure uses that clearance to offset a known high spot in the wheel-and-tire assembly. Radial runout describes the assembly's high-and-low variation as it rotates. Road Force is also influenced by tire stiffness, so a small change in mounting position can affect the result.
guides.why: The prescribed position and loading work together. Placing the high spot at the bottom establishes the intended orientation, while slight ground contact loads the assembly before final tightening. Allowing the vehicle's full weight onto the tires at that stage breaks the specified method. This is a targeted mounting adjustment following identification of a high spot.

when.summary: When a radial-runout or Road Force high spot has been identified and wheel-to-hub optimization is appropriate.
notes: A vibration complaint alone does not identify the high spot or establish that this adjustment will resolve it.

prepare.title: Have a known high-spot location
prepare.detail: Use the identified radial-runout or Road Force high spot from wheel-and-tire assessment. The mounting procedure begins with that location already established.

prepare.title: Arrange controlled lifting and tightening
prepare.detail: Provide vehicle lifting capability that allows the tires to touch the ground without taking full vehicle weight, and torque equipment for the Mustang wheel installation procedure.

prepare.title: Protect the tire and wheel
prepare.detail: Before tire servicing, ask whether sealant has been injected; it may be flammable. If additional tire-machine work is needed on carbon-fiber or alloy wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer and a balancer that does not contact the wheel face.

steps.title: Prepare the wheel for positioning
steps.body: Use the [Mustang wheel and tire procedure](#/document/G1686507) for the required removal and handling. Keep the identified high spot recognizable when positioning the assembly on the vehicle.

steps.title: Place the high spot at the bottom
steps.body: Position the assembly with its radial-runout or Road Force high spot at the 6 o'clock position. Install the wheel nuts by hand until snug, as directed by the [optimization procedure](#/document/G1686504).

steps.title: Apply only slight loading
steps.body: Lower the vehicle until the tires contact the ground and the suspension is slightly loaded. Do not allow the full vehicle weight to rest on the tires while tightening the nuts.

steps.title: Complete wheel fastening
steps.body: Tighten the wheel nuts according to the Mustang Wheel and Tire procedure while maintaining the specified light loading. Use its fastening requirements for the fitted wheel.

watchFor.title: Wrong orientation or excessive loading
watchFor.body: Both the bottom-positioned high spot and slight suspension loading are required parts of the optimization.

notes: The shared procedure also references Super Duty wheel installation; that branch does not apply to this Mustang job.
The amount of improvement depends on available wheel-to-hub clearance and tire stiffness.

verification.title: Confirm the mounting conditions
verification.body: Confirm the identified high spot was at the bottom and final tightening occurred with only slight suspension loading.

verification.title: Confirm wheel installation completion
verification.body: Verify the wheel nuts were tightened according to the applicable Mustang wheel installation requirements.

procedures.purpose: Wheel-to-hub runout optimization through high-spot orientation and light loading.
Mustang wheel and tire removal, installation and wheel-nut fastening requirements.
Tire-sealant precautions and equipment requirements protecting carbon-fiber and alloy wheels.

guides.title: Replace the ambient air temperature sensor
guides.summary: Replace the front-mounted ambient air temperature sensor using the access route for SVT Performance Package or non-SVT vehicles.
guides.introduction: The ambient air temperature sensor measures the air outside the vehicle. Replacing it involves releasing its electrical connector and mounting, but reaching it accounts for most of the work. The access route differs substantially between SVT Performance Package and non-SVT vehicles, so identify the fitted equipment before removing surrounding parts.
guides.why: The sensor and its connector are separate attachments, and the removal order changes with the equipment branch. Following that order avoids pulling on the wiring while trying to free the sensor. Correct lifting and careful restoration of the shields matter because the work takes place beneath the front of the vehicle.

when.summary: When the ambient air temperature sensor requires replacement following diagnosis or physical damage.
notes: An outside-temperature concern alone does not establish that the sensor needs replacement.
Confirm whether the vehicle has the SVT Performance Package before choosing the access sequence.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and follow the jacking and lifting procedure. Identify the marked lifting points and check adapter clearance around suspension, exhaust and steering components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Plan the equipment-specific access
prepare.detail: Have suitable equipment for shield retainers and, on SVT Performance Package vehicles, right-hand front wheel removal and installation.

steps.title: Position and lift the vehicle
steps.body: Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on a hoist using the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Establish secure access before working beneath the front bumper area.

steps.title: Remove the appropriate underbody shielding
steps.body: On SVT Performance Package vehicles, remove the right-hand front wheel and tire using the [wheel procedure](#/document/G1686507), then follow the underbody-shield removal stages in the [sensor procedure](#/document/G1676756). On non-SVT vehicles, remove the underbody shield to reach the sensor.

steps.title: Complete the SVT access route
steps.body: For the SVT Performance Package branch, remove the pin-type retainers and right-hand brake cooling duct. Remove the splash-shield retainers and position the splash shield aside. Non-SVT vehicles proceed directly to sensor removal.

steps.title: Release the sensor and connection
steps.body: On SVT Performance Package vehicles, disconnect the ambient temperature sensor connector before removing the sensor. On non-SVT vehicles, release the sensor from its mounting first, then disconnect the connector. Follow the branch illustration for the attachment location.

steps.title: Reinstall through the same access route
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal sequence. Restore the sensor mounting and connector, then refit the displaced shields and retainers. On SVT Performance Package vehicles, also restore the brake cooling duct and reinstall the wheel and tire using its procedure.

watchFor.title: Illustration clearance
watchFor.body: The front bumper cover is removed in an illustration for clarity; that does not make bumper-cover removal part of this job.

watchFor.title: Restricted wiring movement
watchFor.body: Release the connector and mounting in the prescribed order rather than using the wiring to move the sensor.

notes: Right-hand access applies to the SVT Performance Package branch; do not add that wheel-removal operation to the non-SVT branch.

verification.title: Check the restored assembly
verification.body: Confirm the sensor is retained in its mounting, its electrical connector is engaged, and every displaced shield, duct and retainer has been restored.

verification.title: Complete wheel installation where required
verification.body: For the SVT Performance Package branch, complete the wheel-and-tire installation requirements before returning the vehicle to service.

procedures.purpose: Sensor removal and installation, including separate SVT Performance Package and non-SVT access sequences.
Lifting points, hoist positioning and safe vehicle support.
Right-hand front wheel removal and installation for the SVT Performance Package branch.

guides.title: Replace and program the driver memory seat module
guides.summary: Replace the driver front seat module, complete its programming, and establish the seat travel limits.
guides.introduction: The driver front seat module (DSM) controls the memory-equipped driver power seat. It receives adjustment requests, powers the appropriate motors and uses motor position signals to track seat movement. It also supports stored positions and easy entry/exit. Replacement therefore involves both a physical module change and an electronic setup process; installing the module alone does not finish the repair.
guides.why: Programmable module installation (PMI) must begin while the original module is still connected so the scan tool can carry out the required configuration process. After replacement, the module also needs established travel limits. These soft stops halt movement just before the mechanical end stops, reducing unnecessary stress on the seat and motors.
searchTerms: memory seat moves in short bursts

when.summary: When diagnosis establishes that the driver memory seat module requires replacement.
notes: A non-memory power seat uses direct switch control and does not follow this DSM replacement path.
PMI and the replacement-specific travel-learning steps apply when installing a new module.

prepare.title: Provide programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of DSM PMI. Keep the original module installed until the initial programming stage has begun; if it cannot communicate, the tool may request As-Built Data.

prepare.title: Provide access and controlled tightening
prepare.detail: The seat must move fully rearward and upward for access. Have suitable screw tools and a torque tool capable of the module's low tightening value.

steps.title: Begin programming with the original module
steps.body: When fitting a new DSM, start PMI with the existing DSM installed and follow the scan-tool prompts. Do this before disconnecting the module. Follow any As-Built Data request if the original module does not respond.

steps.title: Position the driver seat
steps.body: Move the seat to its fully rearward and fully upward position. This creates the working access shown in the [replacement procedure](#/document/G1695506). The left-hand-drive illustration also applies to the similar right-hand-drive arrangement.

steps.title: Remove the module
steps.body: Disconnect the DSM electrical connectors, then remove its screws and lift out the module. Keep the operation focused on the module and its attachments.

steps.title: Install and reconnect
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to fit the DSM. Tighten its screws to 18 lb.in (2 Nm), then restore the electrical connections.

steps.title: Complete module programming
steps.body: For a new DSM, finish PMI using the diagnostic scan tool and its on-screen instructions. This completes the electronic configuration stage of replacement.

steps.title: Establish the seat's soft stops
steps.body: With a new module installed, operate the seat in every direction through its full travel. Follow the [hard-stop and soft-stop description](#/document/G1695508) when establishing the limits. The module learns a stopping position before the physical end of travel to prevent premature stopping after the vehicle is returned.

watchFor.title: Premature stopping after replacement
watchFor.body: Do not treat a short travel range as an acceptable finished result. Complete programming and the required full-travel operation.

watchFor.title: Different seat systems
watchFor.body: Seat heating and cooling are controlled by a separate climate-controlled seat module; a temperature complaint does not by itself identify a DSM fault.

notes: Travel limits also require setting or resetting after replacement of the driver seat track or horizontal motor.

diagnostics.finding: A seat motor moves briefly, stops, and requires the switch to be released and pressed again.
diagnostics.meaning: This is jog mode, associated with loss of a motor position-sensor signal; a diagnostic trouble code is stored in the DSM.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the position-sensor fault before deciding that the DSM itself needs replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The original DSM does not respond during PMI.
diagnostics.meaning: The scan tool may need As-Built Data to continue the replacement configuration.
diagnostics.next: Follow the scan-tool prompts rather than omitting the initial PMI stage.

verification.title: Confirm learned travel
verification.body: Check that the seat has been operated through its full range in every direction and does not stop prematurely.

verification.title: Record setup completion
verification.body: Record completion of PMI and the full-travel soft-stop setting operation for the new module.

procedures.purpose: Driver front seat module removal, installation, replacement programming and travel-limit setup.
Memory-seat operation, position-sensor jog mode and DSM hard-stop/soft-stop behavior.

guides.title: Remove and refit the convertible parcel shelf
guides.summary: Release the convertible's parcel shelf by disconnecting both sensor connectors and moving the top tension-belt adjuster brackets into the interior.
guides.introduction: The convertible parcel shelf forms the trim surface behind the rear seating area. Its removal involves more than releasing the visible shelf retainers: surrounding trim, tonneau cover sensor wiring and convertible-top tension-belt adjuster brackets must also be released. The work moves between the luggage compartment and interior, with matching operations on both sides.
guides.why: The adjuster brackets remain locked to the body until their tabs are released. Trying to lift the shelf before completing these surrounding operations can load connected wiring or retained components. Working through each attachment in sequence makes it clear what still holds the assembly and preserves the parts needed for refitting.

when.summary: When the convertible parcel shelf needs replacement or must be removed for access.
notes: Complete the paired operations on both sides, even where an illustration shows only one side.

prepare.title: Provide access from both areas
prepare.detail: Arrange working access to the luggage compartment and the interior behind the rear seats. The tension-belt adjusters are released from the luggage compartment and then passed inward.

prepare.title: Identify the attachments
prepare.detail: Review the loadspace-trim and parcel-shelf procedures so the pin-type retainers, cover clips, electrical connectors and bracket locking tabs can be released individually.

steps.title: Remove the loadspace trim
steps.body: Remove the loadspace trim panels on both sides using the [convertible loadspace-trim procedure](#/document/G1692610). This exposes the surrounding connections needed for shelf removal.

steps.title: Disconnect the sensors
steps.body: Disconnect the tonneau cover sensor electrical connectors on both sides. Complete this before moving the trim assembly so connected wiring does not restrict removal.

steps.title: Remove both D-tower covers
steps.body: Remove each cover's pin-type retainers, release its clip and remove the cover. The left and right sides follow the same operation.

steps.title: Release the tension-belt adjusters
steps.body: From the luggage compartment, push inward on the rear of each convertible-top tension-belt adjuster to release its locking tabs. Pull the rear of the adjuster downward to disconnect its bracket from the body.

steps.title: Pass the brackets inward and remove the shelf
steps.body: On both sides, push the released adjuster bracket through the body opening into the interior. Then remove the shelf's pin-type retainers and lift out the parcel shelf, following the [parcel-shelf procedure](#/document/G1692611).

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Reinstall the shelf and its retainers, return the adjuster brackets through the body and restore their locked attachments. Refit the D-tower covers, reconnect both sensor connectors and reinstall the loadspace trim panels.

watchFor.title: An adjuster that remains locked
watchFor.body: Release the rear locking tabs before pulling the adjuster downward; shelf movement is not the release action.

watchFor.title: An unfinished opposite side
watchFor.body: Check both sides before lifting the shelf, especially the electrical connectors and adjuster brackets.

notes: This procedure releases the tension-belt adjuster brackets from the body; it does not call for changing their adjustment.

verification.title: Check paired attachments
verification.body: Confirm both adjuster brackets are restored to their locked body attachments and both tonneau cover sensor connectors are reconnected.

verification.title: Check trim retention
verification.body: Confirm the parcel-shelf retainers, D-tower cover clips and retainers, and both loadspace trim panels are restored.

procedures.purpose: Convertible parcel-shelf removal and installation, including sensor connections and tension-belt adjuster bracket release.
Convertible loadspace trim removal and installation for access on both sides.

guides.title: Replace the rear seat cushion cover
guides.summary: Remove the rear cushion and replace its upholstery cover while preserving the foam's hook-and-loop attachments.
guides.introduction: The rear seat cushion cover is retained in two ways: J-clips and pin-type retainers secure it underneath, while hook-and-loop strips hold it against the shaped foam. Replacement requires removing the cushion from the vehicle, freeing the underside attachments and carefully separating the cover from the foam. The foam pad needs particular care because its fastening strips can be torn away during separation.
guides.why: Pulling harder is the wrong response to either of the main retaining systems. The cushion's floor locking tabs must be pressed to release them, and the cover's hook-and-loop strips must be separated without pulling their anchors out of the foam. Preserving these attachments allows the refitted cover and cushion to remain properly secured.

when.summary: When the rear cushion cover needs replacement or removal for access to the cushion foam.
notes: Plan to remove the complete rear cushion before separating its cover.

prepare.title: Create working access
prepare.detail: Move both front seats fully forward. Provide space to remove the rear cushion and turn it over to reach the cover attachments underneath.

prepare.title: Recognize the different retainers
prepare.detail: Identify the cushion-to-floor locking tabs separately from the cover's J-clips, attaching straps, pin-type retainers and hook-and-loop strips.

steps.title: Release and remove the cushion
steps.body: At the front of the rear cushion, press in the locking tabs to release it from the floor. Lift and release the cushion, then remove it using the [rear-cushion procedure](#/document/G1692168). Do not lift against tabs that remain locked.

steps.title: Free the underside attachments
steps.body: Release the cover's J-clips and pin-type retainers from the underside of the cushion frame. Pass the J-clip attaching straps through the openings in the foam so they no longer tether the cover beneath the cushion.

steps.title: Separate the cover from the foam
steps.body: Carefully separate the cover from each hook-and-loop strip and remove it. Watch the foam-side attachment as you work: the strip must remain attached to the pad. Use the [cover procedure](#/document/G1692169) and its illustration to follow the attachment locations.

steps.title: Restore the cover and cushion
steps.body: Reverse the sequence to fit the cover, engage the hook-and-loop attachments, route the attaching straps through the foam openings and restore the underside J-clips and retainers. Reinstall the cushion with the seatbelt webbing untwisted and the belts and buckles accessible to occupants.

watchFor.title: Foam-side strips lifting away
watchFor.body: If a fastening strip begins pulling out of the foam, stop pulling the cover in that manner and separate the hook-and-loop connection carefully.

watchFor.title: Trapped seatbelts
watchFor.body: Keep the belts and buckles accessible as the cushion returns to position; do not finish with webbing twisted beneath it.

notes: Release the attaching straps before separating the cover so the underside fastenings do not resist removal.

verification.title: Check cover retention
verification.body: Confirm the hook-and-loop attachments are engaged, their foam-side strips remain attached, and the J-clips and pin-type retainers are restored.

verification.title: Check cushion and restraint access
verification.body: Confirm the cushion's floor attachments are engaged and every rear belt and buckle remains accessible with untwisted webbing.

procedures.purpose: Rear seat cushion cover removal and installation, including underside retainers and foam attachment precautions.
Rear cushion removal and installation, floor-tab release and seatbelt positioning.

guides.title: Replace the A/C compressor outlet line
guides.summary: Replace the compressor outlet line using the correct engine procedure, new seals and controlled refrigerant and oil servicing.
guides.introduction: The air conditioning (A/C) compressor outlet line carries refrigerant away from the compressor into the refrigerant circuit. Its connections must contain pressurized refrigerant and remain clean internally. Replacement also involves disconnecting the pressure transducer's electrical connector. The 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures share the same purpose, but their connection layouts and seal instructions must be followed separately.
guides.why: Refrigerant recovery must precede opening the circuit. Once disconnected, exposed ports can admit contamination that then travels through the system. New seals restore the disturbed joints, while the correct quantity of clean refrigerant oil maintains system lubrication. Neither the oil quantity nor the seal-lubrication material should be guessed from another engine's arrangement.

when.summary: When the compressor outlet line is damaged or diagnosis establishes that it requires replacement.
notes: An A/C cooling complaint alone does not establish that the outlet line needs replacement.
Select the engine-specific procedure before opening the refrigerant circuit.

prepare.title: Provide refrigerant-service capability
prepare.detail: Use appropriate recovery, evacuation and charging equipment with the capability to follow the complete refrigerant-service procedure. Recover the refrigerant before loosening a line connection.

prepare.title: Prepare clean protection and new seals
prepare.detail: Have suitable caps or other protective closures ready for every opening. All branches require new O-rings; the 3.7L and 5.0L instructions also require new gasket seals.

prepare.title: Confirm lubrication requirements
prepare.detail: Obtain the correct clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) oil and determine the required amount through the oil-adding procedure. For 2.3L and 5.2L seal lubrication, use only the specified material.

steps.title: Select the engine branch and recover refrigerant
steps.body: Use the matching procedure for [2.3L](#/document/G1676744), [3.7L](#/document/G1676746), [5.0L](#/document/G1676748) or [5.2L](#/document/G1727496). Complete refrigerant recovery through the [system servicing procedure](#/document/G1912323) before opening either connection.

steps.title: Release the compressor connection
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the outlet-line retainer and position the line aside. On the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L, remove the nut and disconnect the outlet line. Protect the open ports immediately. The 3.7L and 5.0L branches require the removed O-rings and gaskets to be discarded.

steps.title: Disconnect the sensor wiring and remove the line
steps.body: Disconnect the A/C pressure transducer electrical connector, then remove the remaining nut and outlet line. Keep every exposed opening protected. Discard the disturbed O-rings and gaskets as directed for the 3.7L and 5.0L branches.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement joints
steps.body: For the 2.3L and 5.2L, install new O-rings and lubricate them only with the specified material. For the 3.7L and 5.0L, install new O-rings and gasket seals. Keep protective closures in place until the connections are ready to be assembled, then remove them.

steps.title: Refit the engine-specific line
steps.body: Reverse the selected removal sequence, restoring the line connections and pressure transducer connector. The connection fasteners identified in each of these procedures are tightened to 159 lb.in (18 Nm). Use the matching illustration to identify the correct attachments.

steps.title: Restore oil and complete system servicing
steps.body: Add the correct amount of clean PAG oil using the [refrigerant oil-adding procedure](#/document/G1912330). Complete the applicable evacuation and charging operations through the linked system servicing procedure, using the vehicle's specified requirements.

watchFor.title: Unprotected openings
watchFor.body: Cap or otherwise protect disconnected ports promptly, and remove the protective materials before assembly.

watchFor.title: Seal requirements carried between engines
watchFor.body: The 3.7L and 5.0L explicitly require gasket seals as well as O-rings. Follow each engine's instructions for its actual joints.

watchFor.title: Assumed oil quantities
watchFor.body: Determine the oil addition from the appropriate procedure rather than estimating it from the replacement line.

notes: The engine-specific illustrations show different outlet-line layouts; use the one matching the vehicle.

verification.title: Confirm the closed assembly
verification.body: Verify new seals are installed, protective closures are removed, the specified connection fasteners are tightened and the pressure transducer connector is restored.

verification.title: Record refrigerant-service completion
verification.body: Record the engine branch, specified oil addition and completion of the applicable evacuation and charging procedure before considering the repair complete.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost outlet-line removal and installation, including retainer release and specified O-ring lubrication.
3.7L Duratec outlet-line removal and installation, including discarded and renewed O-ring and gasket seals.
5.0L outlet-line removal and installation, including discarded and renewed O-ring and gasket seals.
5.2L outlet-line removal and installation, including contamination protection and specified O-ring lubrication.
Refrigerant recovery before opening the circuit and the applicable evacuation and charging operations.
Determine and add the correct amount of clean refrigerant oil after line replacement.

guides.title: Replace the instrument-panel speaker with SYNC, SYNC 2 or SYNC 3
guides.summary: Remove the center trim and speaker grille, exchange the instrument-panel speaker and restore its connector and mountings.
guides.introduction: The instrument-panel speaker converts an electrical audio signal into sound through its grille. Replacement involves a small amount of dashboard trim removal followed by disconnecting the speaker itself. The SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedures use the same removal sequence, although the surrounding audio systems differ. Choose the procedure matching the fitted system.
guides.why: The center finish panel must come off before the speaker grille. Releasing the trim clips with the specified trim tool gives access without treating the panel as a rigid, bolted part. An optional electrical connection behind the finish panel must also be disconnected before that panel is moved away.

when.summary: When the instrument-panel speaker needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: Establish the reason for replacement through the appropriate audio diagnosis; this procedure is a removal and installation path.

prepare.title: Trim and fastener tools
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover, suitable speaker-bolt tools and torque equipment capable of accurately applying the small specified tightening value.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted connections
prepare.detail: The center finish panel may have an optional ICM electrical connector. Follow the actual panel configuration and disconnect that connector if fitted.

steps.title: Open the center-panel access
steps.body: Follow the [center finish panel procedure](#/document/G1693976). Use the interior trim remover to release the right-hand instrument-panel trim clips and remove that panel. Release the center finish panel clips, then disconnect its optional electrical connector before removing the panel.

steps.title: Remove the grille and release the speaker
steps.body: Remove the instrument-panel speaker grille. Remove the speaker bolts and lift the speaker sufficiently to reach its electrical connector. Follow the [SYNC procedure](#/document/G1704852) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure](#/document/G1704856), according to the fitted equipment.

steps.title: Disconnect and exchange the speaker
steps.body: Disconnect the speaker’s electrical connector and remove the speaker. During refitting, reverse this sequence: reconnect the electrical connection, position the speaker and install its bolts. Tighten the speaker bolts to 2.5 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the dashboard trim
steps.body: Refit the speaker grille. Reconnect the optional center-panel connector if it was disconnected, then reinstall the center finish panel and right-hand trim in reverse removal order. Make sure the released clips engage so the panels are retained.

watchFor.title: A tethered finish panel
watchFor.body: If the optional connector is present, disconnect it before carrying the center panel away from the dashboard.

watchFor.title: Small speaker fasteners
watchFor.body: Use the specified low tightening value rather than judging tightness by feel.

notes: Removal instructions also contain the speaker’s installation torque.

verification.title: Speaker installation
verification.body: Confirm the speaker connector is attached and the mounting bolts are tightened to specification.

verification.title: Trim restoration
verification.body: Confirm the grille, center finish panel and right-hand trim are refitted, including any optional panel connection.

procedures.purpose: Instrument-panel speaker removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC.
Instrument-panel speaker removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Right-hand trim and center finish panel removal and refitting to access the speaker grille.

guides.title: Replace the 5.0L muffler inlet pipe
guides.summary: Separate the exhaust connections, release the inlet pipe’s ball clamp and bracket tab, then refit and check for leaks.
guides.introduction: The muffler inlet pipe carries exhaust toward the muffler assembly through a removable section of the exhaust system. This job opens the neighboring clamped connections and releases the inlet pipe’s own ball-clamp joint and retaining tab. It is an underbody repair requiring proper hoist access and careful reassembly of the exhaust joints.
guides.why: Exhaust connections must be clean before they are reassembled so their mating surfaces can seat properly. The bracket tab must be released along with the ball clamp before the pipe is removed. The two clamp locations have different tightening specifications, and a final leak check establishes whether the reassembled system seals.

when.summary: When the muffler inlet pipe requires replacement or removal for access.
notes: An exhaust leak needs to be located before deciding which pipe or connection requires repair.

prepare.title: Safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and identify the approved lifting points from the stamped triangles. Position adapters clear of exhaust, suspension and other underbody components.

prepare.title: Joint and clamp work
prepare.detail: Have suitable clamp tools, torque equipment and the means to clean every exhaust connection opened during the job.

steps.title: Position the vehicle on the hoist
steps.body: Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and follow the [jacking and lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Check lift clearance and adapter placement before raising the vehicle; incorrect contact can damage the exhaust or make the vehicle unstable.

steps.title: Separate the adjoining exhaust assembly
steps.body: Following the [5.0L inlet-pipe procedure](#/document/G1689452), loosen the clamps and separate the muffler and tailpipe from the right-hand catalytic converter and left-hand muffler inlet pipe. These connections must be released before removing the inlet pipe.

steps.title: Release and remove the inlet pipe
steps.body: Loosen the ball clamp, release the bracket tab and remove the muffler inlet pipe. Account for both the clamped joint and the retaining tab rather than trying to withdraw the pipe while either remains engaged.

steps.title: Clean, refit and check
steps.body: Clean all opened exhaust connections before assembly. Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the inlet pipe and bracket engagement, then the muffler and tailpipe connections. Tighten the ball clamp to 30 Nm and the adjoining muffler/tailpipe clamps to 48 Nm. Check the exhaust system for leaks.

watchFor.title: Incorrect vehicle support
watchFor.body: Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The vehicle’s emergency jack is not intended for this repair.

watchFor.title: Confusing clamp specifications
watchFor.body: Keep the inlet pipe’s ball-clamp specification separate from the adjoining exhaust-clamp specification.

notes: This sequence and its clamp specifications apply to the 5.0L exhaust arrangement.

diagnostics.finding: An exhaust leak remains after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The repair has not passed its required sealing check.
diagnostics.next: Locate and correct the leaking connection, then repeat the check.

verification.title: Assembly completion
verification.body: Confirm the bracket tab is restored and each opened clamp is tightened to its correct specification.

verification.title: Recorded leak-check result
verification.body: Record whether the completed exhaust-system leak check passed and identify any connection requiring further correction.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L muffler inlet pipe removal, installation, clamp tightening and final exhaust leak check.
Approved lifting points, hoist positioning and vehicle-support precautions.

guides.title: Replace the 3.7L front-cover coolant-pipe seal
guides.summary: Remove the coolant pump, extract the coolant-pipe seal with the dedicated tool and seat its replacement before refitting the pump.
guides.introduction: This seal closes the joint between the coolant pipe and the engine front cover. On the 3.7L engine, the coolant pump must be removed to reach it. The repair uses a dedicated remover/installer that first extracts the old seal and then supports the replacement as it is driven into position. This is precision sealing work rather than a general pry-out operation.
guides.why: The tool must be engaged and operated in the specified order to release the seal. Correct seating and a damage inspection are equally important during installation. Cleanliness matters throughout: debris entering an oil passage, coolant passage or the oil pan can cause engine failure, including debris produced while cleaning the sealing area.

when.summary: When the front-cover coolant-pipe seal requires replacement during 3.7L engine repair.
notes: Plan the complete coolant-pump removal and installation alongside the seal work.

prepare.title: Dedicated seal tooling
prepare.detail: Have water tube seal remover/installer 303-1528 and a brass hammer. Be able to control the tool’s engagement, extracting screw and installation position.

prepare.title: Pump access and cleanliness
prepare.detail: Follow the linked 3.7L coolant-pump procedure for its preparation, removal and refitting requirements. Arrange cleaning so foreign material cannot enter engine passages or the oil pan.

steps.title: Remove the coolant pump
steps.body: Complete the removal phase of the [3.7L coolant-pump procedure](#/document/G1694559). This provides the access required for the seal tool; the seal replacement sequence begins after the pump has been removed.

steps.title: Engage the removal tool
steps.body: Reset the center bolt of tool 303-1528 to its retracted position. Screw the tool onto the front-cover coolant-pipe seal until it bottoms out. This establishes the tool engagement required before extraction.

steps.title: Release and extract the seal
steps.body: Give the tool a slight inward tap with the brass hammer to loosen the radial seal in the front cover. Then turn the tool’s center bolt clockwise to remove the seal. Follow the illustrated arrangement in the [seal procedure](#/document/G1681523).

steps.title: Clean and install the replacement
steps.body: Clean the front-cover coolant-pipe seal area while keeping debris out of the engine. Position the replacement seal on the special tool, then position the tool into the front cover. Tap the tool with the brass hammer until the seal bottoms out.

steps.title: Inspect before restoring the pump
steps.body: Inspect the installed seal for correct placement and damage before covering the area. Once it is satisfactory, complete the coolant-pump installation using its linked procedure and all associated refitting requirements.

watchFor.title: Contamination from cleaning
watchFor.body: Material removed from the sealing area must not fall into coolant or oil passages or the oil pan.

watchFor.title: Incorrect tool sequence
watchFor.body: Retract the center bolt before threading the tool onto the old seal; the inward release tap precedes turning the extracting screw.

watchFor.title: Damage during seating
watchFor.body: A seal that has bottomed out still requires inspection. Seating depth alone does not establish that it is undamaged.

notes: Use the brass hammer and specified tool for both the release and installation operations.

diagnostics.finding: The installed seal is damaged or incorrectly positioned.
diagnostics.meaning: The required installation inspection has failed.
diagnostics.next: Correct the seal installation before refitting the coolant pump.

verification.title: Record the exposed-seal inspection
verification.body: Confirm and record that the seal is fully seated, correctly installed and free of visible installation damage before the pump is refitted.

verification.title: Complete pump reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the coolant-pump installation and its associated completion requirements have been carried out.

procedures.purpose: 3.7L front-cover coolant-pipe seal extraction, cleaning, installation and inspection using tool 303-1528.
3.7L coolant-pump removal for seal access and installation after the seal inspection.

guides.title: Release a seatbelt locked in its stowed position
guides.summary: Use the appropriate front or rear slack-release sequence, escalating to anchor access or retractor replacement only if the belt remains locked.
guides.introduction: A seatbelt retractor stores webbing on a spool and locks it when restraint is needed. A belt that retracts quickly can sometimes remain locked when stowed without the retractor having failed. Returning a little webbing to the spool may release it. The front and rear procedures create that slack differently, then require a restraint functional test.
guides.why: Only a few millimeters of inward webbing movement may be needed, so controlled feeding is central to this repair. Being able to pull the belt out afterward does not establish that its protective locking functions work correctly. Persistent locking has a defined escalation path rather than calling for immediate replacement.

when.summary: When seatbelt webbing will not extract from its fully stowed position.
notes: Rapid retraction can cause this temporary condition.
Distinguish it from normal automatic locking after a passenger belt has been fully extended.

prepare.title: Identify the seating position and equipment
prepare.detail: Choose the front or rear sequence. Use shoulder-height adjustment or rear-backrest reclining only where actually fitted.

prepare.title: Plan any escalation
prepare.detail: Anchor or pretensioner detachment requires restraint-service capability and the applicable removal and installation instructions, including their safety prerequisites and fastener specifications. Have the appropriate Seatbelt Systems functional test available.

steps.title: Front belt: use the height adjuster where fitted
steps.body: Slowly lower the shoulder-height adjuster so webbing feeds back onto the spool, then try extracting the belt slowly. If the adjuster is already fully down, or this does not release the belt, continue with the pull-and-feed sequence.

steps.title: Front belt: create and return slack
steps.body: Firmly pull out as much belt as possible. Slowly feed the resulting slack into the retractor, then slowly try extracting the belt. If it releases, proceed to restoration and testing. If it remains locked, use the anchor-access stage below.

steps.title: Rear belt: use the seatback to create slack
steps.body: Slowly pull the belt out as far as possible. Compress the backrest foam and recline the rear backrest if equipped, allowing more webbing to return to the spool. Slowly feed in the slack and check whether the belt extracts.

steps.title: Rear belt: repeat with a firm pull
steps.body: If the initial rear sequence does not release the belt, firmly extract as much webbing as possible. Slowly return the slack, then slowly extract the belt again. If it releases, proceed to restoration and testing.

steps.title: Obtain additional slack through the appropriate anchor procedure
steps.body: For a still-locked front belt, follow the applicable procedure to remove the fastener and detach the anchor or anchor-and-pretensioner. For a rear belt, follow its anchor procedure. An inflatable-belt union is a separate equipment-dependent branch requiring confirmed applicability and its own procedure. Feed the freed slack inward, then retry extraction.

steps.title: Restore the attachment or replace the retractor
steps.body: If the belt now extracts, reinstall every removed fastener and tighten to the applicable specification. If it still does not extract after the anchor-slack stage, install a new retractor using the correct removal and installation procedure.

steps.title: Perform the restraint functional test
steps.body: Carry out the appropriate Seatbelt Systems functional test after restoration or replacement. Follow the [release procedure](#/document/G1883858) through this final check; successful webbing release alone is not the completion criterion.

watchFor.title: Confusing automatic locking with a fault
watchFor.body: Passenger-belt Automatic Locking Retractor (ALR) mode engages after full extension and clicks during retraction. Allowing the belt to retract fully disengages this child-seat locking mode.

watchFor.title: Assuming equipment from an illustration
watchFor.body: The illustrated shoulder adjuster is a typical arrangement. It does not establish the equipment fitted to a particular Mustang.

notes: Emergency Locking Retractor (ELR) operation responds to vehicle movement such as hard braking or cornering; use the specified functional test to assess it.

diagnostics.finding: The stowed belt releases after slack is fed inward.
diagnostics.meaning: The release sequence has relieved the locking condition.
diagnostics.next: Restore any disturbed attachments and perform the functional test.

diagnostics.finding: The belt remains locked after the applicable anchor-slack stage.
diagnostics.meaning: The prescribed release sequence has not restored extraction.
diagnostics.next: Replace the retractor, then complete the functional test.

verification.title: Mechanical restoration
verification.body: Confirm all removed attachments are restored and tightened to their applicable specifications.

verification.title: Recorded functional result
verification.body: Record the seating position, whether replacement was needed and the result of the appropriate restraint functional test.

procedures.purpose: Front and rear locked-retractor release sequences, escalation to replacement and required functional testing.
Explanation of emergency and automatic retractor locking modes and their functional-test distinctions.

guides.title: Run audio bezel diagnostics with SYNC, SYNC 2 or SYNC 3
guides.summary: Enter the equipment-specific diagnostic menus to exercise speakers and displays, read module information and record findings for further diagnosis.
guides.introduction: Bezel diagnostics uses the audio controls and display to access built-in checks and identification information. It can exercise speaker outputs, display supported screen tests and retrieve module details or a satellite-radio identifier. Menu availability and entry buttons depend on the fitted system. A failed check narrows the investigation; it does not by itself identify a component for replacement.
guides.why: The two procedures specify different button combinations, especially without a CD player. Speaker testing also moves between the audio control module (ACM) and digital signal processing (DSP) module according to equipment. Choosing the correct branch prevents an unavailable menu or unsuccessful entry attempt from being mistaken for a module failure.

when.summary: When checking audio or display operation, or retrieving module identifiers and satellite-radio information.
notes: Available tests depend on the display, controls and audio equipment actually fitted.

prepare.title: Review service precautions
prepare.detail: Review the linked Health and Safety Precautions. Disable remote start before applicable service work and use the specified personal protection.

prepare.title: Identify the controls
prepare.detail: Identify SYNC generation, CD-player provision and display type. The front controls interface module (FCIM) is the audio control panel; the display may be a front control/display interface module (FCDIM) or front display interface module (FDIM).

steps.title: Set the operating state
steps.body: Switch the ignition ON and operate the audio system in AM/FM mode. Use the entry sequence in the procedure matching the installed equipment.

steps.title: Enter using the SYNC procedure
steps.body: In [G1839609](#/document/G1839609), a CD-equipped system uses EJECT held first, then SEEK UP pressed and held within 1 second. Without a CD player, simultaneously hold steering-wheel SEEK UP and FCIM TUNE UP.

steps.title: Enter using the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure
steps.body: In [G1818028](#/document/G1818028), SYNC equipment with an integrated CD player uses simultaneous control-panel EJECT and SEEK UP. Without an integrated CD player, simultaneously hold steering-wheel SEEK UP and control-panel SEEK UP. Hold until entry; this can take up to 20 seconds.

steps.title: Allow the speaker test to finish
steps.body: If supported, the Speaker Walk-Around Test begins and identifies each speaker on the display. Afterward, use the AHU menu, which identifies the ACM, for speaker testing without DSP; use DSP Diagnostics where that module provides the test.

steps.title: Select the relevant information menu
steps.body: For FCDIM equipment, AHU, EFP/EFP-ICP and supported MFD menus provide software, hardware and calibration numbers. MFD identifies the display. On touchscreen equipment, accessory protocol interface module (APIM) menus provide part/software, configuration and location information. G1839609 lists Global Positioning System (GPS) information; G1818028 also lists IVSU Versions. Other menus identify the ACM, DSP, controls or display.

steps.title: Capture findings and exit
steps.body: Record the relevant test observations and identifiers. If satellite radio is equipped, retrieve its electronic serial number (ESN). Exit with the control-panel On/Off button or Exit Diagnostics.

watchFor.title: Unsupported menu choices
watchFor.body: An absent option may reflect equipment. Do not assume every listed test is available.

watchFor.title: Different control-module labels
watchFor.body: EFP identifies controls communicating over Controller Area Network (CAN); ICP identifies controls using Local Interconnect Network (LIN). G1818028 also provides SDM display identification.

notes: The shared no-SYNC entry and CHR menu branch is outside this SYNC-equipped guide.

diagnostics.finding: A speaker is silent during the walk-around test.
diagnostics.meaning: The commanded output needs investigation; this does not establish a failed speaker.
diagnostics.next: Record the indicated speaker and continue the applicable audio diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: A reception concern needs assessment.
diagnostics.meaning: AHU Radio Signal Strength provides an observation, not a specified pass/fail verdict here.
diagnostics.next: Record the reading; FCDIM equipment may require OK to display it.

diagnostics.finding: A display or touchscreen concern is present.
diagnostics.meaning: Supported MFD Display Test or APIM Touchscreen Activation, Display Test Pattern and red/green/blue (RGB) Pixel Test address different display functions.
diagnostics.next: Record the failing function. Touch Screen Calibration belongs only to the applicable G1839609 touchscreen branch.

diagnostics.finding: Touchscreen-system audio output needs checking.
diagnostics.meaning: APIM Tones Test provides an additional output check; G1839609 also lists Rear Tones Test where equipped.
diagnostics.next: Run the supported test and record the observed output.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostics cannot be entered because controls, display or an applicable audio module are inoperative.
diagnostics.meaning: Identification must be obtained another way while the inoperative component is diagnosed.
diagnostics.next: Read the module label for its part number. For satellite-radio identification unavailable through diagnostics or channel 0, use the ACM label; continue the appropriate Group 415 diagnosis.

verification.title: Recorded diagnostic result
verification.body: Retain the entry procedure used, available tests, observations and required module identifiers. The G1839609 satellite identifier is a 12-digit ESN.

verification.title: Exit confirmed
verification.body: Confirm the system has left bezel diagnostics using On/Off or Exit Diagnostics.

procedures.purpose: SYNC bezel entry, equipment-dependent display and audio menus, satellite ESN retrieval and exit.
SYNC 2/SYNC 3 bezel entry, option-dependent module menus, functional checks and exit.
General health and safety prerequisites for service work.

guides.title: Remove and replace the center air registers
guides.summary: Remove the instrument-panel trim, release the center register clips, and refit the outlets with the trim wiring reconnected.
guides.introduction: The center registers are the adjustable outlets that direct climate-controlled air into the cabin. The climate controls determine temperature, blower speed and air distribution; the registers guide the air leaving these particular openings. Replacing a register involves the surrounding instrument-panel trim and its electrical connection before the register retaining clips become accessible.
guides.why: The registers are held by clips around their bodies. Releasing those clips is the important mechanical step: pulling on the visible outlet does not release its attachment to the trim. The center upper trim also has an electrical connector, so it must be disconnected as part of removal and reconnected during assembly.

when.summary: When a center air register requires removal or replacement.
notes: The illustrated arrangement has center gauges; the procedure for vehicles without center gauges is similar.

prepare.title: Plan the trim access
prepare.detail: Be prepared to remove the instrument-panel side trim and center upper trim, disconnect a trim-panel electrical connector, and release the register clips.

prepare.title: Identify the retaining points
prepare.detail: Use the register illustration to locate the clips around the outlet bodies before attempting to separate them from the panel.

steps.title: Remove the side trim
steps.body: Remove the instrument-panel side trim panel first. This is the opening stage of the access sequence in the [center register procedure](#/document/G1676807).

steps.title: Remove the center upper trim
steps.body: Remove the instrument-panel center upper trim panel and disconnect its electrical connector. Treat the wiring connection as part of panel removal, rather than allowing the loose panel to remain attached by its wiring.

steps.title: Release the registers
steps.body: Locate and release the retaining clips, then remove the center registers. The illustration shows the clips around the register bodies; release these attachments before withdrawing the outlets.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Install the registers into the trim and engage their retaining clips. Reconnect the center upper trim electrical connector, reinstall that panel, and then reinstall the instrument-panel side trim.

watchFor.title: A register remains attached
watchFor.body: Check the retaining clips before applying more force. An attachment that has not released can keep the register secured to the panel.

watchFor.title: A forgotten trim connector
watchFor.body: Reconnect the electrical connector before completing center upper trim installation.

notes: This repair changes the air outlet assembly. It does not establish the cause of a heating, cooling or blower complaint.

verification.title: Confirm the reverse assembly is complete
verification.body: Confirm the register clips are engaged, the center upper trim connector is reattached, and both removed trim panels are installed.

procedures.purpose: Center register removal and installation, including trim access and clip release; vehicles with center gauges are illustrated, with nongauge vehicles similar.

guides.title: Replace transmission cooler tubes on 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L models
guides.summary: Replace the automatic-transmission cooler tubes using the correct quick-disconnect tool, engine-specific access sequence and final fluid-level procedure.
guides.introduction: The automatic transmission sends fluid through an external cooler ahead of the radiator and receives it back through the cooler tubes. Air passing over the cooler carries away heat from the fluid. This job replaces the connecting tubes and restores their supported, sealed connections. The three engine versions share the same general sequence, but the 3.7L requires additional access work at the left-hand catalyst monitor sensor.
guides.why: The quick-connect fittings have secondary latches that must be removed before disconnection and restored afterward. The transmission connection uses band seals and backing rings, which require lubrication during assembly. Brackets secure the tube routing, while the final fluid-level check addresses any fluid lost during the work.

when.summary: When a transmission cooler tube or its connection has been identified as requiring repair or replacement.
notes: Choose the procedure by engine; the catalyst monitor sensor removal applies to the 3.7L branch.

prepare.title: Provide safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist with the vehicle in NEUTRAL. Follow the lifting procedure, locating the triangle-marked lifting points and checking hoist clearance. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Have the fitting tool and specified fluid
prepare.detail: Use quick-disconnect tool 307-695. Seal and backing-ring lubrication requires Motorcraft MERCON LV Automatic Transmission Fluid, XT-10-QLVC, specification WSS-M2C938-A.

prepare.title: Prepare for engine-specific work
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastening and torque equipment. For the 3.7L, also have the catalyst monitor sensor procedure available; all versions require the 6R80 fluid-level procedure.

steps.title: Lift using the correct procedure
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on the hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Check that the adapters and lifting equipment will not contact vulnerable underbody components.

steps.title: Disconnect the cooler fittings
steps.body: Remove the fittings' secondary latches, then use tool 307-695 to disconnect the cooler tube fittings. Follow the matching [2.3L](#/document/G1694309), [3.7L](#/document/G1694316) or [5.0L](#/document/G1694318) procedure.

steps.title: Release the supports and additional access
steps.body: Remove the bracket-to-engine mount nut and bracket-to-transmission nut. On the 3.7L, next remove the left-hand catalyst monitor sensor using its [removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1692247).

steps.title: Remove the tubes and prepare the seals
steps.body: Remove the retaining bolt and cooler tubes. If necessary, remove the backing rings and band seals from the transmission. Lubricate the band seals and backing rings with the specified transmission fluid for assembly.

steps.title: Attach the tubes at the transmission
steps.body: Position the tubes, attach them to the transmission and install the bolt to the specified torque. On the 3.7L, reinstall the left-hand catalyst monitor sensor at this stage.

steps.title: Restore the brackets and fitting locks
steps.body: Install and tighten the bracket-to-transmission nut, followed by the bracket-to-engine mount nut, using the matching procedure's torque specifications. Connect the cooler tube fittings and reinstall their secondary latches.

steps.title: Complete the fluid-level check
steps.body: Check and adjust the transmission fluid level using the [6R80 fluid-level procedure](#/document/G1692053). Tube installation alone does not establish the correct operating fluid level.

watchFor.title: Missing secondary latches
watchFor.body: Fitting reconnection is incomplete until the secondary latches have also been installed.

watchFor.title: Incorrect seal assumptions
watchFor.body: The procedure calls for conditional removal and lubrication of the band seals and backing rings; it does not direct blanket disposal of those parts.

notes: The selected illustration shows the 5.0L tube assembly at the transmission.

verification.title: Check assembly completion
verification.body: Confirm the transmission attachment, both bracket attachments and fitting secondary latches are restored. On the 3.7L, include catalyst monitor sensor reinstatement.

verification.title: Record the fluid-level result
verification.body: Record completion of the prescribed fluid-level check and whether adjustment was required.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost transmission cooler tube removal and installation.
3.7L Duratec transmission cooler tube removal and installation, including left-hand catalyst monitor sensor access.
5.0L transmission cooler tube removal and installation.
Correct lifting points, hoist positioning and underbody support precautions.
3.7L catalyst monitor sensor removal and installation required during cooler tube access.
Final 6R80 transmission fluid-level check and adjustment.

guides.title: Replace and configure the SYNC non-touchscreen display module
guides.summary: Remove the front control/display interface module and use the scan-tool installation process to transfer its configuration when fitting a replacement.
guides.introduction: The front control/display interface module (FCDIM) provides the non-touchscreen display in this SYNC information and entertainment system. It works within a system that also has a separate audio unit, SYNC interface and front control panel. Removing it requires access through the front controls interface module (FCIM). Replacing it also requires configuration work, so the job begins before the old display is disconnected.
guides.why: A replacement module needs the vehicle's existing configuration information. The programmable module installation (PMI) process uploads that information to a diagnostic scan tool before removal and downloads it into the replacement after installation. Fitting the hardware without completing that process leaves the replacement work unfinished.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for FCDIM replacement, or the module must be removed for access.
notes: Configuration upload must precede removal when a new module is being installed.
The final PMI completion step is required when replacing the component.

prepare.title: Arrange scan-tool capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of performing FCDIM PMI and follow its on-screen instructions. Plan configuration capture while the original module is still installed.

prepare.title: Prepare the control-panel access
prepare.detail: Be able to remove and reinstall the FCIM before working on the display module behind it. Have suitable tools for the module bolts and their low tightening torque.

steps.title: Begin the configuration process
steps.body: Begin FCDIM PMI with the diagnostic scan tool as directed in the [module procedure](#/document/G1704851). If installing a new module, upload the existing configuration before removing the original unit.

steps.title: Remove the front control panel
steps.body: Remove the FCIM to expose the display-module attachment. Keep the distinction clear: the access panel and the FCDIM are separate components in this sequence.

steps.title: Release and disconnect the display module
steps.body: Remove the FCDIM mounting bolts, remove the module and disconnect its electrical connector. The illustration identifies the mounting points and the connector at the rear of the unit.

steps.title: Install the module and restore access trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the electrical connector, position the FCDIM and install its bolts. Tighten the bolts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm), then reinstall the FCIM.

steps.title: Complete PMI for a replacement
steps.body: When a replacement module has been fitted, complete FCDIM PMI using the scan tool's on-screen instructions. Download the configuration captured before removal into the new module.

watchFor.title: Old module removed too early
watchFor.body: Do not dismantle first and leave configuration capture until afterward. Uploading the configuration is a prerequisite to removing a module that will be replaced.

watchFor.title: Replacement configuration unfinished
watchFor.body: A connected and bolted-in replacement is not the end of the job; the required PMI process must also be completed.

notes: A display complaint alone does not establish that the FCDIM has failed; it is one component within the information and entertainment system.
