This procedure applies to the specified non-touchscreen SYNC display arrangement.

verification.title: Confirm physical installation
verification.body: Confirm the electrical connector is reattached, the mounting bolts are tightened and the FCIM is reinstalled.

verification.title: Record configuration completion
verification.body: For a replacement, record completion of PMI and the configuration download. If the scan-tool process cannot be completed, retain that as an unresolved installation issue.

procedures.purpose: SYNC FCDIM removal and installation, including configuration capture before replacement and PMI completion afterward.

guides.title: Replace the 6R80 transmission output shaft seal
guides.summary: Remove the driveshaft and output flange, install a new output shaft seal, and secure the flange with a new tightened and staked retaining nut.
guides.introduction: The output shaft seal retains transmission fluid where the rotating output assembly leaves the transmission. The output flange connects that assembly to the driveshaft. Reaching the seal therefore requires driveshaft and flange removal, followed by controlled installation of a new seal. This is an external sealing repair on the 6R80 automatic transmission, with a final fluid-level check before completion.
guides.why: The flange retaining nut is mechanically locked by staking. Its stakes must be removed before the nut is undone to avoid damaging the output shaft. The old nut and output shaft seal are discarded. Dedicated installers position the new seal, and the replacement nut must be both tightened and staked to prevent it from coming loose.

when.summary: When the output shaft seal has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: The work requires driveshaft removal and installation as separate access operations.

prepare.title: Have the access procedure available
prepare.detail: Be equipped to perform the applicable Driveshaft removal and installation procedure before opening the transmission output assembly.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified installers
prepare.detail: Use installer 205-199 (T83T-3132-A1), Installer, Spindle/Axle Shaft, together with 307-715, Installer, Output Seal (4X2). A punch is required for removing and making the nut stakes.

prepare.title: Obtain the required new parts
prepare.detail: Have a new output shaft seal and a new output shaft flange retaining nut. Also have suitable torque equipment and access to the 6R80 fluid-level procedure.

steps.title: Remove the driveshaft
steps.body: Follow the applicable Driveshaft procedure to expose the output flange. Use the [output shaft seal procedure](#/document/G1692057) for the subsequent transmission-side sequence.

steps.title: Remove the nut stakes before loosening
steps.body: Use a punch to remove the stakes from the output shaft flange retaining nut. Only after releasing this mechanical lock should the nut be removed; discard the old nut.

steps.title: Remove the flange and old output seal
steps.body: Remove the output shaft flange seal and the output shaft flange. Then remove and discard the output shaft seal. Keep the flange seal distinct from the output shaft seal being replaced.

steps.title: Install the new output shaft seal
steps.body: Position the new seal on the specified special-tool assembly. Use installers 205-199 and 307-715 to install it as directed, rather than improvising a seating depth or installation method.

steps.title: Restore the flange assembly
steps.body: Install the output shaft flange and its flange seal. Fit a new output shaft flange retaining nut and tighten it to 59 lb.ft (80 Nm).

steps.title: Stake the tightened nut
steps.body: After tightening, use the punch to stake the nut slots. This is the required locking operation that prevents the retaining nut from coming loose.

steps.title: Reinstall the driveshaft and check fluid
steps.body: Install the driveshaft using its applicable procedure, then perform the [transmission fluid-level check](#/document/G1692053). Complete that check rather than assuming the previous level remains correct.

watchFor.title: Turning a nut that is still staked
watchFor.body: The stakes must be removed first. Forcing the retained nut loose can damage the output shaft.

watchFor.title: Reusing a discarded part
watchFor.body: Both the output shaft seal and flange retaining nut require new replacements.

watchFor.title: Tightening without locking
watchFor.body: Torque and staking are separate required operations; completing one does not replace the other.

notes: The output shaft flange seal is removed and reinstalled in this sequence; it is not the same part as the output shaft seal explicitly marked for disposal.

verification.title: Confirm the flange is secured
verification.body: Confirm the new retaining nut has been tightened to specification and its slots staked, and that driveshaft installation is complete.

verification.title: Record the final fluid check
verification.body: Record the result of the prescribed transmission fluid-level check alongside completion of the nut tightening and staking operations.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 output shaft seal removal and installation, including flange removal, new seal and nut requirements, and nut staking.
Transmission fluid-level check after output shaft seal and driveshaft installation.

guides.title: Replace the front door side impact sensor
guides.summary: Depower the restraint system, replace the door-mounted impact sensor with a flush mounting joint, and complete the prescribed repowering procedure.
guides.introduction: The front door side impact sensor supplies information to the supplemental restraint system (SRS). The restraints control module evaluates sensor inputs and determines whether appropriate restraint components need to deploy during a crash. Replacement requires door-trim access, an electrical disconnection and a precisely restored mounting joint. Although the sensor is small, its installation is part of the vehicle's crash-protection system.
guides.why: Correct restraint operation depends on following the repair sequence, including SRS depowering before access and repowering after assembly. The sensor mating surfaces must be smooth and permit flush attachment. Incorrect repair can compromise restraint operation and increase the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.
searchTerms: front door side impact sensor replacement

when.summary: When restraint-system diagnosis identifies a need to remove or replace the front door side impact sensor.
notes: An illuminated airbag warning indicator alone does not identify the door sensor as the failed component.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system service capability
prepare.detail: Have the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures available and the capability to perform them. These are required stages of the repair.

prepare.title: Prepare trim and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have the front door trim procedure, suitable fastener tools and a torque tool capable of accurately tightening the sensor's small mounting bolts.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete [SRS Depowering](#/document/G1696297) before beginning door-trim and sensor removal. Follow the entire procedure rather than substituting an assumed power-disconnection shortcut.

steps.title: Expose the sensor
steps.body: Remove the front door trim panel using the [door trim procedure](#/document/G1692600). This provides access to the sensor and its connector.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Following the [side impact sensor procedure](#/document/G1696303), disconnect the electrical connector, remove the mounting bolts and remove the sensor. Preserve this order while the SRS remains depowered.

steps.title: Check the mounting interface
steps.body: Before installation, confirm that the sensor and door mating surfaces are smooth and allow flush attachment. If they cannot meet flush, resolve the mounting condition before fastening the sensor.

steps.title: Install and reconnect
steps.body: Reverse removal: position the sensor, install its bolts and tighten them to 17 lb.in (1.9 Nm). Reconnect the electrical connector and reinstall the front door trim panel.

steps.title: Repower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete [SRS Repowering](#/document/G1696298) after assembly. Repowering is a prescribed procedure, not simply an instruction to restore electrical power by any convenient method.

watchFor.title: A sensor that will not sit flush
watchFor.body: Do not treat tightening the bolts as a way to compensate for an unsuitable mating surface.

watchFor.title: An unresolved airbag warning
watchFor.body: An illuminated indicator after repowering requires further restraint-system diagnosis; physical replacement alone does not establish that the system is fault-free.

notes: Connector Position Assurance (CPA) details for deployable restraint components must not be assumed to describe the door sensor connector.

diagnostics.finding: An airbag warning is associated with below-threshold resistance at a deployable-component circuit.
diagnostics.meaning: A CPA tab that is not fully seated can leave that component's shorting bars engaged even though its connector pins make contact. This does not prove a failed door sensor.
diagnostics.next: Continue the applicable restraint-system diagnosis under its required safety procedures and address the identified connector condition.

verification.title: Confirm mounting and reassembly
verification.body: Confirm flush sensor attachment, correct bolt tightening, connector reconnection and door-trim installation.

verification.title: Record restraint-system completion
verification.body: Record completion of the prescribed repowering procedure and any remaining airbag warning indication. Keep an unresolved warning open for diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: Front door side impact sensor removal and installation, including mounting-surface and bolt-tightening requirements.
Required SRS depowering before sensor access and disconnection.
Front door trim removal and installation for sensor access.
Required SRS repowering after sensor and trim installation.

guides.title: Remove, refit and center the transmission support crossmember
guides.summary: Support the transmission, preserve the crossmember’s orientation and center it around the support-insulator studs before tightening.
guides.introduction: The transmission crossmember bolts to the body and supports the transmission through its support insulator. It also contributes to underbody structural support. Removing it temporarily interrupts that support, so the transmission needs its own stand before any mounting hardware comes off. Refitting involves both restoring the original orientation and centering the crossmember around the insulator studs.
guides.why: The crossmember’s orientation affects the driveline angle. Installing it incorrectly can produce shudder when accelerating from a stop or make engine vibration more noticeable. Centering, called neutralizing in the procedure, establishes equal clearance around the insulator studs before the hardware locks the crossmember in place.
searchTerms: shudder accelerating from a stop after crossmember work
engine vibration after transmission support work

when.summary: When the crossmember needs removal for repair or refitting after transmission support work.
notes: The procedure illustrates an automatic transmission; the manual-transmission operation is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange secure lifting and transmission support
prepare.detail: Use a hoist, a vehicle/axle stand and a wooden block. Follow the lifting procedure, identify the correct support points and check that hoist adapters cannot damage nearby suspension, exhaust or steering components.

prepare.title: Preserve the installation position
prepare.detail: Have a clear way to record the crossmember’s orientation and component positions before removal, plus torque tools for the mounting hardware. The vehicle’s emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this work.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle in neutral
steps.body: Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on the hoist following the lifting procedure. Check underbody clearance and support-point engagement before working underneath; never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

steps.title: Support the transmission and record the orientation
steps.body: Support the transmission with the stand and wooden block. Note the crossmember’s installed direction and the positions of its associated components so those relationships can be restored.

steps.title: Remove the crossmember
steps.body: Remove the two nuts joining the transmission support insulator to the crossmember. Then remove the four crossmember bolts and the crossmember, leaving the transmission independently supported.

steps.title: Refit with the hardware loose
steps.body: Position the crossmember in exactly its original orientation. Loosely install the insulator nuts, followed by the crossmember bolts. Leaving both connections loose allows the assembly to move for centering.

steps.title: Neutralize and tighten in order
steps.body: Move the crossmember forward, rearward and sideways until the gaps between the insulator studs and crossmember are equal. Maintain that position while tightening the insulator nuts to 80 Nm, then the crossmember bolts to 63 Nm.

watchFor.title: Unequal clearance around the studs
watchFor.body: Unequal gaps mean the neutralizing operation is unfinished. Correct the position before final tightening.

watchFor.title: A reversed crossmember
watchFor.body: Bolt alignment alone does not establish correct orientation. Compare the installed direction with the positions recorded before removal.

notes: Orientation and neutralization are separate requirements; completing one does not establish the other.

diagnostics.finding: Launch shudder or increased engine vibration appears after crossmember work.
diagnostics.meaning: An incorrectly oriented crossmember can change the driveline angle; the symptom alone does not identify a failed component.
diagnostics.next: Recheck the installed orientation and the required neutralization.

verification.title: Confirm the installed relationship
verification.body: Verify that the crossmember matches its original orientation and that the insulator-stud gaps are equal.

verification.title: Record final fastening
verification.body: Record completion of neutralization and the final tightening of the insulator nuts followed by the crossmember bolts.

procedures.purpose: Complete crossmember removal, original-orientation installation, neutralization and final tightening.
Correct vehicle lifting points, hoist positioning and support precautions.

guides.title: Replace the rear lower arm in the front suspension
guides.summary: Replace the front suspension’s rear lower arm using new mounting hardware, loaded-suspension tightening and the applicable calibration and toe checks.
guides.introduction: Here, rear lower arm means the rearward lower arm of the front suspension. It connects the frame to the front wheel spindle through a pivot and ball joint, helping locate the wheel while allowing suspension movement. Replacement requires controlled ball-joint separation, new specified fasteners and final tightening with the suspension at its normal resting height.
guides.why: The ball-joint seal can be damaged by the wrong separating tool or by allowing the released parts to fall into position. Tightening the frame pivot with the suspension hanging can produce incorrect clamp load and damage the bushing. Vehicles with dynamic suspension also need their height-sensor linkage protected and their ride height recalibrated after reassembly.
searchTerms: front suspension rear lower arm replacement
ride height calibration after lower arm replacement
front toe after suspension arm replacement

when.summary: When an established front-suspension repair requires removal or replacement of the rear lower arm.
notes: The height-sensor and scan-tool operations apply only to vehicles with dynamic suspension.

prepare.title: Gather the specified separator and support equipment
prepare.detail: Use lower-arm ball-joint separator 204-592, vehicle/axle stands and appropriate torque tools. Arrange wheel-removal access and the ability to support the suspension at curb height.

prepare.title: Obtain new critical fasteners
prepare.detail: Have a new arm-to-frame bolt and a new outboard nut. Suspension fasteners must meet the original or equivalent specification; inferior-quality or substitute-design hardware is unsuitable.

prepare.title: Plan the finishing work
prepare.detail: Arrange a front-toe check and adjustment capability. Dynamic-suspension vehicles also require a scan tool that can perform the Ride Height Calibration routine.

steps.title: Expose the arm and protect the height sensor
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire using the linked procedure. On dynamic-suspension vehicles, remove the ride-height sensor arm bracket bolt and position the bracket aside before disturbing the suspension.

steps.title: Separate the outboard ball joint
steps.body: Remove and discard the outboard nut. Separate the arm from the wheel spindle with separator 204-592. Control the released components as they settle so the ball-joint seal is not damaged.

steps.title: Remove the frame connection
steps.body: Remove and discard the arm-to-frame bolt, then remove the arm. Both discarded fasteners must be replaced during installation.

steps.title: Fit the arm without locking the frame pivot
steps.body: Position the arm and install the new frame bolt finger tight only. Attach the arm to the wheel spindle, install the new outboard nut and tighten it to the specified torque.

steps.title: Load the suspension before tightening the pivot
steps.body: Support the suspension at curb height with vehicle/axle stands, then tighten the frame bolt as specified. This preserves the required bushing installation condition instead of clamping the pivot with the suspension hanging.

steps.title: Restore dynamic-suspension equipment where fitted
steps.body: Reposition the height-sensor arm bracket and tighten its bolt as specified. Connect the scan tool and complete Ride Height Calibration, following the tool’s directions.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and check front toe
steps.body: Install the wheel and tire using its procedure. Check front toe and adjust it if necessary using the Front Toe Adjustment procedure referenced in the arm instructions.

watchFor.title: Prying against the joint or seal
watchFor.body: Do not insert a pry tool or separator fork between the ball joint and wheel knuckle. Any permitted pry-bar use is through the lower arm’s body opening only.

watchFor.title: A connected height-sensor linkage during removal
watchFor.body: Leaving the sensor attached can damage the sensor or dynamic-suspension system as the arm moves.

notes: Curb height describes the suspension’s normal resting position, not the fully extended position produced by lifting the body.

verification.title: Confirm the fastening conditions
verification.body: Confirm that the outboard nut and frame bolt are new, and that the frame bolt received final tightening with the suspension loaded.

verification.title: Record the finishing results
verification.body: Record the front-toe check and any adjustment. Where dynamic suspension is fitted, also record successful completion of Ride Height Calibration.

procedures.purpose: Front suspension rear-lower-arm removal and installation, including the dynamic-suspension branch and final toe check.
Wheel-and-tire removal and installation for access to the front suspension arm.

guides.title: Remove and refit the climate control housing using the correct engine procedure
guides.summary: Remove the climate control housing behind the instrument panel, then restore its refrigerant and coolant connections using engine-specific instructions.
guides.introduction: The climate control housing forms the cabin heating and cooling assembly behind the instrument panel, with connections to the heater core and air-conditioning evaporator. Removing it opens both the refrigerant and engine-coolant circuits. The work therefore combines substantial interior access with controlled fluid-system service, even though the housing itself comes out as an assembly.
guides.why: Open refrigerant connections must stay protected from contamination, and their seals require the correct installation materials. Refrigerant oil replacement and cooling-system filling are part of completing the repair. Engine variants share the general removal path, but their fastener details, hose access and finishing procedures must remain with the correct engine.

when.summary: When an established repair requires removal or replacement of the climate control housing.
notes: Select the engine-specific procedure before starting; the housing instructions do not diagnose a heating or cooling complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange the required service capabilities
prepare.detail: Provide refrigerant recovery, evacuation and charging capability, instrument-panel removal capability, and equipment for the correct engine’s cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare connection protection and materials
prepare.detail: Have suitable caps or other protective closures, specified seal lubricant and the required clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) refrigerant oil. Obtain new O-rings where required by the selected engine procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare the engine-specific access
prepare.detail: The 5.0L route also requires engine appearance-cover removal and locking pliers to clamp the heater hoses before disconnection.

steps.title: Recover refrigerant and remove the instrument panel
steps.body: Choose the housing procedure for the fitted engine. Recover the refrigerant before opening the air-conditioning circuit, then remove the instrument panel following its complete access procedure and prerequisites.

steps.title: Disconnect and protect the refrigerant lines
steps.body: Remove the nut and thermostatic expansion valve (TXV) bracket. Disconnect the condenser outlet and evaporator outlet lines, immediately protecting their open ports against debris.

steps.title: Disconnect the heater-core hoses
steps.body: Disconnect the heater-core inlet and outlet hoses. On the 5.0L, first remove the appearance cover and clamp the hoses with locking pliers. If cover grommets remain in the cover, move them onto the intake manifold before refitting it.

steps.title: Release the housing mountings
steps.body: Follow the selected procedure’s illustrated sequence for the bolts, washers, nuts and retaining bracket, then remove the housing. Keep the hardware associated with its mounting location.

steps.title: Position and fasten the housing
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, using the chosen engine’s fastener locations and tightening specifications. The 3.7L has a different torque at the second nut-and-washer location; use its own mounting instructions.

steps.title: Restore the connections and refrigerant oil
steps.body: Remove protective closures before reconnecting the hoses and lines. The 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures specifically require new O-rings lubricated only with the specified material. Follow the selected connection instructions and add the correct amount of clean PAG oil using Refrigerant Oil Adding.

steps.title: Complete refrigerant and cooling-system service
steps.body: Finish reassembly through the instrument-panel procedure. Use the linked recovery, evacuation and charging procedure to restore refrigerant service, and fill and bleed the cooling system using the procedure for the fitted engine.

watchFor.title: Unprotected openings
watchFor.body: Protect openings throughout removal, but remove every temporary closure before its connection is assembled.

watchFor.title: Borrowed specifications
watchFor.body: Do not transfer seal lubricant, oil quantity, charge quantity or cooling-system instructions between engine variants.

notes: Electronic manual temperature control and dual automatic temperature control provide different cabin controls; neither changes the need to select the correct engine service route.

verification.title: Check connection and mounting completion
verification.body: Confirm that the housing and bracket are fastened to the engine-specific instructions, the hoses and lines are reconnected, and required new seals were installed.

verification.title: Record fluid-service completion
verification.body: Record the selected engine, refrigerant-oil addition, completion of refrigerant service, and completion of the matching cooling-system fill and bleed.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost housing removal and installation, including new refrigerant seals.
3.7L Duratec housing removal and installation with its distinct mounting torque.
5.0L housing removal and installation, including appearance-cover access, hose clamping and new seals.
5.2L housing removal and installation, including new refrigerant seals.
Instrument-panel removal and installation for housing access.
Air-conditioning refrigerant recovery, evacuation and charging.
Determine and add the correct refrigerant-oil amount.
2.3L cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.
3.7L cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.
5.0L cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.
5.2L cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.

guides.title: Replace the front brake disc shield with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Remove the front brake disc for shield access, then reinstall the shield and brake assembly with new caliper bolts.
guides.introduction: The brake disc shield is a stationary protective panel beside the rotating front disc. On the 5.2L with the SVT Performance Package, reaching its mounting bolts requires removing the disc first. The shield replacement is brief, but the surrounding brake work demands careful caliper support, clean disc mounting faces and correct fastener replacement.
guides.why: The brake hose must not carry the caliper’s weight while the disc is removed. Dirt left between disc mating surfaces can prevent proper seating. The caliper bolts are discarded during removal, so new bolts are part of this job even though the shield instructions simply call for reversing the removal sequence.
searchTerms: SVT Performance Package front brake disc shield

when.summary: When an established front-brake repair requires removal or replacement of the disc shield.
notes: Use the brake-disc procedure specifically for the SVT Performance Package.

prepare.title: Arrange wheel access and caliper support
prepare.detail: Follow the wheel-and-tire access instructions referenced by the brake-disc procedure. Have suitable support for the removed caliper, new caliper bolts and appropriate torque tools.

prepare.title: Prepare the disc-cleaning materials
prepare.detail: Have a wire brush and the specified Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner or Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B.

steps.title: Move the caliper clear
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire. Remove and discard the caliper bolts, then position the caliper and pads aside with the caliper supported independently of its brake hose.

steps.title: Remove the disc and shield
steps.body: Handle the brake disc carefully during removal. With the disc clear, remove the shield bolts and lift away the shield, following the illustrated mounting arrangement.

steps.title: Install the shield and restore the disc
steps.body: Refit the shield and tighten its bolts to 12 Nm. Clean the brake-disc mating surfaces with the wire brush and specified cleaner before reinstalling the disc.

steps.title: Complete the brake assembly
steps.body: Restore the caliper and pads using new caliper bolts tightened to the brake-disc procedure’s specification. Refit the wheel and tire, then apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake-system operation.

watchFor.title: Caliper weight on the hose
watchFor.body: Do not let the caliper hang from the brake hose; this can damage the hose.

watchFor.title: Confusing fastener specifications
watchFor.body: The shield and caliper bolts have different tightening requirements. Use the specification for the fastener being installed.

notes: The brake-disc access procedure is an essential part of completing the shield replacement.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Check that the shield is fastened, the disc mating surfaces were cleaned and new caliper bolts were used.

verification.title: Verify brake operation
verification.body: Complete the specified repeated brake-pedal applications and verify correct brake-system operation before returning the vehicle to use.

procedures.purpose: SVT Performance Package front brake-disc-shield removal, installation and bolt tightening.
SVT Performance Package disc access, caliper-bolt replacement, mating-surface cleaning and brake-operation verification.

guides.title: Replace an active noise control microphone: front, coupe rear or convertible rear
guides.summary: Access the identified active noise control microphone through the appropriate trim, release its retaining tabs and connector, and restore the assembly.
guides.introduction: An active noise control (ANC) microphone provides cabin-sound information to the noise-control system. Replacing it involves releasing its mounting tabs and electrical connection, but reaching it depends on its location and the body style. The front microphone is accessed through the overhead console; rear access differs substantially between a coupe and a convertible.
guides.why: Choosing the correct access branch avoids disturbing unrelated trim. The microphone must be released from its retaining features rather than pulled free with them engaged, and its electrical connection must be restored during installation. Confirm the actual equipment first: the system feature overviews identify ANC on the 2.3L only.

when.summary: When an identified ANC microphone requires replacement or removal during related interior work.
notes: Confirm the microphone location, body style and installed infotainment system before selecting the access route.
A cabin-noise concern alone does not establish that a microphone needs replacement.

prepare.title: Select the matching procedure
prepare.detail: Use the SYNC microphone procedure or the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 version for the installed system. Both describe front, coupe-rear and convertible-rear access branches.

prepare.title: Arrange the required trim access
prepare.detail: Be prepared to remove the overhead console, lower the coupe headliner, or remove the convertible rear seat backrest and upper loadspace trim. Follow the complete access procedure named for the selected branch.

steps.title: Identify the microphone being serviced
steps.body: Confirm whether the repair concerns the front microphone or a rear microphone. Follow only the relevant location and body-style branch below; these are alternative access routes.

steps.title: Front microphone: remove the overhead console
steps.body: Remove the console using its linked procedure. Release the microphone retaining tab and disconnect its electrical connector, then remove the microphone. The attachment and connector are separate release points.

steps.title: Coupe rear microphone: lower the headliner
steps.body: Use the Headliner - Lowering procedure referenced in the microphone article. Once access is available, release the microphone tabs, remove the microphone from its mounting and disconnect the electrical connector.

steps.title: Convertible rear microphone: open the loadspace trim access
steps.body: Remove the rear seat backrest using the convertible-specific procedure. Position the safety-belt guide aside, release the trim clips and remove the upper loadspace trim panel. Disconnect the electrical connector, then release the microphone tabs and remove it. The illustrated right-hand operation also applies similarly on the left.

steps.title: Install and restore the selected access route
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence for the branch used, reconnecting the electrical connection and engaging the microphone retainers. Restore the overhead console, coupe headliner, or convertible trim, safety-belt guide and backrest through their respective installation instructions.

watchFor.title: Confusing microphone functions
watchFor.body: The system descriptions also list a SYNC microphone. Confirm that the identified part is the ANC microphone before following this replacement route.

watchFor.title: Missing a convertible access step
watchFor.body: The rear seat backrest, safety-belt guide and upper loadspace trim all form part of convertible access. Restore each item during reassembly.

notes: Do not infer ANC fitment on another engine solely from the broad applicability of a microphone removal article.

verification.title: Confirm microphone attachment
verification.body: Check that the microphone is retained by its tabs and its electrical connector is reconnected before closing the access area.

verification.title: Confirm interior restoration
verification.body: Verify completion of the selected console, headliner or convertible trim installation, including the safety-belt guide and backrest where disturbed.

procedures.purpose: ANC microphone removal and installation for SYNC, covering front, coupe-rear and convertible-rear locations.
ANC microphone removal and installation for SYNC 2/SYNC 3, covering the same location and body-style branches.
Overhead-console removal and installation for front-microphone access.
Convertible rear-seat-backrest removal and installation for rear-microphone access.

applicability.equipment: Active noise control with SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3; coupe or convertible

guides.title: Adjust Front Toe at the Steering Tie Rods
guides.summary: Measure both front wheels, adjust the inner tie rods without twisting the steering boots, then recheck alignment and road test.
guides.introduction: Front toe describes how far the front wheels point inward or outward when viewed from above. The tie rods connect the steering gear to the wheels, and rotating their threaded adjustment changes each wheel’s direction. This job brings measured toe into specification while keeping the steering wheel straight ahead. It requires a wheel alignment system because the result must be measured accurately on both sides.
guides.why: The straight-ahead steering position and level working surface establish the conditions for a useful measurement. The outer tie rod jam nuts secure the adjustment. The steering gear bellows protect the moving linkage, so they must remain untwisted while the inner rods turn; otherwise the adjustment can leave the boots distorted.

when.summary: Adjust when an alignment measurement shows front toe outside the applicable specification.
notes: Measure both sides before deciding how much adjustment is needed.
Use the alignment equipment manufacturer’s instructions for setup and measurement.

prepare.title: Arrange measured alignment capability
prepare.detail: Use a wheel alignment system on a level surface. Have the applicable toe specification available rather than estimating wheel direction by eye.

prepare.title: Prepare access to both tie rods
prepare.detail: Provide access to the outer tie rod jam nuts, inner tie rods and steering gear boot clamps. Have suitable tools and a torque wrench for securing the adjustment.

steps.title: Establish the starting readings
steps.body: With the vehicle standing level and the steering wheel straight ahead, check front toe on both sides using the alignment system. Follow its manufacturer’s instructions so the readings provide a reliable starting point.

steps.title: Release the adjustment points
steps.body: Loosen the outer tie rod end jam nut on each side. Position the steering gear boot clamps aside as directed in the front toe procedure, allowing the rods to turn without winding up the bellows.

steps.title: Adjust while watching the readings
steps.body: Rotate the inner tie rods until the toe readings are within specification. Watch the bellows during rotation and prevent them from twisting. The illustrated adjustment points help distinguish the jam nut, boot clamp and rotating rod.

steps.title: Secure and remeasure
steps.body: Restore the boot clamps and secure the jam nuts to the specified 103 Nm. Recheck toe on both sides and adjust again if necessary; the final readings must confirm the secured setting.

steps.title: Complete the road test
steps.body: Road test the vehicle after the adjustment is secured and the measurements have been confirmed. Record any concern that remains rather than assuming an in-spec toe reading explains every steering complaint.

watchFor.title: Bellows winding around the rod
watchFor.body: A twisting boot means the adjustment is loading the bellows. Correct this before continuing to rotate the inner tie rod.

diagnostics.finding: One or both front toe readings are outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The measured wheel direction requires correction; the reading alone does not establish a failed steering component.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the inner tie rods, secure the adjustment and repeat the measurements.

verification.title: Record the final alignment result
verification.body: Record the final toe reading for each front wheel and confirm both are within the applicable specification.

verification.title: Confirm physical and driving completion
verification.body: Confirm the jam nuts are secured, the boot clamps are restored, the bellows are untwisted and the required road test is complete.

procedures.purpose: Complete front toe measurement and adjustment procedure, including both tie rods, boot precautions, fastening torque and road test.

guides.title: Remove and Reseal the Differential Housing Cover
guides.summary: Remove the differential assembly, renew the cover’s silicone seal, reinstall the assembly and refill it with clean differential fluid.
guides.introduction: The rear differential transfers driveshaft rotation to the rear halfshafts while allowing them to turn at different speeds during a corner. Its cast housing cover closes the rear of the assembly and retains the fluid used by the gears and bearings. The cover joint uses silicone sealant as its gasket. Servicing this joint involves removing the differential assembly, preparing the mating surfaces and rebuilding the seal before refilling.
guides.why: A successful seal depends on the condition of both mating surfaces and the specified sealant application. Simply tightening the cover does not renew that joint. The cover bolts also have low-profile external Torx heads requiring the specified socket. Although the cover work is straightforward once accessible, assembly removal and refitting make this a substantial workshop repair.

when.summary: When the differential cover needs removal, replacement or resealing.
notes: If investigating a fluid leak, establish that the cover joint is the repair target before beginning assembly removal.
The cover procedure requires the differential assembly to be removed from the vehicle.

prepare.title: Plan the complete access operation
prepare.detail: Use the linked axle assembly procedure for removal and installation, including its lifting, support and fastening requirements. Have the capability to complete that work before opening the cover.

prepare.title: Gather the sealing equipment
prepare.detail: Provide an EPL16 socket for the low-profile external Torx cover bolts, a plastic scraper and a torque wrench. Use Motorcraft Ultra Silicone Sealant TA-29 meeting WSS-M4G323-A8.

prepare.title: Prepare for refilling
prepare.detail: Have clean differential fluid selected through the linked draining and filling procedure. Use that procedure for the applicable fluid and fill requirements.

steps.title: Remove the differential assembly
steps.body: Follow the axle assembly removal procedure to make the differential available for cover service. Complete its access and support operations before proceeding to the cover.

steps.title: Remove the cover
steps.body: Use the EPL16 socket to remove the cover bolts, then remove the differential housing cover. The supplied illustration identifies the cover and its perimeter fasteners.

steps.title: Prepare both mating surfaces
steps.body: Clean the cover and housing mating surfaces using a plastic scraper and the linked room-temperature-vulcanizing silicone sealing-surface preparation procedure. This prepares the joint for a fresh, consistent seal.

steps.title: Apply the specified sealant
steps.body: Apply a 2mm bead of the specified Motorcraft Ultra Silicone Sealant to form the cover gasket. Follow the complete cover procedure for its application rather than choosing an arbitrary bead size.

steps.title: Install and secure the cover
steps.body: Install the differential housing cover and its bolts. Tighten the cover bolts to 46 Nm to secure the newly sealed joint.

steps.title: Reinstall and refill
steps.body: Reinstall the differential assembly using the axle assembly procedure. Then fill it with clean differential fluid using the separate draining and filling procedure.

watchFor.title: Residual sealant at the joint
watchFor.body: Both mating faces require preparation before the new bead is applied. Follow the specified cleaning method with the plastic scraper.

watchFor.title: Incorrect socket engagement
watchFor.body: The low-profile external Torx bolts specifically require an EPL16 socket for removal.

notes: The fluid specification and filling method belong to the draining and filling procedure; the cover procedure does not supply substitute values.

verification.title: Confirm the complete repair path
verification.body: Confirm the cover is secured, differential installation is complete and the clean-fluid refill has been performed.

verification.title: Record fastening and filling completion
verification.body: Record the cover-bolt torque completion and the refill result established through the applicable draining and filling procedure.

procedures.purpose: Differential housing cover removal, mating-surface preparation, sealant application and installation.
Required removal and installation of the differential assembly for cover access.
Required cleaning and preparation of the silicone-sealed cover and housing mating surfaces.
Differential draining and filling requirements, including the clean-fluid refill after installation.

guides.title: Replace the Climate-Control Air Inlet Door Actuator
guides.summary: Access the air inlet door actuator behind the right-hand lower instrument panel insulator, replace it and restore its connector and trim.
guides.introduction: The air inlet door actuator provides movement for the door controlling air entry into the climate-control unit. It is an electrically connected component mounted behind the right-hand lower instrument panel insulator. Replacing it means removing that access panel, disconnecting the actuator and releasing its retainers. The heating and cooling system also controls temperature, air distribution and blower speed, so an inlet-door concern needs to be identified before choosing this component for replacement.
guides.why: The access insulator and the actuator have separate retainers. Removing them in the stated order exposes the component and frees it from both the wiring and its mounting. Reverse-order installation restores the actuator first, then the electrical connection and finally the lower panel. This sequence keeps the connector accessible until the actuator is secured.

when.summary: When the air inlet door actuator has been identified for removal or replacement.
notes: A general heating or cooling complaint does not by itself identify the air inlet actuator as the cause.

prepare.title: Arrange right-hand lower-panel access
prepare.detail: Be ready to work beneath the right-hand instrument panel and remove its lower insulator. Use tools suitable for the panel and actuator retainers.

prepare.title: Identify the component before removal
prepare.detail: Use the actuator location illustration to identify its mounting retainers and electrical connector. Keep the panel retainers distinguishable from those securing the actuator.

steps.title: Remove the lower insulator
steps.body: Remove the retainers securing the right-hand lower instrument panel insulator, then remove the insulator. This provides the access used by the actuator replacement procedure.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the actuator
steps.body: Disconnect the air inlet door actuator electrical connector. Remove the actuator retainers and take out the actuator. Disconnecting first frees the component from the harness before it leaves its mounting.

steps.title: Install and reconnect the actuator
steps.body: Reverse the actuator removal operations: position the actuator at its mounting, install its retainers and reconnect the electrical connector. Complete these connections while the lower access area remains open.

steps.title: Restore the instrument panel insulator
steps.body: Refit the right-hand lower insulator and its retainers. This completes the reverse-order installation specified for the job.

watchFor.title: Confusing different climate-control functions
watchFor.body: Temperature selection, blower speed and air distribution are separate system functions. A complaint involving one of them needs diagnosis before an inlet actuator is selected.

watchFor.title: An overlooked connector
watchFor.body: The actuator’s electrical connector must be restored before the lower insulator closes the access area.

notes: Electronic manual temperature control and dual automatic temperature control both manage cabin heating and cooling; this repair concerns the air inlet door actuator.

verification.title: Check reverse-order installation
verification.body: Confirm the actuator retainers are installed, its connector is reconnected and the right-hand lower instrument panel insulator is secured with its retainers.

procedures.purpose: Air inlet door actuator removal and installation through the right-hand lower instrument panel insulator opening.

guides.title: Replace the Rear Keyless Entry Antenna
guides.summary: Remove the luggage compartment scuff plate to disconnect and replace the rear keyless entry antenna, then reinstall the trim.
guides.introduction: The rear keyless entry antenna is an electrically connected part of the vehicle’s entry system, mounted behind the luggage compartment scuff plate. The broader passive entry system can request door locking or unlocking and release the luggage compartment lid latch. This repair replaces the rear antenna through the luggage compartment opening. The illustrated arrangement is a coupe, with a similar procedure for the convertible.
guides.why: The scuff plate covers the antenna access area and must come off before the antenna can be disconnected and released. Its thumb-nut retainers are separate from the antenna’s mounting retainers. Keeping those operations distinct makes the removal sequence easy to follow and ensures both the electrical component and the protective trim are restored during installation.
searchTerms: luggage compartment scuff plate antenna access

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the rear keyless entry antenna for replacement, or the antenna requires removal.
notes: A keyless-entry complaint alone does not establish that the rear antenna has failed.

prepare.title: Open the luggage compartment
prepare.detail: Provide access to the scuff plate at the luggage compartment opening. The luggage compartment lid stays installed for this operation.

prepare.title: Identify the separate retaining points
prepare.detail: Locate the scuff plate’s thumb-nut retainers, then use the antenna illustration to identify the electrical connector and antenna mounting retainers behind it.

steps.title: Expose the antenna access area
steps.body: Open the luggage compartment lid. Remove the thumb-nut type retainers securing the luggage compartment scuff plate, then remove the plate to expose the rear antenna.

steps.title: Disconnect and release the antenna
steps.body: Disconnect the rear antenna electrical connector. Remove the antenna retainers and remove the antenna from its mounting. The connector and retainers are separate operations in the removal sequence.

steps.title: Install the antenna and restore its connection
steps.body: Reverse the antenna removal sequence: position the antenna, install its retainers and reconnect the electrical connector. Complete the connection before covering the access area.

steps.title: Refit the scuff plate
steps.body: Return the luggage compartment scuff plate to its installed position and refit its thumb-nut retainers. This restores the trim removed to reach the antenna.

watchFor.title: Illustration-only lid removal
watchFor.body: The luggage compartment lid is omitted from the component view for clarity. Removing the lid is not part of this repair.

watchFor.title: Incomplete reassembly behind the trim
watchFor.body: Confirm the antenna mounting and connector are restored before installing the scuff plate.

notes: The coupe illustration provides location guidance; the convertible procedure is described as similar.

verification.title: Confirm installation is complete
verification.body: Check that the antenna retainers are installed, its electrical connector is connected and the scuff plate is secured by its thumb-nut retainers.

procedures.purpose: Rear keyless entry antenna removal and reverse-order installation, including luggage compartment scuff plate access for coupe and similar convertible arrangements.

guides.title: Remove and Install the Steering-Wheel Driver Airbag
guides.summary: Depower the restraint system, release the driver airbag’s spring retainers, restore its electrical connections and repower through the prescribed procedure.
guides.introduction: The driver airbag sits in the steering wheel and forms part of the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS). The restraints control module monitors sensor information and commands deployment when it determines that deployment is necessary. This job releases the airbag from its spring-clip mountings and disconnects its electrical connections for removal or replacement. Correct mechanical attachment and connector engagement are essential to restoring the assembly.
guides.why: Airbag work requires restraint-system service capability because incorrect actions can cause accidental deployment or compromise operation in a crash. Electrical connector security also affects self-diagnostics. Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tabs secure deployable-component connectors and disengage their protective shorting bars. A connector can appear attached while an incompletely seated tab leaves the shorting bars applied, producing a low-resistance fault.
searchTerms: airbag warning indicator after connector installation

when.summary: When authorized restraint-system repair or steering-wheel access requires driver airbag removal.
notes: An illuminated airbag warning indicator does not by itself prove that the driver airbag needs replacement.
The complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures are mandatory parts of this job.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system service capability
prepare.detail: Have the full driver airbag, SRS depowering and SRS repowering procedures available. Follow every required step before handling or reconnecting the component.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified release tool
prepare.detail: Use a 3 mm Allen key to operate the steering-wheel spring clips through the side access holes. Follow the illustrated tool orientation to contact the clips.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete the linked SRS depowering procedure before beginning airbag removal. This prerequisite establishes the required condition for working on the deployable component; do not substitute a guessed isolation or waiting sequence.

steps.title: Release the spring-clip retainers
steps.body: Insert the Allen key into the side opening in the steering-wheel cover. Angle its inserted end upward and toward the front of the vehicle, then push the spring clip to release the airbag retainer. Repeat the specified side-access release operation for the remaining attachment.

steps.title: Separate and disconnect the airbag
steps.body: Pull the released driver airbag away from the steering wheel to access its connections. Disconnect the 3 driver airbag electrical connectors and remove the airbag.

steps.title: Reconnect under depowered conditions
steps.body: Before installation, make sure the SRS remains depowered in accordance with the required procedure. Connect all 3 electrical connectors and fully seat the applicable CPA tabs so the connections are secured and the shorting bars disengage.

steps.title: Engage the airbag mountings
steps.body: Align the driver airbag with the steering wheel and push it into position, engaging the airbag retainers with the spring clips. Correct engagement restores its mechanical attachment.

steps.title: Repower through the prescribed procedure
steps.body: Complete the linked SRS repowering procedure after the connectors and mountings are restored. Follow that procedure for returning the restraint system to service.

watchFor.title: Reconnection before depowering
watchFor.body: The installation warning specifically requires a depowered restraint system before reconnecting the component. Incorrect handling can cause accidental deployment and serious injury.

watchFor.title: A connector with an unseated assurance tab
watchFor.body: Electrical pins can make contact while the shorting bars remain applied. An apparently connected plug is therefore not sufficient evidence of correct installation.

notes: Some release illustrations omit the airbag to show the spring clip clearly; follow the stated tool direction with the assembly in place.

diagnostics.finding: An airbag warning indicator and circuit-resistance-below-threshold fault occur with a CPA tab incompletely seated.
diagnostics.meaning: The shorting bars may still be applied even though the connector pins are touching. This condition does not establish a failed airbag.
diagnostics.next: Have connector engagement checked using the required SRS depowering precautions, then complete the prescribed repowering procedure and reassess the fault.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical and electrical completion
verification.body: Confirm all 3 connectors and their applicable assurance tabs are seated, and the airbag retainers are engaged with the spring clips.

verification.title: Record the restraint-system result
verification.body: Record completion of the repowering procedure and the warning-indicator or self-diagnostic result. An illuminated airbag warning indicator requires further diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: Driver airbag spring-clip release, electrical disconnection, reconnection and installation in the steering wheel.
Mandatory SRS depowering before driver airbag removal and before reconnecting the component.
Mandatory SRS repowering after the driver airbag has been fully installed.

guides.title: Replace the 6R80 Automatic Transmission Support Insulator
guides.summary: Support the 6R80 transmission at the specified fluid-pan rib while replacing its support insulator and restoring the mounting fasteners.
guides.introduction: The transmission support insulator forms part of the mounting that supports the transmission and reduces vibration transfer into the vehicle. This procedure applies to the 6R80 six-speed automatic transmission with the listed 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines. The work takes place beneath the vehicle and uses temporary transmission support while the insulator is removed. The transmission’s weight must remain controlled throughout the change.
guides.why: The temporary support has a specific contact location: the wooden block and stand must bear on the outer rib of the transmission fluid pan. Choosing a different area changes where the supporting force enters the assembly and risks damage. Vehicle lifting is equally important because the technician works underneath while releasing part of the transmission mounting.

when.summary: When the 6R80 transmission support insulator has been identified for removal or replacement.
notes: Confirm the fitted transmission before using this procedure.
The replacement sequence requires a hoist and separate temporary support for the transmission.

prepare.title: Arrange safe under-vehicle access
prepare.detail: Use the jacking and lifting procedure to position the vehicle on a hoist. Identify the correct lifting points and check that adapters clear the suspension, exhaust, steering components and axle cover.

prepare.title: Prepare the transmission support
prepare.detail: Provide a vehicle/axle stand and wooden block suitable for the prescribed support operation. Be able to position their contact at the outer rib of the transmission fluid pan.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled fastening
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools and a torque wrench for the insulator nuts and bolts. These fastener groups have different tightening specifications.

steps.title: Position and raise the vehicle
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on the hoist using the linked lifting procedure. Locate the designated lifting points and check for interference before raising it.

steps.title: Remove the insulator nuts
steps.body: Remove the transmission support insulator nuts as the first mounting-disconnection step. Keep their installation requirement distinct from that of the insulator bolts.

steps.title: Support the transmission at the specified rib
steps.body: Use the stand and wooden block to support the transmission. Make sure their contact is on the outer rib of the transmission fluid pan before proceeding to remove the insulator bolts.

steps.title: Remove the insulator
steps.body: With the transmission supported, remove the bolts and the transmission support insulator. The supplied illustration identifies the insulator and its bolt attachment beneath the transmission.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the insulator and tighten its bolts to 103 Nm. Reverse the temporary-support operation once the insulator is installed, then restore the insulator nuts and tighten them to 80 Nm. Follow the complete procedure while transferring support back to the mounting.

watchFor.title: Support away from the outer pan rib
watchFor.body: The specified rib contact is a required support condition. Check the stand and block position before releasing the insulator bolts.

watchFor.title: Unsafe vehicle support
watchFor.body: Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this repair, and bumpers are not lifting points.

notes: The vehicle certification label has a transmission-code location marked TR; the transmission case also carries an identification tag.
On a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance first. On a two-column hoist, position the forks clear of suspension components and mounting brackets.

verification.title: Confirm the restored mounting
verification.body: Confirm the insulator is installed, both fastener groups are secured and the temporary transmission support has been removed after restoring the mounting.

verification.title: Record the separate torque results
verification.body: Record completion of the insulator bolt tightening at 103 Nm and the insulator nut tightening at 80 Nm.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 automatic transmission support insulator removal and installation for the listed 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications, including temporary support and fastener torques.
Required vehicle lifting-point identification, hoist positioning and under-vehicle support precautions.

guides.title: Replace a front-seat side or upper side airbag
guides.summary: Replace the seat-mounted airbag while preserving its deployment chute, upholstery attachments and electrical connector locks.
guides.introduction: The seat side airbag is part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). The restraints control module decides when deployment is necessary, while the seat’s deployment chute provides the intended path through the upholstery. This repair involves both the airbag assembly and careful backrest-trim work. The side-airbag and upper-side-airbag branches share initial access but use different attachments.
guides.why: The cover, foam and deployment chute influence how the airbag emerges during a crash. Damaged trim or an incorrectly restored chute can compromise that path. Electrical connector locks also matter: an incompletely seated connector assurance tab can leave the internal shorting bars engaged and produce a restraint-system fault.

when.summary: When the seat airbag requires replacement or removal, or damage requires renewal of its cover or deployment chute.
notes: An illuminated airbag warning indicator alone does not identify a failed airbag.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician competent in SRS and seat-trim work. Have the complete SRS depowering procedure in section 501-20B available; the system must be depowered before reconnecting the airbag.

prepare.title: Seat access and equipment
prepare.detail: Follow the front-seat removal procedure. Have hog ring pliers for the upper-airbag upholstery attachments and torque equipment suitable for the airbag fasteners.

prepare.title: Replacement trim and chute
prepare.detail: Plan to replace damaged components. A front-seat backrest trim cover used with a side airbag cannot be repaired, although cleaning is permitted.

steps.title: Remove the front seat
steps.body: Follow [Front Seat](#/document/G1695491) to remove the seat and establish access to the backrest. Continue with the appropriate branch of [Side Airbag](#/document/G1696309).

steps.title: Free the harness and lower cover
steps.body: Release the electrical connector retainers and move the harnesses aside. Position the backrest cover and detach its straps. Where a blower-motor snorkel is fitted, route the straps out through it before moving the cover aside.

steps.title: Open the backrest upholstery
steps.body: Remove the cover insert and its pin-type retainers, then move the cover upward. Move the snorkel aside if fitted. Release the J-clip and draw the cover out from between the seat cushion and backrest.

steps.title: Expose the deployment chute
steps.body: Partially invert the cover, separating hook-and-loop attachments carefully so they do not tear away from the foam. Detach the chute retainers, pull the chute through the foam, and release the four backrest-cover J-clip retainers.

steps.title: Remove the fitted airbag assembly
steps.body: For the side airbag, remove its nuts and detach it from the frame. For the upper side airbag, first release the frame J-clip, remove the hog rings and carefully detach the hook-and-loop strips, then remove the mounting bolt. In either branch, slide out the connector locking wedge, disconnect the connector and remove the airbag.

steps.title: Inspect the deployment path
steps.body: Inspect the airbag, cavity, mounting surface and deployment chute. Remove foreign material. Replace a damaged airbag or chute. If the airbag cover is damaged, separated from its mounting or exposes airbag material, replace the complete airbag assembly; do not repair it.

steps.title: Reconnect and rebuild the backrest
steps.body: Confirm SRS depowering before reconnection. Reverse removal, tightening the airbag nuts or upper-airbag bolt to 6 Nm. Restore the chute, upholstery attachments, straps and harness retainers; use hog ring pliers where required. Reinstall the seat through its linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Foam attachments pulling loose
watchFor.body: Stop pulling if the hook-and-loop strip starts lifting from the foam. Damage here changes how the upholstery is retained.

watchFor.title: Repairing a deployment component
watchFor.body: Neither a damaged airbag assembly nor an airbag-equipped backrest trim cover is a repairable upholstery item.

notes: The blower-motor snorkel instructions apply only where that equipment is fitted.

diagnostics.finding: A connector assurance tab is not fully seated.
diagnostics.meaning: The connector pins may contact the airbag while its shorting bars remain engaged, producing a below-threshold resistance fault.
diagnostics.next: Resolve connector engagement under the prescribed depowered conditions rather than assuming the airbag has failed.

verification.title: Deployment-path inspection
verification.body: Confirm that foreign material is removed, damaged components are renewed, and the chute and trim attachments are restored.

verification.title: Connector and inspection record
verification.body: Confirm the locking wedge is seated and record the condition of the airbag, mounting area and chute. A warning indicator remaining on when the vehicle is powered requires further diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: Side and upper side airbag removal, damage inspection and installation.
Front-seat removal and installation required for backrest access.

applicability.equipment: Front seats with seat side airbags

guides.title: Replace the starter motor: 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove and refit the starter, inspect both meshing gears, and use the correct engine and transmission mounting instructions.
guides.introduction: The starter motor turns the engine through its drive gear and the flywheel ring gear. Replacing it requires access beneath the vehicle and disconnection of its battery feed and solenoid-control wire. The engines share this purpose, but access, removal order and mounting requirements differ. Identify the engine and transmission before choosing the procedure.
guides.why: The starter battery terminal can deliver enough current to heat a shorted tool and cause burns. Battery isolation must therefore precede work on that terminal. Inspecting both gears matters because installing another starter does not correct damage to the ring gear it engages.

when.summary: After diagnosis establishes the need for starter replacement, or when the starter must be removed for related work.
notes: A failure to crank does not, by itself, prove that the starter motor is defective.

prepare.title: Safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points, identified by the stamped triangles. Check adapter clearance around surrounding components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Battery isolation and fastening
prepare.detail: Have the battery disconnect/connect procedure and suitable hand and torque tools available. Disconnect the battery ground cable at the battery before disconnecting the starter battery lead.

prepare.title: Choose the transmission branch
prepare.detail: The 5.0L instructions distinguish the 10R80 automatic from the MT82 manual. Their starter mounting torques differ.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and isolate the battery
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on a hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Disconnect the battery through [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356) before handling either starter connection.

steps.title: Follow the engine-specific access order
steps.body: On the [2.3L](#/document/G1673178), release the harness retainers from the mounting studbolts, move the harness aside, remove the studbolts and reposition the starter before disconnecting its leads. On the [5.2L](#/document/G1804813), complete the underbody-shield removals before accessing the electrical connections.

steps.title: Disconnect the starter leads
steps.body: Open the solenoid battery-cable cover. Remove the battery-cable nut and disconnect that cable, then remove the solenoid-wire nut and disconnect the control wire. Keep the repositioned 2.3L starter supported while completing these operations.

steps.title: Release the remaining mounts
steps.body: On the [3.7L](#/document/G1692845) automatic, remove the transmission cooling-tube bracket nut and move the bracket aside before removing the starter studbolts. The manual branch proceeds directly to those studbolts. On the [5.0L](#/document/G1692948), use the applicable transmission branch to remove the mounting bolts. Remove the 5.2L mounting bolts as directed. The already-unfastened 2.3L starter can now be removed.

steps.title: Inspect both gears
steps.body: Inspect the starter drive gear and flywheel ring gear using the engine-matched inspection procedure listed below. Establish whether additional gear work is needed before treating starter replacement as the complete repair.

steps.title: Reassemble in the correct reverse order
steps.body: Reverse the selected removal branch; on the 2.3L, reconnect the leads before returning the starter to its mounting position. The 2.3L and 3.7L mounting studbolts use 47.5 Nm. For the 5.0L, mounting bolts use 47.5 Nm with the 10R80 or 25 Nm with the MT82. On the 5.2L, install bolts hand tight, then follow the illustrated tightening sequence: starter-to-engine bolts use 25 Nm and the bracket-to-engine-mount bolt uses 55 Nm. Follow each procedure for terminal and ancillary fastener torques. Restore the cable cover, applicable bracket, harness retainers and shielding, then reconnect the battery.

watchFor.title: Transferring a mounting torque
watchFor.body: Engine size alone does not select the 5.0L mounting specification; the transmission branch is essential.

watchFor.title: Leaving the battery terminal exposed
watchFor.body: Restore its protective cover during reassembly rather than leaving an accessible live connection.

notes: The 5.0L procedure covers 10R80 and MT82 installations. Another transmission requires its matching instructions.
The selected illustration shows the 2.3L electrical connections.

diagnostics.finding: A 2.3L or 3.7L engine does not crank.
diagnostics.meaning: Starter operation also depends on start-request, transmission or clutch, relay and control-module inputs.
diagnostics.next: Establish the cause of the no-crank condition before authorizing a starter solely from the symptom.

diagnostics.finding: Gear inspection identifies damage.
diagnostics.meaning: The starter and ring gear form a meshing pair; replacing the starter may leave another fault present.
diagnostics.next: Follow the engine-specific inspection procedure to determine the additional repair.

verification.title: Reassembly and operation
verification.body: Check restored connections, covers and variant-specific attachments. After battery reconnection and safe return from the hoist, confirm that a start request cranks the engine.

verification.title: Record the mechanical findings
verification.body: Record the engine/transmission branch used and the results of both gear inspections, including any further repair required.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L starter removal and installation, including repositioning before lead disconnection.
3.7L starter removal and installation, including the automatic-transmission cooling-tube bracket.
5.0L starter removal and installation with separate 10R80 and MT82 mounting specifications.
5.2L starter removal and installation, shielding access and mounting tightening sequence.
Vehicle lifting points and hoist precautions.
Battery disconnection and reconnection.
2.3L starter drive gear and flywheel ring gear inspection.
3.7L starter drive gear and flywheel ring gear inspection.
5.0L starter drive gear and flywheel ring gear inspection.
5.2L starter drive gear and flywheel ring gear inspection.

guides.title: Replace the driver knee airbag
guides.summary: Remove the lower instrument-panel trim and knee airbag, restore its attachments, and complete the prescribed SRS repowering procedure.
guides.introduction: The driver knee airbag occupies the lower instrument panel beneath the steering wheel and forms part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). Its deployment is controlled by the restraints control module. Replacement requires several surrounding trim pieces to be removed before the airbag mounts and connector become accessible. Left-hand-drive and right-hand-drive vehicles share most of the work, with an additional harness retainer on the right-hand-drive branch.
guides.why: SRS depowering controls the risk of accidental deployment during service. Correct mounting and connector engagement are also essential for crash operation. A connector can appear attached while its assurance tab remains incompletely seated, leaving an electrical fault that must not be mistaken automatically for a defective replacement airbag.
searchTerms: airbag warning after knee airbag work

when.summary: When diagnosis or an established repair requires removal or replacement of the driver knee airbag.
notes: The warning indicator alone does not establish that this particular airbag needs replacement.

prepare.title: SRS service capability
prepare.detail: Arrange a technician competent in restraint-system service, with access to the complete depowering and repowering procedures.

prepare.title: Trim and fastener access
prepare.detail: Prepare appropriate trim and fastener tools and low-range torque equipment. Access is needed beside and beneath the instrument panel.

prepare.title: Identify the steering layout
prepare.detail: Use the correct left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive connector-removal branch. The illustration shows left-hand drive.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete [SRS Depowering](#/document/G1696297) before beginning the airbag removal sequence. Use that procedure’s full instructions rather than assuming that an unplugged connector makes the system safe.

steps.title: Remove the side and lighting-switch trim
steps.body: Release the clips and remove the left-hand instrument-panel trim panel. Remove the lighting-switch trim screw, release its clips, detach the panel and disconnect its electrical connector.

steps.title: Clear the remaining trim
steps.body: Remove the next trim panel’s screws, detach it and disconnect its connector. Then detach the ambient-air-temperature grille panel, disconnect its connector and release its tether. Freeing the tether prevents it from remaining attached as the panel is removed.

steps.title: Separate the knee airbag from the panel
steps.body: From beneath the instrument panel, remove the airbag retaining nuts. Remove the screws, disengage the clips and separate the airbag from the panel, keeping it supported while its wiring remains connected.

steps.title: Disconnect the appropriate harness arrangement
steps.body: On left-hand-drive vehicles, detach and disconnect the electrical connector, then remove the airbag. On right-hand-drive vehicles, first detach the harness pin-type retainer, then detach and disconnect the connector and remove the airbag.

steps.title: Refit and repower
steps.body: Confirm that the SRS remains depowered before reconnection. Reverse [Driver Knee Airbag](#/document/G1696302), restoring connector retention, clips, trim wiring and the grille tether. Tighten the airbag nuts to 8 Nm; the airbag screws and lighting-switch trim screw use 2.5 Nm. Finish with [SRS Repowering](#/document/G1696298).

watchFor.title: A panel still held by wiring or its tether
watchFor.body: Release the specified connection before carrying the panel away; clips and screws are not its only attachments.

watchFor.title: Assuming connector contact means full engagement
watchFor.body: The connector assurance feature must be fully seated to secure the connection and disengage the airbag’s shorting bars.

notes: Apply the listed screw torques only to their identified locations; the intervening trim-panel screws do not have a torque stated in this procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The airbag warning remains illuminated after return to service.
diagnostics.meaning: An incompletely seated connector assurance tab can cause a below-threshold resistance fault, but the warning alone does not isolate the cause.
diagnostics.next: Continue SRS diagnosis. Any reconnection work must again follow the depowering requirement.

verification.title: Mechanical restoration
verification.body: Confirm the airbag mounts, trim clips, electrical connections and grille tether are restored, including the extra harness retainer on right-hand-drive vehicles.

verification.title: Record return-to-service results
verification.body: Complete the prescribed repowering procedure and record the resulting airbag-warning status and any unresolved restraint-system fault.

procedures.purpose: Driver knee airbag removal and installation, including both steering-layout branches.
Required SRS depowering before removal and airbag reconnection.
Required SRS repowering after installation.

guides.title: Replace the convertible tonneau-cover sensor assembly
guides.summary: Replace the affected D-tower cover and its integrated sensor, then check roof operation with the tonneau covers removed.
guides.introduction: Each optional tonneau cover contains a magnet that activates a Hall-effect sensor, an electronic switch responsive to a magnetic field. The roof control modules use these signals to prevent the convertible top from being raised with the covers installed. The sensor being serviced is part of the D-tower cover, so replacement means changing that assembly rather than removing a separate sensor.
guides.why: Cover detection is an operating interlock. A refusal to raise the roof may be correct behavior when a cover is fitted. Confirming the actual cover condition and other roof operating requirements helps avoid replacing a working assembly.

when.summary: When the integrated tonneau-cover sensor or its D-tower cover assembly has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Left and right sides use similar operations; replace the affected assembly.

prepare.title: Assembly and trim access
prepare.detail: Obtain the appropriate D-tower cover assembly. Have tools suitable for trim clips and pin-type retainers, and the convertible loadspace-trim procedure available.

prepare.title: Establish the complaint
prepare.detail: Note whether the tonneau covers are physically installed and which message appears. A cover-removal message with covers fitted is expected.

steps.title: Expose the affected side
steps.body: Remove the loadspace trim only as necessary using [Loadspace Trim Panel — Convertible](#/document/G1692610). Establish access to the connector and D-tower cover on the side being repaired.

steps.title: Disconnect the harness
steps.body: Disconnect the sensor harness connector before releasing the cover assembly. The connector operation is similar on both sides.

steps.title: Remove the D-tower cover
steps.body: Remove the bumper stop and the two pin-type retainers, then release the remaining clip and remove the cover. Follow [Tonneau Cover Sensor](#/document/G1723917) for the attachment locations.

steps.title: Install the complete replacement
steps.body: Reverse removal: engage the cover clip, restore the retainers and bumper stop, reconnect the harness and reinstall the disturbed loadspace trim. The sensor stays part of the replacement cover assembly.

watchFor.title: Confusing the two covers
watchFor.body: The removable tonneau cover carries the magnet; the D-tower cover contains the sensor being replaced.

notes: The roof switch must be held in the requested direction during roof movement.
