diagnostics.finding: TOP DISABLED — REMOVE COVERS appears with a tonneau cover installed.
diagnostics.meaning: The roof is reporting an expected closing interlock.
diagnostics.next: Remove the tonneau covers before requesting roof raising.

diagnostics.finding: The same message appears with both covers removed.
diagnostics.meaning: The reported cover condition needs investigation; the message alone does not prove which sensor or circuit is responsible.
diagnostics.next: Establish the affected side and cause before replacing an assembly.

diagnostics.finding: The roof remains inoperative without a cover warning.
diagnostics.meaning: Roof operation also depends on accessory-delay status, vehicle speed and confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully lowered.
diagnostics.next: Continue roof-system diagnosis rather than assuming the new sensor is defective.

verification.title: Check closing under valid conditions
verification.body: With the vehicle stationary, accessory delay active and tonneau covers removed, hold the UP switch. Confirm the windows lower and the roof raises.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record roof response and whether a cover-removal message remains despite both covers being physically removed.

procedures.purpose: Tonneau sensor and D-tower cover assembly removal and installation.
Convertible loadspace-trim removal and installation for access.
Cover-sensor operation, roof interlocks and message interpretation.

guides.title: Remove and install the 5.2L 3160 input-shaft bearing
guides.summary: Use a hydraulic press and bearing separator to remove the input-shaft bearing, then press the roller bearing onto the shaft during assembly.
guides.introduction: The input shaft brings engine torque into the 3160 manual transmission. Most ratios transfer that torque through the countershaft; fifth gear connects the input and output shafts through the synchronizer sleeve for direct drive. The input-shaft bearing supports this rotating assembly. This job covers bearing removal and installation on the bench, with the shaft already accessible outside the assembled gearbox.
guides.why: Bearing service is a controlled pressing operation. The removal phase specifically requires a bearing separator together with the hydraulic press, while installation requires the press. Correct component identification matters because the input-shaft bearing, its housing cup and the adjacent output-shaft front roller bearing are distinct parts.

when.summary: When input-shaft bearing service is required during a 3160 gearbox overhaul.
notes: This operation is not a diagnosis of transmission noise or difficult shifting.

prepare.title: Bench access
prepare.detail: Have the input shaft removed through the applicable gearbox disassembly process. Transmission removal and case dismantling are separate prerequisites.

prepare.title: Press equipment and capability
prepare.detail: Provide a hydraulic press, bearing separator and an operator experienced in transmission-bearing work. Establish a suitable support arrangement before applying force.

steps.title: Identify the bearing on the shaft
steps.body: Use [Input Shaft](#/document/G1849276) and the geartrain identification view to distinguish the bearing being serviced from the separate bearing cup and neighboring output-shaft bearing.

steps.title: Press the bearing off
steps.body: Use the bearing separator with the hydraulic press to remove the input-shaft bearing. The separator is part of the specified removal equipment; the finished-assembly illustration does not establish its positioning or the press support arrangement.

steps.title: Press the roller bearing onto the shaft
steps.body: For assembly, use the hydraulic press to install the input-shaft roller bearing on the input shaft. Follow the illustrated component orientation without inventing a press force or installation-depth measurement.

steps.title: Return the subassembly to gearbox assembly
steps.body: Once the bearing operation is complete, continue through the applicable transmission assembly process. Bearing pressing alone does not establish the completed gearbox’s shim selection or adjustment.

watchFor.title: Treating the photograph as a press setup
watchFor.body: The illustration identifies the installed bearing; it does not show press adapters, support locations or an acceptance measurement.

notes: The bearing procedure provides no press-force, installed-height or clearance specification. Do not substitute an assumed value.

verification.title: Confirm the subassembly
verification.body: Check component identity and orientation against the installation illustration. Any dimensional acceptance must come from the applicable gearbox assembly requirements.

verification.title: Record the scope completed
verification.body: Record bearing removal and installation separately from completion of the remaining transmission assembly and checks.

procedures.purpose: 3160 input-shaft bearing bench disassembly and assembly for the 5.2L application.
3160 powerflow and identification of the input-shaft bearing, bearing cup and adjacent geartrain parts.

guides.title: Check A/C operating pressures on the 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Measure stabilized refrigerant pressures under controlled conditions to distinguish airflow, charge, restriction and compressor concerns.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning compressor circulates refrigerant through a low-pressure suction side and a high-pressure discharge side. Comparing both pressures helps explain poor cooling, but only when temperature, airflow and control settings are consistent. This test applies to the 5.2L system and accommodates either manual or dual automatic temperature controls.
guides.why: Ambient temperature and condenser airflow affect operating pressures. A reading taken before pressures settle can suggest the wrong fault. Variable-compressor diagnosis also depends on the correct refrigerant charge, so pressure results alone must not lead straight to compressor replacement.
searchTerms: refrigerant high and low pressure test

when.summary: When investigating inadequate cooling or abnormal compressor operation in sufficiently warm ambient conditions.
notes: Testing requires ambient temperature of at least 21°C (70°F).
The supplied chart ranges extend to 49°C (120°F); do not extrapolate beyond the applicable chart.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant-service capability
prepare.detail: Use an air-conditioning service unit and someone capable of connecting and operating it correctly. Variable-compressor assessment may also require refrigerant recovery and recharging to the vehicle specification.

prepare.title: Select the correct charts
prepare.detail: Use the paired suction and discharge charts for 21–38°C (70–100°F), at 30–60% relative humidity, or the hotter-condition charts for 38–49°C (100–120°F), at 15–40% relative humidity.

steps.title: Warm the engine and connect the service unit
steps.body: Run the engine to normal operating temperature, then connect the air-conditioning service unit. Choose the ambient-temperature branch in the [pressure-test procedure](#/document/G1727492).

steps.title: Establish the specified cooling demand
steps.body: Select the lowest temperature, disable dual temperature operation if equipped, set the blower manually to HI, select FRESH air where available and switch A/C on. Open all windows and leave the hood open.

steps.title: Confirm operation and let pressures settle
steps.body: Confirm that the compressor and engine cooling fans are operating or engaged. Let the engine idle until both pressures stabilize or fluctuate within a repeating range.

steps.title: Record and compare both pressures
steps.body: Record shop temperature, discharge pressure and suction pressure. For fluctuating readings, record the average. Compare each pressure with its corresponding chart; the attached illustration is only the lower-temperature discharge chart.

steps.title: Follow the pressure pattern to the next check
steps.body: Use the findings below to guide diagnosis. Before replacing a variable compressor, recover and recharge the system to the vehicle specification, then retest above 70°F. Keep that requirement separate from the general minimum test temperature.

watchFor.title: Other reasons for inadequate compressor operation
watchFor.body: Consider a loose drive belt, slipping clutch, an open or shorted clutch coil or loose mounting, dirty or sticking switch contacts, circuit resistance, an open circuit or blown fuse, and engine-computer interruption.

watchFor.title: Contributors to compressor damage
watchFor.body: The diagnostic table also identifies incorrect clutch air gap, a blocked suction-accumulator refrigerant-oil bleed hose and refrigerant leaks.

notes: Rear-door and rear-hatch opening directions apply only to body configurations with those openings.
A pressure pattern identifies possible causes; it does not establish that a particular component has failed.

diagnostics.finding: High discharge pressure with normal-to-high suction pressure.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible inadequate condenser airflow or engine overheating.
diagnostics.next: Investigate airflow and engine temperature.

diagnostics.finding: Normal-to-high discharge pressure with normal suction pressure.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible refrigerant overcharge or air in the refrigerant.
diagnostics.next: Investigate charge condition.

diagnostics.finding: Normal-to-low discharge pressure with high suction pressure.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible low compressor performance.
diagnostics.next: Apply the charge-and-retest requirement before condemning a variable compressor.

diagnostics.finding: Normal-to-low discharge pressure with normal-to-high suction pressure.
diagnostics.meaning: A suction-line restriction downstream of the service access valve is possible.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the suction line and restriction location.

diagnostics.finding: Normal-to-low discharge pressure with low suction pressure.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible low charge from leakage, or a suction-line restriction upstream of the service access valve.
diagnostics.next: Distinguish leakage from restriction.

diagnostics.finding: Erratic operation or no compressor operation.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible poor connections at the ambient-air-temperature sensor, pressure transducer or evaporator-temperature sensor, or low charge from leakage.
diagnostics.next: Check these possibilities before selecting a replacement component.

verification.title: Keep a usable test record
verification.body: Record ambient temperature, both pressures, whether averages were used, the selected chart range and whether each result was within its normal band.

verification.title: Document any required retest
verification.body: For variable-compressor assessment, record the results after recovery and correct recharging, with the retest performed above 70°F.

procedures.purpose: Complete 5.2L refrigerant-pressure test, including both ambient-temperature branches, chart selection and diagnostic decisions.

guides.title: Replace the auxiliary power point socket
guides.summary: Extract the auxiliary power point with its dedicated remover, then connect and seat a new socket in the retainer.
guides.introduction: The auxiliary power point provides an electrical connection for plug-in accessories. Its socket sits inside a retainer and connects to the vehicle wiring behind it. This repair replaces the socket while following a controlled extraction sequence: engage the remover, fit its receiver cup, pull the socket out and then disconnect the wiring.
guides.why: The extractor needs a positive hold in the socket's adjacent slots. Its receiver cup and wing nut provide the controlled pulling action that separates the socket from the retainer. Understanding that arrangement makes the job much clearer than treating the visible cover or surrounding trim as the removal point.

when.summary: When the auxiliary power point socket has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: A complaint about accessory power does not by itself establish that the socket needs replacement.

prepare.title: Have the specified extractor
prepare.detail: Use special service tool 501-194, Remover, Power Point, including its receiver cup and wing nut. The extraction sequence depends on these parts working together.

prepare.title: Prepare the replacement socket
prepare.detail: Have a new power point socket ready. Be prepared to release and reconnect the electrical connector once the old socket has been withdrawn.

steps.title: Open the cover and engage the remover
steps.body: Open the power point cover. Position tool 501-194 so that it engages the adjacent slots inside the socket. Establish that engagement before applying the extraction load.

steps.title: Assemble the pulling arrangement
steps.body: Install the receiver cup, then install and tighten the wing nut as shown in the [socket replacement procedure](#/document/G1693972). These are separate setup actions before pulling the socket from its retainer.

steps.title: Withdraw and disconnect the old socket
steps.body: Tighten the wing nut to pull the socket out of the retainer. Once withdrawn, disconnect its electrical connector. The connector is released after extraction in this procedure.

steps.title: Connect and install the new socket
steps.body: Connect the electrical connector to the new socket, then push the socket into the retainer. Complete the connection before seating the socket, while the connector remains accessible.

watchFor.title: Incomplete extractor engagement
watchFor.body: If the remover has not engaged the adjacent socket slots, correct its position before tightening the pulling arrangement.

watchFor.title: A connector still attached during withdrawal
watchFor.body: The socket remains connected electrically until the extraction step is complete; account for that connection when handling the withdrawn socket.

notes: Installation specifies a new socket.
This is a socket replacement procedure; it provides no electrical fault-finding sequence.

verification.title: Confirm installation is complete
verification.body: Confirm that the electrical connector is connected and the new socket has been pushed fully into its retainer.

procedures.purpose: Auxiliary power point extraction with tool 501-194 and installation of a new socket.

guides.title: Replace the windshield wiper motor
guides.summary: Remove the wiper linkage assembly, separate its links and motor bracket carefully, and install the replacement motor.
guides.introduction: The windshield wiper motor drives the linkage that moves the wiper arms. It also contains operating logic and sensors that monitor arm position, so it does more than simply turn when power is applied. The motor controls wiping modes and the washer relay. Replacement involves removing the linkage assembly and separating the motor from it.
guides.why: The link seals need protection when the links are detached from the motor crank. Damage here can leave poor wiper performance even after the motor has been replaced. Electrical control also matters: high speed has a separate fail-safe command path, so unusual operation does not automatically prove that the motor itself has failed.
searchTerms: wipers only work on high speed
rain sensing wipers use intermittent mode

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the windshield wiper motor requires replacement.
notes: Identify whether the vehicle has ordinary intermittent or rain-sensitive wipers when assessing the original complaint.

prepare.title: Plan removal of the complete linkage
prepare.detail: Follow the separate [wiper linkage assembly procedure](#/document/G1694633) for access and removal. The motor procedure starts with that assembly removed.

prepare.title: Prepare for careful link and bracket work
prepare.detail: Provide a suitable working area for the removed assembly and fastening equipment capable of applying the motor-bracket torque. Identify both links and their seals before separating them.

steps.title: Remove the wiper linkage assembly
steps.body: Complete the linked assembly-removal procedure before beginning motor separation. This provides access to the links, motor crank and mounting bracket as an assembly.

steps.title: Separate the links from the motor crank
steps.body: Remove the left-hand link, followed by the right-hand link. Protect the link seals throughout separation; the [motor procedure](#/document/G1694635) specifically warns that seal damage can impair wiping.

steps.title: Remove the motor bracket
steps.body: Remove the bracket mounting bolts, then slide the bracket out in the illustrated direction. Keep this sliding movement distinct from removing the motor itself.

steps.title: Separate and replace the motor
steps.body: Remove the windshield wiper motor from the linkage assembly. Install the replacement by reversing the removal sequence, restoring the motor, bracket and link connections.

steps.title: Secure the bracket and reinstall the assembly
steps.body: Tighten the motor-bracket mounting bolts to 115 lb.in (13 Nm). Complete reinstallation using the separate linkage-assembly procedure, which governs the assembly's return to the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Damaged link seals
watchFor.body: Treat any seal damage during separation as a concern requiring attention before the assembly is returned to service.

watchFor.title: Confusing a feature fault with a motor fault
watchFor.body: Rain-sensitive operation can fall back to ordinary intermittent wiping when a rain-sensing fault is detected.

notes: The bracket torque applies to the motor-bracket mounting bolts; do not transfer it to other linkage or vehicle fasteners.
The steering column control module sends normal commands over the Local Interconnect Network, abbreviated LIN.

diagnostics.finding: High-speed wiping works while other modes do not.
diagnostics.meaning: High speed has a direct ground-command fail-safe path that bypasses the motor's normal LIN-controlled logic.
diagnostics.next: Consider command and communication faults before treating this behavior as proof of a failed motor.

diagnostics.finding: Rain-sensitive wiping has changed to timed intermittent operation.
diagnostics.meaning: This is the described fallback behavior for a rain-sensitive feature fault.
diagnostics.next: Investigate that feature rather than selecting a motor solely from this symptom.

verification.title: Check the completed mechanical assembly
verification.body: Confirm that the bracket is secured, both links are reattached with their seals protected, and linkage installation is complete.

verification.title: Check and record the affected function
verification.body: Compare the original complaint with operation after installation. Check the relevant mist, low, high, washer and intermittent or rain-sensitive functions against their described behavior.

procedures.purpose: Motor separation from the removed linkage assembly and reverse-order installation, including bracket torque and seal precautions.
Required removal and reinstallation of the complete wiper linkage assembly.
Operating behavior used to distinguish command, rain-sensing and motor concerns and to assess the repaired function.

guides.title: Replace the automatic transmission fluid cooler on 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L models
guides.summary: Disconnect the cooler tubes, follow the engine-specific access route, replace the cooler and complete the transmission fluid level check.
guides.introduction: The external transmission fluid cooler sits in front of the radiator. Fluid travels from the automatic transmission through the cooler and back through its tubes, transferring heat to passing air. Replacement opens that fluid circuit and requires access through the front cooling assembly. The three engines share the cooler's purpose, but their access procedures differ.
guides.why: The tube fittings have secondary latches and require a dedicated disconnect tool. Access also needs careful planning: the 2.3L procedure removes the air-conditioning condenser, while the 3.7L and 5.0L procedures reposition it. Finishing the mechanical work is only part of the job because the transmission fluid level must then be checked and adjusted.

when.summary: When the external automatic transmission fluid cooler has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Select the procedure by its engine-specific title before starting access work.

prepare.title: Obtain the disconnect and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Use special service tool 307-695, Tool, Quick Disconnect, for the cooler tube fittings. Have torque equipment suitable for the cooler and any radiator-bracket fasteners.

prepare.title: Arrange the correct access capability
prepare.detail: For the 2.3L, arrange the refrigerant-service capability required by the linked condenser-removal procedure. For the 3.7L or 5.0L, have the matching air-cleaner outlet-pipe procedure available.

prepare.title: Plan the fluid-level check
prepare.detail: Use the complete 6R80 fluid-level procedure for its checking conditions and adjustment method. Do not estimate the final level from the amount lost.

steps.title: Select the engine-specific path
steps.body: Use the [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1694308), [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1694310) or [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1694311). Keep the selected access sequence through removal and reinstallation.

steps.title: Disconnect the cooler tubes
steps.body: Remove the tube-fitting secondary latches first. Then use tool 307-695 to disconnect the fittings. Removing the secondary latches does not replace the tool-assisted release step.

steps.title: On the 2.3L, remove the condenser
steps.body: Follow the complete [2.3L condenser procedure](#/document/G1676761), including its refrigerant-system requirements. This branch calls for condenser removal; the other engines' repositioning method is not a substitute.

steps.title: On the 3.7L or 5.0L, create access around the radiator
steps.body: Remove the matching air-cleaner outlet pipe, then the pushpins and radiator sight shield. Remove the radiator-bracket bolts and brackets. Move the radiator toward the engine, release the upper tabs and position the condenser aside.

steps.title: Remove the cooler
steps.body: With the selected access work complete, remove the cooler bolts and the cooler. Keep the cooler fasteners distinct from the radiator-bracket fasteners used on the 3.7L and 5.0L.

steps.title: Reverse the selected removal sequence
steps.body: Install the cooler and tighten its bolts to 53 lb.in (6 Nm). On the 3.7L and 5.0L, tighten the radiator-bracket bolts to 97 lb.in (11 Nm). Restore the engine-specific access components, tube fittings and secondary latches.

steps.title: Set the transmission fluid level
steps.body: Follow the [6R80 transmission fluid level check](#/document/G1692053) and adjust as necessary. This is a required completion step after cooler replacement.

watchFor.title: Mixing condenser access methods
watchFor.body: Condenser removal belongs to the 2.3L branch; repositioning belongs to the 3.7L and 5.0L branches.

watchFor.title: Omitted secondary latches
watchFor.body: Reverse-order installation includes restoring the secondary latches after reconnecting the cooler tube fittings.

notes: The 3.7L and 5.0L procedures show the front bumper removed for clarity; that note is not a separate bumper-removal instruction.
Use the engine-matched outlet-pipe procedure even though the remaining access sequences are similar.

verification.title: Confirm the assembly is restored
verification.body: Confirm cooler fastening, tube connections and secondary latches, together with the condenser, radiator supports and intake components disturbed by the selected branch.

verification.title: Record the final fluid-level result
verification.body: Record completion of the specified transmission fluid level check and whether adjustment was necessary.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L cooler removal and installation using condenser removal for access.
3.7L cooler removal and installation using outlet-pipe removal and radiator/condenser repositioning.
5.0L cooler removal and installation using outlet-pipe removal and radiator/condenser repositioning.
Required 2.3L air-conditioning condenser removal and installation for cooler access.
3.7L air-cleaner outlet-pipe removal and installation.
5.0L air-cleaner outlet-pipe removal and installation.
Required final 6R80 transmission fluid level check and adjustment.

guides.title: Replace rear wheel studs with the hub removed
guides.summary: Remove the rear bearing and hub assembly, press out the affected stud, inspect the assembly and press in its replacement.
guides.introduction: Rear wheel studs provide the threaded attachment used by the wheel nuts to clamp the wheel to the hub. The studs are retained in the hub itself. This procedure replaces a stud using a hydraulic press after the wheel bearing and hub assembly has been removed from the vehicle.
guides.why: Stud replacement and hub condition are linked. After the old stud is pressed out, the bearing and hub must be inspected for damage; installing another stud does not resolve damage to the assembly that carries it. The job therefore includes a decision about whether the existing bearing and hub remain suitable for use.
searchTerms: press wheel stud out of rear hub

when.summary: When a rear wheel stud requires replacement and the bearing/hub assembly can be removed for press work.
notes: This procedure concerns rear wheel studs.
The required bearing-and-hub inspection determines whether stud replacement alone is sufficient.

prepare.title: Arrange hydraulic press capability
prepare.detail: Use a hydraulic press and the support arrangement shown in the [wheel stud procedure](#/document/G1686659). The operator must be able to position and support the removed assembly correctly.

prepare.title: Plan rear hub removal and installation
prepare.detail: Follow the complete [rear wheel bearing and hub procedure](#/document/G1686657) for vehicle access, support and attachment requirements. Have the capability to complete that work as well as the bench operation.

steps.title: Remove the bearing and hub assembly
steps.body: Complete the linked rear bearing-and-hub removal procedure. The stud work begins with this assembly removed; the illustrated press arrangement is for the removed assembly.

steps.title: Press out the affected stud
steps.body: Position the assembly as illustrated and use the hydraulic press to press the stud out. Follow the shown support and pressing direction without inventing fixture dimensions or a press-force specification.

steps.title: Inspect before proceeding
steps.body: Inspect the wheel bearing and wheel hub for damage. Replace them as necessary. Make this decision after stud removal and before installing the replacement stud.

steps.title: Press in the replacement and reinstall the hub
steps.body: Use the hydraulic press to install the replacement stud in the bearing and hub assembly. Then reinstall the assembly using the separate rear bearing-and-hub procedure.

watchFor.title: Damage to the bearing or hub
watchFor.body: A damaged assembly requires the replacement decision specified by the procedure; a new stud alone is not the completion criterion.

watchFor.title: An unsuitable press setup
watchFor.body: Use the illustrated support arrangement. Correct support is part of performing the specified press operation.

notes: Both stud removal and installation use the hydraulic press.
Complete hub reinstallation through its own procedure rather than inferring fastening details from the stud illustration.

diagnostics.finding: Bearing or hub damage is found after pressing out the stud.
diagnostics.meaning: The repair may require more than replacement of the stud.
diagnostics.next: Replace the bearing and hub as necessary before completing installation.

verification.title: Confirm both phases are complete
verification.body: Confirm the replacement stud has been pressed in and the bearing-and-hub assembly has been reinstalled through its complete procedure.

verification.title: Record the inspection decision
verification.body: Record whether the bearing and hub were retained after inspection or replaced because damage was found.

procedures.purpose: Rear wheel stud hydraulic-press removal, bearing/hub damage inspection and stud installation.
Required rear wheel bearing and hub removal before press work and installation afterward.

guides.title: Replace a right-hand front door midwoofer or woofer
guides.summary: Remove the right-hand door trim panel, replace the selected speaker and restore the panel's fasteners, wiring and latch cable.
guides.introduction: The front door woofer and midwoofer reproduce lower-frequency portions of the audio signal. They sit behind the door trim panel and connect to the vehicle wiring through electrical connectors. This guide covers the right-hand speaker procedures for SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3, including the trim removal needed to reach the selected speaker.
guides.why: Most of the access work concerns the door panel rather than the speaker. The panel has staged clip releases, electrical connections where fitted and a latch cable that must be released before it can be set aside. Restoring those connections is as much a part of the repair as fastening the speaker.
searchTerms: door trim removal for speaker access

when.summary: When the right-hand front door midwoofer or woofer has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Choose the procedure and replacement speaker for the fitted audio system.
The midwoofer and woofer headings are separate component branches; identify which speaker needs work.

prepare.title: Match the audio equipment
prepare.detail: SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 have different audio-system configurations. Use the matching speaker procedure even though their listed mechanical removal sequences are the same.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and connector work
prepare.detail: Have equipment for the panel and speaker fasteners, including accurate low-torque tightening. Follow the [door trim procedure](#/document/G1692600), including its referenced window-control-switch removal procedure.

steps.title: Identify the speaker branch
steps.body: Select the [SYNC procedure](#/document/G1694050) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure](#/document/G1693898). Identify the right-hand midwoofer or woofer being replaced before removing the panel.

steps.title: Remove the panel's initial attachments
steps.body: Remove the cover and upper trim-panel bolt. Remove the front door window control switch through its referenced procedure, then remove the center bolt and lower retainers.

steps.title: Release the panel in stages
steps.body: Move the rear upper portion away and release its clip and pin-type retainers. Next move the rear and lower portion away, releasing the pin-type retainer and clip. Continue positioning the panel away and release the remaining pin-type retainers in the illustrated sequence.

steps.title: Lift the panel free and release its connections
steps.body: Lift the panel up and out. Disconnect electrical connectors where fitted and release the latch cable before setting the panel aside. The panel remains tethered until these connections are released.

steps.title: Remove the selected speaker
steps.body: For either the midwoofer or woofer branch, remove the bolts and speaker, then disconnect its electrical connector. Follow the branch for the selected component; the procedure does not require replacing both speakers.

steps.title: Install the replacement speaker
steps.body: Reverse the speaker-removal sequence: connect the electrical connector, position the speaker and install its bolts. Tighten the speaker bolts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). This value applies to both listed speaker branches.

steps.title: Restore the door trim
steps.body: Transfer panel parts as necessary and reverse trim removal, reconnecting the latch cable and fitted electrical connectors. Restore all clips and retainers. Tighten the upper and center panel bolts to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), and the lower retainers to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). Reinstall the window switch and cover.

watchFor.title: A panel that is still attached
watchFor.body: Do not treat outward panel movement as full release. Retainers are released in stages, followed by the lift-out movement and disconnection of the cable and fitted wiring.

watchFor.title: Confusing fastening values
watchFor.body: Speaker bolts, upper/center panel bolts and lower panel retainers have different tightening values.

watchFor.title: Selecting a speaker from a symptom alone
watchFor.body: These replacement procedures do not establish the cause of an audio complaint. Identify the affected component before choosing the midwoofer or woofer branch.

notes: Right-hand refers to the vehicle side and should not automatically be read as passenger side.
The trim procedure illustrates left-hand drive and states that right-hand drive is similar.

verification.title: Confirm speaker installation
verification.body: Confirm that the selected speaker's connector is attached and its mounting bolts have been tightened to the specified value.

verification.title: Confirm the panel is fully restored
verification.body: Confirm that the latch cable, fitted electrical connectors, window switch, clips, pin-type retainers, bolts and cover have all been restored through the reverse installation sequence.

procedures.purpose: Right-hand front door midwoofer or woofer removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC.
Right-hand front door midwoofer or woofer removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Required door trim removal and installation, including staged retainer release, electrical connections, latch cable and panel fastening values.

guides.title: Remove and refit the intake manifold: 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove the intake manifold using the correct engine branch, assess its condition and seals, then restore its plumbing and electrical connections.
guides.introduction: The intake manifold distributes incoming air to the engine’s cylinders. Its surrounding hoses, wiring and supports must be released before it can move freely. The engines share this purpose, but the 2.3L removal route differs substantially from the V8 procedures, particularly around the fuel system and rear connections.
guides.why: Clean sealing surfaces protect the engine from contamination. Metal left inside a manifold after valve or piston damage can damage the repaired engine, while incorrect gasket reuse can compromise the intake seal.

when.summary: When manifold repair or removal is required, or during inspection following upper-engine damage.
notes: Confirm the engine variant before selecting parts and procedures; check the V8 engine identification labels.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capability
prepare.detail: Have suitable torque tools, including angle-tightening capability for the V8 procedures. The 2.3L requires a hoist; use the marked lifting points and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have new V8 manifold gaskets and new 5.2L strut-brace nuts available. Keep debris from entering exposed engine passages during cleaning.

steps.title: Establish engine-specific access
steps.body: For the 2.3L, place the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist and remove the appearance cover. For either V8, release fuel pressure and disconnect both battery cables using their procedures. Remove the strut brace if fitted on the 5.0L; on the 5.2L, remove it and discard its nuts. Remove the 5.0L appearance cover, then the applicable V8 air-cleaner outlet pipe, cowl grille, extension and initial heater-hose support.

steps.title: Release the 2.3L external connections
steps.body: Follow the [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1660523). Disconnect the evaporative-emission purge coupling, release the fuel and vapor tubes from their retainer, and move the disconnected purge valve aside. Release the manifold pressure/temperature sensor and throttle wiring, charge-air-cooler outlet tube, rear vacuum coupling and coolant-tube mounting nut.

steps.title: Release the V8 plumbing and fuel connections
steps.body: Use the [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1685326) or [5.2L procedure](#/document/G1800279). Release the vacuum, crankcase ventilation and evaporative-emission connections, throttle wiring and remaining heater-hose support. Disconnect both injector banks and the fuel supply. Remove the 5.0L fuel-rail insulators; disconnect the 5.2L fuel-pressure sensor. Remove the rail bolts, leaving the rail with the manifold.

steps.title: Move the manifold only far enough to release its rear attachments
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the mounting bolts, move the manifold back, disconnect the positive crankcase ventilation tube and detach the knock-sensor connector retainers. On either V8, loosen the manifold bolts and lift it upward and forward to disconnect the rear wiring and retainers. Then remove the manifold.

steps.title: Assess the manifold and sealing surfaces
steps.body: After upper-engine failure, inspect for metal debris; replace the manifold if any is found. Discard V8 gaskets and clean and inspect their sealing surfaces. The 2.3L gaskets may be reused only if free of nicks, cuts and abrasions.

steps.title: Reconnect concealed attachments before seating
steps.body: On the 2.3L, attach the knock-sensor retainers and crankcase ventilation coupling, then position the manifold on the coolant-tube stud with the tube correctly located. On the V8s, fit new gaskets and reconnect rear wiring before final positioning. Follow the engine-specific tightening instructions, including the V8 manifold and fuel-rail torque-and-angle stages.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding assemblies
steps.body: Reconnect each branch’s tubes, wiring, retainers and supports in installation order. Restore V8 fuel connections, insulators where applicable, cowl parts and inlet pipe. Put the 5.0L cover grommets on the manifold before fitting its cover. Refit the applicable brace, using new 5.2L nuts, and reconnect the V8 battery cables.

watchFor.title: Trapped rear connections
watchFor.body: Do not fully seat the manifold before reconnecting the attachments reached by its partial movement.

watchFor.title: Coolant-tube position on the 2.3L
watchFor.body: The tube must be correctly positioned as the manifold is installed on its stud.

notes: Use each engine’s own coupling and tightening instructions throughout.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris inside the manifold following upper-engine failure
diagnostics.meaning: Reusing the manifold risks further engine damage.
diagnostics.next: Install a new manifold.

verification.title: Confirm restoration
verification.body: Check the selected installation procedure for every coupling, connector, retainer, support and cover disturbed.

verification.title: Record inspection and road-test results
verification.body: Record the debris inspection and gasket disposition. If a new manifold was installed, complete and record the required road test.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L intake manifold removal, inspection and installation.
5.0L intake manifold removal and installation.
5.2L intake manifold removal and installation.
Lifting points and hoist precautions for 2.3L access.
2.3L quick-release coupling handling.
5.0L fuel-pressure release before removal.
5.2L fuel-pressure release before removal.
Battery disconnection and reconnection for the V8 branches.
5.0L air-cleaner outlet pipe removal and installation.
Cowl grille removal and installation for V8 access.
5.0L quick-release coupling handling.
5.2L quick-release coupling handling.

guides.title: Remove and refit the front bumper beam
guides.summary: Remove the front bumper beam after clearing its cover, wiring guides and any fitted grille-shutter or adaptive-cruise hardware.
guides.introduction: The front bumper beam is the transverse structural member behind the outer bumper cover. Removing it involves more than exposing its mounting bolts: sensor brackets, wiring guides and optional equipment occupy the same working area. This job provides the route for beam replacement or removal for access.
guides.why: Clearing the attached equipment first prevents the beam from pulling on wiring as it comes away. Its width also makes controlled support important; plan removal and installation as a two-person operation.

when.summary: When the front bumper beam requires replacement or must be removed for access.
notes: Check whether active grille shutters or adaptive cruise control are fitted before planning the work.

prepare.title: Arrange support and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have a second person available to support the beam and a torque wrench suitable for its mounting bolts.

prepare.title: Allow for the access procedures
prepare.detail: The bumper cover comes off first. If fitted, the grille shutters and cruise control module with its bracket each require their own removal and installation procedure.

steps.title: Remove the outer cover
steps.body: Follow the [front bumper cover procedure](#/document/G1694213) to expose the beam. Keep the distinction between the cover and the bolted beam clear when identifying the parts being removed.

steps.title: Clear the sensor bracket and optional equipment
steps.body: Position the ambient-air-temperature sensor bracket and wiring-harness guide aside. Remove the [active grille shutter assembly](#/document/G1693244), if fitted. If adaptive cruise control is fitted, remove the [cruise control module and bracket](#/document/G1693160). Complete these access operations before releasing the beam.

steps.title: Separate the guides and remove the beam
steps.body: Separate the wiring-harness guides. With both people supporting the beam, remove the eight illustrated mounting bolts and take the beam away. Keep the displaced wiring clear as the assembly moves.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Position the beam and install its bolts, tightening them to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm). Reassemble the harness guides, then restore any removed cruise-control and grille-shutter assemblies using their procedures. Return the ambient sensor bracket and wiring guide to position and reinstall the bumper cover.

watchFor.title: A remaining attachment
watchFor.body: If the beam is still restrained after unbolting, check the guides and surrounding equipment before moving it farther.

watchFor.title: Optional equipment affects the work
watchFor.body: Removing a cruise-control module or grille-shutter assembly adds its complete installation procedure to this job.

notes: The beam mounting torque given alongside removal is the installation tightening value.

verification.title: Confirm the beam and surrounding equipment are restored
verification.body: Confirm all eight beam bolts are tightened, the harness guides are joined, the ambient sensor bracket is back in position and every applicable equipment procedure is complete before finishing the cover installation.

procedures.purpose: Front bumper beam removal and installation.
Outer bumper cover removal and installation for access.
Active grille shutter removal and installation, if equipped.
Adaptive-cruise control module and bracket removal and installation, if equipped.

guides.title: Replace a front brake flexible hose
guides.summary: Replace the flexible connection between the front brake tube and caliper, renew its sealing washers and pressure-bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The flexible hose carries hydraulic pressure from the rigid brake tube to the moving front caliper. Replacing it opens the hydraulic circuit at both ends. The repair therefore includes restoring the connections and bleeding the system before the brakes return to service.
guides.why: Open connections admit contamination and air. Air compresses under pressure and interferes with hydraulic brake operation, so tightening the fittings alone does not finish this repair. The caliper connection also depends on sound sealing washers.

when.summary: When a front brake hose requires replacement or removal as part of an established repair.
notes: Identify the fitted caliper before selecting the appropriate removal branch.

prepare.title: Prepare for an open hydraulic circuit
prepare.detail: Arrange access to the caliper connection, brake-tube union and hose mountings. Have suitable caps or plugs to seal every opening, replacement sealing washers and torque tools.

prepare.title: Have bleeding capability ready
prepare.detail: Obtain the Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure and the equipment it requires before disconnecting the hose. Bleeding is a required part of completion.

steps.title: Detach the caliper end
steps.body: Follow the branch for the fitted 2-, 4- or 6-piston caliper. Remove the caliper flow bolt and detach the hose, sealing the exposed openings. At the illustrated joint, discard both sealing washers and use new ones during installation.

steps.title: Release the remaining hose attachments
steps.body: If fitted, remove the flexible-hose bracket mounting bolt. Disconnect the brake-tube fitting, then remove the hose mounting bolt and hose. Keep all disconnected openings sealed throughout the work.

steps.title: Install the hose and restore the joints
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Tighten the hose mounting bolt to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm), the brake-tube fitting to 155 lb.in (17.5 Nm), and the optional bracket bolt to 177 lb.in (20 Nm). Reconnect the caliper joint with new sealing washers; the flow-bolt torque is 30 lb.ft (40 Nm) for each listed caliper branch.

steps.title: Bleed the brake system
steps.body: Complete Brake System Pressure Bleeding after installation. Use that procedure for the actual bleeding method; do not return the vehicle to service with the required hydraulic work unfinished.

watchFor.title: Brake fluid on paint
watchFor.body: Immediately wash any affected paintwork with cold water.

watchFor.title: Unsealed openings
watchFor.body: Keep both hose ends and their mating openings protected until each connection is reassembled.

notes: The caliper piston count selects the branch, but all three branches specify the same flow-bolt torque.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical and hydraulic completion
verification.body: Check that both hydraulic connections and all applicable hose mountings have been restored to their specified torque.

verification.title: Record the bleeding completion
verification.body: Record completion of the required pressure-bleeding procedure as part of the hose repair.

procedures.purpose: Front brake hose removal and installation for 2-, 4- and 6-piston calipers, followed by the referenced pressure-bleeding procedure.

guides.title: Remove and refit the steering column lower shaft
guides.summary: Disconnect and reinstall the collapsible lower steering shaft using new bolts, then complete its required collapsed check.
guides.introduction: The lower steering shaft connects the upper column shaft to the coupling leading to the steering gear. It transmits steering-wheel movement and incorporates a collapsible section. Whenever either end is disconnected, the shaft must be measured using the collapsed-check procedure, even if it appears undamaged.
guides.why: Forcing this assembly can damage steering components. Allowing the disconnected column to rotate can damage its electrical components. Loosening the dash seal first, holding the wheel straight ahead and renewing the shaft bolts are essential parts of the repair.

when.summary: When lower-shaft removal or replacement is required; measure it after disconnection from either end.
notes: Select the correct left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive fastening branch.

prepare.title: Arrange safe access and wheel restraint
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the prescribed lifting points. Have a steering-wheel holding device, such as Hunter® 28-75-1 or equivalent, to maintain the straight-ahead position.

prepare.title: Prepare fasteners and inspection capability
prepare.detail: Have new shaft bolts, suitable torque tools and the Steering Column Collapsed Check procedure available. Its measurement and acceptance criteria are required to finish the job.

steps.title: Position the vehicle and hold the wheel
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on the hoist using the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Secure the steering wheel straight ahead with the holding device. Maintain that position while the shaft system is disconnected.

steps.title: Loosen the dash seal before separating the shaft
steps.body: Follow the [lower-shaft procedure](#/document/G1721916) to loosen the dash seal and remove its nuts. Loosen the seal as directed, then hand-start the nuts. Minimize damage to the sealer foam and keep the dash-seal brackets attached to their retainer pins.

steps.title: Remove and discard the shaft bolts
steps.body: Remove the common shaft bolt and the applicable left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive bolt. Discard the removed bolts; they must not be reused. The handedness branches are alternatives, not instructions to remove an additional bolt from every vehicle.

steps.title: Separate the shaft without force
steps.body: Pull the lower shaft apart from the coupling, then from the upper steering shaft. Do not hammer, pry or force the assembly. If separation is resisted, check that the dash seal and its fasteners have been loosened before proceeding.

steps.title: Refit with new bolts
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence while keeping the dash seal loose for shaft engagement. Use new shaft bolts. The common bolt is tightened to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm); the handedness-specific bolt uses 22 lb.ft (30 Nm) on left-hand-drive vehicles or 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm) on right-hand-drive vehicles. Restore the dash seal and tighten its nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm).

steps.title: Complete the collapsed check
steps.body: Inspect and measure the lower shaft using [Steering Column Collapsed Check](#/document/G1721912). Follow that procedure’s decision criteria before returning the steering system to service; visual appearance alone does not complete this check.

watchFor.title: Damaged dash sealing
watchFor.body: Excessive foam or bracket damage can allow engine noise, fumes, air or water into the passenger compartment.

watchFor.title: Column rotation or forced engagement
watchFor.body: Keep the wheel restrained and stop if assembly requires hammering, levering or force.

notes: The illustration shows left-hand drive; use the right-hand-drive branch where applicable.
Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

diagnostics.finding: The lower shaft has been disconnected from the upper shaft or coupling
diagnostics.meaning: A collapsed-shaft measurement is required.
diagnostics.next: Complete the specified check regardless of whether replacement was initially planned.

verification.title: Confirm fastening and sealing
verification.body: Confirm new shaft bolts were fitted using the correct handedness branch and that the dash seal and its fasteners are restored.

verification.title: Record the measured result
verification.body: Record the collapsed-check measurement and the resulting decision against the linked procedure’s criteria.

procedures.purpose: Lower steering shaft removal and installation, including handedness-specific fasteners.
Vehicle lifting points and support precautions.
Required lower-shaft inspection and measurement after disconnection.

guides.title: Replace the 5.2L 3160 transmission extension housing gasket
guides.summary: Remove the transmission’s rear extension housing, renew its case-joint gasket and restore the fluid and any disturbed cooler connections.
guides.introduction: The 3160 six-speed manual transmission has an aluminum extension housing around its rear output-shaft area. A gasket seals the joint between this housing and the main case. Replacing it requires draining the transmission and removing the gearshift lever and output flange before the housing can slide off the shaft.
guides.why: A new gasket needs clean mating faces to seal correctly. Cooler-equipped versions add another inspection task: seals and backing rings can remain in the case when the tubes are withdrawn, so every piece must be accounted for before reassembly.
searchTerms: transmission fluid leak at rear housing

when.summary: For a confirmed extension-housing joint leak or gasket renewal after removing the housing.
notes: Fluid near the rear of the transmission does not by itself identify the housing gasket as the cause.

prepare.title: Plan the connected procedures
prepare.detail: This requires transmission-housing work, controlled fluid drainage and accurate torque tightening. Arrange access and capability for the separate gearshift-lever, output-flange and draining/filling procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare the gasket and specified materials
prepare.detail: Have a new housing gasket, Motorcraft Thread Sealant with PTFE TA-24-B (WSK-M2G350-A2), and Motorcraft MERCON LV Automatic Transmission Fluid XT-10-QLVC (WSS-M2C938-A). Cooler seals and backing rings are replaced if damaged.

steps.title: Drain the transmission
steps.body: Remove the drain plug and drain the fluid. Apply the specified thread sealant to the plug and reinstall it at 21 lb.ft (28 Nm), following the [gasket procedure](#/document/G1805396).

steps.title: Remove the lever and output flange
steps.body: Complete [gearshift lever removal](#/document/G1796480), followed by [output shaft flange removal](#/document/G1805399). These are separate access operations with their own installation requirements.

steps.title: Move cooler tubes aside where fitted
steps.body: Remove the cooler-tube nuts and bolts and position the tubes aside. Inspect the case to confirm the seals and backing rings came out with the tubes. Remove any that remain stuck in the case.

steps.title: Release wiring and withdraw the housing
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connectors and harness retainers, then position the harness aside. Remove the housing bolts and slide the extension housing off the output shaft.

steps.title: Renew the case-joint gasket
steps.body: Clean the old gasket material from both the transmission case and extension-housing sealing surfaces. Fit a new gasket on the case, install the housing and tighten its fasteners to 24 lb.ft (33 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the wiring and cooler connections
steps.body: Reconnect the electrical connectors and retainers. If cooler tubes were removed, inspect their backing rings and seals and replace damaged pieces. Use the specified fluid for the seal installation step. Refit the tubes, matching each fastener to its tightening callout in the complete procedure; the cooler fasteners do not all share one torque.

steps.title: Restore the flange, lever and fluid
steps.body: Reinstall the output flange, then the gearshift lever, using their procedures. Fill the transmission using [Transmission Draining and Filling](#/document/G1794233) for the correct filling method and final level.

watchFor.title: A seal left behind
watchFor.body: Check inside the cooler-tube connection in the case; inspecting only the removed tube can miss a retained seal or backing ring.

watchFor.title: Gasket residue
watchFor.body: Clean both mating faces before positioning the replacement gasket.

notes: The fluid drain and refill are part of opening this housing, not a newly introduced maintenance interval.

diagnostics.finding: A cooler-tube seal or backing ring is damaged
diagnostics.meaning: That sealing component is unsuitable for reuse.
diagnostics.next: Install a new seal or backing ring as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: The origin of rear-transmission fluid leakage is uncertain
diagnostics.meaning: The housing gasket, output-shaft seal and flange sealing parts are distinct components.
diagnostics.next: Establish the leaking joint before selecting this gasket repair.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly and filling
verification.body: Confirm the housing, harness, applicable cooler tubes, output flange and gearshift lever are restored, and complete the linked filling procedure.

verification.title: Record the sealing work
verification.body: Record gasket renewal, cooler seal/backing-ring inspection and any replacements, together with completion of the transmission refill.

procedures.purpose: 3160 extension housing removal, gasket renewal and installation.
3160 gearshift lever removal and installation for access.
3160 output shaft flange removal and installation.
3160 transmission draining and final filling.

applicability.equipment: 3160 six-speed manual transmission; transmission fluid cooler if equipped

guides.title: Inspect connector terminal fit and release damaged wire terminals
guides.summary: Check mating-terminal fit, identify the correct connector release geometry and use the specified tools to avoid damaging the terminals.
guides.introduction: An electrical connector’s plastic shell positions and retains the metal terminals that carry the circuit. The male and female terminals must fit correctly for a durable connection. This job checks that fit and provides a route to terminal removal when repair is needed; a connector fault does not establish that its attached module has failed.
guides.why: An unsuitable probe can distort a terminal during testing. A terminal guide can also add friction that masks weak mating contact. Removal requires equal care because different shells place their terminal-release tangs at different depths.

when.summary: When connector inspection is required during electrical diagnosis or a damaged terminal needs removal.
notes: Identify the actual connector shell and terminal position before choosing a release dimension.

prepare.title: Apply the relevant safety precautions
prepare.detail: Read Health and Safety Precautions and the applicable system warnings first. Disable remote start where fitted, prevent unauthorized starting and use the required protection. Follow system-specific isolation requirements; this general procedure does not authorize probing an airbag igniter.

prepare.title: Use the specified connection tools
prepare.detail: Use Rotunda Flex Probes NUD105-R025D or Terminal Probe Kit 29-011A when connecting test equipment or jumper wires. Have the correct mating terminal for fit assessment and a suitable terminal-removal tool that can be marked for insertion depth.

steps.title: Identify the connector arrangement
steps.body: Match the shell to the [terminal inspection and removal procedure](#/document/G1939867). One illustrated arrangement for the Audio Front Control Module, Body Control Module and Instrument Panel Cluster identifies an external terminal-release tang and a connector locking tab. Distinguish these features before attempting release.

steps.title: Assess the actual mating fit
steps.body: Use the mating terminal to check for normal separation force. Very low force indicates a damaged or poorly fitting terminal. The relevant check is terminal-to-terminal engagement, rather than how firmly the complete plastic connector seems to latch.

steps.title: Account for guide or retainer friction
steps.body: For small terminals, determine whether the terminal guide or retainer adds drag during insertion or withdrawal. If it does, remove it as required for an accurate fit check. Otherwise, its friction can make weak terminal engagement seem satisfactory.

steps.title: Select dimensions for the exact terminal position
steps.body: The shared Audio Front Control Module, Front Controls Interface Module, Gateway Module A and heating, ventilation and air-conditioning control-module arrangement distinguishes inner and outer terminals. The separate Body Control Module layouts also distinguish terminal widths and inner, outer or lower release positions. Use the matching illustration and table, rather than selecting a dimension from the module name alone.

steps.title: Match in-line and seat connectors separately
steps.body: The two body-harness in-line layouts have different release geometry. The body-harness/seat-harness and body-harness/seat-module arrangements also use different release depths, despite sharing a listed terminal width. Confirm which shell and cavity are present before preparing the tool.

steps.title: Mark the tool and follow the release operation
steps.body: The listed hard-shell dimension is measured from the connector’s front face to the terminal-release tang engagement point. Mark that distance on the removal tool before insertion. Follow the matching illustrated release operation and the linked repair demonstration for damaged terminal or connector replacement; the dimensions alone do not specify a universal release motion.

watchFor.title: A probe that changes the fault
watchFor.body: Avoid forcing an unsuitable test connection into the terminal. Use the specified probe equipment whenever test leads or jumpers are connected.

watchFor.title: Similar connector names
watchFor.body: Several entries share a module or harness name while describing different shells or terminal positions.

notes: The complete procedure retains the connector-specific widths and release-depth tables needed at the vehicle.

diagnostics.finding: Very low separation force between mating terminals
diagnostics.meaning: The terminal fit is compromised.
diagnostics.next: Identify the damaged terminal or connector and follow its replacement instructions.

diagnostics.finding: The terminal guide contributes insertion or removal drag
diagnostics.meaning: The apparent resistance does not accurately represent mating-terminal fit.
diagnostics.next: Remove the guide or retainer where necessary and repeat the assessment.

verification.title: Confirm terminal fit
verification.body: After any terminal repair, repeat the mating-terminal fit assessment without misleading guide or retainer drag.

verification.title: Record the finding
verification.body: Record the connector and cavity assessed, the fit finding and any terminal replacement. Keep this result separate from conclusions about the connected module.

procedures.purpose: Terminal fit assessment, connector-specific release dimensions and terminal-removal guidance.
Required general and applicable system-specific service precautions.

guides.title: Remove and install a rear halfshaft
guides.summary: Remove the rear halfshaft, renew its differential seal and retaining circlip, and verify secure engagement before restoring the differential fluid level.
guides.introduction: The rear halfshaft carries drive from the differential to the rear wheel. Its constant velocity (CV) joints accommodate movement between the differential and wheel as the suspension travels. Removing it involves the wheel knuckle as well as the connection inside the differential, so careful handling matters throughout the job.
guides.why: The inner circlip retains the shaft inside the differential, while the seal keeps lubricant around the rotating connection. Both require attention whenever the shaft comes out: the circlip is discarded and the seal must be replaced. Rough handling can damage a joint or cut a boot internally without leaving an obvious external mark.

when.summary: When a rear halfshaft requires replacement or must be removed for related driveline work.
notes: Seal replacement is required after every halfshaft removal, even when the same shaft will be refitted.

prepare.title: Plan the suspension access
prepare.detail: Have the lifting, support and suspension-service capability needed for the wheel-knuckle procedure. Follow its complete removal and installation requirements before working at the differential.

prepare.title: Have the replacement parts ready
prepare.detail: Prepare a new inner halfshaft circlip, a new halfshaft seal and a pry bar. Arrange to check and correct the differential fluid level after assembly.

steps.title: Remove the wheel knuckle
steps.body: Follow the [wheel-knuckle procedure](#/document/G1686658) to clear the outer end of the halfshaft. Support and handle the shaft as an assembly; never pick it up or hold it solely by either CV joint.

steps.title: Release the inner connection
steps.body: Use a pry bar as shown in the [halfshaft procedure](#/document/G2214772) to release the shaft from the differential. Do not hammer it out or use the shaft itself to lever another component into position.

steps.title: Inspect and renew the sealing and retaining parts
steps.body: Inspect the inner seal-running surface and splines for damage, then remove and discard the inner circlip. Replace the differential-side halfshaft seal using the [seal procedure](#/document/G2214752), and install a new circlip on the shaft.

steps.title: Seat the halfshaft positively
steps.body: Insert the halfshaft until the circlip is fully seated. Correct engagement can be felt as the clip snaps into the differential side-gear groove. Pull on the inner end afterward to establish that the circlip has locked.

steps.title: Restore the suspension and fluid level
steps.body: Install the wheel knuckle using its complete procedure. Finish by checking and topping off the rear differential fluid using the Differential Fluid Level Check referenced in the halfshaft procedure.

watchFor.title: Boot contact and hidden impact damage
watchFor.body: Keep the boots away from sharp edges and hot exhaust components. Do not drop an assembled shaft: impact can cut a boot from inside even when its outside looks intact.

watchFor.title: A shaft that appears seated
watchFor.body: Insertion alone does not establish retention. The required pull check is made at the inner end after installation.

notes: Do not use a hammer during either removal or installation.
A new seal does not eliminate the need to inspect the shaft surface that runs through it.

diagnostics.finding: Damage is visible on the inner sealing surface or splines.
diagnostics.meaning: The mating surfaces need attention before the assembly can be considered ready for installation.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the damage before refitting; do not rely on a new seal or circlip to compensate for it.

verification.title: Record retention and lubrication
verification.body: Confirm and record that the inner-end pull check established circlip retention and that the differential fluid level was checked and corrected.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Verify that the wheel-knuckle installation is complete and that the shaft boots were not trapped, cut or exposed to damaging contact during the work.

procedures.purpose: Rear halfshaft removal, inspection, seal and circlip renewal requirements, installation and final fluid check.
Remove and reinstall the rear wheel knuckle for halfshaft access.
Replace the rear halfshaft seal whenever the shaft is removed.

guides.title: Drain both sides of the saddle-type fuel tank
guides.summary: Lower the fuel level through the capless filler, then drain the left and right tank saddles through their separate service openings.
guides.introduction: The saddle-shaped fuel tank has left and right sections that must each be emptied during complete draining. The initial transfer through the filler lowers the fuel beneath the pump mounting flange; it does not finish the job. Access beneath the rear seat then allows the remaining fuel to be removed through the pump-and-sender opening and the separate fuel-level-sensor opening.
guides.why: Opening the tank before lowering the fuel level can release fuel at the mounting flange. The float arms are easily damaged during handling, and the flange sealing surfaces determine whether the tank can seal correctly afterward. Damaged sealing surfaces require component replacement rather than polishing or reshaping.

when.summary: When a repair requires the fuel tank to be completely drained.
notes: Choose the pressure-release and fuel-coupling procedures for the actual engine.
The draining endpoint leaves the tank units positioned aside; subsequent installation requires the applicable component procedures.

prepare.title: Provide fuel-transfer capability
prepare.detail: Use Fuel Tanker 100 GPM, special tool 292-00004, and fuel tank lock-ring tool 310-123. This work requires controlled fuel transfer, storage and fuel-system pressure release.

prepare.title: Prepare filler and cabin access
prepare.detail: Locate the supplemental refueling adapter in the luggage compartment. Prepare a 6 ft. length of 5/8 in. semi-rigid fuel drain tube and access to the rear seat cushion.

steps.title: Release pressure before disconnecting the battery
steps.body: Complete the engine-specific Fuel System Pressure Release procedure, then disconnect the battery ground cable using the battery procedure. Preserve this order before opening fuel connections.

steps.title: Lower the level through the filler
steps.body: Insert the supplemental adapter and drain tube into the Easy Fuel filler until the tube reaches the tank. Connect the tanker and remove as much fuel as possible through this route. This first transfer lowers fuel below the pump-and-sender flange and removes most residual fuel from the filler pipe.

steps.title: Open the pump-and-sender access
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion and position the pump access cover aside. Disconnect the electrical connector and fuel-tube quick-release coupling using the engine-matched coupling procedure. Carefully engage the lock-ring tool and remove the ring without damaging the unit.

steps.title: Empty the left saddle
steps.body: Position the pump-and-sender unit aside without damaging its float arm. Use the tanker to drain the left saddle completely. Inspect the unit flange and tank O-ring contact surfaces, then remove and discard the pump-and-sender O-ring.

steps.title: Empty the right saddle
steps.body: Position the fuel-level-sensor access cover aside. Clean the connections, flange and immediate surrounding area before disconnecting the electrical connector. Carefully remove the lock ring, move the sensor aside while protecting its float arm, and drain the right saddle completely.

steps.title: Assess the second sealing joint
steps.body: Inspect the fuel-level-sensor flange and tank O-ring contact surfaces, then remove and discard its O-ring. If either opening has a bent, scratched or corroded sealing contact area, replace the affected unit or tank. Do not polish or adjust these surfaces.

watchFor.title: Fuel remaining after the filler transfer
watchFor.body: Little or no further fuel coming through the filler tube does not establish that both saddles are empty.

watchFor.title: Fragile float arms
watchFor.body: Both the pump-and-sender unit and the separate level sensor require careful handling while positioned aside.

notes: Discard both removed O-rings; plan replacement seals for the subsequent installation.
The shared draining sequence does not make engine-specific pressure-release or coupling instructions interchangeable.

diagnostics.finding: A flange sealing contact area is bent, scratched or corroded.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing joint requires more than O-ring renewal.
diagnostics.next: Install a new pump-and-sender unit, fuel-level sensor or fuel tank as appropriate to the damaged surface.

verification.title: Record the draining result
verification.body: Confirm that the left and right saddles were each completely drained, rather than recording only the initial filler transfer.

verification.title: Document sealing-surface condition
verification.body: Record any flange damage and required replacement, and confirm that both old O-rings were discarded before handing the tank over to the next repair phase.

Carry out the required battery disconnection.

guides.title: Replace the rear floor panel on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Replace the damaged welded rear floor, restore its attachments and protective materials, and complete the additional convertible reinforcement work where applicable.
guides.introduction: The rear floor is part of the welded body shell and includes the spare-wheel well and attachments for surrounding panels and brackets. Replacing it involves restoring body shape, separating welded and bonded joints, fitting the new panel, and rebuilding its sealing, sound-deadening and corrosion protection. Convertible bodies also require crossmember and reinforcement work.
guides.why: A replacement panel can preserve existing distortion if the body is not restored before fitting. Weld positions and quantities govern how the new floor joins the surrounding structure. Sealer, foam, mastic and corrosion protection complete those joints and must be restored along with the metal.

when.summary: When assessed rear-body damage requires replacement or permitted sectioning of the rear floor panel.
notes: Select the sectioning plan from the permitted cut points for the actual damage.
Most operations are shared; crossmember and additional reinforcement operations are convertible-only.

prepare.title: Arrange structural repair capability
prepare.detail: Provide body measurement and dimensional restoration capability, resistance spotwelding, metal inert gas (MIG) brazing and MIG/metal active gas (MAG) welding equipment. Follow Joining Techniques for the selected joints.

prepare.title: Prepare separation and fitting tools
prepare.detail: Have a spot-weld drill bit, spherical cutter, straight-edge scraper, knife, hot-air gun, locking pliers and an 8 mm drill bit. Protect adjacent areas from cutting, grinding and welding.

prepare.title: Plan component removal
prepare.detail: Arrange safe access and support for rear-subframe removal and the engine-matched fuel-system and exhaust procedures. Include supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering in the work plan.

steps.title: Depower and establish body shape
steps.body: Depower the SRS using its dedicated procedure. If required, dimensionally restore the vehicle to its pre-damage condition using Body and Frame before separating the floor.

steps.title: Clear the working area
steps.body: Remove the rear seat, quarter trim and body-style-specific loadspace trim. Move carpeting, modules and wiring away. Remove the fitted evaporative-emission canister, fuel tank, rear subframe, muffler and tailpipe, back panel and reinforcement, and wheel-and-tire components through their respective procedures.

steps.title: Expose the panel joints
steps.body: On a convertible, drill out the crossmember spot welds and remove the crossmember. Remove the noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) mastic. Heat may assist softening, but must not exceed 170°C.

steps.title: Separate the old floor
steps.body: Drill the floor-seam spot welds and grind away the brazed material. On both sides, drill the lower quarter-panel-extension welds and remove the foam carrier strips. Remove the floor assembly; heat used to soften its adhesive must also remain at or below 170°C.

steps.title: Prepare and fit the replacement
steps.body: Drill the specified plug-weld holes in the replacement floor and both rear floor extensions using the 8 mm bit. Properly position and clamp the floor, then position and clamp the extensions before joining.

steps.title: Rebuild the floor joints
steps.body: Follow the [rear floor procedure](#/document/G1687560) and Joining Techniques for the welding and brazing locations. Complete the floor and extension joints on both sides, including the connections to the quarter-panel extensions.

steps.title: Complete convertible reinforcement
steps.body: For a convertible, install and weld the underbody crossmember. Drill the replacement reinforcement's plug-weld holes, then position, clamp and weld it as directed.

steps.title: Restore brackets and foam
steps.body: Drill the vapor-canister and spare-tire brackets for plug welding, then position, clamp and weld them. Apply the specified NVH expanding foam to the foam carrier strips and install them on both sides.

steps.title: Finish and protect the repair
steps.body: Dress the welds as required, seal every seam to production level and restore NVH material in its original locations. Refinish with a Ford-approved paint system and restore corrosion protection.

steps.title: Reassemble the vehicle
steps.body: Reinstall the removed underbody components, back panel and reinforcement, and wheels using their procedures. Return wiring, modules and carpet to their original positions, install the trim and rear seat, then repower the SRS.

watchFor.title: Substitute weld locations
watchFor.body: Replacement resistance welds must sit adjacent to the original locations and match the factory quantity. MAG plug welds must match both factory location and quantity.

watchFor.title: Heat and nearby components
watchFor.body: The heat allowance for softening material does not remove the need to protect adjacent areas or move wiring and modules away.

notes: The illustrations generally show the coupe and left side; follow the corresponding operations on the right side.
The listed engine-specific canister, tank and exhaust references cover 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. For a 5.2L vehicle, establish the matching access procedures before removal.

diagnostics.finding: The rear body is dimensionally displaced.
diagnostics.meaning: Correct panel fit depends on restoring the surrounding structure first.
diagnostics.next: Carry out the required dimensional restoration before floor replacement.

verification.title: Record structural completion
verification.body: Record the dimensional assessment and any restoration, and verify that completed welds satisfy the required locations and quantities.

verification.title: Confirm protective and vehicle restoration
verification.body: Check completion of seam sealing, foam, NVH material, refinishing and corrosion protection. Confirm component reinstallation and completion of the SRS repowering procedure.

guides.title: Inspect and restore the restraint system after deployment
guides.summary: Determine the required post-collision restraint replacements, inspect related structure and fuel-system damage, and complete the specified resets before vehicle release.
guides.introduction: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) uses airbags and seatbelt pretensioners to respond to a collision. Its restraints control module (RCM) monitors sensors and selects the devices to deploy, so a collision may activate one device or several. Repair must address the deployed equipment, its supporting structure and stored crash information as one coordinated job.
guides.why: Replacing visible airbags alone can leave damaged mounts, deployed belt components or unresolved control-system faults. The occupant classification system (OCS) also needs its own assessment and reset when components are replaced. The vehicle must have a fully operational, fault-free SRS before release.

when.summary: After restraint deployment or collision-related B1193:00 storage requiring the specified inspection and repair.
notes: Rear pretensioner and side-curtain requirements apply only where that equipment is fitted.
Stored crash information must be interpreted by module; the RCM and OCS module have different repair decisions.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint personnel
prepare.detail: Pyrotechnic service requires qualified personnel and the [pyrotechnic safety precautions](#/document/G1693191). Follow each component's removal, isolation and installation requirements. Never probe airbag connectors or back-probe deployable-device connectors.

prepare.title: Provide diagnostic capability
