prepare.detail: A diagnostic scan tool is required to read module faults, perform the OCS Reset when required, clear diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), and check or reset body control module (BCM) crash status.

prepare.title: Handle deployed and live devices correctly
prepare.detail: Do not handle pyrotechnic components immediately after deployment. Use protective gloves, safety glasses and breathing protection against residues. Carry live airbags with the deployment face away from the body and never set them face-down.

steps.title: Establish the deployment and module record
steps.body: Identify every deployed device and read the RCM and occupant classification system module (OCSM) faults. Apply the separate B1193:00 decisions below. When any deployable device has activated, or the RCM contains that code, replace all deployed devices, all impact sensors and the RCM with new components.

steps.title: Inspect structure and mounting points
steps.body: Inspect the instrument panel, its mounts, braces, brackets and knee bolsters; seats and seat mounts; fitted curtains and their mounts; belts, buckles, retractors and anchors; and SRS wiring and connectors. Repair or replace damaged components. Restore damaged RCM or sensor mounting areas to production configuration and replace the component mounted there, even if airbags did not deploy.

steps.title: Restore steering and seatbelt systems
steps.body: Driver-airbag deployment requires a new steering wheel, clockspring and adaptive energy absorption steering column. Replace the corresponding front seatbelt systems after front pretensioner deployment, including retractors, buckles and height adjusters. Rear pretensioner deployment, where equipped, requires new second-row retractors and buckles. Inspect all belt components as part of collision repair.

steps.title: Address side-airbag and curtain damage
steps.body: After seat side-airbag deployment, replace the airbag, backrest cover and foam; inspect its mounting area and replace a deformed backrest frame. After curtain deployment, install a new headliner, roof-pillar upper trim and attaching hardware, including new torque-prevailing J-nuts. Confirm the headliner AIRBAG marking at each roof B-pillar trim interface.

steps.title: Complete occupant-classification repairs
steps.body: If the OCSM stores B1193:00 after a collision, inspect the OCS and repair damage. Required OCS component replacement must use an OCS service kit. Keep calibrated assemblies together and free of contamination. After installing new OCS components, perform the scan-tool OCS Reset as directed.

steps.title: Finish installation and inspect the fuel system
steps.body: Inspect for fuel-system damage or leaks and repair or replace affected parts. Complete restraint installation through each component procedure, including specified mounting torques and connector locking. Clear DTCs from all required modules after repairs.

steps.title: Resolve BCM crash status
steps.body: Read the BCM CRASH parameter identification (PID) value. If present and reading Yes, perform BCM Crash Status Reset under Electrical - Service Functions. A No value or absent parameter does not cancel any remaining repair or SRS verification requirement.

watchFor.title: Steering-column damage without driver-airbag deployment
watchFor.body: A bent, loose or damaged wheel or shaft; binding, sticking, abnormal movement, bearing damage or incorrect shaft length also requires a new adaptive energy absorption column. Use the Steering Column Collapsed Check. Never fit a repaired, rebuilt or remanufactured column.

watchFor.title: Connector and module handling
watchFor.body: Replace damaged restraint terminals with service connector pigtails; do not repair the terminals. Never tamper with restraint components or move a connected RCM with the ignition on.

notes: A connector-position-assurance tab that is not fully seated can leave the component's shorting bars engaged and produce a low-resistance fault. A fault alone does not prove the airbag is defective.

diagnostics.finding: Any deployable device activated, or the RCM stores B1193:00.
diagnostics.meaning: The mandatory post-event replacement scope applies.
diagnostics.next: Install new deployed devices, all impact sensors and a new RCM.

diagnostics.finding: The OCSM stores B1193:00 after a collision.
diagnostics.meaning: The OCS requires inspection; this code does not itself establish which OCS component is damaged.
diagnostics.next: Repair identified damage, use a service kit for required OCS replacement and perform the required reset.

diagnostics.finding: BCM CRASH reads Yes.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM crash status requires resetting.
diagnostics.next: Run BCM Crash Status Reset with the diagnostic scan tool.

verification.title: Establish release readiness
verification.body: Confirm the SRS is fully operational and free of faults, all required collision repairs are complete, and fuel-system damage or leaks have been addressed.

verification.title: Record the final diagnostic result
verification.body: Record replaced devices and sensors, module fault results, any OCS Reset performed, and the BCM CRASH reading and reset action where applicable.

procedures.purpose: Post-deployment replacement decisions, whole-vehicle inspection and final crash-status handling.
Required pyrotechnic handling, mounting, connector and collision-repair precautions.
Check steering-column collapse and shaft length when assessing column replacement.

guides.title: Replace the hood latch release cable
guides.summary: Remove the cabin release and routed cable, then restore the latch connection, retaining clips and cowl grommet during installation.
guides.introduction: The hood release cable carries the driver's pull from the interior release to the hood latch. Its route passes through the cowl and continues around the engine compartment to the latch. Replacement therefore involves both interior trim and the radiator sight shield, along with the clips and bracket that locate the cable.
guides.why: The cable ends transmit the pull, while the routing clips and bracket hold the assembly in its intended position. Restoring only the end connections leaves the installation incomplete. The cowl grommet also needs to return to its opening when the new cable is routed through.

when.summary: When the hood latch release cable requires replacement or removal for related repair.
notes: The procedure shows left-hand drive; right-hand drive is similar.
Audio digital signal processing module removal applies only when that module is fitted.

prepare.title: Prepare trim-release tools
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and a 10 mm, 1/4 inch drive socket. The socket is used to release the hood-release-handle clips, rather than as an instruction to remove a fastener.

prepare.title: Plan access at both ends
prepare.detail: Allow access to the driver scuff plate, release handle, cowl trim and radiator sight shield. If fitted, use the Audio Digital Signal Processing (DSP) Module procedure for its removal and refitting.

steps.title: Expose the interior release
steps.body: Remove the DSP module if fitted, then remove the driver door scuff plate with the trim remover. Remove the handle access cover, release the handle clips with the specified socket and remove the handle. Release the clips and remove the left-hand cowl trim panel in the illustrated arrangement.

steps.title: Detach the release assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the cable from the hood latch release, remove the release bolts and remove the release assembly. Free the cable's routing clips and pass the cable through the cowl as directed in the [complete cable procedure](#/document/G1695906).

steps.title: Free the engine-compartment route
steps.body: Remove the radiator sight-shield retainers and shield. Remove the cable grommet, release the routing clips and position the cable aside. Release it from the routing bracket, disconnect its latch-end connection and remove the cable.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Reconnect the latch end and restore the routing bracket, cable clips and grommet as removal is reversed. Route the cable through the cowl, reinstall and reconnect the interior release assembly, then restore the handle, trim, sight shield and any removed DSP module.

watchFor.title: Clips and grommet left out
watchFor.body: Treat the routing attachments as part of the repair. Cable-end engagement does not replace the need to reinstall the bracket, clips and grommet.

watchFor.title: Interior handle clips
watchFor.body: Use the specified clip-release method before removing the handle instead of forcing it away from its mounting.

notes: The engine-compartment illustration identifies the cable route, grommet and clips; use the full procedure for the cabin-side sequence.

verification.title: Confirm the restored cable path
verification.body: Check that both cable ends are connected, the routing bracket and clips are restored, and the cowl grommet is seated.

verification.title: Confirm access components are refitted
verification.body: Check the release assembly, handle and access cover, cowl trim, scuff plate, radiator sight shield and any removed DSP module against the reverse-removal sequence.

procedures.purpose: Remove and reinstall the complete hood latch release cable and its interior and engine-compartment attachments.
Remove and reinstall the audio DSP module where fitted on vehicles with SYNC 2 or SYNC 3.

guides.title: Replace the intake manifold runner-control actuators on 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Remove the intake manifold and position sensors, replace the runner-control actuators, and reinstall everything using the correct engine-specific procedures.
guides.introduction: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) actuators move the manifold's runner-control mechanism, while separate position sensors provide information about its position. Actuator replacement is a manifold-off repair on both engines. Although the overall sequence is shared, the manifold access and sensor instructions must follow the engine fitted to the vehicle.
guides.why: Most of the work lies in reaching the actuators and restoring the connections disturbed during manifold removal. Cleanliness protects exposed engine passages, and correct sealing prevents the repair from creating another problem. The actuator and position sensor are separate components, so replacement should follow an established repair decision.

when.summary: When diagnosis or inspection establishes that an IMRC actuator requires replacement.
notes: This is a removal-and-installation path, not a diagnostic test for choosing between an actuator, sensor or another fault.
Use the 5.2L manifold procedure for that engine; the detailed 5.0L access and sealing instructions are engine-specific.

prepare.title: Provide manifold-service capability
prepare.detail: Arrange a clean work area and the tools required by the engine-matched manifold procedure. For the 5.0L, this includes fuel-pressure release, battery ground and positive cable disconnection, and new manifold gaskets.

prepare.title: Prepare controlled tightening
prepare.detail: Use a torque tool suitable for the actuator retainers. The 5.0L manifold and fuel-rail installation also uses staged torque-and-angle tightening; follow those exact stages in its manifold procedure.

steps.title: Select the correct access procedure
steps.body: Use [5.0L manifold removal](#/document/G1685326) or [5.2L manifold removal](#/document/G1800279). On the 5.0L, release fuel pressure before disconnecting both battery cables. Keep foreign material out of exposed engine passages throughout the work.

steps.title: Remove the intake manifold
steps.body: Follow the selected access sequence. On the 5.0L this includes any fitted strut-tower brace, cover and cowl access, hose supports, tubes, electrical connections and fuel connection. The fuel rail need not be separated from the manifold assembly. After releasing the fasteners, raise the manifold and move it forward to disconnect the rear harness connections. Discard the removed 5.0L manifold gaskets and clean and inspect the sealing surfaces.

steps.title: Remove the position sensors
steps.body: For the 5.0L, use the [IMRC position-sensor procedure](#/document/G1710272) to remove the left and right sensors and their retainers. The 5.2L actuator procedure directs sensor removal through its intake-manifold procedure; follow that route for the 5.2L assembly.

steps.title: Remove the actuators
steps.body: Remove the hoses, retainers and actuators using the illustration for the actual engine: [5.0L](#/document/G1692280) or [5.2L](#/document/G1802185). Keep the hose connections and actuator locations identifiable for installation.

steps.title: Refit actuators and sensors
steps.body: Reverse removal to install the actuators, retainers and hoses. Both actuator procedures specify 53 lb.in (6 Nm) for the retainers. Reinstall the sensors through their applicable procedure; the separate 5.0L sensor procedure also specifies 53 lb.in (6 Nm), which should not be assumed for the 5.2L sensors.

steps.title: Restore the manifold and connections
steps.body: Complete the engine-specific manifold installation. On the 5.0L, use new gaskets and the prescribed manifold and fuel-rail tightening stages, then restore fuel, injector, vapor, crankcase, vacuum and electrical connections, supports and access components. Place the appearance-cover grommets on the manifold before fitting the cover, reinstall any fitted brace, and reconnect both battery cables through the battery procedure.

watchFor.title: Debris after upper-engine damage
watchFor.body: For the 5.0L, an engine repair involving upper-engine failure requires inspection of the manifold for metal debris. Finding debris requires a new manifold.

watchFor.title: Assuming both engines assemble identically
watchFor.body: The shared actuator-retainer torque does not make manifold fasteners, sealing requirements or sensor installation details interchangeable.

notes: Installation details appear within the removal procedures, so read both phases before beginning.
The selected illustration shows the 5.0L actuator arrangement.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris is found in the 5.0L intake manifold after upper-engine failure.
diagnostics.meaning: The manifold can retain material capable of causing further engine damage.
diagnostics.next: Install a new intake manifold instead of completing actuator work on the contaminated manifold.

verification.title: Confirm assembly restoration
verification.body: Verify actuator retainers were tightened, hoses and sensors were restored, and all connections and sealing work required by the engine-specific manifold procedure are complete.

verification.title: Record the applicable final check
verification.body: If a new intake manifold was installed on the 5.0L, road test the vehicle as required by that manifold procedure and record the result.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L IMRC actuator removal and installation after manifold and sensor removal.
5.2L IMRC actuator removal and installation using its engine-specific manifold and sensor access route.
5.0L manifold removal, fuel and battery prerequisites, new gaskets, installation stages and conditional road test.
Remove and reinstall the left and right 5.0L IMRC position sensors.
5.2L manifold removal and installation, including the sensor-removal route referenced by its actuator procedure.

guides.title: Replace the combined MAF/IAT sensor on the 5.0L or 5.2L
guides.summary: Disconnect and remove the combined intake-air sensor, then refit it using the procedure for the correct engine.
guides.introduction: The mass air flow (MAF) and intake air temperature (IAT) sensor provides the engine controls with information about the air entering the engine. This job removes the combined sensor assembly from its mounting and restores its electrical connection afterward. Use it once the need for removal or replacement has been established through engine-control diagnosis.
guides.why: The electrical connector must come off before the sensor is released from its retainers, so the wiring does not restrain the removed component. Engine identification also matters: the 5.2L procedure specifies a retainer torque that must not be carried across to the 5.0L.

when.summary: When an established engine-control repair requires removal or replacement of the combined MAF/IAT sensor.

prepare.title: Choose the engine-specific procedure
prepare.detail: Identify whether the engine is the 5.0L or 5.2L before selecting installation details. The attached illustration shows the 5.0L installation beside the flexible intake duct.

prepare.title: Prepare for the retainers
prepare.detail: Have a suitable retainer driver available. For the 5.2L, use torque equipment capable of accurately applying the specified small tightening value.

steps.title: Disconnect the sensor
steps.body: Locate the combined MAF/IAT sensor using the appropriate engine procedure and disconnect its electrical connector. Complete this separation before loosening the sensor mounting.

steps.title: Remove the retainers and sensor
steps.body: Remove the retainers, then remove the sensor assembly. Keep the retainers available for refitting; neither procedure directs that they be discarded.

steps.title: Refit the sensor and retainers
steps.body: Reverse the mechanical removal sequence. On the 5.2L, tighten the retainers to 18 lb.in (2 Nm). No retainer torque is specified here for the 5.0L; do not substitute the 5.2L setting.

steps.title: Restore the electrical connection
steps.body: Reconnect the sensor after securing its mounting. This completes the reverse-removal sequence and restores the connection through which the engine controls receive its measurements.

watchFor.title: Wiring still attached
watchFor.body: If the connector remains attached, complete its disconnection before removing the sensor from the intake.

watchFor.title: Engine-specific tightening
watchFor.body: A shared component name does not make the installation specifications interchangeable between these engines.

notes: These removal and installation procedures do not prescribe an additional learning or initialization operation.

verification.title: Check the completed installation
verification.body: Confirm that the sensor and retainers are installed and the electrical connector is reconnected. For the 5.2L, confirm completion of the specified retainer tightening.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L combined MAF/IAT sensor removal and installation.
5.2L combined MAF/IAT sensor removal and installation, including retainer torque.

guides.title: Manually release an automatic transmission selector stuck in Park
guides.summary: Use the brake shift interlock override to move the selector into Neutral, then verify brake-light operation before driving.
guides.introduction: The brake shift interlock normally prevents the automatic transmission selector from leaving Park until the brake pedal is applied with the ignition on. Its actuator is built into the selector assembly and mechanically blocks the selector’s detent mechanism. This procedure manually releases that block when the normal release fails, allowing the selector to move into Neutral.
guides.why: In normal operation, the brake pedal position switch provides the input that allows the body control module to energize the interlock actuator. An override bypasses the mechanical restraint without establishing why it failed to release. Neutral also leaves the transmission output shaft free to turn, making the parking brake and applied brake pedal essential during the release.
searchTerms: cannot shift out of Park with brake applied
Park release and brake lights not working

when.summary: When the selector will not leave Park with the ignition on and the brake pedal applied.
notes: The override releases the selector; the cause of the failed normal release still needs attention.

prepare.title: Secure the vehicle
prepare.detail: Fully apply the parking brake before exposing or operating the override. Moving into Neutral removes the transmission’s Park restraint.

prepare.title: Prepare access to the selector
prepare.detail: Have a small screwdriver for the actuator and be ready to lift the selector bezel carefully from its front corners.

steps.title: Apply the parking brake and switch off
steps.body: Fully apply the parking brake, then set the ignition switch to the 0 position, meaning ignition off. This is the starting condition for the manual release.

steps.title: Lift the selector bezel
steps.body: Starting at the front corners, carefully pry the bezel upward and position it out of the way. This exposes the actuator on the selector lever assembly.

steps.title: Operate the manual release
steps.body: Use a small screwdriver to push forward on the brake shift interlock actuator. Apply the brake pedal, press the selector knob button and move the selector into N, or Neutral.

steps.title: Start the engine
steps.body: With the selector in Neutral, start the engine. Maintain control of the vehicle with the brakes because Neutral does not hold the transmission output shaft.

steps.title: Restore the bezel
steps.body: Snap the bezel back into place after starting the engine. Verify brake-light operation before any driving.

watchFor.title: Brake lights may also be inoperative
watchFor.body: A blown fuse is a possible reason the override is needed, and the brake lights may not work. Do not drive until their operation has been verified.

notes: The actuator is integral to the selector assembly. Successful manual release does not establish that the actuator itself caused the fault.

diagnostics.finding: The selector remains in Park with ignition on and the brake pedal applied.
diagnostics.meaning: The normal interlock release has not occurred.
diagnostics.next: Secure the vehicle and follow the manual override sequence when release is necessary.

diagnostics.finding: The brake lights do not operate when checked.
diagnostics.meaning: The interlock complaint may coincide with a blown fuse and loss of brake-light operation.
diagnostics.next: Investigate and correct the fault before driving.

verification.title: Confirm release and trim restoration
verification.body: Confirm that the selector reached Neutral, the engine started and the bezel was snapped back into place.

verification.title: Record the brake-light result
verification.body: Check and record whether the brake lights operate before allowing the vehicle to be driven.

procedures.purpose: Manual activation of the automatic transmission brake shift interlock override.
Explain normal interlock operation and why Neutral does not restrain vehicle movement.

guides.title: Replace the front brake caliper with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Remove and refit the SVT front caliper with new mounting bolts and hose washers, then pressure-bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The front brake caliper converts hydraulic pressure into clamping force at the brake pads. This job separates the caliper from its brake hose and mounting, then removes the pad-retaining components so they can be installed during reassembly. Opening the hose connection makes restoration of the hydraulic system a required part of the repair.
guides.why: The hose connection washers and caliper mounting bolts must be discarded during removal and replaced for installation. Sealing every open connection protects the hydraulic system while it is exposed. Pressure bleeding is required after reassembly because reconnecting the hose alone does not complete the hydraulic work.
searchTerms: SVT Performance Package front brake caliper replacement
SVT brake pad pins and spring retainer

when.summary: When an established front-brake repair requires removal or replacement of the SVT Performance Package caliper.

prepare.title: Arrange brake-service capability
prepare.detail: Provide safe access and support for front-brake work. Have hydraulic-brake service capability and the equipment and complete instructions for Brake System Pressure Bleeding available before disconnecting the hose.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts and sealing equipment
prepare.detail: Have new hose-connection washers, new caliper mounting bolts, suitable means of sealing openings and appropriate torque tools. If fitting new pads, retain all hardware, lubricant and instructions supplied with the pad kit.

steps.title: Disconnect the brake hose
steps.body: Remove the caliper flow bolt and disconnect the hose. Discard the washers and seal all openings. If brake fluid reaches paintwork, immediately wash the affected area with cold water.

steps.title: Remove the caliper
steps.body: Remove the caliper mounting bolts and take off the caliper. Discard those bolts and keep the replacements ready for reassembly.

steps.title: Remove the pad components
steps.body: Remove the brake pad pins, followed by the pads, then the brake pad spring retainer clip. Keep the component positions clear so the reverse sequence can be followed during assembly.

steps.title: Prepare the contact surfaces
steps.body: Clean the pad-to-caliper contact surfaces and apply the lubricant supplied with the brake pad kit as directed by its instruction sheet. If installing new pads, install all new hardware supplied with them.

steps.title: Reassemble and reconnect
steps.body: Reverse removal to install the spring retainer clip, pads and pins, then the caliper. Tighten the new mounting bolts to 136 lb.ft (185 Nm). Reconnect the hose with new washers and tighten the flow bolt to 35 lb.ft (48 Nm).

steps.title: Pressure-bleed the brake system
steps.body: Complete the required Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure after reconnecting the hose. Use that procedure for the bleeding method and its completion requirements.

watchFor.title: Exposed hydraulic openings
watchFor.body: Keep every opening sealed while disconnected; do not leave the hose or caliper connection exposed during the remaining work.

watchFor.title: Discarded parts returning to service
watchFor.body: The removed hose washers and caliper mounting bolts are not installation parts. Reassembly requires replacements.

notes: This procedure is specific to the SVT Performance Package front caliper. Its fasteners and tightening values must remain with this brake configuration.

verification.title: Check mechanical assembly
verification.body: Confirm installation of the pad spring clip, pads and pins, new caliper bolts and new hose washers, with both connections tightened to their respective specifications.

verification.title: Record hydraulic completion
verification.body: Record completion of the required pressure-bleeding procedure after hose reconnection. Do not treat mechanical assembly alone as completion of the repair.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L SVT Performance Package front caliper removal, pad-component transfer, installation and required pressure-bleeding referral.

guides.title: Replace the front brake caliper anchor plate with 2-piston calipers
guides.summary: Remove the front pads and supported caliper, replace the anchor plate using new bolts, and restore the pad hardware correctly.
guides.introduction: The anchor plate is the fixed carrier that supports the front brake pads and provides the mounting arrangement for the sliding caliper. Replacing it requires moving the caliper aside and removing the pads first. The pad clips also need attention because the upper and lower clips are different and must return to their correct positions.
guides.why: Supporting the displaced caliper prevents its weight from loading and damaging the brake hose. New anchor-plate bolts are mandatory because the removed bolts are discarded. Correct clip placement matters to the pad installation: the clip with a tab belongs at the top of the anchor plate.
searchTerms: front brake caliper anchor plate replacement

when.summary: When the front caliper anchor plate requires removal or replacement during an established brake repair.

prepare.title: Prepare wheel access and caliper support
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment to lift and support the vehicle and remove the wheel using the applicable wheel procedure. Provide a means of supporting the caliper independently of its hose.

prepare.title: Gather installation parts and tools
prepare.detail: Obtain new anchor-plate bolts and suitable torque tools. If fitting new pads, have a C-clamp, a worn pad and the new pad kit’s hardware, lubricant and instruction sheet available.

steps.title: Expose and support the caliper
steps.body: Follow the linked 2-piston brake-pad procedure: remove the wheel and tire, remove the caliper guide-pin bolts and position the caliper aside. Support it so it cannot hang from the brake hose.

steps.title: Remove pads and clips
steps.body: Note the component positions before removal. Remove the pads, then the upper and lower pad clips. Identify the tabbed clip so it can return to the top position.

steps.title: Remove the anchor plate
steps.body: Remove the two anchor-plate mounting bolts and the plate. Discard the bolts; the installation requires new ones.

steps.title: Install the plate and pad hardware
steps.body: Reverse the anchor-plate removal sequence and tighten the new bolts to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Refit the clips with the tabbed clip at the top. When installing new pads, use all new hardware and lubricant supplied with the kit, following its lubricant instructions.

steps.title: Restore the pads and caliper
steps.body: If installing new pads, use a C-clamp and a worn pad to compress the caliper pistons into their bores as part of refitting. Restore the pads and caliper, tightening the guide-pin bolts to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). Complete wheel and tire installation through the applicable procedure.

steps.title: Complete the brake-pedal and fluid checks
steps.body: Depress the brake pedal, check the reservoir fluid level and top up as necessary using the brake fluid specified in Brake System—General Information, Specifications.

watchFor.title: Caliper weight on the hose
watchFor.body: Reposition the support if the hose is carrying the caliper’s weight. The hose must not serve as a hanger.

watchFor.title: Upper and lower clips exchanged
watchFor.body: The two clip types are not interchangeable in position. Correct a tabbed clip installed anywhere other than the top before completing pad assembly.

notes: Piston compression is the additional installation branch for new pads; anchor-plate removal itself does not call for that operation.

verification.title: Confirm the installation details
verification.body: Check that new anchor-plate bolts were used, the tabbed clip is at the top and both anchor-plate and guide-pin bolts received their respective tightening values.

verification.title: Record the final brake check
verification.body: Record completion of the brake-pedal application and reservoir-level check, including any necessary fluid top-up.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L and 3.7L front caliper anchor-plate removal and installation with replacement mounting bolts.
Required 2-piston caliper pad removal and refitting, including caliper support, clip orientation and final pedal/fluid checks.

guides.title: Replace the convertible top tension belt
guides.summary: Remove the convertible top assembly, release the material at the floating bow, and replace the tension belt with the roof partly open.
guides.introduction: The tension belt is a mechanical part of the convertible roof’s material-support arrangement, attached at the floating bow by a sliding connection and retaining screw. Replacing it involves the surrounding roof material and its retaining clips as well as the belt itself. The complete convertible top assembly must be removed before the belt work.
guides.why: The roof must be partly open to provide slack in the top material and associated components. Working with the material under closed-roof tension makes the attachments harder to service. The material-retaining clips must also return to their proper locations so that releasing the floating bow does not leave the roof material incorrectly attached.

when.summary: When a confirmed roof repair requires removal or replacement of the convertible top tension belt.
notes: A roof that will not operate needs its operating conditions checked before the tension belt is treated as the cause.

prepare.title: Plan for complete top removal
prepare.detail: Have the full Convertible Top Assembly removal and installation procedure available, together with the handling capability and workspace it requires. Assembly removal is a prerequisite to belt access.

prepare.title: Prepare for clips and screw tightening
prepare.detail: Be ready to preserve the material-retaining clip locations. Have an appropriate screw driver and torque equipment for the tension-belt retaining screw.

prepare.title: Use the service position
prepare.detail: The procedure illustrations show the roof fully closed, but the actual service position is approximately 25–50 percent open to provide slack.

steps.title: Position and remove the top assembly
steps.body: Use the partly open service position and follow the complete Convertible Top Assembly procedure to remove the assembly. Follow that procedure’s handling and removal requirements before proceeding to the belt.

steps.title: Release material from the floating bow
steps.body: Remove the convertible top material retaining clips from the floating bow and partially disconnect the material. Preserve the proper clip locations for installation. The right-hand side is illustrated; the left-hand side is similar.

steps.title: Remove the tension belt
steps.body: Remove the belt retaining screw, then slide the belt out of the floating bow. The illustration identifies the screw attachment and sliding engagement; maintain slack while working at these connections.

steps.title: Install the belt and restore the material
steps.body: Reverse removal to slide the belt into the floating bow and install its retaining screw. Tighten the screw to 62 lb.in (7 Nm). Reattach the roof material, placing its retaining clips on the material in their proper locations.

steps.title: Reinstall the top assembly
steps.body: Complete refitting through the Convertible Top Assembly procedure. Restore the assembly before checking powered roof operation and follow any completion requirements in that procedure.

watchFor.title: Taut material during service
watchFor.body: Do not copy the fully closed position shown in the illustrations. Establish the specified partly open position so the material and related components have service slack.

watchFor.title: Lost clip locations
watchFor.body: Removing the material from the floating bow includes removing its retaining clips. Their correct placement on the material must be restored during installation.

notes: The roof uses coordinated electric motors and waits for both rear quarter windows to report fully lowered before moving. An operating inhibition does not by itself identify a belt problem.

diagnostics.finding: The roof does not move and both rear quarter windows have not reported fully down.
diagnostics.meaning: The roof control system inhibits movement until it receives both window-down signals.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the window position or related operating fault before attributing the stopped roof to the tension belt.

diagnostics.finding: TOP DISABLED — REMOVE COVERS appears when raising the roof.
diagnostics.meaning: Installed tonneau covers prevent the roof from being raised.
diagnostics.next: Remove the covers before checking closing operation.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical restoration
verification.body: Check the belt’s sliding engagement, retaining-screw tightening and restoration of the roof-material clips to their proper locations.

verification.title: Check operation under valid conditions
verification.body: With the vehicle stationary and accessory delay active, hold the roof switch in the requested direction. Release the latch for opening and remove any tonneau covers for closing. Confirm that the windows lower before roof movement and that the roof reaches the requested position.

procedures.purpose: Tension-belt removal and installation, including service position, floating-bow material clips and retaining-screw tightening.
Required complete convertible top assembly removal and subsequent installation.
Roof operating sequence, window prerequisites and tonneau-cover inhibition used during post-installation checks.

guides.title: Replace the MAPT sensor on the 2.3L or 3.7L
guides.summary: Remove and refit the manifold pressure-and-temperature sensor using the correct engine’s access steps and retainer torque.
guides.introduction: The manifold absolute pressure and temperature (MAPT) sensor measures pressure and air temperature within the intake manifold, providing the engine controls with information about intake conditions. This job removes the combined sensor and restores its mounting and electrical connection. The two engines share the basic sequence but have different access and tightening details.
guides.why: The 2.3L requires appearance-cover removal before sensor access, while the 3.7L procedure begins at the sensor connector. Their retainer torques also differ. Keeping each engine’s instructions together avoids applying the wrong tightening value to a small sensor mounting.

when.summary: When an established engine-control repair requires removal or replacement of the MAPT sensor.

prepare.title: Identify the engine
prepare.detail: Select the 2.3L or 3.7L procedure before starting. The hero illustration shows the 3.7L sensor installation; the 2.3L has its own installation illustration.

prepare.title: Prepare small-fastener tools
prepare.detail: Have suitable drivers and torque equipment for the sensor retainer. The 2.3L also requires tools for its engine appearance-cover nuts.

steps.title: Establish access
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the nuts and engine appearance cover. On the 3.7L, begin at the sensor as directed by its procedure; no appearance-cover removal is specified in that sequence.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Disconnect the MAPT electrical connector before removing the retainer. Remove the sensor once its electrical and mechanical connections have been released.

steps.title: Refit using the correct mounting details
steps.body: Reverse removal to install the sensor. Tighten the 2.3L retainer to 44 lb.in (5 Nm), or the 3.7L retainer to 35 lb.in (4 Nm). On the 3.7L, a second fastener hole is available for use during reinstallation if needed.

steps.title: Restore the connector and cover
steps.body: Reconnect the MAPT electrical connector. On the 2.3L, reinstall the appearance cover and tighten its nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm), completing the reverse-removal sequence.

watchFor.title: Sensor and cover settings confused
watchFor.body: The 2.3L cover nuts and sensor retainer have separate tightening values. Keep them identified throughout reassembly.

watchFor.title: Alternate mounting-hole applicability
watchFor.body: The second-fastener-hole installation note belongs to the 3.7L procedure.

notes: Neither engine’s removal and installation procedure specifies a subsequent learning or initialization operation.

verification.title: Confirm the restored installation
verification.body: Check that the sensor is retained using the engine-specific tightening value and its connector is reconnected. On the 2.3L, also confirm that the appearance cover and nuts are installed and tightened.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost MAPT sensor removal and installation, including appearance-cover access and separate tightening values.
3.7L Duratec MAPT sensor removal and installation, including retainer torque and the optional second fastener hole.

guides.title: Rebuild piston assemblies: 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Renew piston rings and pin retainers while preserving the piston-to-rod relationship and each engine’s specific assembly details.
guides.introduction: The piston receives combustion pressure and transfers that force through its pin to the connecting rod. Compression rings seal against the cylinder wall, while oil-control rings regulate the oil film. This bench overhaul separates those parts for inspection and rebuilds the assembly. It begins with the piston assembly already removed; engine dismantling and installation into the cylinder are separate operations.
guides.why: These engines share the same basic arrangement, but their assembly details differ. Ring facing, gap placement and piston orientation establish the intended sealing arrangement. Pin-retainer gap direction is particularly easy to confuse: the 5.2L requirement is opposite to the stated 3.7L and 5.0L requirement.

when.summary: During engine overhaul when piston assemblies need inspection, new rings or replacement pistons or connecting rods.
notes: Select the procedure for the actual engine before choosing parts or beginning assembly.

prepare.title: Arrange engine bench-work capability
prepare.detail: Have the removed assembly, a clean working area and the Piston Inspection procedure available. Inspection must establish whether existing components can be retained.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts
prepare.detail: Obtain new piston rings and piston pin retainers. Both are discarded during dismantling, even when the piston and connecting rod will be reused.

prepare.title: Use the correct assembly oil
prepare.detail: The 3.7L specifies SAE 5W-20 synthetic blend oil meeting WSS-M2C945-B1; the 5.2L specifies Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 full synthetic oil meeting WSS-M2C931-E1. The 2.3L and 5.0L instructions call for clean engine oil; do not borrow another variant’s specification.

steps.title: Record the original relationship
steps.body: Before separating a piston and connecting rod intended for reuse, mark their relative orientation. Keep that relationship identifiable throughout inspection so the parts can be reunited as originally assembled.

steps.title: Dismantle the assembly
steps.body: Remove and discard the rings, then remove and discard the pin retainers. Withdraw the piston pin and separate the piston from the connecting rod.

steps.title: Inspect before rebuilding
steps.body: Follow [Piston Inspection](#/document/G1661751). The 3.7L procedure calls for inspection of the piston and rod; the 5.0L and 5.2L procedures also explicitly require cleaning them. Resolve their suitability before fitting new rings.

steps.title: Orient the piston and rod
steps.body: Restore the marks on reused components. With new 3.7L or 5.0L components, the rod orientation marks and piston crown arrow face the engine front. On the 5.2L, identify the left-hand or right-hand piston, then face its crown arrow and the connecting-rod bump toward the engine front.

steps.title: Fit the pin and new retainers
steps.body: Position the piston on its rod, lubricate the pin with the appropriate clean oil and install it. Fit new retainers. Their gaps face the piston crown on the 3.7L and 5.0L, but the piston bottom on the 5.2L. Follow the 2.3L procedure separately.

steps.title: Install the oil-control rings
steps.body: Lubricate and fit the oil-control components using the matching procedure. The 5.2L explicitly sequences the lower oil-control ring, expander and upper ring. Keep each engine’s ring arrangement separate.

steps.title: Install the compression rings
steps.body: On the 3.7L, both compression-ring “O” marks face the crown. On the 5.0L, install the lower ring with its “O” upward and hook downward, then the upper ring with its “O” upward. The 5.2L uses the same stated facing directions with identification marks. Use the separate 2.3L instructions.

steps.title: Set the ring gaps
steps.body: Use the engine-specific assembly layout for exact gap placement. The 2.3L identifies both oil segments and the spacer. The 3.7L and 5.0L layouts group the expander and lower-compression gap location. The 5.2L identifies all gaps separately, referencing the expander to a centerline parallel to the pin bore.

watchFor.title: Opposite retainer directions
watchFor.body: Do not carry the 3.7L or 5.0L crown-facing retainer-gap rule into a 5.2L assembly.

watchFor.title: Missing orientation information
watchFor.body: Resolve uncertain piston-to-rod orientation before assembly; resemblance between engines is insufficient.

notes: The ring-removal illustration identifies discarded components; use the assembly procedure for gap placement.

verification.title: Check the completed bench assembly
verification.body: Confirm piston orientation, new retainers, correct retainer-gap direction, ring facing and the prescribed ring-gap layout before proceeding with engine assembly.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost piston bench disassembly and assembly, including orientation and ring alignment.
3.7L Duratec piston bench disassembly and assembly, including oil, ring marks and retainer orientation.
5.0L piston bench disassembly and assembly, including compression-ring facing and gap layout.
5.2L piston bench disassembly and assembly, including handed pistons, rod orientation and distinct retainer requirements.
Piston inspection before deciding which dismantled components can be reused.

guides.title: Replace the rear lower arm vertical link
guides.summary: Replace the rear suspension’s upright lower-arm link using new bolts tightened with the suspension at its loaded position.
guides.introduction: The lower arm vertical link connects the lower arm and wheel-knuckle area of the independent rear suspension. It helps maintain their relationship as the wheel moves over the road. Replacing it requires wheel removal and access to its upper and lower attachments. The short procedure has an important setup requirement: support the suspension at curb height before releasing the link.
guides.why: The link’s bushing attachments must be tightened with the suspension loaded or the vehicle resting on its tires. Tightening with the suspension hanging can produce incorrect clamp load and damage the bushings. The upper and lower bolts also have different tightening requirements, so treating them as interchangeable can leave the repair incorrectly secured.
searchTerms: rear lower arm vertical link replacement

when.summary: When the rear lower arm vertical link requires replacement or removal during an established suspension repair.

prepare.title: Provide safe access and suspension support
prepare.detail: Use the Wheel and Tire procedure for wheel access. Have vehicle/axle stands available to support the suspension at curb height throughout link removal and fastening.

prepare.title: Have new bolts and tightening capability
prepare.detail: Both removed link bolts are discarded. Obtain the correct replacement bolts and a torque wrench suitable for the specified upper and lower values.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and establish curb height
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire using the linked procedure. Support the suspension at curb height with vehicle/axle stands before loosening the link, preserving the required suspension position.

steps.title: Release the old link
steps.body: Remove the upper and lower link bolts, discard both and remove the vertical link. Keep the suspension supported while its connection is released.

steps.title: Fit the link with new bolts
steps.body: Position the replacement link and install both new bolts. With the suspension loaded, tighten the upper bolt to 76 lb.ft (103 Nm), followed by the lower bolt to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm).

steps.title: Restore wheel installation
steps.body: After securing the link, install the wheel and tire following its complete procedure. Use that procedure’s wheel-fastening requirements separately from the link-bolt values.

watchFor.title: Suspension hanging during tightening
watchFor.body: Correct torque alone does not satisfy the procedure if the suspension is unloaded.

watchFor.title: Substitute fasteners
watchFor.body: Suspension fasteners are critical parts. Use the same or equivalent quality and design; do not fit lesser-quality substitutes or reuse the discarded bolts.

notes: This replacement procedure does not establish the cause of an unexplained suspension complaint.

verification.title: Confirm loaded fastening
verification.body: Verify that both new bolts received their respective tightening values with the suspension loaded.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record the upper and lower bolt tightening and completion of the separate wheel-installation procedure.

procedures.purpose: Rear lower arm vertical link removal and installation, including curb-height support, new bolts and loaded tightening.
Wheel and tire removal for access and correct wheel installation after the link repair.

guides.title: Replace the front seat backrest release handle
guides.summary: Remove the backrest trim and foam to replace the release handle and restore its cable connection to the recline mechanism.
guides.introduction: The backrest release handle operates a cable connected to the recline mechanism. The handle, cable conduit and cable attachment work together to transmit hand movement to that mechanism. Access requires removal of the backrest cover and foam, with additional steps for Recaro seats and seats with a backrest blower manifold. Most of the work involves uncovering the mechanism without losing the original trim and cable arrangement.
guides.why: The cable’s conduit must be anchored as well as its inner cable connected, so handle movement reaches the recline mechanism correctly. Foam must be moved away from the handle before it can be removed. Where a safety belt guide strap is fitted, retaining its original position is an explicit reassembly requirement.
searchTerms: front seat backrest release handle replacement

when.summary: When the backrest release handle requires replacement or removal during a confirmed mechanical seat repair.
notes: Identify the seat type before selecting the cover and upper-foam removal branches.

prepare.title: Plan the cover-removal work
prepare.detail: Have the appropriate standard-seat or Recaro backrest-cover procedure available and the capability to complete its access and safety requirements.

prepare.title: Preserve the installed arrangement
prepare.detail: Note the cable route, conduit mounting and any safety belt guide strap position before moving the foam. Allow working space for the removed cover and foam.

steps.title: Remove the matching backrest cover
steps.body: Follow the standard [Backrest Cover procedure](#/document/G1702539) or the [Recaro procedure](#/document/G1695529), according to the fitted seat. This exposes the foam and the components surrounding the handle.

steps.title: Follow the equipment-specific foam branch
steps.body: If fitted, disconnect the backrest blower motor manifold from the backrest cushion. Recaro seats require upper-backrest foam removal. On the GT 350 Recaro branch, first pull that foam away from the release handle, then remove it.

steps.title: Remove the remaining backrest foam
steps.body: Record the safety belt guide strap position if present. Pull the backrest foam away from the backrest, then lift it free. This opens access to the release cable and handle mountings.

steps.title: Disconnect the cable at the mechanism
steps.body: Detach the cable conduit and disconnect the cable from the recline mechanism. Position the released cable as directed so the handle can be removed without pulling against its remaining attachments.

steps.title: Remove the handle mountings
steps.body: Remove the release handle’s front bolts. Remove the cable mounting tie strap and the handle’s side bolts, then remove the handle. Keep track of the different mounting locations for reassembly.

steps.title: Rebuild in reverse order
steps.body: Install the handle and restore its side mountings, cable mounting strap and front mountings. Reconnect the cable and anchor its conduit. Refit the foam, preserving the belt guide strap position, reconnect any blower manifold and reinstall the appropriate backrest cover.

watchFor.title: Foam still caught around the handle
watchFor.body: On the GT 350 Recaro seat, clear the upper foam from the handle before lifting it away.

watchFor.title: An unanchored cable conduit
watchFor.body: Reconnect both the cable and its conduit during reverse assembly; attaching only the cable leaves the original arrangement incomplete.

notes: The illustrated left-hand-drive power driver seat is representative; other seats follow the corresponding equipment branches.

verification.title: Check the concealed connections
verification.body: Before the cover conceals them, confirm the handle mountings, cable mounting strap, conduit attachment and recline-mechanism connection are restored.

verification.title: Check the seat-specific restoration
verification.body: Confirm the foam is back in position, the safety belt guide strap matches its original placement and any disconnected blower manifold is reconnected.

procedures.purpose: Release-handle removal and reverse installation, including cable, foam and seat-equipment branches.
Standard front seat backrest-cover removal and installation for handle access.
Recaro front seat backrest-cover removal and installation for handle access.

applicability.equipment: Standard or Recaro front seats, including GT 350 Recaro seats; backrest blower manifold where fitted

guides.title: Remove and replace the front fender splash shield
guides.summary: Remove the wheel and shield retainers to replace the wheel-arch liner, then restore the wheel using the specified mounting precautions.
guides.introduction: The fender splash shield lines the front wheel opening and forms a barrier between road spray and the surrounding body area. Its removal provides access behind the liner or allows a damaged shield to be replaced. The shield itself is retained mechanically; the significant supporting work is safe wheel removal and correct wheel installation afterward.
guides.why: Both retainer-removal stages must be completed before withdrawing the shield. During wheel installation, dirt or corrosion between mounting faces can prevent proper seating and allow the nuts to loosen. Lubricant belongs only at the specified pilot interface, because the wheel-nut tightening specification depends on clean, dry threads.

when.summary: When the front fender splash shield needs replacement or must be removed for access behind the wheel-arch liner.
notes: The left-hand side is illustrated; the right-hand side is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange wheel access
prepare.detail: Provide a hoist and the capability to follow the vehicle lifting procedure referenced by Wheel and Tire. Position the vehicle in NEUTRAL as directed.

prepare.title: Prepare for wheel installation
prepare.detail: Have torque-controlled wheel-fastening equipment and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 available for the specified pilot interface.

steps.title: Remove the wheel assembly
steps.body: Follow [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) to lift the vehicle and remove the wheel. Do not apply heat to a seized wheel nut; this can damage the wheel and bearing.

steps.title: Release the shield retainers
steps.body: Complete both retainer-removal stages in the splash-shield procedure. Follow their illustrated locations rather than assuming the first set releases the entire liner.

steps.title: Remove and refit the shield
steps.body: Withdraw the released splash shield. Position the replacement or retained shield and reverse the removal sequence to restore its retainers.

steps.title: Restore the wheel mounting
steps.body: Clean the wheel and hub or brake-disc mounting faces, and ensure rotor fasteners do not interfere. Apply a thin coat of XL-2 only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot. Fit the wheel nuts finger-tight, then tighten in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), with the vehicle resting on its tires.

watchFor.title: Lubricant outside the pilot interface
watchFor.body: Keep anti-seize off mounting faces, studs, nuts, brake pads and brake friction surfaces.

watchFor.title: A shield that remains attached
watchFor.body: Recheck both retainer-removal stages before attempting to withdraw it further.

notes: Wheel-nut torque applies to clean, dry stud and nut threads.

verification.title: Confirm restoration
verification.body: Check that the shield is positioned and retained, and record completion of the wheel’s final star-pattern tightening.

verification.title: Arrange the required wheel-nut recheck
verification.body: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after wheel installation.

procedures.purpose: Front fender splash-shield retainer release, shield removal and reverse installation.
Wheel access, mounting-face preparation, pilot lubrication, final tightening and subsequent wheel-nut recheck.

guides.title: Replace and configure the instrument panel cluster
guides.summary: Capture the cluster configuration and odometer information before removal, then install the replacement and complete scan-tool programming.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) presents gauges, indicators and message-center information using inputs from vehicle systems. It also controls warning-chime requests. Replacement therefore involves both physical removal and electronic setup. The surrounding trim provides access, while programmable module installation (PMI) transfers the configuration needed by a new cluster.
guides.why: Configuration information must be uploaded before the original module is removed and downloaded to the replacement afterward. The odometer reading also needs to be recorded before access to the original cluster is lost. Working through the trim sequence exposes concealed clips, connectors and the steering-column gap hider without pulling against attached parts.

when.summary: After diagnosis establishes that the IPC needs replacement, or when the cluster must be removed for access.
notes: A warning displayed by the cluster can originate in another vehicle system; the message alone does not establish cluster failure.

prepare.title: Arrange module-programming capability
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of carrying out IPC PMI and following its on-screen instructions. Begin replacement work while the original module is still installed.

prepare.title: Prepare trim access
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover and suitable controlled-tightening tools. Have the center finish-panel procedure available and keep the different trim fasteners identifiable.

steps.title: Begin PMI and record mileage
steps.body: Use the scan tool to begin IPC PMI. When installing a new module, upload the original configuration before removal. Record the original odometer value; if its display has failed, follow the retrieval branch below.

steps.title: Open the center and left trim areas
steps.body: Remove the instrument panel center finish panel using its linked procedure. Release the clips and remove the left-hand instrument panel trim panel with the interior trim remover.

steps.title: Remove the switch and finish panels
steps.body: Remove the lighting-switch panel bolts, release its clips and disconnect its electrical connector. Then remove the left-hand finish-panel bolt, release that panel’s clips and disconnect its connector.

steps.title: Expose the cluster surround
steps.body: Release the lower instrument panel cover clips and position the cover aside. Remove the IPC trim-panel bolts, release its clips and detach the gap hider from the upper steering-column trim cover.

steps.title: Remove the IPC
steps.body: Remove its bolts, release the clips and disconnect the electrical connector as the cluster is removed. Keep the connector accessible for installation.

steps.title: Install the cluster and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, reconnecting the cluster and panel connectors and restoring the gap hider. Apply each procedure step’s specified tightening value to its corresponding fasteners.

steps.title: Complete electronic installation
steps.body: Use the diagnostic scan tool to finish IPC PMI following the on-screen instructions. For a new cluster, complete the configuration download required after installation.

watchFor.title: Different tightening units
watchFor.body: The IPC mounting specification uses lb.ft, while adjacent trim specifications use lb.in. Read the value and unit together.

watchFor.title: Chime complaints
watchFor.body: Most warning chimes sound through audio speakers. The IPC sounds the turn-signal tick and provides backup chimes, so a chime complaint needs diagnosis before cluster replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The original odometer value cannot be read because the IPC display has failed.
diagnostics.meaning: Direct recording of the original reading is unavailable.
diagnostics.next: Perform the specified diagnostic routine. If it still cannot obtain the value, obtain the customer’s approximate odometer value and identify it as an estimate.

verification.title: Confirm physical installation
verification.body: Check restoration of disconnected connectors, trim clips, fasteners and the steering-column gap hider.

verification.title: Record programming and odometer information
verification.body: Record completion of the scan-tool PMI process and the odometer value used, including whether it came from the original display, diagnostic retrieval or a customer estimate.

procedures.purpose: IPC removal and installation, original configuration capture, odometer handling and completion of PMI.
Instrument panel center finish-panel removal and installation required for cluster access.

guides.title: Replace the rear stub shaft pilot bearing
guides.summary: Replace the rear halfshaft pilot bearing with the specified removal and installation tools, then fit a new halfshaft seal.
guides.introduction: The stub shaft pilot bearing supports the halfshaft where it enters the rear differential. The procedure also calls it the rear halfshaft pilot bearing. The halfshaft connects to a differential side gear and carries rotation toward the wheel, while the differential allows the wheels to turn at different speeds through corners. This repair renews the local shaft support and the adjacent seal.
guides.why: Access requires removing the halfshaft seal before extracting the bearing. Both parts must be renewed: the bearing is discarded during removal, and installation calls for a new seal. The dedicated bearing remover and installer set provide the specified method for extracting the old bearing and fitting its replacement.

when.summary: When the rear halfshaft pilot bearing has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Plan the bearing and halfshaft seal work together; seal removal is the first access operation.

prepare.title: Arrange the bearing tools
prepare.detail: Have bearing cup remover 308-047 (T77F-1102-A) and a slide hammer. Installation requires handle 205-907, halfshaft pilot bearing installer 205-504 and rear axle pilot bearing installer 205-1013.

prepare.title: Prepare parts and access
prepare.detail: Obtain a new pilot bearing and a new rear halfshaft seal. Be equipped to complete the linked halfshaft seal removal and installation procedure, which is an essential part of this job.

steps.title: Remove the halfshaft seal
steps.body: Follow the removal phase of [Rear Halfshaft Seal](#/document/G2214752). Removing the seal exposes the bearing for the specified extraction operation.

steps.title: Extract and discard the bearing
steps.body: Use the bearing cup remover with the slide hammer as shown in [Stub Shaft Pilot Bearing](#/document/G2274512). Remove the rear halfshaft pilot bearing and discard it; this operation is followed by replacement.

steps.title: Install the new pilot bearing
steps.body: Use the specified handle and both pilot bearing installers to fit the replacement bearing. Follow the installation arrangement in the bearing procedure so the new part is installed with the intended tooling.

steps.title: Fit the new seal and complete reassembly
steps.body: Return to the installation phase of the halfshaft seal procedure and install a new seal. Complete that linked procedure to restore the parts disturbed for bearing access.

watchFor.title: Missing replacement seal
watchFor.body: The bearing job ends with a new halfshaft seal, even when bearing replacement was the original reason for opening the assembly.

watchFor.title: Incomplete installer set
watchFor.body: The installation specifies the handle and both bearing installers; arrange the complete set before removing the old bearing.

verification.title: Confirm both replacement stages
verification.body: Confirm that the new pilot bearing was installed before the new halfshaft seal, and that neither discarded part was reused.

verification.title: Close the access procedure
verification.body: Check that the linked halfshaft seal installation has been completed, including the reassembly required by that procedure.

procedures.purpose: Rear stub shaft pilot bearing removal and installation, including mandatory bearing replacement and the specified tooling.
Prerequisite rear halfshaft seal removal and installation of the required new seal after bearing replacement.

guides.title: Replace the SYNC 2 or SYNC 3 touchscreen display
guides.summary: Remove the front display interface module, separate its attached electronics, refit the assembly and complete touchscreen calibration.
guides.introduction: The front display interface module (FDIM) is the touchscreen through which the driver operates the SYNC information and entertainment system. It works with other modules, including the attached accessory protocol interface module (APIM). Display replacement involves removing the assembly from the center stack and separating these two components. The job finishes with touchscreen calibration so touch input is correctly aligned with the display.
guides.why: The display mountings and the screws joining the APIM to the display have different tightening values. Keeping those fastener groups distinct helps preserve the assembly during reinstallation. Calibration is also a required part of the repair: securing the screen and reconnecting its wiring does not complete the touch-input setup.

when.summary: When removal or replacement of the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 front display interface module is required.
notes: Arrange access to the touchscreen calibration procedure before starting the hardware work.

prepare.title: Prepare for center-stack access
prepare.detail: Be able to remove and reinstall the front control panel using the linked Front Control/Display Interface Module procedure. That access operation comes before display removal.

prepare.title: Control the small fasteners
prepare.detail: Have suitable bolt and screw tools and torque equipment capable of the specified low tightening values. Keep display mounting bolts separate from the APIM attachment screws.

prepare.title: Plan the calibration stage
prepare.detail: Have the linked Touchscreen Calibration procedure and the capability to carry it out after the display assembly is installed.

steps.title: Remove the front control panel
steps.body: Use the [Front Control/Display Interface Module](#/document/G1704851) access procedure cited by the display repair. This clears the front of the display assembly so its mountings can be reached.

steps.title: Release the display assembly
steps.body: Following [Front Display Interface Module](#/document/G1704008), remove the display mounting bolts, release the display and disconnect its electrical connectors. Support the assembly while disconnecting it so the wiring does not carry its weight.

steps.title: Separate the APIM
steps.body: Remove the attachment screws and separate the APIM from the FDIM. Keep this fastening group identifiable for reassembly; these screws use a lower tightening value than the display mounting bolts.

steps.title: Reassemble and reinstall
steps.body: Reverse removal. Attach the APIM to the display and tighten its screws to 9 lb.in (1 Nm). Reconnect the electrical connectors and install the display mounting bolts at 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Restore the front control panel using its linked procedure.

steps.title: Calibrate the touchscreen
steps.body: Complete [Touchscreen Calibration](#/document/G1702410) after installation. Use that procedure for the actual calibration sequence rather than assuming that reconnecting the display establishes touch alignment.

watchFor.title: Fastener values exchanged
watchFor.body: The APIM screws and display mounting bolts have separate torque specifications. Apply each value to its own fastening group.

watchFor.title: Calibration left unfinished
watchFor.body: Keep calibration in the repair plan even when removal and refitting appear straightforward.

verification.title: Confirm assembly restoration
verification.body: Check that the APIM is attached, the display connectors are reconnected, both fastening groups are secured correctly and the front control panel is restored.

verification.title: Record calibration completion
verification.body: Record whether the linked touchscreen calibration completed successfully. An incomplete calibration leaves a required stage of the repair outstanding.

procedures.purpose: SYNC 2/SYNC 3 FDIM removal and installation, APIM separation and the two attachment torque specifications.
Front control panel removal and installation required to access the FDIM.
Required touchscreen calibration after FDIM installation on SYNC 2/SYNC 3 equipment.

guides.title: Remove and install the side curtain airbag
guides.summary: Depower the restraint system, remove the roof-mounted curtain assembly and reinstall it with correct attachment, connector locking and repowering.
guides.introduction: The side curtain airbag is a roof-mounted part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). The restraints control module (RCM) monitors sensor inputs and commands the appropriate restraint components when it determines that deployment is needed. This repair removes the curtain assembly from behind the headliner, then restores its mounting and electrical connection. Its installed position matters because the curtain must deploy correctly along the roofline.
guides.why: This work controls two serious risks: accidental deployment during repair and incorrect deployment during a crash. Depowering protects the repair operation, while sound roof structure, correct curtain orientation and the specified fastening sequence protect its installed function. Connector locking also matters electrically; a connector can make contact while its assurance tab remains incompletely seated.

when.summary: When side curtain airbag removal or replacement is required and SRS service capability is available.
notes: An illuminated airbag warning indicator alone does not establish that the curtain assembly needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: The person doing the work must be able to follow the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures and handle deployable-component connectors correctly.

prepare.title: Prepare access and fastening information
prepare.detail: Have the headliner procedure, suitable screw and retainer tools, and torque equipment. Use the numbered installation diagram to identify the screw positions and tightening sequence.

prepare.title: Allow for mounting repairs
prepare.detail: Installation requires inspection of the roofline. Damaged sheet metal must be restored to its original condition and structural integrity, damaged fasteners renewed and foreign material removed.

steps.title: Depower the SRS
steps.body: Complete [SRS Depowering](#/document/G1696297) before disturbing the curtain connection. Follow the full procedure precisely; its requirements govern safe disconnection and later reconnection.

steps.title: Remove the headliner
steps.body: Follow [Headliner](#/document/G1692615) to expose the curtain and its attachments. This provides access to the connector, screw groups and retainers without pulling against concealed fixings.

steps.title: Disconnect and release the screw groups
steps.body: In the order shown in [Side Curtain Airbag](#/document/G1696310), disconnect the electrical connector and remove the screws, then remove the next screw group. Note the unique installation instructions for these locations before proceeding.

steps.title: Release the retainers and T-tab
steps.body: Remove the A-pillar pin-type retainers, disengage the retainer and move the curtain away from the A-pillar. Disengage the remaining pin-type retainers, remove the final pin-type retainer, then slide the assembly forward and out to disengage its T-tab from the sheet metal.

steps.title: Prepare the roofline for installation
steps.body: Inspect the mounting area and resolve roofline damage before fitting the curtain. Remove foreign material and replace damaged fasteners. Check the curtain orientation so it is not twisted 360° between attachment points.

steps.title: Refit and tighten in sequence
steps.body: Reverse removal, following the installation diagram for attachment and screw positions. Keep the SRS depowered before reconnecting the component. Tighten screws 1 and 2 to 106 lb.in (12 Nm), then screws 3 through 7 to 80 lb.in (9 Nm), in the illustrated sequence.

steps.title: Restore trim and repower
steps.body: Complete headliner reinstallation and then follow [SRS Repowering](#/document/G1696298). Repowering is the final required phase of the curtain installation.

watchFor.title: Roofline damage or a twisted curtain
watchFor.body: Either can interfere with correct deployment. Resolve structural damage and curtain orientation before closing the headliner.

watchFor.title: Reconnection while powered
watchFor.body: The restraint system must be depowered before the component is reconnected; incorrect handling can cause accidental deployment.

notes: The numbered installation diagram is essential for identifying the two screw groups; do not infer their positions from the removal view.

diagnostics.finding: The deployable-component connector is attached, but its Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tab is not fully seated.
diagnostics.meaning: The connector pins can make contact while the component's shorting bars remain applied. The RCM can detect resistance below threshold and illuminate the airbag warning indicator.
diagnostics.next: Treat connector seating as a diagnostic consideration rather than proof of a failed curtain. Follow SRS depowering before correcting the connection, then complete the prescribed repowering process.

verification.title: Check installation before covering it
verification.body: Confirm roofline condition, curtain orientation, retainer and T-tab engagement, connector locking and completion of the numbered screw-tightening sequence.

verification.title: Record the repowering result
verification.body: Record completion of the repowering procedure and whether the airbag warning indicator reports a fault afterward. A remaining warning requires diagnosis rather than assuming the replacement curtain is defective.

procedures.purpose: Side curtain airbag removal and installation, roofline inspection, attachment orientation and numbered screw-tightening sequence.
Required SRS depowering before curtain disconnection or reconnection.
Headliner removal for curtain access and installation after the curtain is secured.
Required SRS repowering after installation is complete.

guides.title: Replace the rear differential drive pinion seal
guides.summary: Remove the drive pinion flange, renew the oil seal with its dedicated installer and complete the flange installation procedure.
guides.introduction: The drive pinion seal retains lubricant around the rotating input to the rear differential. The driveshaft turns the pinion flange, which turns the pinion and ring gear to transmit drive to the halfshafts. Replacing this seal requires removing the flange first. Although the seal itself has a short replacement sequence, the surrounding pinion assembly needs controlled reassembly.
guides.why: The pinion bearings operate with preload maintained by a collapsible spacer and adjusted through the pinion nut. Flange removal and installation therefore form an important part of the repair. The seal instructions do not provide a substitute pinion-nut setting: use the complete flange procedure for that work and the specified installer for the new seal.

when.summary: When lubricant leakage has been traced to the drive pinion seal, or the seal otherwise requires renewal.
notes: Include drive pinion flange removal and installation in the repair plan.

prepare.title: Have the specified seal tools
prepare.detail: Prepare a flat-headed screwdriver for seal removal and drive pinion oil seal installer 205-208 (T83T-4676-A) for installation. Obtain a replacement seal before dismantling.

prepare.title: Prepare for flange work
prepare.detail: Be equipped to complete the linked Drive Pinion Flange procedure. Understand that the pinion nut affects bearing preload through the collapsible spacer before disturbing the assembly.

steps.title: Remove the drive pinion flange
steps.body: Follow the removal phase of [Drive Pinion Flange](#/document/G2214749). This exposes the seal while keeping the flange-related operations within their complete technical sequence.

steps.title: Remove and discard the seal
steps.body: Use a flat-bladed screwdriver to remove the seal as illustrated in [Drive Pinion Seal](#/document/G2214751). Discard the removed seal; it is replaced during reassembly.

steps.title: Install the replacement seal
steps.body: Use installer 205-208 (T83T-4676-A) to fit the new drive pinion oil seal. Follow the installation arrangement in the seal procedure rather than estimating a fitting method from the removal illustration.

steps.title: Reinstall the flange
steps.body: Complete the installation phase of the drive pinion flange procedure. Keep its instructions governing the pinion assembly part of this job, because pinion-nut adjustment affects bearing preload.

watchFor.title: Casual pinion-nut adjustment
watchFor.body: The pinion nut adjusts a bearing arrangement that uses a collapsible spacer. Follow the flange procedure rather than choosing a generic tightening value.

watchFor.title: Reusing the removed seal
watchFor.body: The old seal is explicitly discarded. Have the new seal and correct installer ready before removal.

verification.title: Confirm seal replacement
verification.body: Confirm that the discarded seal was replaced using the specified drive pinion oil seal installer.

verification.title: Confirm flange installation is complete
verification.body: Check completion against the linked flange installation procedure. The seal repair remains incomplete until that dependent assembly work is finished.

procedures.purpose: Drive pinion seal removal, discard and installation using the dedicated oil seal installer.
Drive pinion flange removal before seal access and complete flange installation after seal replacement.

guides.title: Remove, strip and rebuild the rear bumper cover
guides.summary: Remove the rear bumper cover, inspect its mounting brackets, transfer its electrical and trim components, then rebuild and reinstall it.
guides.introduction: The rear bumper cover is the exterior panel around the rear of the car. Its assembly includes a cover reinforcement, wiring, lamps, reflectors, a decklid release switch and park aid sensors.
