Renewing or rebuilding the cover therefore involves both vehicle removal and bench disassembly. The GT version adds a separate lower-cover removal stage.
guides.why: The cover is retained by screws, push pins and bracket engagements, with electrical connections released at different stages. Supporting it while those connections are exposed prevents the wiring from carrying the panel. Bracket inspection is equally important: refitting a cover over damaged mountings leaves the underlying attachment problem unresolved.

when.summary: When the rear bumper cover needs replacement, rebuilding or removal for access to its attached components.
notes: The separate lower bumper cover disassembly branch applies to GT vehicles.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and assistance
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and identify the correct lifting points by their stamped triangles. Have a second person available for cover removal. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; floor stands are required when supporting a raised vehicle with that method.

prepare.title: Protect the vehicle during lifting
prepare.detail: Do not lift against either bumper or use the emergency tire-change jack for this work. Check drive-on clearance and position hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust, steering parts, mounting brackets, the axle and rear cover.

prepare.title: Prepare for access and stripdown
prepare.detail: Have suitable screw, nut and retainer tools and low-range torque equipment. Be able to complete the linked wheel-and-tire and rear-lamp procedures, and keep the different attachment groups organized.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and release the initial attachments
steps.body: Follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631), then the opening sequence in [Rear Bumper Cover removal](#/document/G1694215). Remove the push pins and screws. On both sides, disconnect the rear bumper harness connector and separate its wiring guide.

steps.title: Complete wheel and lamp access
steps.body: Remove the rear wheels and tires using [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Remove the specified screw and pushpins on both sides, then the cover-to-bracket screws. Remove the rear lamp assemblies using [Rear Lamp Assembly](#/document/G1694124).

steps.title: Release and remove the cover
steps.body: Release the cover sides from their brackets first, then its center from the rear brackets. Position it aside for access to the remaining bumper wiring connector and disconnect it. With assistance, remove the cover.

steps.title: Inspect the mounting brackets
steps.body: Inspect both side brackets and the rear brackets for damage. When required, follow the removal instructions for the side, outer rear or center rear brackets. Resolve mounting damage before reinstalling the cover.

steps.title: Remove reinforcement, wiring and sensors
steps.body: Follow [Rear Bumper Cover disassembly](#/document/G1694221). Separate the harness guides from the cover reinforcement, remove its pin-type retainers, release its tabs and remove it. Disconnect the harness connectors and guides to remove the harness, then remove the rear park aid sensors.

steps.title: Strip the lamps and remaining fittings
steps.body: Remove the reversing-lamp screws and lamp. Release the tabs for both license plate lamps and the decklid release switch. On both sides, remove the reflector nut, release its tabs and remove the reflector; then release the side-marker tab and remove the lamp.

steps.title: Remove the GT lower cover when applicable
steps.body: For GT vehicles, remove the lower bumper cover screws, release its tabs and remove the lower cover. This additional stripdown stage belongs to the GT branch.

steps.title: Rebuild and reinstall
steps.body: Reverse bench disassembly, then reverse vehicle removal. Reattach the wiring guides and connectors as their stages become accessible. Tighten reversing-lamp screws to 15 lb.in (1.7 Nm) and reflector nuts to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). Apply 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm) to the cover and bracket screw groups identified with that value in the removal procedure.

watchFor.title: An electrical connection still attached
watchFor.body: The early harness disconnections do not eliminate the later connector-access step. Support the cover until that remaining connection is released.

watchFor.title: Tabs pulled before release
watchFor.body: Reinforcement, lamps, reflectors and the GT lower cover use tab retention as well as their listed fasteners. Release each attachment before removing the part.

diagnostics.finding: A side or rear mounting bracket is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The cover's supporting attachment needs attention before reinstallation.
diagnostics.next: Use the appropriate side, outer rear or center rear bracket removal branch as required, and resolve the damage before fitting the cover.

verification.title: Record bracket condition
verification.body: Record the inspection result for both side brackets and the rear brackets, including any corrective work completed before the cover conceals them.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Check that transferred components, reinforcement, wiring guides and connectors are restored; cover engagements and fasteners are secured; and rear lamps, wheels and tires have been reinstalled through their respective procedures.

procedures.purpose: Rear bumper cover bench disassembly and assembly, including electrical fittings, reinforcement and the GT-only lower cover branch.
Rear bumper cover vehicle removal and installation, staged connector access and side/rear bracket inspection and removal.
Correct lifting points, vehicle support and hoist-clearance precautions for bumper access.
Rear wheel and tire removal and installation required during cover access.
Rear lamp assembly removal and installation required to release and refit the cover.

guides.title: Replace the convertible rear seat backrest cover
guides.summary: Remove the convertible rear backrest, release its cover attachments carefully and refit the upholstery without damaging the foam-mounted fastening strips.
guides.introduction: The rear backrest cover is the upholstery fitted over the foam pad and secured around the backrest frame. J-clips and pin-type retainers secure its edges and carpet section, while hook-and-loop strips hold portions of the cover against the foam. Replacing the cover requires removing the backrest from the convertible first, then releasing these different attachment types in sequence.
guides.why: The foam-mounted hook-and-loop strips are the vulnerable part of this operation. Pulling the cover away carelessly can tear those strips out of the foam, creating an attachment problem during a trim repair. Releasing the frame fixings first leaves the final separation focused on the hook-and-loop connection.
searchTerms: convertible rear seat backrest cover replacement

when.summary: When the convertible rear backrest upholstery needs replacement or removal for access beneath the cover.
notes: Plan for complete backrest removal before releasing the cover.

prepare.title: Prepare for backrest removal
prepare.detail: Be able to complete the linked convertible backrest removal and installation procedure. The cover work begins with the backrest removed from the vehicle.

prepare.title: Identify the attachment types
prepare.detail: Locate the frame J-clips, carpet pin-type retainers, upper frame retainers and foam-mounted hook-and-loop strips. Distinguishing them helps avoid pulling against a fixing that is still engaged.

steps.title: Remove the backrest assembly
steps.body: Follow [Rear Seat Backrest — Convertible](#/document/G1709034). With the backrest removed, proceed to the cover attachments described in [Rear Seat Backrest Cover — Convertible](#/document/G1709035).

steps.title: Release the frame attachments
steps.body: Release the cover J-clips from the frame. Release the carpet pin-type retainers and fold the carpet forward, then release the cover pin-type retainers from the top of the frame. This clears the mechanical fixings before separating the upholstery from the foam.

steps.title: Separate the cover from the foam
steps.body: Carefully separate the hook-and-loop strips between the cover and foam, then remove the cover. Watch the foam-side strips during separation: they must remain attached to the foam rather than being pulled out with the cover.

steps.title: Refit the cover and backrest
steps.body: Reverse removal. Restore the hook-and-loop attachment, upper frame retainers, carpet position and retainers, and frame J-clips. Complete backrest installation using the linked convertible backrest procedure.

watchFor.title: Foam-side strips lifting
watchFor.body: If a strip begins pulling away from the foam, stop pulling the cover in that manner. The specified precaution is to preserve those strips during separation.

notes: The carpet is folded forward after its retainers are released; include its return and fastening in reassembly.

verification.title: Check the foam attachments
verification.body: Confirm that the hook-and-loop strips remain attached to the foam and have been re-engaged with the cover.

verification.title: Confirm every retention stage
verification.body: Check the upper retainers, carpet retainers and J-clips, then confirm completion of the convertible backrest installation procedure.

procedures.purpose: Convertible rear backrest cover removal and installation, including the attachment sequence and foam-strip damage precaution.
Convertible rear backrest removal before upholstery work and installation after the cover is restored.

guides.title: Remove and refit the windshield wiper arms
guides.summary: Remove the wiper arms with a two-leg puller, establish the motor’s PARK position, and align the blades with the windshield marks.
guides.introduction: The windshield wiper arms connect the motor-driven pivots to the blades that clear the glass. Their installed position determines where the blades rest when the motor parks. This job removes and refits those external arms; correct alignment matters just as much as securely tightening their retaining nuts.
guides.why: The motor has its own position monitoring and operating logic. Its PARK position must be established before the arms are aligned, otherwise correctly tightened arms can still leave the blades resting in the wrong place. The specified puller releases each arm at its pivot without relying on levering against nearby bodywork.

when.summary: When a wiper arm requires removal, replacement, or correction of its installed position.
notes: An operating fault does not by itself establish that a wiper arm needs replacement.

prepare.title: Have the puller and tightening equipment ready
prepare.detail: Use a two-leg puller, suitable tools for the nut covers and retaining nuts, and a torque wrench capable of the specified nut setting.

prepare.title: Identify the alignment marks
prepare.detail: Locate the blade-position marks on the windshield before refitting. The hood is omitted from the illustration for clarity; hood removal is not a listed operation.

steps.title: Expose and remove the retaining nuts
steps.body: Remove the wiper pivot-arm nut covers, then remove the nuts. This releases the fasteners that hold the arms on their pivots, but the arms may still need the specified puller to separate them.

steps.title: Pull the arms from their pivots
steps.body: Use the two-leg puller to remove the windshield wiper pivot arms, following the arrangement illustrated in the linked procedure. Keep the extraction force at the arm-to-pivot connection.

steps.title: Establish the motor’s PARK position
steps.body: Before installing either arm, turn the ignition ON and use the wiper switch to run one complete cycle. Allow the motor to finish in PARK. This gives the blade alignment a defined starting position.

steps.title: Align and secure the arms
steps.body: Install the arms with the blades inside the windshield marks. Fit and tighten the retaining nuts to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm). Turn the ignition OFF, then reinstall the nut covers.

watchFor.title: Positioning before the motor has parked
watchFor.body: Do not use an arbitrary motor stopping point to establish blade alignment. Complete the prescribed parking cycle first.

notes: Rain-sensitive wiping, where fitted, changes how wiping is requested; it does not replace the mechanical blade-alignment step.

diagnostics.finding: The motor reaches PARK but the blades sit outside the windshield marks.
diagnostics.meaning: The installed arm position needs checking.
diagnostics.next: Refit and align the arms using the prescribed PARK-position sequence.

verification.title: Confirm the installed position
verification.body: Check that both blades remain inside their windshield marks after the nuts are tightened.

verification.title: Confirm the fastening sequence is complete
verification.body: Verify the retaining nuts received the specified torque, the ignition is OFF, and the nut covers are installed.

procedures.purpose: Complete wiper-arm removal and installation, including puller use, motor parking, blade alignment and nut tightening.

guides.title: Remove and refit the 2.3L EcoBoost charge-air cooler intake pipes
guides.summary: Follow the separate upper- or lower-pipe access sequence, protect the open air passages, and reconnect the pipes at the specified clamp torque.
guides.introduction: The charge-air cooler (CAC) reduces the temperature of compressed intake air in the turbocharger system. Its intake pipework provides the air path to the cooler. The upper and lower sections have different removal sequences: upper-pipe work includes an electrical connection and bypass tube, while lower-pipe removal requires hoist access.
guides.why: Cleanliness is critical whenever turbocharger air passages are opened. Even small particles can damage the compressor vanes, so every open port must be protected and every component inspected and cleaned before assembly. Correct clamp tightening also matters: these connections use an inch-pound torque setting, which must not be confused with a foot-pound setting.
searchTerms: 2.3L EcoBoost charge air cooler intake pipe
lower charge air cooler pipe removal

when.summary: When an upper or lower CAC intake pipe needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: Choose the upper or lower branch for the pipe being removed; their access steps are different.

prepare.title: Provide clean port protection
prepare.detail: Have suitable clean covers ready before disconnecting the pipework. All opened ports require cleaning, inspection and covering, and all components require inspection and cleaning before reassembly.

prepare.title: Prepare clamp-tightening equipment
prepare.detail: Use appropriate clamp tools and a torque wrench capable of 44 lb.in (5 Nm), the setting specified for the clamps released in this procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lower-pipe access
prepare.detail: Lower-pipe work requires the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist. Identify the lifting points by their stamped triangles and position the hoist adapters without contacting vulnerable suspension, exhaust or steering components.

steps.title: Upper pipe: release its attached connections
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector and detach the wiring-harness retainers. Disconnect the bypass tube and position it aside. Freeing these attachments allows the pipe to be removed without leaving them connected to the moving assembly.

steps.title: Upper pipe: separate the pipe joints
steps.body: Loosen the clamp and move the lower intake pipe aside. Then loosen the upper intake-pipe clamp and remove the upper pipe. Clean and inspect the exposed ports and keep them covered.

steps.title: Lower pipe: establish hoist access
steps.body: For lower-pipe removal, place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on a hoist using the Jacking and Lifting procedure. Confirm the adapters and vehicle clearances before raising it.

steps.title: Lower pipe: release the adjoining pipework
steps.body: Loosen the clamp and position the lower intake pipe aside, then loosen the clamp and position the upper intake pipe aside. Remove the underbody shielding specified for the vehicle where fitted.

steps.title: Lower pipe: remove and protect
steps.body: Loosen the remaining lower-pipe clamp and remove the lower intake pipe. Clean, inspect and cover every open port so the system remains protected during the repair.

steps.title: Reassemble the selected branch
steps.body: After inspecting and cleaning the components, reverse the applicable removal sequence. Tighten the released clamps to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Restore the bypass tube, connector and harness retainers for upper-pipe work, and the removed underbody shielding for lower-pipe work.

watchFor.title: Uncovered air passages
watchFor.body: Do not leave open ports exposed while other work continues; small debris can damage the turbocharger.

watchFor.title: Unsupported underbody access
watchFor.body: Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The vehicle’s emergency jack is not intended for this repair.

notes: The upper-pipe illustration identifies its clamp connection; it does not replace the separate lower-pipe access sequence.

verification.title: Check cleanliness and connections
verification.body: Confirm inspection and cleaning are complete, all opened pipe joints are reconnected, and the specified clamp torque has been applied.

verification.title: Check the branch-specific refit
verification.body: Verify all connections, harness retainers and shields disturbed by the chosen removal branch have been restored.

procedures.purpose: Separate upper- and lower-CAC-intake-pipe removal and installation procedures for the 2.3L EcoBoost.
Lifting-point identification, hoist positioning and support precautions for lower-pipe access.

guides.title: Activate TPMS sensors to refresh tire-pressure readings
guides.summary: Wake each tire-pressure sensor with the activation tool, follow the specified retries for an unresponsive sensor, and check whether the warning remains.
guides.introduction: The tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) uses battery-powered sensors mounted at the tire valve stems. Their radio messages reach a receiver, which relays pressure information to the body control module (BCM). Sensors sleep while the vehicle is stationary to conserve their batteries. Activation wakes them so they can transmit current readings.
guides.why: A missing reading is not automatically a failed sensor. It can reflect a sleeping sensor or pressure information cleared during a module reset. Equally, a beep from the activation tool does not prove the vehicle received the message. The useful result is updated system information and the warning state after tire pressures have been addressed.

when.summary: When sleeping sensors need to transmit fresh pressure readings, including after a BCM reset.
notes: Activation does not correct an incorrectly inflated tire.

prepare.title: Use the specified activation equipment
prepare.detail: Have Tire Pressure Monitor tool 204-D081A (204-D081) available. A customer activation tool, if available, is used in the retry sequence.

prepare.title: Address actual tire pressure
prepare.detail: Be able to check and adjust the tire pressures as needed before judging the remaining warning. Do not use a module’s reset default as an inflation target.

steps.title: Switch the ignition ON
steps.body: Turn the ignition switch to ON. Start at the left-front tire so activation proceeds through the prescribed starting point.

steps.title: Activate the left-front sensor
steps.body: Place the tool against the tire sidewall at the valve stem. Press its test button to activate the sensor at least twice. A flashing green light and beep may accompany a successful response, but neither proves that the BCM heard it.

steps.title: Repeat at the remaining tires
steps.body: Use the same sidewall position at each valve stem and activate each remaining sensor at least twice. Complete the process for every tire before assessing the overall result.

steps.title: Follow the response-recovery sequence
steps.body: If a sensor does not respond, move the vehicle enough to rotate the wheels at least one-fourth of a turn and retry that sensor. If it still does not respond, try the customer activation tool when available. If it still fails to train, attempt training with the vehicle doors open.

steps.title: Check the remaining warning
steps.body: After adjusting pressures and activating every sensor, check the TPMS indicator. If it remains illuminated, continue with the linked TPMS Diagnosis and Testing procedure instead of assuming that a particular sensor needs replacement.

watchFor.title: Misleading tool feedback
watchFor.body: Expected tool feedback may be absent, and feedback that is present is not confirmation of vehicle reception.

notes: The TPMS warning can indicate low pressure or a system fault; activation alone does not distinguish every cause.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure data show 1033 kPa (149.96 psi) and the cluster displays dashes after a BCM reset.
diagnostics.meaning: The pressure data identifiers (DIDs) can contain this factory default after stored readings are cleared. It is not a measured tire pressure.
diagnostics.next: Check actual pressures and activate the sensors to request fresh information.

diagnostics.finding: A sensor remains unresponsive after the prescribed retries.
diagnostics.meaning: Activation has not established normal communication; this result alone does not identify the failed component.
diagnostics.next: Continue through TPMS diagnosis and testing.

verification.title: Record the activation outcome
verification.body: Record whether the indicator cleared after pressure adjustment and activation, and identify any sensor that remained unresponsive.

procedures.purpose: Sensor activation, tool positioning, repeated activation and the specified nonresponse recovery sequence.
Further TPMS diagnosis when the warning remains after pressure adjustment and sensor activation.

guides.title: Remove and refit a Traction-Lok or Torsen differential carrier
guides.summary: Remove the differential carrier with controlled housing spread, preserve bearing-part locations, and verify ring-gear backlash after refitting.
guides.introduction: The differential carrier supports the ring gear and the mechanism that allows the rear wheels to turn at different speeds when cornering. Bearings locate it within the rear drive housing. Shims beside the bearing cups establish bearing preload and ring-gear backlash—the clearance between the meshing ring and pinion teeth. Removing the carrier therefore requires controlled measurement and careful tracking of parts.
guides.why: Housing spread creates the clearance needed to remove and install the carrier. It must be measured, and the clamp contact points must be protected against cracking. Bearing cups, shims, caps and cap bolts also have established locations that must be preserved when reused. Returning those parts correctly does not eliminate the final backlash check.
searchTerms: ring gear backlash after carrier installation

when.summary: When an established repair requires differential-carrier removal or replacement.
notes: The illustrated limited-slip procedure also applies similarly to the Torsen carrier.
The Torsen carrier is serviced only as an assembly.

prepare.title: Arrange supported bench work
prepare.detail: Use holding fixture 307-003 (T57L-500-B). Have the Differential Housing Cover procedure available for opening and closing the assembly; vehicle-level access must be addressed before this bench sequence.

prepare.title: Prepare the spreading and extraction equipment
prepare.detail: Use gauge 308-021 (T75L-4201-A), a dial indicator, a 12” / 300 mm C-clamp, a tire lever, a wrench and wooden protection. The clamp requires 2” x 2” x ¾” wood blocks at its housing contact points.

prepare.title: Prepare for measured reassembly
prepare.detail: Have differential-shim installer 205-220, a soft-face copper mallet, suitable torque equipment, and the selected or original shims ready. Maintain identifiable locations for every part that will be reused.

steps.title: Open and secure the assembly
steps.body: Remove the differential housing cover using its dedicated procedure, then secure the differential assembly on the holding fixture. This provides support while the bearing retention and carrier are removed.

steps.title: Identify the bearing components
steps.body: Mark the bearing caps before removing their bolts and the caps. Preserve each bolt’s original location as well. Mark the shims and carrier-bearing cups if they will be reused, so they return to their original positions.

steps.title: Measure the housing spread
steps.body: Install the gauge and dial indicator with the gauge tip inside the rear drive unit (RDU) housing guide hole, then zero the indicator. Position the protected C-clamp at the housing’s 12 and 6 o’clock positions. Tighten it until the measured spread is 0.020” / 0.50 mm.

steps.title: Extract the carrier and inspect the case
steps.body: Remove the dial indicator while retaining the clamp. Place a wood block on the housing sealing surface and use the tire lever, block and wrench in the illustrated arrangement to remove the carrier, bearing cups and shims. Remove the clamp, then inspect the differential case.

steps.title: Prepare the housing for installation
steps.body: Reinstall and zero the gauge and indicator, then repeat the protected clamping arrangement to obtain 0.020” / 0.50 mm spread. Have the selected or previously removed shims immediately available. Their chamfers must face outboard.

steps.title: Insert the carrier and bearing cups
steps.body: Remove the dial indicator and install the carrier and its bearing cups. Hold them in position until the shims are installed; they must remain supported during the following operations.

steps.title: Install the right-hand shim and cap
steps.body: Install the right-hand ring-gear backlash shim. If the original right-hand shim is unavailable, install the largest available shim as directed. Move the differential toward the right-hand side and install that bearing cap with its bolts only finger-tight.

steps.title: Install the selected left-hand shim
steps.body: Use the shim installer and soft-face copper mallet to install the selected left-hand backlash shim, chamfer outward. The clamp can be removed after the selected shim is installed. Fit the left-hand bearing cap with its bolts only finger-tight.

steps.title: Tighten the caps and check backlash
steps.body: Tighten the bearing-cap bolts to 71 lb.ft (96 Nm). Check ring-gear backlash using the linked adjustment procedure and follow its requirements before considering the carrier installation complete.

steps.title: Close the assembly
steps.body: Remove the differential assembly from the holding fixture and reinstall the housing cover using the dedicated cover procedure. This completes the carrier removal-and-refit sequence.

watchFor.title: Unmeasured spread or unprotected clamp contact
watchFor.body: Use the dial indicator to establish spread and the specified wood blocks to protect the housing against cracking.

watchFor.title: Mixed locations or reversed shims
watchFor.body: Return reused cups, shims, caps and cap bolts to their identified locations. Both bearing shims require their chamfers facing outboard.

notes: The largest available right-hand shim is the specified installation branch when the original is unavailable; it is not a substitute for checking and adjusting backlash.

verification.title: Record backlash
verification.body: Record the measured ring-gear backlash and confirm it meets the requirements of Ring Gear Backlash Adjustment.

verification.title: Confirm retention and closure
verification.body: Verify cap locations and bolt torque, completion of case inspection, and housing-cover installation through its dedicated procedure.

procedures.purpose: Carrier removal and installation for the illustrated limited-slip differential and similar Torsen application, including controlled housing spread and shim installation.
Required ring-gear backlash check and adjustment after the carrier and bearing caps are installed.
Explain carrier support, shim-controlled preload and backlash, and the Torsen assembly-only service restriction.

guides.title: Replace a side lamp bulb
guides.summary: Access the side lamp from underneath, disconnect its wiring, and replace the bulb before refitting the holder.
guides.introduction: The side lamp contributes to the vehicle’s visibility from the side. Its bulb, holder and electrical connector are separate parts of the replacement job: the bulb produces light, the holder locates it in the lamp, and the connector supplies its electrical connection. Access for this procedure requires raising the vehicle on a hoist.
guides.why: The small size of the repair does not reduce the importance of safe access. Correct lifting points protect both the vehicle and the person underneath it, while following the removal sequence keeps the bulb, holder and connector operations clear.

when.summary: When the side lamp bulb requires replacement and safe access from underneath is available.
notes: This is a bulb replacement procedure; it does not establish the cause of every side-lamp lighting concern.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist and follow the linked lifting procedure. Identify the lifting points by the triangles stamped into the body or frame, and check adapter clearance around nearby components.

prepare.title: Identify the connection
prepare.detail: Use the illustration to locate the side-lamp electrical connector. Have the replacement bulb ready before dismantling the lamp connection and holder.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle
steps.body: Raise the vehicle on the hoist using the specified lifting points. Position the supports carefully so they do not interfere with suspension, exhaust or steering components.

steps.title: Disconnect the lamp wiring
steps.body: Disconnect the side-lamp bulb electrical connector shown in the illustration. This separates the electrical connection before the bulb and holder are removed.

steps.title: Remove the bulb and holder
steps.body: Remove the bulb from its holder. Then turn the bulb holder counterclockwise and remove it. Keep these as separate actions in the stated order.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the holder, install the replacement bulb and reconnect the electrical connector. Follow the complete side-lamp procedure through its reverse-order installation.

watchFor.title: Unsafe underbody support
watchFor.body: Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The vehicle’s emergency jack is intended for changing a deflated tire, not for this repair.

watchFor.title: Lifting damage
watchFor.body: Do not lift against either bumper. Check for underbody interference before using a drive-on lift and for component interference when positioning hoist adapters.

notes: The illustration identifies the connector; it does not add extra removal operations.

verification.title: Complete the reverse assembly
verification.body: Confirm that the holder is refitted, the replacement bulb is installed in it, and the electrical connector is reconnected.

procedures.purpose: Complete side-lamp bulb removal and reverse-order installation.
Lifting-point identification, hoist positioning and underbody support precautions.

guides.title: Replace the MT82 pilot bearing on 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines
guides.summary: Remove the clutch assembly, extract the pilot bearing with the specified remover, and drive its replacement into the crankshaft.
guides.introduction: The pilot bearing supports the transmission input shaft where it meets the engine, allowing relative rotation when the clutch is disengaged. Replacing it restores that bearing support. The bearing operation is brief, but access requires removal of the clutch disc and pressure plate, so the work must be planned around the correct engine-specific clutch procedure.
guides.why: Extraction and installation use different tools: the remover withdraws the bearing, while a driver installs its replacement. Selecting the correct clutch procedure also matters because a shared pilot-bearing operation does not make the surrounding engine-specific work interchangeable.

when.summary: When pilot-bearing replacement is required on a 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine with the MT82 transmission.
notes: Clutch removal provides access; it does not by itself establish that the pilot bearing needs replacement.

prepare.title: Plan the clutch access work
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment required by the clutch-disc and pressure-plate procedure for the fitted engine. Complete its prerequisites before attempting bearing removal.

prepare.title: Prepare the bearing tools
prepare.detail: Use pilot-bearing remover 308-001 (T58L-101-B). Have a driver available for installing the replacement bearing in the crankshaft.

steps.title: Remove the clutch assembly
steps.body: Follow the linked clutch-disc and pressure-plate removal procedure for the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. This exposes the pilot bearing for the dedicated extraction operation.

steps.title: Extract the pilot bearing
steps.body: Use special tool 308-001 (T58L-101-B) to remove the bearing. The illustration shows the specified remover acting at the central bearing location.

steps.title: Install the replacement
steps.body: Position the pilot bearing in the crankshaft, then install it using a driver. Follow the pilot-bearing installation procedure without adding an assumed installation dimension.

steps.title: Restore the clutch
steps.body: Install the clutch disc and pressure plate using the same engine-specific procedure selected for removal. Bearing installation alone does not complete the repair.

watchFor.title: Different 5.2L arrangement
watchFor.body: The pilot bearing is not separately serviceable on the 5.2L engine. That application requires a new flywheel and is outside this separate-bearing replacement path.

notes: Use the engine-specific clutch instructions for the surrounding work; the bearing procedure supplies the extraction and installation method.

verification.title: Bearing and clutch installation complete
verification.body: Confirm that the replacement bearing has been installed in the crankshaft and that clutch-disc and pressure-plate installation is complete under the matching engine procedure.

procedures.purpose: Pilot-bearing extraction and installation for the listed MT82 applications.
2.3L EcoBoost clutch-disc and pressure-plate removal and installation for bearing access.
3.7L Duratec clutch-disc and pressure-plate removal and installation for bearing access.
5.0L clutch-disc and pressure-plate removal and installation for bearing access.

guides.title: Replace a blind-spot detection module or its mounting bracket
guides.summary: Remove the rear bumper cover to service the left or right radar module, completing programmable module installation when replacing the module.
guides.introduction: The side obstacle detection modules sit behind the rear bumper cover, rearward of the rear wheels. The left module (SODL) and right module (SODR) use radar to detect targets for the Blind Spot Information System (BLIS) and Cross Traffic Alert (CTA). This job replaces a module or services its mounting bracket, with an additional scan-tool process whenever a module is replaced.
guides.why: A blocked sensor, a system fault and an operating limitation are different conditions. Establishing which is present avoids treating every missed alert as a failed module. When replacement is justified, programmable module installation (PMI) must begin before removal and finish after installation.

when.summary: When diagnosis requires replacement of a side obstacle detection module, or its mounting bracket needs service.
notes: PMI applies when replacing SODL or SODR; it is not specified for bracket-only work with the original module retained.

prepare.title: Identify the side and repair scope
prepare.detail: Establish whether the left module, right module or bracket requires service. Check the rear bumper sides for debris, stickers or damage that could affect detection.

prepare.title: Arrange programming and access
prepare.detail: For module replacement, have a diagnostic scan tool capable of the required PMI process. Prepare to remove and reinstall the rear bumper cover using its linked procedure.

steps.title: Begin PMI when replacing a module
steps.body: Before removal, use the diagnostic scan tool to begin PMI for the affected SODL or SODR. Follow its on-screen instructions. Omit this step when retaining the existing module.

steps.title: Expose the module
steps.body: Remove the rear bumper cover using the linked procedure. This provides access to the radar module and its bracket.

steps.title: Remove the module
steps.body: Disconnect the module’s electrical connector, remove its screws and remove SODL or SODR. Module removal is also the prerequisite for removing the bracket.

steps.title: Service the bracket if required
steps.body: With the module removed, disconnect the wiring-harness guide. Remove the bracket screws and the side obstacle detection module bracket.

steps.title: Reassemble and finish programming
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure, restoring the bracket, harness guide, module connection and bumper cover as applicable. If a module was replaced, complete PMI with the scan tool, following the on-screen instructions.

watchFor.title: Obstructed radar area
watchFor.body: Do not place bumper stickers or body filler over the rear bumper areas near the modules. Mud, snow and heavy rain can also degrade detection.

watchFor.title: System limits
watchFor.body: BLIS assists the driver; it does not prevent contact. Rapidly passing targets and obstructed cross-traffic views can produce missed alerts without establishing module failure.

notes: BLIS operates in forward gear above its activation threshold; CTA operates in reverse. A MyKey restricted key prevents either system from being switched off through the message center.

diagnostics.finding: A SENSOR BLOCKED message appears.
diagnostics.meaning: Blocked operation is a normal response to degraded detection, not itself a system fault.
diagnostics.next: Address visible obstruction and reassess. The state can self-clear; cycling the ignition may clear it temporarily, but persistent blockage can trigger it again.

diagnostics.finding: BLIND SPOT SYSTEM FAULT or CROSS TRAFFIC SYSTEM FAULT appears.
diagnostics.meaning: A system concern exists, but the message alone does not identify a failed module. Some concerns store diagnostic trouble codes; others are symptom-based.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the concern before choosing replacement. Remember that a CTA fault may not appear until reverse is selected.

verification.title: Observe startup indications
verification.body: At startup, the modules command the exterior-mirror indicators on for approximately 3 seconds. Check the indications and message center, including whether a CTA fault appears when reverse is selected.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the side serviced, whether the module or bracket was changed, PMI completion when applicable, and any remaining warning messages.

procedures.purpose: Left or right module and bracket removal, installation and conditional PMI.
Rear bumper cover removal and installation for module access.
Operating indications, blocked-sensor behavior and detection limitations.

applicability.equipment: Blind Spot Information System and Cross Traffic Alert

guides.title: Activate or deactivate the driver or passenger Belt-Minder reminder
guides.summary: Change one front-seat Belt-Minder setting through a timed buckle sequence and confirm acceptance at the safety-belt warning indicator.
guides.introduction: Belt-Minder provides a reminder associated with front-seat belt use. The driver and front passenger settings are controlled independently. This procedure changes the selected reminder setting through the belt buckle and ignition sequence; the safety-belt warning indicator provides the confirmation. A diagnostic scan tool can also perform activation or deactivation.
guides.why: Timing and buckle speed are part of the command. If the buckle sequence is too fast, the restraints control module (RCM) may miss an input. Keeping the other seating position unbuckled also preserves the required conditions while changing the selected seat.

when.summary: When the driver or front passenger Belt-Minder setting needs to be activated or deactivated.
notes: A MyKey programmed key prevents deactivation, re-enables a previously disabled reminder and prevents its usual 5-minute timeout.

prepare.title: Read the required safety information
prepare.detail: Before beginning, refer to Safety Warnings in section 100-00 General Information.

prepare.title: Choose the seat and method
prepare.detail: Select the driver or front passenger position. Use the manual sequence below or a diagnostic scan tool. For the manual method, be ready to watch the indicator and follow the timing windows.

steps.title: Secure the vehicle and establish the starting state
steps.body: Apply the parking brake. Select Park for an automatic transmission or Neutral for a manual transmission. Switch the ignition OFF and unbuckle both front safety belts.

steps.title: Wait for the initial indicator to go out
steps.body: Turn the ignition to RUN without starting the engine. Wait until the safety-belt warning indicator turns off, approximately 1 minute. The next two buckle-sequence steps must both finish within 30 seconds of that event.

steps.title: Enter the three-cycle sequence
steps.body: At the selected seat, buckle and unbuckle the belt 3 times at a moderate rate, ending unbuckled. Leave the other seat’s belt unbuckled. After this step, the warning indicator turns off.

steps.title: Enter the final cycle
steps.body: Within 7 seconds of the indicator turning off, buckle and unbuckle the selected belt once more at a moderate rate. Keep this action within the overall 30-second window.

steps.title: Observe confirmation
steps.body: Starting from its off state, the warning indicator flashes for 4.5 seconds to confirm activation or deactivation. After that confirmation, the procedure is complete. Change the other seat separately if required.

watchFor.title: Rushed buckle inputs
watchFor.body: A rapid sequence can go unrecognized and require repetition. Use a moderate, deliberate rate while still meeting the timing limits.

watchFor.title: Restricted-key behavior
watchFor.body: Belt-Minder remaining active with a MyKey programmed key is expected behavior, not evidence that the reminder system has failed.

notes: The same confirmation pattern is used for enabling and disabling; the flashes alone do not distinguish the resulting setting.

diagnostics.finding: The confirmation flash does not occur.
diagnostics.meaning: Successful completion has not been confirmed; a missed buckle input or timing requirement may explain it.
diagnostics.next: Re-establish the starting conditions and repeat the sequence at a moderate rate, observing both timing windows.

verification.title: Confirm acceptance
verification.body: Observe the specified 4.5-second warning-indicator flash after the final buckle/unbuckle action.

verification.title: Record the selected position
verification.body: Record which seat was changed, the intended setting and whether the confirmation appeared.

procedures.purpose: Independent driver or front passenger Belt-Minder activation/deactivation, timing and confirmation.

guides.title: Replace a cylinder block core plug
guides.summary: Extract the core plug, assess its bore and install the correct replacement using the cup-type or expansion-type method.
guides.introduction: Core plugs close openings in an engine casting. Their seal depends on both the plug and the surrounding bore, so replacing a leaking plug involves more than fitting another piece into the opening. This repair covers extraction, bore inspection and two installation branches: cup-type plugs and expansion-type plugs.
guides.why: Bore damage can prevent a replacement plug from sealing. Installation technique also matters: a distorted cup sealing surface or an expansion plug expanded before it is seated can leave a leak. Keep the work contamination-free because foreign material introduced during engine repair can cause premature engine failure.

when.summary: When a core plug requires replacement and access to the plug has been established.
notes: Identify the engine and actual plug type before selecting replacement parts or an installation branch.

prepare.title: Establish access and cleanliness
prepare.detail: Arrange the engine-specific access work before beginning this exposed-plug repair. Keep parts and the work area free of contamination.

prepare.title: Prepare extraction and installation tools
prepare.detail: Have slide hammer 100-001 (T50T-100-A), a commercially available body dent puller attachment or freeze-plug puller, and a freeze-plug installer.

prepare.title: Obtain the specified sealant
prepare.detail: Both installation branches use Motorcraft Threadlock 262, TA-26, specification WSK-M2G351-A6. Arrange machining capability if inspection reveals bore damage that prevents correct sealing.

steps.title: Extract the existing core plug
steps.body: Remove the plug with the specified slide hammer and suitable commercial attachment or freeze-plug puller. Removal exposes the bore for the inspection that determines how the repair should proceed.

steps.title: Inspect the sealing bore
steps.body: Look for damage that would interfere with correct sealing. If the bore is damaged, bore it for the next oversize plug. An oversize plug is identified by OS stamped on the flat on its cup side.

steps.title: Install a cup-type plug when fitted
steps.body: Lightly coat the plug and bore with the specified sealant, then install the plug with a freeze-plug installer. Avoid disturbing or distorting the cup’s sealing surface. Its flanged edge must finish below the bore’s chamfered edge to seal effectively.

steps.title: Use the alternative expansion-type method when fitted
steps.body: For an expansion-type plug, lightly coat the plug and bore with the same specified sealant and install it using a freeze-plug installer. Do not contact the crown: that can expand the plug before it is seated and cause leakage.

steps.title: Finish the selected installation
steps.body: After installing the applicable plug type, remove excess sealant. Check the completed installation against the requirements for that type rather than applying both installation branches to one plug.

watchFor.title: Damage that sealant cannot correct
watchFor.body: A damaged sealing bore requires the specified oversize repair path. Extra sealant is not the prescribed response to bore damage.

watchFor.title: Premature expansion or cup distortion
watchFor.body: Avoid crown contact on expansion-type plugs and protect the sealing surface on cup-type plugs throughout installation.

notes: The block core plug is illustrated; cylinder-head core-plug work is described as similar. The illustration does not establish which plug type is fitted to every engine.

diagnostics.finding: Bore damage would interfere with the plug seal.
diagnostics.meaning: A replacement plug alone does not address the damaged sealing surface.
diagnostics.next: Bore for the next oversize plug and use the corresponding replacement.

verification.title: Check the applicable installation requirements
verification.body: For a cup-type plug, confirm that its flange is below the bore chamfer and its sealing surface remains undistorted. For either type, confirm that excess sealant has been removed.

verification.title: Record an oversize repair
verification.body: If machining was necessary, record the bore repair and the oversize plug installed.

procedures.purpose: Core-plug extraction, bore assessment, oversize repair and the separate cup-type and expansion-type installation methods.

guides.title: Replace the brake booster on 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L Mustangs
guides.summary: Replace the vacuum brake booster using the correct engine-specific access sequence, renew discarded hardware and bleed the disturbed hydraulic systems.
guides.introduction: The brake booster uses vacuum assistance to reduce the pedal effort needed to operate the brake master cylinder. Replacement involves the engine compartment and pedal connection, including removal of the master cylinder and brake tubes. The three engine procedures share that purpose but differ in cowl access, nearby components and battery-disconnection requirements.
guides.why: Opening the brake circuit makes bleeding part of the repair. Manual-transmission vehicles also require clutch bleeding after their reservoir connection is disturbed. The stoplamp switch must be handled with the pedal at rest, and specified mounting hardware and the pushrod locking pin must be renewed.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the brake booster requires replacement.
notes: These procedures cover replacement, not diagnosis of the cause of a brake-assistance complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange hydraulic-service capability
prepare.detail: Have torque tools and the equipment and instructions for Brake System Pressure Bleeding (206-00). Manual-transmission vehicles also need a suitable reservoir suction device and the linked clutch-bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Obtain replacement hardware
prepare.detail: Prepare new master-cylinder mounting nuts, booster mounting nuts and a booster pushrod clevis-locking pin. The 5.0L procedure additionally discards the cross-brace nuts.

prepare.title: Protect painted surfaces
prepare.detail: If brake fluid reaches paintwork, immediately wash the affected area with cold water.

steps.title: Begin the correct engine access sequence
steps.body: Remove the cowl panel grille. On the 5.0L, disconnect the battery cables using the linked procedure. On all three engines, detach the vacuum check valve from the booster and position it aside.

steps.title: Disconnect the manual-transmission reservoir connection
steps.body: For manual-transmission vehicles, remove the reservoir cap and siphon out the brake fluid with a suitable suction device. Disconnect the clutch master-cylinder tube and detach its bracket from the master-cylinder studs.

steps.title: Remove the cowl obstruction
steps.body: Detach the battery-cable retainer. On the 2.3L and 3.7L, remove the cowl-extension bolts and nuts, then the extension. On the 5.0L, remove the cross brace and discard its nuts, remove the cowl-extension bolts and extension, then release the noise-generator clamp and pin-type retainer and position the generator aside.

steps.title: Remove the master cylinder and tubes
steps.body: Disconnect the fluid-level sensor and detach the reservoir wiring retainer. Disconnect the brake tubes at the hydraulic control unit (HCU), then unclip them. Remove and discard the master-cylinder nuts, and remove the master cylinder with its brake tubes.

steps.title: Release the remaining engine-side connections
steps.body: Disconnect the vacuum-sensor connector. On the 2.3L, detach the fuel pressure line from its intake-manifold clip and position it aside; on the 3.7L, release it from the valve-cover clip. Follow the respective engine procedure for these access differences.

steps.title: Remove the stoplamp switch before disturbing the pedal
steps.body: Keep the brake pedal at rest and remove the switch using its linked procedure. The switch plunger must be compressed for rotation in the bracket; removing it with the plunger extended during pedal application can damage it.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the booster
steps.body: Remove and discard the pushrod clevis-locking pin, then position the pushrod aside. Remove and discard the booster mounting nuts and remove the booster.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Reverse the matching engine procedure, using new hardware wherever disposal was specified and its stated tightening values. Attach the booster pushrod before installing the stoplamp switch. Keep the pedal at rest and do not press, pull or otherwise move it during switch installation.

steps.title: Bleed and complete the repair
steps.body: Carry out Brake System Pressure Bleeding. On a manual-transmission vehicle, also bleed the clutch using its linked procedure. If a new brake booster was installed, complete the required road test after reassembly and bleeding.

watchFor.title: Reusing the locking pin
watchFor.body: The pushrod clevis-locking pin is single-use. Fit a new one whenever it has been removed.

watchFor.title: Incorrect switch adjustment
watchFor.body: Installing the stoplamp switch with the pedal displaced can misadjust or damage it. The pushrod must already be attached and the pedal must remain at rest.

notes: Tightening instructions appear within the removal procedures as well as the installation path. Use the values belonging to the selected engine and fastening location.

verification.title: Confirm required finishing work
verification.body: Confirm completion of brake bleeding, clutch bleeding when applicable, and the road test required after installing a new booster.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the engine and transmission configuration, renewed hardware, completed bleeding procedures and the road-test result.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost booster removal and installation, including intake-manifold fuel-line clip access.
3.7L Duratec booster removal and installation, including valve-cover fuel-line clip access.
5.0L booster removal and installation, including battery, cross-brace and noise-generator access.
Cowl panel grille removal and installation for access on all three engines.
Stoplamp-switch removal and installation with the required pedal position.
Clutch-system bleeding for manual-transmission vehicles after reassembly.
Battery cable disconnection and reconnection required by the 5.0L booster procedure.

guides.title: Check piston ring end gap
guides.summary: Measure the top and second piston ring end gaps in their cylinder bores and compare them with the correct engine specifications.
guides.introduction: A piston ring forms a seal against the cylinder wall while moving with the piston. Its split ends need clearance, including room for expansion as the ring heats up. This check measures that clearance with the ring inside the bore. It belongs within engine repair work, when the rings and cylinders are accessible.
guides.why: The measurement depends on both the ring and the bore containing it. A tapered or out-of-round cylinder cannot provide a sound basis for accepting ring fit. Careful positioning also protects the ring and cylinder surface, while keeping rings assigned to their original pistons preserves the identity of the parts being checked.

when.summary: During engine repair, when checking the fit of the top and second piston rings.
notes: Obtain the appropriate Section 303-01 specifications for the engine being repaired.

prepare.title: Arrange engine access and measuring equipment
prepare.detail: Have the cylinder bore accessible, a piston without rings, and a feeler gauge set. Engine disassembly and subsequent assembly require the applicable engine procedures.

prepare.title: Confirm bore condition and part identity
prepare.detail: Establish that cylinder taper and out-of-round are within specification before measuring ring gaps. Keep parts contamination-free and each ring associated with its own piston.

steps.title: Select the correct limits
steps.body: Identify the engine and obtain its top-ring and second-ring end-gap specifications. The shared checking method covers the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines, but acceptance limits must come from the appropriate engine section.

steps.title: Position the top ring
steps.body: Carefully place the top piston ring into its cylinder. Use a piston without rings to push it to the bottom of ring travel, establishing the specified measuring position without damaging the ring or bore.

steps.title: Measure both ring gaps
steps.body: Measure the top ring's end clearance with the feeler gauge. Position the second ring in the same manner and measure its end gap. Keep the readings identified by cylinder and ring position.

steps.title: Decide whether the fit is acceptable
steps.body: Compare each reading with its corresponding specification. Resolve an out-of-specification result through the applicable engine repair requirements before assembly; this checking procedure provides no ring-modification method.

watchFor.title: Ring or bore damage
watchFor.body: Handle rings carefully during insertion and positioning. Do not transfer rings between pistons.

notes: Keep foreign material out of engine components throughout the work.

diagnostics.finding: Cylinder taper or out-of-round is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The bore does not meet the prerequisite for accepting ring fit.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the bore condition using the applicable engine specifications and repair procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Either ring gap is outside its specified limits.
diagnostics.meaning: That ring-and-bore combination has not passed the fit check.
diagnostics.next: Determine the permitted corrective work; replace a component that cannot be restored to specification.

verification.title: Record the fit decision
verification.body: Record the cylinder, ring position, measured gap, applicable limits and acceptance result. Confirm both rings were checked at the bottom of ring travel.

procedures.purpose: Top and second piston ring end-gap checking method for the listed engines.
Engine identification, contamination precautions and specification-based repair decisions.

guides.title: Remove and refit the rear brake caliper anchor plate
guides.summary: Remove the rear brake pads and caliper for access, then refit the anchor plate with new mounting bolts.
guides.introduction: The rear brake caliper anchor plate supports the brake pads and locates the caliper assembly beside the disc. Removing it involves the pad-service sequence first. The job finishes by restoring the pad and caliper arrangement, seating the brakes with the pedal and checking the reservoir level.
guides.why: The brake hose must remain free of the caliper's weight throughout the work because hanging the assembly from it can damage the hose. The anchor-plate bolts are discarded during removal. Correct piston-to-pad alignment also matters: the rear caliper incorporates a parking-brake mechanism that affects piston retraction.
searchTerms: rear caliper piston will not retract

when.summary: When rear brake service requires removal or replacement of the caliper anchor plate.
notes: Plan the work together with the rear Brake Pads procedure.

prepare.title: Provide wheel access and caliper support
prepare.detail: Arrange safe vehicle lifting and wheel removal using the procedure referenced by Brake Pads. Have a means of supporting the caliper independently of its hose.

prepare.title: Have replacement fasteners and suitable tools
prepare.detail: Obtain new anchor-plate bolts and a torque wrench. A brake caliper piston retractor is required if new pads will be installed.

steps.title: Remove the pads for access
steps.body: Follow the rear Brake Pads procedure: remove the wheel and tire, remove the caliper bolts, and position the supported caliper aside. Remove the pads and their clips.

steps.title: Release the anchor plate
steps.body: Remove the two anchor-plate mounting bolts and the plate. Discard those bolts. Keep the caliper supported while the mounting area is exposed.

steps.title: Install the anchor plate
steps.body: Reverse the plate-removal operation using new mounting bolts. Tighten them to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm). This is the anchor-plate specification.

steps.title: Prepare the pads and piston
steps.body: If fitting new pads, use the piston retractor to compress the caliper piston. Apply moderate to heavy force toward the piston so the internal parking-brake clutch cone engages. Restore the clips and pads, and ensure the piston notch aligns with the pin on the inboard pad.

steps.title: Restore the caliper and wheel
steps.body: Refit the caliper without disturbing the piston-notch alignment. Tighten its bolts to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm), then complete wheel and tire installation using the referenced wheel procedure.

steps.title: Seat the brakes and check fluid
steps.body: Depress the brake pedal. Check the brake-fluid reservoir level and top up as necessary with the fluid specified in Brake System — General Information.

watchFor.title: Hose carrying the assembly
watchFor.body: Support the caliper whenever its fasteners are removed; the hose must not carry the caliper or anchor-plate assembly.

watchFor.title: Different bolt specifications
watchFor.body: Keep the anchor-plate and caliper mounting operations distinct. Their tightening specifications differ.

notes: Piston retraction is conditional on installing new brake pads.

diagnostics.finding: The piston does not compress during new-pad preparation.
diagnostics.meaning: Insufficient inward force can prevent the internal parking-brake clutch cone from engaging.
diagnostics.next: Follow the retractor method and required inward loading in the Brake Pads procedure; resistance alone does not establish caliper failure.

verification.title: Confirm assembly and completion
verification.body: Confirm new anchor-plate bolts were used, both bolt groups were tightened correctly, and the piston notch matches the inboard-pad pin.

verification.title: Record the final checks
verification.body: Record completion of pedal application and the reservoir-level check, including any necessary top-up.

procedures.purpose: Rear caliper anchor-plate removal and installation, including discarded bolts and mounting torque.
Rear pad and caliper access, conditional piston retraction, pad alignment and final pedal/fluid checks.

guides.title: Adjust the SVT Performance Package parking brake cable
guides.summary: Set cable tension so both rear wheels resist rotation at the first parking-brake position and spin freely when released.
guides.introduction: The parking-brake cables transmit movement from the hand lever to the rear brake mechanisms. Their adjustment establishes how much braking action develops as the lever moves. For this 5.2L SVT Performance Package procedure, the setting is checked at the first click, followed by a released-brake check with the rear suspension hanging freely.
guides.why: Too much cable tension can leave the rear brakes dragging after the lever is released. Tightening until a wheel locks also overshoots the specified setting. Checking wheel rotation repeatedly lets you stop when resistance appears, then confirm that releasing the lever removes that resistance from both sides.
searchTerms: rear wheels drag with parking brake released

when.summary: When parking-brake cable adjustment is required on a 5.2L vehicle with the SVT Performance Package.
notes: Complete both the first-click resistance check and the fully released free-rotation check.

prepare.title: Provide suitable lifting access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the lifting points identified by stamped triangles. Position adapters clear of suspension, exhaust, steering and mounting components; check underbody clearance where applicable.

prepare.title: Arrange access to the adjuster and wheels
prepare.detail: Have suitable access to the cable adjustment nut and both rear wheels so rotation can be checked frequently during adjustment.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist using the Jacking and Lifting procedure.

steps.title: Establish the lever position
steps.body: Set the parking brake to its first click or position. This is the specified reference position for adjusting cable tension.

steps.title: Adjust while checking both wheels
steps.body: Raise the vehicle and tighten the cable adjustment nut, checking rear-wheel rotation often. Stop when both wheels have resistance and no longer spin freely. Neither wheel may be locked.

steps.title: Confirm full release
steps.body: Lower the vehicle as needed while keeping the wheels off the ground and the suspension in full rebound. Release the parking brake and confirm that both rear wheels spin freely.

watchFor.title: Overtightening
watchFor.body: A locked wheel at the first click is beyond the required setting. Check rotation throughout adjustment.

watchFor.title: Unsafe support
watchFor.body: Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The vehicle's emergency tire-change jack is unsuitable for this work, and bumpers must not be used as lifting points.

notes: Keep both rear wheels off the ground for the released-brake check; full rebound means the suspension is hanging rather than carrying vehicle weight.

diagnostics.finding: A rear wheel locks at the first lever position.
diagnostics.meaning: The required resistance-without-locking condition has not been met.
diagnostics.next: Correct the adjustment and repeat the checks on both wheels.

diagnostics.finding: Either wheel fails to spin freely with the parking brake released.
diagnostics.meaning: The final release check has failed.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the remaining resistance before accepting the adjustment.

verification.title: Record both operating states
verification.body: Record that each rear wheel has resistance without locking at the first click and spins freely with the lever released at full rebound.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L SVT Performance Package parking-brake cable adjustment and wheel-rotation acceptance checks.
Correct lifting points, support precautions and hoist-clearance requirements.

guides.title: Replace the SVT Performance Package rear brake caliper
guides.summary: Remove and install the rear caliper using new mounting bolts and hose-sealing washers, then bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The rear caliper uses hydraulic pressure to press the brake pads against the disc. On this 5.2L SVT Performance Package arrangement, removal also involves the parking-brake cable's shoe actuation lever and support bracket. The job opens the hydraulic circuit, so mechanical reassembly must be followed by brake-system bleeding.
guides.why: Sealing exposed hydraulic openings protects the fluid path during removal. The hose connection requires fresh washers, and the caliper mounting bolts must also be renewed. Cleaning and correctly lubricating the pad contact surfaces prepares the caliper for proper pad movement after assembly.

when.summary: When the SVT Performance Package rear caliper requires removal or replacement.
notes: Have the applicable Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure available before opening the hydraulic connection.

prepare.title: Arrange access and hydraulic-service capability
prepare.detail: Follow the linked SVT rear Brake Pads procedure for access. Have suitable means to seal all exposed openings and the capability and equipment required by the pressure-bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have new caliper mounting bolts, new brake-hose sealing washers and a torque wrench. If fitting new pads, retain all hardware, lubricant and instructions supplied with the pad kit.

steps.title: Remove the rear pads
steps.body: Follow Brake Pads — Vehicles With: SVT Performance Package. Complete that access phase before disconnecting the hose or removing the caliper mounting hardware.

steps.title: Disconnect the hydraulic hose
steps.body: Remove the caliper flow bolt and disconnect the brake hose. Discard the sealing washers and seal every exposed opening to protect the hydraulic system during the remaining work.

steps.title: Free the parking-brake cable
steps.body: Disconnect the cable from the parking-brake shoe actuation lever. Press the retaining tabs inward and detach the cable from its bracket.

steps.title: Remove the bracket and caliper
steps.body: Remove and discard the mounting bolts. Remove the bracket, followed by the caliper. Keep the bracket and cable arrangement identifiable for reassembly.

steps.title: Prepare the pad contact surfaces
steps.body: Clean the brake pad-to-caliper contact surfaces and apply the lubricant supplied with the brake pad kit according to its instruction sheet. If fitting new pads, install all new hardware and lubricant supplied with that kit.

steps.title: Reassemble with new fasteners and washers
steps.body: Reverse removal to restore the caliper, bracket, cable and hose connections. Tighten the new caliper mounting bolts to 81 lb.ft (110 Nm). Reconnect the hose using new sealing washers and tighten the flow bolt to 35 lb.ft (48 Nm). Complete pad installation through the linked SVT procedure.

steps.title: Bleed the brake system
steps.body: Carry out Brake System Pressure Bleeding as required by the caliper installation procedure. Opening the hose connection makes bleeding part of completing this repair; use the applicable bleeding instructions for its equipment, sequence and completion checks.

watchFor.title: Brake fluid on paint
watchFor.body: Immediately wash affected paintwork with cold water if fluid is spilled.

watchFor.title: Reused sealing or mounting parts
watchFor.body: The removed hose washers and caliper mounting bolts are discarded parts. Prepare their replacements before reassembly.

watchFor.title: Unsealed openings
watchFor.body: Keep hydraulic openings sealed while disconnected so the exposed fluid path remains protected.

notes: The parking-brake cable connection described here is at the shoe actuation lever. Restore that connection and its bracket retention during reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Confirm the bracket and cable retention are restored, pad contact surfaces are prepared, and the required new bolts and washers are installed.

verification.title: Record fastening and bleeding completion
verification.body: Record tightening of the mounting bolts and hose flow bolt to their respective specifications, and completion of the required brake-system pressure bleed.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L SVT Performance Package rear caliper removal and installation, hose sealing, parking-brake cable release, new fasteners and required final bleeding.
SVT Performance Package rear brake-pad removal and installation before and after caliper replacement.

guides.title: Replace the front seat power lumbar assembly
guides.summary: Replace the backrest-mounted lumbar unit while protecting the upholstery, wiring and side-airbag deployment chute.
guides.introduction: The power lumbar assembly changes the support behind your lower back. Its motor is serviced with the assembly, so this repair replaces the complete backrest-mounted unit. Access involves removing the seat and progressively lifting its trim cover. On seats with a backrest blower, the blower and its snorkel also affect the access route.
guides.why: The main challenge is reaching the lumbar unit without damaging the surrounding seat. Pulling the cover away carelessly can tear the hook-and-loop strips from the foam. The side-airbag deployment chute also passes through this area; its condition and correct restoration matter to how the airbag deploys in a crash.
searchTerms: power lumbar support will not adjust

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the power lumbar assembly as requiring replacement.
notes: A lumbar adjustment complaint alone does not establish that the assembly has failed.
The illustrated left-hand-drive driver seat is representative; the other seats follow a similar procedure.

prepare.title: Establish safe seat removal
prepare.detail: Be equipped to complete the linked Front Seat removal and installation procedure and its prerequisites. This work exposes parts of the seat side-airbag deployment path.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted backrest equipment
prepare.detail: Check whether a blower and snorkel are present. Have the separate backrest blower procedure available for that branch.

prepare.title: Plan careful trim handling
prepare.detail: Be able to release pin retainers, J-clips and hook-and-loop attachments without pulling their mountings out of the foam.

steps.title: Remove the seat
steps.body: Follow the [Front Seat procedure](#/document/G1695491). With the seat accessible, release the electrical connector retainers and move the wire harnesses aside.

steps.title: Free the cover straps
steps.body: Position the backrest cover to detach its straps. Where a blower snorkel is fitted, route the straps out through it before positioning the cover aside.

steps.title: Open the rear cover access
steps.body: Release the pin-type retainers for the backrest cover insert and move the cover upward. Position the blower snorkel aside where fitted.

steps.title: Release the lower cover attachments
steps.body: Release the J-clip and draw the cover out from between the cushion and backrest. Carefully separate the hook-and-loop strips, then lift the cover; avoid tearing the strips from the foam pad.

steps.title: Free the deployment chute
steps.body: Detach the side-airbag deployment chute retainers and move them aside. Pull the chute through the backrest foam, then release the remaining backrest cover J-clips and move the cover upward.

steps.title: Remove the lumbar unit
steps.body: If fitted, remove the [backrest blower motor](#/document/G1695511). Disconnect the lumbar electrical connector, release its J-hooks and remove the assembly.

steps.title: Inspect and rebuild the backrest
steps.body: Before reversing removal, inspect the side airbag, airbag cavity, mounting surface and deployment chute. Remove all foreign material. Replace a damaged airbag or damaged deployment chute. Install the lumbar assembly and restore the blower, chute, cover attachments, straps and wiring using the [lumbar procedure](#/document/G1695516), then reinstall the seat.

watchFor.title: Airbag damage or contamination
watchFor.body: Damage or foreign material can prevent correct side-airbag deployment and increase the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

watchFor.title: Cover resistance
watchFor.body: If the cover remains attached, locate the remaining clip, strap or hook-and-loop connection before pulling harder.

notes: The lumbar motor is serviced as part of the power lumbar assembly.
Driver seat module programming and stop-setting requirements concern other specified component replacements; this lumbar replacement procedure does not call for them.

verification.title: Confirm the deployment path is restored
verification.body: Confirm the airbag-area inspection is complete and the chute and its retainers have been restored during reassembly.

verification.title: Check the reversed removal sequence
verification.body: Confirm the lumbar J-hooks and connector, cover attachments, harness retainers and any blower or snorkel are restored before completing seat installation.

procedures.purpose: Complete power lumbar assembly removal and installation, including trim access and side-airbag-area inspection.
Front seat removal before backrest work and installation afterward.
Backrest blower removal and installation when fitted.

applicability.equipment: Front seats with power lumbar adjustment; backrest blower where fitted

guides.title: Replace the audio front control module on SYNC-equipped vehicles
guides.summary: Remove the audio module through the correct SYNC access route and transfer its configuration when fitting a replacement.
guides.introduction: The audio front control module (ACM) is part of the vehicle's radio and entertainment system and contains the disc mechanism addressed by this procedure. It sits behind the front controls. Replacing it involves both physical installation and configuration transfer, so a mechanically secure replacement is only part of the job.
guides.why: Configuration must be captured before the original module is removed and transferred to its replacement afterward. Access also changes with the fitted entertainment system: SYNC 2/SYNC 3 requires removal of the touchscreen display in addition to the front controls. Selecting the correct branch keeps both the dismantling and programming sequence appropriate to the vehicle.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for ACM replacement, or the module must be removed for access.
notes: An audio complaint or trapped disc alone does not prove that the ACM needs replacement.
Configuration completion is required when replacing the component.

prepare.title: Identify the entertainment system
prepare.detail: Select the SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure before removing trim. Their access paths differ.

prepare.title: Arrange programming capability
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of programmable module installation (PMI). Capture the existing module configuration before removing an ACM that will be replaced.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled fastening
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and a torque tool appropriate for the specified ACM and, where applicable, display bolts.

steps.title: Remove any media
steps.body: Eject media from the ACM before dismantling. If a disc will not eject, leave it in place rather than forcibly extracting it.

steps.title: Begin configuration transfer
steps.body: Follow the scan-tool prompts to begin ACM PMI and upload its configuration before removal. On SYNC 2/SYNC 3 vehicles equipped with a digital audio control module C (DACMC), also begin that module's PMI process. These replacement preparations must precede physical removal.

steps.title: Remove the front controls
steps.body: Remove the front controls interface module (FCIM) using the matching [SYNC procedure](#/document/G1704003) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure](#/document/G1704007).

steps.title: Follow the appropriate display branch
steps.body: For SYNC, proceed to the ACM. For SYNC 2/SYNC 3, first remove the front display interface module (FDIM) bolts, disconnect its electrical connectors and remove the display.

steps.title: Exchange the ACM and rebuild
steps.body: Remove the ACM bolts, disconnect its electrical connectors and remove the module. Reverse removal to install it. Tighten ACM bolts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). The SYNC 2/SYNC 3 FDIM bolts also use 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm); follow the separate FCIM procedure for its installation.

steps.title: Complete replacement programming
steps.body: For a replacement ACM, complete PMI with the scan tool so the captured configuration is downloaded. On the applicable SYNC 2/SYNC 3 branch, also complete DACMC PMI. Follow the full [SYNC](#/document/G1704002) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3](#/document/G1704006) module procedure.

watchFor.title: Configuration not captured
watchFor.body: Removing the original module before starting the replacement workflow bypasses the required configuration upload.

watchFor.title: Additional programming branch
watchFor.body: The SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure requires a separate DACMC sequence where fitted; completing ACM PMI alone does not complete that branch.

notes: The equipment overviews identify DACMC within the ACM on the described 2.3L and 5.2L configurations.
The selected illustration shows the SYNC ACM removal arrangement.

verification.title: Confirm physical installation
