verification.body: Check that disconnected connectors are restored, the module is secured, and any removed display and front controls are installed.

verification.title: Record programming completion
verification.body: Record completion of ACM PMI and, where required, DACMC PMI after replacement. Do not treat a completed bolt-up as completion of configuration transfer.

procedures.purpose: ACM removal, installation and replacement configuration for vehicles with SYNC.
ACM removal and installation for SYNC 2/SYNC 3, including display access and conditional DACMC programming.
FCIM removal and installation for the SYNC access branch.
FCIM removal and installation for the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 access branch.

guides.title: Lubricate the door latch
guides.summary: Apply the specified grease spray to the closed latch, then operate the door to distribute it and remove the excess.
guides.introduction: The door latch holds the door closed and releases when the handle is operated. Lubricating it helps its internal moving surfaces work smoothly. The vehicle also has electrical lock and entry functions, but this procedure is a mechanical lubrication service; it does not establish the cause of an electrical locking or entry complaint.
guides.why: The latch is placed in its fully closed position while the door remains open so lubricant can be applied through the intended opening. Operating the handle and door afterward distributes the grease inside. More grease is not better: excessive lubricant can damage the internal lock motor.
searchTerms: door latch does not release smoothly

when.summary: When a door latch requires lubrication during service.
notes: No routine lubrication interval is specified.

prepare.title: Use the specified lubricant
prepare.detail: Have Motorcraft Multi-Purpose Grease Spray XL-5-A, specification ESB-M1C93-B.

prepare.title: Prepare the latch and cleanup tools
prepare.detail: Have a flat-bladed screwdriver to operate the exposed latch and a cloth to wipe away excess grease.

steps.title: Close the latch with the door open
steps.body: Open the door. Use the flat-bladed screwdriver to move the latch fully closed through 2 clicks. The door itself stays open for the lubricant application.

steps.title: Apply a controlled amount
steps.body: Spray the specified grease into the latch opening for approximately 5 seconds. Use the opening shown in the [lubrication procedure](#/document/G1695899) and avoid excessive application.

steps.title: Release and exercise the latch
steps.body: Use the exterior door handle to reopen the latch. Confirm it has released before moving the door shut, then open and close the door several times to circulate the lubricant.

steps.title: Remove the surplus
steps.body: Open the door again and wipe off excess grease. This completes the distribution and cleanup sequence without leaving unnecessary lubricant around the opening.

watchFor.title: Excess grease
watchFor.body: Do not continue spraying to compensate for a persistent complaint; over-lubrication can damage the internal lock motor.

watchFor.title: Latch remains closed
watchFor.body: If the exterior handle has not reopened the latch, do not attempt to shut the door against it.

notes: Exterior handles may release mechanically or electronically; use the fitted exterior handle to reopen the latch.
The typical left front door illustration represents a similar process for the other door.

verification.title: Confirm the operating sequence
verification.body: Confirm the exterior handle reopened the latch and the door was opened and closed several times to distribute the grease.

verification.title: Confirm cleanup
verification.body: Check that excess grease has been wiped away with the door open.

procedures.purpose: Complete latch positioning, specified lubricant application, operation and cleanup.

guides.title: Check low-side fuel pressure on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Measure fuel supply pressure through the correct engine-specific connection after pressure release, controlled reconnection and a leak inspection.
guides.introduction: This check measures the low-pressure fuel supply. On the 2.3L engine, the gauge connects ahead of the high-pressure pump; on the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines, it connects between the jumper tube and fuel rail. The result helps assess fuel delivery, but it does not by itself identify which component caused an abnormal reading.
guides.why: The gauge must be installed at the correct connection after pressure release. Pump-control connectors disconnected during that release must be restored before testing, or the setup can produce a misleading result. The leak inspection comes before completing the pressure test, and residual fuel must be drained deliberately before removing the kit.

when.summary: When fuel-system diagnosis requires a measured low-pressure supply reading.
notes: Use the pressure specification and test conditions applicable to the engine being checked.

prepare.title: Obtain the test equipment
prepare.detail: Use Fuel Pressure Test Kit 310-D009 (D95L-7211-A) and an appropriate container for fuel drained from the kit.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capabilities
prepare.detail: Be competent in pressurized-fuel work, the engine-specific pressure-release and quick-coupling procedures, and battery disconnection and reconnection.

prepare.title: Have the acceptance criteria ready
prepare.detail: Obtain the applicable engine's fuel-pressure specification before interpreting the reading. No numerical pressure range is supplied here.

steps.title: Select the engine path
steps.body: Use the [2.3L](#/document/G1671507), [3.7L](#/document/G1671533), [5.0L](#/document/G1671554) or [5.2L](#/document/G1794915) check. For the 2.3L, first remove the nuts and engine appearance cover.

steps.title: Release pressure before disconnecting
steps.body: Carry out the matching Fuel System Pressure Release procedure, then disconnect the battery ground cable using the [battery procedure](#/document/G1692356). Preserve this order before opening the fuel coupling.

steps.title: Install the gauge in the supply connection
steps.body: Follow the engine-specific quick-release coupling procedure. On the 2.3L, disconnect the jumper tube from the high-pressure pump and install the kit between them. On the other engines, install it between the jumper tube and fuel rail.

steps.title: Restore pump control and battery power
steps.body: Reconnect the fuel pump driver module (FPDM) connector disconnected during pressure release on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. On the 5.2L, reconnect both Fuel Pump Control Module connectors. Then reconnect the battery ground cable.

steps.title: Inspect for leaks before testing
steps.body: Perform the required key-on, engine-off (KOEO) visual fuel-leak inspection before completing the pressure test. A leaking connection must be addressed before continuing.

steps.title: Measure and compare
steps.body: Check pressure against the range in the applicable engine's Specifications section. Record the engine, reading, test conditions and specified range so the result can be interpreted accurately.

steps.title: Drain the kit and restore the system
steps.body: After testing, disconnect the battery ground cable. Open the kit's drain valve and collect residual fuel in the appropriate container. Remove the kit by reversing installation and restore the original connections. On the 2.3L, reinstall the appearance cover and tighten its nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm).

watchFor.title: Unrestored pump connectors
watchFor.body: Verify the pressure-release disconnections have been reversed before interpreting absent pressure, especially the two-connector 5.2L branch.

watchFor.title: Wrong pressure circuit
watchFor.body: The 2.3L procedure measures supply to the high-pressure pump; it is not a high-pressure outlet test.

notes: KOEO is explicitly the leak-inspection condition; use the applicable specification to establish the pressure-measurement conditions.
The selected illustration shows the 2.3L gauge connection, not a universal arrangement.

diagnostics.finding: A leak is visible during the KOEO inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: The test connection is not ready for pressure measurement.
diagnostics.next: Stop and address the leak using the required pressure-release and coupling procedures.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure falls outside the applicable specified range.
diagnostics.meaning: Supply pressure does not meet the requirement under the tested conditions; this does not identify a failed pump by itself.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the setup and restored control connections, then continue fuel-system diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure is within the applicable range.
diagnostics.meaning: The measured supply pressure meets the requirement under those conditions.
diagnostics.next: Retain the result and continue investigating any remaining complaint.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Keep the measured pressure, engine, test conditions and comparison range together.

verification.title: Confirm restoration
verification.body: Confirm the kit is removed, original fuel and electrical connections are restored, and the 2.3L appearance cover is refitted where removed.

guides.title: Replace the cabin blower motor
guides.summary: Remove the cabin blower through the right-hand insulation-panel opening, then restore its wiring, retainers and panel light.
guides.introduction: The cabin blower moves air through the heating and cooling system and into the passenger compartment. With Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC), the blower switch varies its speed. With Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC), the system manages cabin temperature and provides blower override buttons. This repair replaces the blower motor reached behind the right-hand insulation panel.
guides.why: The insulation panel, its ambient light and the retained wiring harness all need attention before the motor can be removed. Moving the harness aside creates access without using the wires as a means of pulling the motor free. Correctly restoring those attachments is part of completing the repair.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the cabin blower motor as requiring replacement.
notes: A lack of airflow alone does not establish that the motor has failed.
Blower operation and outlet temperature are separate functions of the climate controls.

prepare.title: Arrange access
prepare.detail: Provide working access to the right-hand insulation panel and its ambient light.

prepare.title: Prepare for retained components
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the panel push pins and blower retainers, and be able to release wiring retainers without pulling on the harness.

steps.title: Remove the insulation panel
steps.body: Remove the push pins and the right-hand insulation panel. Remove the panel's ambient light as directed in the [blower procedure](#/document/G1676757), so it does not remain attached across the work area.

steps.title: Disconnect and clear the harness
steps.body: Disconnect the blower motor electrical connector. Release the wiring harness retainers and position the harness aside before attempting to remove the motor.

steps.title: Remove the blower motor
steps.body: Remove the motor retainers and withdraw the blower. Keep the distinction between wiring retainers and motor retainers clear: both are released, but they secure different parts.

steps.title: Install and restore the access area
steps.body: Reverse removal to install the blower and its retainers. Restore the harness routing, wiring retainers and electrical connector, then reinstall the ambient light, insulation panel and push pins.

watchFor.title: Harness still attached
watchFor.body: If the wiring prevents access, check that its retainers have been released rather than pulling the harness farther.

watchFor.title: Panel light overlooked
watchFor.body: The insulation-panel ambient light is a separate removal and restoration item.

notes: The procedure gives no motor-retainer torque; do not borrow the pressure-transducer or another climate component's specification.

verification.title: Confirm blower installation
verification.body: Confirm the motor retainers, electrical connector and harness retainers have all been restored.

verification.title: Confirm access-panel restoration
verification.body: Check that the ambient light is reinstalled and the insulation panel is secured with its push pins.

procedures.purpose: Cabin blower motor removal and installation through the right-hand insulation-panel opening.

guides.title: Replace the A-pillar outer section and reinforcements
guides.summary: Restore a damaged A-pillar using the permitted outer-panel section, complete inner reinforcements and the specified welded, bonded and sealed joints.
guides.introduction: The A-pillar forms the forward edge of the door opening and carries the door hinges. Its outer panel covers separate structural reinforcements. This repair involves cutting the outer skin, replacing the inner reinforcements at their factory seams and rebuilding the surrounding joints. Coupe and convertible service panels differ, so identify the body style before planning the work.
guides.why: The outer panel and inner reinforcements have different replacement rules. Cutting through an inner reinforcement would depart from the required structural repair. Body dimensions, weld locations, adhesive, noise-control foam and corrosion protection all contribute to the finished result; a tidy painted surface alone does not establish that the structure is correctly restored.

when.summary: When assessed A-pillar damage requires replacement of the outer section and inner reinforcements.
notes: Restore the vehicle to its pre-damage dimensions first where necessary.
Inner A-pillar reinforcements must be replaced at factory seams; sectioning them is prohibited.

prepare.title: Structural repair capability
prepare.detail: Use a body repair facility capable of dimensional restoration, resistance spot welding and MIG/MAG welding, with the correct coupe or convertible service parts.

prepare.title: Cutting and fitting equipment
prepare.detail: Prepare an air body saw, spot-weld drill, grinder, hot-air gun, knife, locking pliers and the specified 8 mm drill for plug-weld preparation.

prepare.title: Bonding and protection materials
prepare.detail: Obtain the specified metal-bonding adhesive, flexible repair foam and seam sealer, together with Ford-approved primer and paint materials.

steps.title: Open access and establish body shape
steps.body: Remove the fixed glass, fender, hood, front door, rocker moulding and body-style-specific A-pillar trim using their individual procedures. Remove the fender bracket and restore body dimensions where required before cutting.

steps.title: Clear the repair area
steps.body: Follow the convertible branch for removal of the vibration damper and reinforcement. Move the carpet and wiring harness away from the repair area, then remove the door hinges from the A-pillar.

steps.title: Remove the outer section
steps.body: Follow the cut locations in the A-pillar procedure and cut only the outer body panel. Drill its spot welds, then soften the noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) foam with the hot-air gun to release the panel. Do not heat the area above 170° C.

steps.title: Release the inner reinforcements
steps.body: Remove the upper reinforcement first by drilling the spot welds, grinding the specified seam welds and softening the foam. Then drill and release the lower reinforcement, using the knife where directed. Maintain the same heat limit throughout.

steps.title: Install the lower reinforcement
steps.body: Prepare its plug-weld holes and apply adhesive and expanding foam at the indicated locations. Clamp the replacement into position, resistance spot weld it and complete the specified plug welds.

steps.title: Install the upper reinforcement
steps.body: Prepare the replacement's plug-weld holes and apply adhesive to the upper flange of the lower reinforcement. Position the upper reinforcement and complete the specified resistance and MIG/MAG welds.

steps.title: Fit the outer replacement section
steps.body: Cut the service panel to the prescribed section and prepare its plug-weld holes. Clamp it accurately, then complete the welding, spot welding and MIG plug welding at the locations shown in the procedure.

steps.title: Finish and protect the joints
steps.body: Metal-finish the repair, apply approved primer and restore sealing to production level. Position, clamp and weld the lower fender bracket; install the upper bracket and reinforcement with their specified fastener torques. Refit the convertible vibration damper where applicable, then refinish and restore corrosion protection.

steps.title: Reassemble and align
steps.body: Install the door hinges, restore carpet and harness routing, and refit the removed glass, panels and trim through their procedures. Adjust the hood and front door as necessary using the alignment procedures.

watchFor.title: Cutting beyond the outer skin
watchFor.body: The permission to section the outer panel does not extend to either inner reinforcement.

watchFor.title: Foam resisting removal
watchFor.body: Use controlled heat within the stated limit; resistance is not a reason to overheat the joint.

notes: The coupe illustrations also guide the similar convertible operations, but convertible hardware and service parts still require their own branch.

verification.title: Check closure fit and protection
verification.body: Confirm hood and door alignment against the applicable body dimensions, and confirm sealing and corrosion protection have been restored.

verification.title: Record the completed structural work
verification.body: Record the dimensional checks, factory-seam reinforcement replacement, completed welds and final alignment results.
