guides.title: Overhaul the MT82 output-shaft sixth-gear and synchronizer assembly
guides.summary: Strip the removed MT82 output shaft, inspect its sixth-gear components and rebuild the assembly with correct lubrication and synchronizer alignment.
guides.introduction: The MT82 output shaft carries drive toward the transmission output. Its fifth/sixth synchronizer provides two different connections: fifth gear locks the input and output shafts together for direct drive, while sixth locks sixth gear to the output shaft. This bench job services that synchronizer assembly, sixth gear, its needle bearing and the associated shaft surfaces.
guides.why: A press can damage sound parts if its force is carried through an unsupported shaft or poorly positioned separator. Assembly also depends on the synchronizer ring sitting in the correct slots. Lubrication protects the contacting surfaces during assembly, but it cannot compensate for worn splines, a damaged bearing race or incorrect ring alignment.

when.summary: When transmission dismantling calls for inspection or repair of the output-shaft sixth-gear assembly.
notes: This sequence begins with the output-shaft subassembly removed; vehicle removal and transmission case dismantling are separate operations.

prepare.title: Press-work capability
prepare.detail: Use a hydraulic press and bearing separator with suitable support for the output shaft. Hand-tighten the separator to avoid damaging the gear.

prepare.title: Assembly lubricant
prepare.detail: Have Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC, specification WSS-M2C200-D2, ready to lubricate every component before reassembly.

prepare.title: Inspection and replacement planning
prepare.detail: Keep the gear, needle bearing, synchronizer ring, cone and retainers identifiable as they are removed. Replacement decisions follow the condition of each component.

steps.title: Remove the synchronizer assembly
steps.body: Remove the fifth/sixth synchronizer snap ring. With the shaft supported and the separator hand-tightened, use the hydraulic press to remove the synchronizer assembly. Inspect the assembly and the sixth-gear synchronizer ring and cone for wear or damage.

steps.title: Strip and inspect sixth gear
steps.body: Remove sixth gear, followed by its needle bearing. Inspect each separately and replace worn or damaged parts. Keeping these decisions separate avoids treating a damaged bearing as evidence that every adjacent component needs replacement.

steps.title: Assess the shaft and pocket-bearing race
steps.body: Inspect the output shaft for scoring and worn or damaged splines; replace the shaft when necessary. Inspect the pocket-bearing inner race. If that race is damaged, remove its snap ring and fit a new inner race.

steps.title: Lubricate and align the synchronizer parts
steps.body: Lubricate all components with the specified fluid. Position the fifth/sixth synchronizer assembly on the bearing separator and press as directed, then install the sixth-gear synchronizer ring and cone. All three ring tabs must engage the three assembly slots.

steps.title: Rebuild the sixth-gear stack
steps.body: Install the sixth-gear needle bearing and sixth gear in the prescribed order. Use the separator and hydraulic press to install the fifth/sixth synchronizer assembly and sixth gear, maintaining shaft support throughout.

steps.title: Restore retention
steps.body: Install the fifth/sixth synchronizer assembly snap ring. Confirm the retainer is installed and the required ring-to-slot alignment has been maintained before the subassembly returns to transmission assembly.

watchFor.title: Misaligned synchronizer tabs
watchFor.body: Pressing together parts with the ring tabs outside their slots can damage both the ring and synchronizer assembly.

watchFor.title: Excessive separator clamping
watchFor.body: The separator is hand-tightened; additional clamping force risks gear damage.

notes: The MT82's input and output shafts share an axis. The overview illustration shows the broader shaft arrangement, not the press setup.

diagnostics.finding: Scoring or worn or damaged output-shaft splines.
diagnostics.meaning: The shaft itself requires a replacement decision, independent of the removable sixth-gear components.
diagnostics.next: Install a new output shaft as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: Damage confined to the pocket-bearing inner race.
diagnostics.meaning: The procedure provides a separate inner-race replacement operation.
diagnostics.next: Remove its snap ring and replace the race.

verification.title: Confirm assembly details
verification.body: Check component lubrication, synchronizer tab engagement and installation of the synchronizer snap ring.

verification.title: Record inspection decisions
verification.body: Record the condition and replacement decision for the shaft, gear, needle bearing, synchronizer components and pocket-bearing race.

procedures.purpose: MT82 output-shaft bench disassembly, inspection and assembly.
MT82 layout and transmission identification.
Fifth- and sixth-gear powerflow and identification of output-shaft components.

guides.title: Replace a front-door glass run and adjust the window
guides.summary: Remove the fore or aft door-glass guide, restore its mounting position, then adjust and initialize the front window.
guides.introduction: The fore and aft glass runs guide the front window as it moves inside the door. Their position helps the glass follow the correct path and meet the weatherstrip. Replacing a run changes that mechanical guidance, so the work finishes with glass adjustment and power-window initialization, not simply tightening its mounting hardware.
guides.why: Marking the retainers preserves a useful starting position for installation, while adjustment establishes the final glass fit. The window also short-drops when the door opens and rises into the weatherstrip when it closes. Its mechanical position and learned operation both matter to that movement. A window that does not close correctly can require adjustment or electrical diagnosis; that symptom alone does not identify a failed run.
searchTerms: door window will not close correctly

when.summary: When an identified fore or aft glass-run problem requires removal or replacement.
notes: The left side is illustrated; the right side follows a similar procedure.
Choose the fore or aft access branch before dismantling the door.

prepare.title: Access and position marking
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools, a way to mark retainer positions and a torque wrench. Fore-run access requires speaker removal; aft-run access requires removal of the door glass.

prepare.title: Adjustment and initialization
prepare.detail: Have the coupe or convertible glass-adjustment procedure available, together with the Power Door Window Initialization procedure referenced by the main repair.

steps.title: Identify the guide and retain the correct access path
steps.body: Determine whether the fore or aft run needs work. For the fore branch, install the window control switch and raise the glass fully. The aft branch instead begins by removing the glass through its separate procedure.

steps.title: Remove the fore run when required
steps.body: Remove the front-door speaker for access. Mark the retainer locations, loosen the upper nut and remove the lower nut. Withdraw the fore run while preserving those reference marks for installation.

steps.title: Remove the aft run when required
steps.body: With the glass removed, unbolt and position the driver door module (DDM) aside in the illustrated arrangement where fitted. Mark the run's retainer positions, loosen the upper nut, then remove the lower bolt and aft run.

steps.title: Refit the run and restore access components
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal branch, using the marks to position the run. Tighten the specified run mounting nuts or bolt to 11 Nm. Refit the displaced module, glass or speaker through the appropriate procedure; the run-fastener torque does not apply to unrelated hardware.

steps.title: Adjust the glass and initialize operation
steps.body: Carry out the body-style-specific door-window glass adjustment. Then perform Power Door Window Initialization as referenced in the main procedure. Use that complete routine rather than improvising a switch-hold sequence.

watchFor.title: Assuming the marks are the final adjustment
watchFor.body: The mounting marks help restore the starting position, but the glass adjustment remains required.

watchFor.title: Expecting coupe features on a convertible
watchFor.body: Convertible models do not have one-touch up or bounce-back operation. Both body styles do have front-window short drop.

notes: Door modules are associated with memory-driver-seat equipment. Moving an existing module aside for access does not make this a module-replacement job.

diagnostics.finding: The glass does not seat correctly after run installation.
diagnostics.meaning: Its final mechanical position still needs to be established.
diagnostics.next: Complete the applicable glass-adjustment procedure, followed by initialization.

diagnostics.finding: One-touch up is unavailable after battery disconnection while the glass was moving.
diagnostics.meaning: On a vehicle equipped with that feature, initialization can be lost.
diagnostics.next: Perform the prescribed initialization before attributing the behavior to the replacement run.

verification.title: Check glass movement and seating
verification.body: Confirm the adjusted glass closes into the weatherstrip and short-drops when the door opens, then reseats when the door closes.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record which run was serviced, the body-style adjustment completed and the initialization result. Check only the automatic functions fitted to the vehicle.

procedures.purpose: Fore and aft glass-run removal and installation, including the required initialization cross-reference.
Front-door speaker removal and installation for fore-run access.
Front-door glass removal and installation for aft-run access.
Coupe door-window glass adjustment after installation.
Convertible door-window glass adjustment after installation.

guides.title: Remove and replace the optional Information Center Module
guides.summary: Release the center instrument-panel trim, disconnect the optional Information Center Module and replace or refit its screw-mounted assembly.
guides.introduction: The Information Center Module (ICM) is an optional unit mounted to the instrument panel center finish panel. Access comes through the clipped trim panels, after which screws release the module itself. Understanding that arrangement helps you separate trim removal from module removal and avoid pulling against the electrical connection behind the panel.
guides.why: The trim is retained by clips, while the module is secured by screws and connected to the vehicle wiring. Each attachment needs to be released in sequence. Also establish which display or warning function is involved before choosing this repair: the message center belongs to the instrument panel cluster (IPC), which also controls warning chimes.

when.summary: When the fitted ICM requires removal, replacement or access behind its mounting panel.

prepare.title: Trim and screw tools
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover and suitable tools for the module screws. Be ready to support the center panel while disconnecting its electrical connector.

prepare.title: Confirm the fitted assembly
prepare.detail: Check that the vehicle has the optional ICM and identify its connector and screw locations in the removal illustration.

steps.title: Release the right-hand instrument-panel trim
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release the clips and remove the right-hand trim panel. This opens the prescribed access path to the center finish panel.

steps.title: Remove the center finish panel
steps.body: Release its clips with the trim remover. As the panel comes free, disconnect the ICM electrical connector so the harness does not remain attached while the panel is removed.

steps.title: Separate the module from the panel
steps.body: Remove the ICM mounting screws shown in the illustration and lift the module from its mounting position. Keep the screws available for reassembly.

steps.title: Install the module and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: position and secure the ICM, reconnect its electrical connector and refit the center finish panel. Reinstall the right-hand trim panel, ensuring the clips engage.

watchFor.title: A panel that remains attached
watchFor.body: Check for retained clips or the electrical connection before pulling farther. The connector is disconnected during center-panel removal.

diagnostics.finding: The complaint concerns message-center warnings or warning chimes.
diagnostics.meaning: Those functions involve the IPC and, for many chimes, the audio-system speakers; the complaint alone does not identify the optional ICM.
diagnostics.next: Establish the affected component before replacing the center-panel module.

verification.title: Confirm physical reassembly
verification.body: Check that the module screws are installed, the electrical connector is attached and both trim panels are secured by their clips.

verification.title: Record the work performed
verification.body: Record whether the ICM was replaced or refitted, separately from the diagnosis of the original complaint.

procedures.purpose: ICM removal from and installation into the center finish panel.
Right-hand trim and center finish-panel removal, connector disconnection and reinstallation.
Identify the IPC message center when distinguishing a warning-display complaint.
Identify IPC and audio-system responsibilities for warning chimes.

guides.title: Adjust the parking brake shoes with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Measure the rear disc’s internal drum and set the parking brake shoe diameter to the specified clearance.
guides.introduction: The parking brake shoes act against the drum surface inside the rear brake disc. This adjustment sets their resting diameter so they have the intended clearance from that surface. The disc must come off because both the drum and the exposed shoes need to be measured.
guides.why: The setting depends on the actual drum diameter. Recording that measurement gives the adjustment a definite target. The specified clearance is expressed as a difference between diameters, so measuring across the widest part of the shoes matters.
searchTerms: SVT Performance Package parking brake adjustment

when.summary: When the SVT Performance Package parking brake shoes require clearance adjustment.
notes: Use the brake-disc procedure matched to this brake package for access and reassembly.

prepare.title: Arrange brake-disc access
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and capability required by the linked rear brake-disc removal and installation procedure before beginning.

prepare.title: Prepare to measure and record
prepare.detail: Use a caliper gauge suitable for the drum’s inside diameter and the shoes’ widest outside diameter. Keep the drum measurement available throughout adjustment.

steps.title: Remove the rear brake disc
steps.body: Follow the [SVT Performance Package brake-disc procedure](#/document/G1716401). Removing the disc exposes the parking brake shoes and gives access to the internal drum surface.

steps.title: Measure the drum
steps.body: Measure the inside diameter of the drum portion of the brake disc with the caliper gauge. Record the result; it is the reference for setting the shoes.

steps.title: Set the shoe diameter
steps.body: Measure across the widest diameter of the parking brake shoes, as illustrated. Remove the backing plate plug and rotate the adjuster until the shoes measure 0.59 mm (0.023 in) less than the recorded drum inside diameter.

steps.title: Close the access and refit the disc
steps.body: Install the backing plate plug, then reinstall the brake disc using the matched removal and installation procedure, including its fastening requirements.

watchFor.title: An off-center measurement
watchFor.body: A measurement that misses the shoes’ widest diameter will give the wrong basis for adjustment.

watchFor.title: An unfinished access opening
watchFor.body: The backing plate plug must be reinstalled after the adjuster has been set.

notes: Keep the recorded drum diameter associated with the shoe assembly being adjusted.

verification.title: Record the final setting
verification.body: Record the final shoe diameter alongside the drum diameter and confirm that their difference matches the specified allowance.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Confirm that the backing plate plug and brake disc are installed and the linked disc procedure is complete.

procedures.purpose: Measure and adjust parking brake shoe clearance for the 5.2L SVT Performance Package application.
Remove and reinstall the rear brake disc for the SVT Performance Package.

guides.title: Restore corrosion protection after body repairs
guides.summary: Protect repaired exterior metal and enclosed body cavities with the specified undercoating and rust inhibitor while keeping door drains clear.
guides.introduction: Body repairs can leave exposed edges, welded flanges and enclosed metal surfaces needing renewed corrosion protection. Undercoating protects exposed repaired surfaces, while rust inhibitor reaches internal rails, door shells and closed channels through an applicator wand. This finishing work follows the metal repair and refinishing stages.
guides.why: Oil, dirt and wax interfere with surface preparation, and neither coating can be welded through. Internal coverage also matters: horizontal surfaces are particularly susceptible to corrosion, while blocked door drains allow moisture to accumulate even inside a coated door.

when.summary: After body welding and refinishing, when exposed repair surfaces and enclosed cavities need corrosion protection.
notes: The illustrations are general references, not vehicle-specific repair maps.

prepare.title: Review body-repair safety
prepare.detail: Follow [Body Repair Health and Safety and General Precautions](#/document/G1693182). Consult each chemical’s material safety data sheet and use the specified protective equipment, including respiratory protection and chemically resistant gloves where directed.

prepare.title: Prepare the application equipment
prepare.detail: Have an undercoating gun, a rust-protection coating gun, a controllable air supply and suitable cavity wands. For best results, the vehicle should be at room temperature.

prepare.title: Use the specified materials
prepare.detail: Prepare the listed ValuGard Premium Undercoating or 3M undercoating, ValuGard Rust Inhibitor or 3M Cavity Wax Plus, and Motorcraft Metal Surface Prep Wipes. Use the product identifiers in the procedure to select the materials.

steps.title: Finish repair work and clean the metal
steps.body: Complete welding and refinishing before applying either coating. Wire-brush the area requiring undercoating, then thoroughly clean and degrease the metal with the specified surface-preparation wipes. Surfaces for rust inhibitor must also be free of oil, dirt, wax, grease and other foreign material.

steps.title: Undercoat the exposed repair surfaces
steps.body: Attach the undercoating canister to its gun and set the air pressure to 552–621 kPa. Apply light mist coats using the fogging pattern. Cover applicable exposed metal and exterior spot-weld flange edges, including repaired rail edges; the material displaces moisture.

steps.title: Set up the cavity-protection gun
steps.body: Attach the rust-inhibitor canister to its dispensing gun and set the air pressure to 448–517 kPa. Select a wand that reaches the enclosed area. The two coating processes use different pressure settings.

steps.title: Fog enclosed rails and channels
steps.body: Insert the wand as far as possible through the access hole. Pull the trigger, wait 2–3 seconds, then slowly withdraw the wand while applying light mist coats. Use this method to cover inner rail surfaces and the closed-channel portions of spot-weld flanges.

steps.title: Protect door and quarter-panel cavities
steps.body: Coat the interior metal surfaces of the door shell with the most suitable wand. Protect exposed repaired edges, quarter-panel flange channels and door-opening flange channels. Pay particular attention to horizontal surfaces, and keep every door drain hole clear.

steps.title: Clean up and check coverage
steps.body: Remove overspray with a mild solvent such as mineral spirits or bug and tar remover. Check accessible treated areas for missed exposed metal, incomplete edge coverage and material obstructing door drainage.

watchFor.title: Further welding after coating
watchFor.body: Neither product can be welded through. Coordinate coating with the completed welding and refinishing work.

watchFor.title: Poor cavity coverage
watchFor.body: A short wand or hurried withdrawal can leave enclosed surfaces untreated. Use suitable reach and the specified fogging sequence.

notes: The full-frame rail illustration is a general example, not a Mustang repair location.
If this follows collision repair, the structural and restraint requirements in the body-repair safety procedure remain part of that repair.

verification.title: Confirm protection of repair areas
verification.body: Check that exposed repaired edges have undercoating and that the applicable enclosed surfaces received rust inhibitor, with attention to horizontal areas.

verification.title: Confirm drainage and cleanup
verification.body: Verify that door drain holes remain open and overspray has been removed.

procedures.purpose: Prepare surfaces and apply exterior undercoating and internal rust inhibitor after body repairs.
Apply chemical-handling, protective-equipment and body-repair safety requirements.

guides.title: Repower the supplemental restraint system and verify its self-test
guides.summary: Follow the correct initial-fault branch, restore power where required and confirm that the restraint system completes its warning-indicator test.
guides.introduction: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) includes airbags and seatbelt pretensioners controlled by the restraints control module (RCM). The RCM monitors inputs and commands deployment when required. Repowering returns this system to service after repair; its prove-out sequence checks for faults before the vehicle is released.
guides.why: Incorrect actions can cause accidental deployment, so the sequence must be followed precisely. An airbag lamp going out is meaningful only after its initial illumination and the complete observation period. Some faults appear late, and an inoperative lamp can be accompanied by an audible or displayed warning.
searchTerms: airbag warning light does not illuminate

when.summary: After restraint-system repair, when restoring operation and completing the required SRS prove-out.
notes: The SRS must be fully operational and free of faults before vehicle release.

prepare.title: Use restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: This requires a technician competent in pyrotechnic-system service. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189), including its system-specific safety references, and disable remote start during servicing.

prepare.title: Establish the correct branch
prepare.detail: Determine whether an SRS fault existed at the beginning of the repair. Have the vehicle’s fuse information from Wiring Diagram Cell 11/Section 700-01 available for the fault-present branch.

prepare.title: Prepare for restoration
prepare.detail: Confirm that all airbags are installed and connected. Have access to the battery connection procedure and a scan tool capable of clearing continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes from all modules.

steps.title: Choose the initial-fault path
steps.body: If no SRS fault was present when repair began, follow that branch directly to the prove-out below. If an SRS fault was present, carry out the fuse, battery and seating sequence first.

steps.title: Restore the specified fuses and battery
steps.body: For the fault-present branch, verify that the ignition is OFF. Install the RCM fuse(s), or the equipment-specific fuse(s) identified by the wiring information. Observe the conditional fuse note below, then connect the battery using [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356).

steps.title: Position yourself before switching on
steps.body: In the fault-present branch, sit upright in the driver seat with no objects between you and any pyrotechnic device. Move the seat fully rearward to maximize distance from the driver airbag, then turn the ignition from OFF to ON.

steps.title: Run the complete prove-out
steps.body: For either branch, verify that all airbags are installed and connected and the ignition is OFF. Wait 10 seconds, then turn the ignition ON. The airbag indicator should illuminate continuously for approximately 6 seconds and then turn off. Continue observing for approximately 30 seconds while the RCM completes testing.

steps.title: Resolve faults and finish the applicable branch
steps.body: If the indicator fails to illuminate, stays on or flashes, diagnose and repair the SRS faults before proceeding with other repairs. For the fault-present branch, after successful repair and prove-out, use the scan tool to clear all Continuous Memory Diagnostic Trouble Codes (CMDTCs) from all modules.

watchFor.title: A connector that appears attached
watchFor.body: An incompletely seated connector position assurance (CPA) tab can leave shorting bars engaged and cause a low-resistance fault. This is a diagnostic possibility, not proof of a failed airbag; corrective work requires the applicable safe SRS procedure.

watchFor.title: Stopping the test early
watchFor.body: Flashing may not begin until approximately 30 seconds after switching the ignition on.

notes: The shared procedure includes a conditional three-blade BECMB/GWM fuse arrangement. Where vehicle wiring confirms that arrangement, remove the two-blade 10A fuse at the GWM position before installing the RCM or applicable BECMB fuse(s). These wiring labels do not establish that this equipment is fitted to the Mustang.

diagnostics.finding: The indicator completes its initial illumination and remains off after 30 seconds, with no chime or SRS message.
diagnostics.meaning: The prove-out indicates no SRS fault is present.
diagnostics.next: Complete the applicable branch and record the result.

diagnostics.finding: The indicator fails to light, remains illuminated or flashes.
diagnostics.meaning: The prove-out has not passed.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose and repair the indicated SRS or warning-indicator fault before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: An inoperative indicator is accompanied by 5 sets of 5 beeps or a message-center warning.
diagnostics.meaning: An SRS fault exists despite the absence of a working warning lamp.
diagnostics.next: Repair both the indicator concern and the SRS fault.

verification.title: Record the complete result
verification.body: Record initial indicator illumination, its subsequent state and any chime or message throughout the full observation period.

verification.title: Confirm readiness for release
verification.body: Confirm fault-free SRS operation and, for the fault-present branch, completion of the all-module CMDTC clearing step.

procedures.purpose: Execute the appropriate initial-fault branch and complete SRS repowering and prove-out.
Review general service safety and the required system-specific precautions.
Reconnect the battery during the fault-present repowering branch.
Understand RCM monitoring and the role of connector position assurance tabs in fault detection.

guides.title: Measure and adjust rear differential ring gear backlash
guides.summary: Measure ring gear free play and redistribute differential bearing shim thickness to bring backlash within the specified range.
guides.introduction: The drive pinion turns the ring gear, which is bolted to the differential case. Backlash is the small amount of free movement between the meshing teeth. Shims between the differential bearing cups and housing position the carrier and establish bearing preload, so adjustment requires controlled measurement and careful carrier removal and refitting.
guides.why: Backlash changes by increasing one side’s shim thickness and decreasing the other by the same amount. This moves the carrier without changing total shim thickness. Keeping reused bearing parts in their original locations and measuring housing spread protects the accuracy of the adjustment and the housing itself.

when.summary: When measured ring gear backlash requires correction during rear differential service.
notes: Have the rear-axle Specifications (205-02), including backlash limits and the shim-selection chart, available before selecting shims.

prepare.title: Prepare for precision differential work
prepare.detail: Arrange access to the carrier and bearing caps. Have selected shims ready before refitting because the carrier and bearing cups must be held in position until the shims are installed.

prepare.title: Gather measuring and installation equipment
prepare.detail: Use a dial indicator with holding fixture, clutch housing gauge 308-021 (T75L-4201-A), differential shim installer 205-220, a 12” / 300mm C-clamp, wooden blocks, tire lever, wrench, soft-face copper hammer and torque wrench.

steps.title: Measure the existing backlash
steps.body: Mount the dial indicator at a 90 degree angle to the ring gear tooth. Move the ring gear and carrier back and forth through free play only. Compare the reading with the rear-axle specification.

steps.title: Determine the shim change
steps.body: Use the backlash chart referenced by the [adjustment procedure](#/document/G2214744). Increase one bearing shim’s thickness and decrease the opposite shim by the same amount. If backlash is zero, the prescribed trial change adds 0.50 mm (0.020 in) to the right-hand shim and subtracts the same amount from the left-hand shim; refit and recheck to obtain a reading before final selection.

steps.title: Identify parts before removal
steps.body: Mark the bearing caps and preserve the original locations of their bolts. Remove the bolts and caps. Mark any bearing cups and shims that will be reused so they return to their original positions.

steps.title: Measure and apply housing spread
steps.body: Install the dial indicator and clutch housing gauge with the gauge tip inside the axle housing guide hole, then zero it. Fit the C-clamp at the 12:00 and 6:00 positions with the specified protective wooden blocks between the clamp and housing. Tighten until measured housing spread is 0.020” / 0.50 mm.

steps.title: Remove the carrier
steps.body: Remove the dial indicator. Protect the housing sealing surface with a wooden block, then use the tire lever, block and wrench as directed to remove the carrier, bearing cups and shims. Keep the clamp in place for refitting.

steps.title: Refit the carrier and right-hand shim
steps.body: Install and hold the carrier and bearing cups in place. Fit the selected or original right-hand shim with its chamfer facing outboard; if the original is unavailable, use the largest available shim as directed. Position the differential toward the right-hand side and install that bearing cap with its bolts finger-tight.

steps.title: Install the left-hand shim and cap
steps.body: Using the shim installer and soft-face copper hammer, fit the selected left-hand backlash shim with its chamfer outboard. If the selected or original shim is unavailable, use the largest shim that can be installed by hand. The clamp can be removed after this shim is installed. Fit the left-hand cap with its bolts finger-tight.

steps.title: Tighten and measure again
steps.body: Tighten the bearing cap bolts to 71 lb.ft (96 Nm). Rotate the differential several times to confirm free rotation, then reinstall the dial indicator and make the final backlash check against the specification.

watchFor.title: Housing damage
watchFor.body: The protective blocks prevent direct clamp loading that can crack the housing. Control spread with the gauge.

watchFor.title: Mixed locations or reversed shims
watchFor.body: Return reused caps, bolts, cups and shims to their identified locations. Shim chamfers face outboard.

notes: The Torsen differential carrier is serviced as an assembly only; this adjustment does not authorize internal carrier disassembly.

diagnostics.finding: Backlash is above or below specification.
diagnostics.meaning: Carrier position requires correction through paired shim changes.
diagnostics.next: Use the specified chart, preserve total shim thickness and remeasure after assembly.

diagnostics.finding: The initial reading shows zero backlash.
diagnostics.meaning: A measurable clearance must be established before final selection.
diagnostics.next: Use the prescribed right-hand/left-hand trial change and recheck.

verification.title: Confirm free rotation
verification.body: After cap-bolt tightening, rotate the differential several times and confirm that it turns freely.

verification.title: Record the final backlash
verification.body: Record the final dial-indicator reading and compare it with the applicable rear-axle specification before accepting the adjustment.

procedures.purpose: Measure backlash, select shims, remove and refit the carrier, and perform the final adjustment checks.
Understand rear differential construction, shim functions and the Torsen carrier service limitation.

guides.title: Replace a halogen front fog lamp bulb
guides.summary: Replace the halogen bulb through the front wheel-arch access, then restore the liner and wheels and check lamp operation.
guides.introduction: The front fog lamps are operated through the fog lamp switch integrated into the headlamp switch and the body control module (BCM). A halogen lamp has a separately removable bulb at the rear of its housing. Access for this job requires a hoist, front wheel removal and moving the inner fender liner aside.
guides.why: Confirming the lamp type prevents applying the bulb procedure to a light-emitting diode (LED) assembly. Correct operating conditions also matter: a fog lamp that is not enabled by the lighting controls can appear inoperative even when its bulb is serviceable.
searchTerms: halogen front fog lamp bulb replacement
fog lamp bulb wheel arch access

when.summary: When a halogen front fog lamp bulb requires replacement.
notes: LED fog lamps are serviced as assemblies; this bulb-removal procedure does not apply to them.

prepare.title: Arrange safe access
prepare.detail: Use a correctly positioned vehicle hoist and the equipment required by the wheel-and-tire procedure. Identify the marked lifting points and check hoist-adapter clearance.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted lamp
prepare.detail: Confirm that the vehicle has a halogen fog lamp before obtaining the replacement bulb and beginning removal.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and remove the front wheels
steps.body: Follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631), then remove the front wheels and tires using the [Wheel and Tire procedure](#/document/G1686507). This provides access to the inner fender liners.

steps.title: Expose the rear of the lamp
steps.body: Remove the push pins and position the inner fender liner aside. Keep the liner clear so the electrical connector and bulb can be reached.

steps.title: Remove the bulb
steps.body: Disconnect the front fog lamp electrical connector. Turn the bulb counterclockwise and remove it from the housing, as shown in the illustration.

steps.title: Install and restore the access area
steps.body: Reverse removal: fit and secure the replacement bulb, reconnect the electrical connector, reposition the liner and install its push pins. Refit the front wheels and tires using their complete installation procedure.

watchFor.title: Unsuitable lifting support
watchFor.body: Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The vehicle’s emergency jack is not intended for this hoisting job.

notes: Where daytime running lamps are fitted, that system also uses the fog lamp assemblies.

diagnostics.finding: The fog lamp does not illuminate during a check.
diagnostics.meaning: The operating conditions may not be satisfied; darkness alone does not prove bulb failure.
diagnostics.next: Check with the ignition in RUN, parking lamps on and high beams off, then operate the fog lamp switch.

verification.title: Check assembly and lighting
verification.body: Confirm that the connector, liner, push pins and wheels are restored. Check fog lamp operation under the specified enabling conditions.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install a halogen front fog lamp bulb.
Identify lifting points and safe hoist positioning.
Remove and reinstall the front wheels and tires.
Establish the front fog lamp operating conditions used for the functional check.

guides.title: Replace and configure the passenger door module
guides.summary: Preserve the passenger door module’s configuration, replace the unit behind the door trim and complete scan-tool programming.
guides.introduction: The passenger door module (PDM) is an electronic control unit mounted behind the passenger front door trim panel. Its replacement has both a physical phase and a configuration phase. Programmable module installation (PMI) begins while the original module is still installed and finishes after the replacement has been connected.
guides.why: When fitting a new PDM, the existing configuration must first be uploaded to the diagnostic scan tool and then downloaded into the replacement. Removing the original module too soon interrupts that required transfer path. Secure mounting and connected plugs alone do not complete the replacement process.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the passenger door module needs replacement, or removal is required for another repair.
notes: Arrange scan-tool access before removing the module.

prepare.title: Prepare the configuration transfer
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of performing the PDM PMI process. Be ready to follow its on-screen instructions and retain the uploaded configuration for the new module.

prepare.title: Prepare access and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have the equipment required for front door trim-panel removal and a torque tool suitable for the PDM mounting bolts. Review the trim-panel procedure before opening the door assembly.

steps.title: Begin PMI with the original module installed
steps.body: Start the PDM PMI process using the diagnostic scan tool and follow its prompts. If installing a new module, upload the original module’s configuration before removal. Complete this stage before disconnecting the PDM.

steps.title: Remove the front door trim panel
steps.body: Follow the [Front Door Trim Panel procedure](#/document/G1692600). Removing the trim exposes the module’s mounting bolts and electrical connections.

steps.title: Remove the PDM
steps.body: Remove the mounting bolts and module, then disconnect its electrical connectors. Support the unit while separating the connections so its weight is not carried by the wiring.

steps.title: Install the module and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the electrical connectors, position the module and install its bolts. Tighten the PDM mounting bolts to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Reinstall the door trim according to its own procedure.

steps.title: Complete PMI
steps.body: Use the diagnostic scan tool to finish the PDM PMI process, following the on-screen instructions. When a new module is installed, download the configuration captured from the original module into the replacement.

watchFor.title: Disconnecting before configuration capture
watchFor.body: For a new-module installation, keep the original PDM installed until its configuration has been uploaded as required.

watchFor.title: Stopping after physical installation
watchFor.body: The scan-tool completion stage remains necessary after the module and trim have been refitted.

notes: The stated torque applies to the PDM mounting bolts. Door trim fasteners follow the trim-panel procedure.

verification.title: Confirm physical installation
verification.body: Check that the electrical connectors are attached, the module is secured at the specified torque and the door trim has been restored.

verification.title: Record programming completion
verification.body: Record completion of the scan-tool PMI process and, for a new PDM, confirmation that the saved configuration was downloaded into it.

procedures.purpose: Begin PMI, remove and install the passenger door module, and complete configuration transfer.
Remove and reinstall the front door trim panel for PDM access.

guides.title: Overhaul the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission case
guides.summary: Prepare the transmission case for reassembly by cleaning its magnet, inspecting the shift shaft bearings and installing the output shaft bearing races.
guides.introduction: The aluminum case supports the working parts of the 3160 six-speed manual transmission. Its bearing races support rotating shafts, while separate shift shaft bearings guide the mechanism that selects gears. This bench operation deals with the stripped case, its guide plate, magnet and bearing races; it is one stage within a transmission overhaul.
guides.why: The shift shaft bearings are a decisive inspection point: damage requires a new transmission case. The output shaft bearing races also use different installation tools, so identifying each location matters before assembly begins.

when.summary: During transmission overhaul when the stripped case requires inspection and bearing-race installation.
notes: Begin with the case accessible as a subassembly; vehicle removal and complete gearbox teardown are separate operations.

prepare.title: Provide transmission bench capability
prepare.detail: This work requires controlled bearing-race removal and installation, component identification and careful inspection of the case bearings.

prepare.title: Have the specified tools ready
prepare.detail: Use a punch or drift for race removal. Installation requires handle 205-153, center support bearing installer 307-655 and differential bearing cup installer 308-163.

steps.title: Remove the guide plate and bearing races
steps.body: Following the disassembly phase of the [case procedure](#/document/G1849278), remove the guide plate bolt and plate. Drive the bearing races out with the specified punch or drift. Keep the race locations identified so the installation tools can be matched correctly.

steps.title: Clean and decide whether the case is reusable
steps.body: Clean the magnet, which collects magnetic particles from the transmission fluid. Clean and inspect the shift shaft bearings for damage; the illustration highlights these bearing locations. If damage is present, install a new transmission case rather than continuing assembly with the damaged case.

steps.title: Install each race with its assigned tooling
steps.body: For the output shaft bearing race, use handle 205-153 with installer 307-655. For the rear output shaft bearing race, use handle 205-153 with installer 308-163. Follow the assembly phase of the case procedure for their placement; the shared handle does not make the two installers interchangeable.

steps.title: Refit the guide plate
steps.body: Install the guide plate and its bolt after completing the internal cleaning, inspection and race installation. Tighten the bolt to 106 lb.in (12 Nm), completing this case-subassembly operation before the wider transmission assembly continues.

watchFor.title: Damaged shift shaft bearings
watchFor.body: The prescribed remedy is case replacement. This operation does not provide an individual shift shaft bearing repair.

watchFor.title: Confusing removal and installation tools
watchFor.body: The punch or drift is specified for removing races; assembly calls for the named handle and installers.

notes: The component description identifies the case, magnet, guide plate and surrounding transmission parts if their names are unfamiliar.

diagnostics.finding: Damage found while inspecting the cleaned shift shaft bearings.
diagnostics.meaning: The case fails the stated reuse condition.
diagnostics.next: Install a new transmission case before proceeding with assembly.

verification.title: Confirm the completed subassembly
verification.body: Check that the magnet is clean, both specified bearing races are installed and the guide plate is secured.

verification.title: Record the inspection decision
verification.body: Record the shift shaft bearing condition, whether the case was replaced and completion of the guide plate bolt tightening.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 transmission case disassembly and assembly, including bearing inspection, race tooling and guide plate tightening.
Identify the case, bearings, magnet and guide plate within the 3160 transmission.

guides.title: Remove and refit the instrument panel
guides.summary: Remove the instrument panel through the left front door after safely disconnecting its restraints, steering shaft, wiring and mounting points.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel is a large assembly secured across the passenger compartment and connected to wiring, the steering column and surrounding trim. Removing it creates substantial access but involves more than cosmetic panels. The automatic-transmission version adds selector removal, and the A-pillar trim procedure depends on whether the car is a coupe or convertible.
guides.why: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) must be depowered before the airbag work. Steering shaft fasteners must be renewed, and the steering wheel must remain secured against rotation to protect the clockspring. New factory upper cowl bolt-and-washer assemblies are also required to prevent water leaks.

when.summary: When an established repair requires removal of the complete instrument panel.
notes: Automatic-transmission vehicles require a hoist for selector cable access.
Use the A-pillar trim procedure for the fitted body style.

prepare.title: Arrange safe access and assistance
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and an assistant available. The work requires SRS and steering-column service capability, plus correct hoist positioning for the automatic-transmission branch.

prepare.title: Obtain replacement fasteners
prepare.detail: Provide new factory upper instrument panel cowl bolt-and-washer assemblies and a new upper steering column shaft-to-column bolt.

steps.title: Create working space and depower the restraints
steps.body: Move both front seats fully rearward. Carry out [SRS depowering](#/document/G1696297) before proceeding with restraint components. Follow the [instrument panel procedure](#/document/G1693975) throughout, including installation details embedded in its removal sequence.

steps.title: Release the cowl attachments
steps.body: Remove the cowl panel grille. Remove the wiper linkage mounting bolts and position the linkage aside. Remove the instrument panel cowl bolts, discarding the upper bolts for replacement with the specified factory assemblies.

steps.title: Clear the console and automatic selector
steps.body: Remove the floor console. On automatic-transmission vehicles, raise the vehicle on a hoist using the correct lifting points, remove the selector cable bracket bolt and cable, then remove the selector assembly and disconnect its electrical connector.

steps.title: Remove the surrounding trim and knee airbag
steps.body: Remove both A-pillar trims and instrument panel end finish panels, moving the weatherstrips aside as directed. Remove the right scuff plate and lower cowl trim, then the left scuff plate. Follow the separate driver knee-airbag and hood-release-handle procedures. Remove the left cowl trim and release its connectors and harness retainer.

steps.title: Disconnect the steering shaft and remaining wiring
steps.body: Secure the steering wheel against rotation; tilting the column upward eases access. Remove and discard the upper shaft-to-column bolt, then move the shaft aside without hammering, prying or forcing it. Release the remaining harness connections and retainers. Remove the right insulation panel and ambient light, and disconnect wiring at the right lower cowl and behind the glove compartment.

steps.title: Release the panel supports
steps.body: Remove the right and left center fasteners, trim cover and center bracket with its bolts and push pin. Release the parking brake. Loosen the A-pillar-to-crossbeam bolts and slide them outward as far as possible; they cannot be withdrawn fully with the doors attached. Disconnect both A-pillar harnesses and retainers, then remove the remaining left and right panel fasteners.

steps.title: Lift the assembly out with assistance
steps.body: Confirm that no wiring or connectors remain caught. With an assistant, rotate the instrument panel face down and remove it through the left front door opening, protecting the panel as it clears the vehicle.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, using the new cowl assemblies and steering shaft bolt. Apply each fastener's specified torque from the complete procedure. Reinstall the knee airbag and other removed components through their linked procedures, including the applicable restraint-system return-to-service requirements.

watchFor.title: Steering shaft resistance
watchFor.body: Do not overcome resistance by hammering, levering or forcing the shaft or column; damage can compromise steering control.

watchFor.title: Trapped wiring
watchFor.body: Stop moving the panel if a connector or harness is still attached or obstructed.

notes: Seats shown removed in illustrations are for clarity; this operation starts by moving them fully rearward.

verification.title: Check reconnection and retention
verification.body: Review the removal sequence to confirm restoration of connectors, harness retainers, the ambient light, trim and panel supports.

verification.title: Record renewed fasteners
verification.body: Record installation of the new factory upper cowl assemblies and steering shaft bolt, with their specified tightening completed.

procedures.purpose: Complete instrument panel removal and installation, including automatic-transmission access and mounting torques.
Required SRS depowering before restraint-component work.
Remove and reinstall the cowl panel grille.
Remove and reinstall the floor console.
Correct lifting points and hoist precautions for automatic-transmission selector access.
Coupe A-pillar trim removal and installation.
Convertible A-pillar trim removal and installation.
Driver knee-airbag removal and installation.
Hood latch release handle removal and installation.

guides.title: Replace a damaged outer rocker panel section
guides.summary: Replace the damaged outer rocker section using seam and resistance spot welding, then restore its finish, sealing and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The rocker panel runs beneath the door opening and forms part of the body's lower side. This repair replaces a damaged section of its outer panel. Coupe and convertible service parts are identified separately, although the illustrated coupe repair method is similar for the convertible. The work combines controlled panel cutting, welding and restoration of protective coatings.
guides.why: Cutting only the outer panel preserves the material behind it. The replacement needs both seam welding and resistance spot welding in the prescribed locations. Welding and metal finishing also disturb protective coatings, making sealing and corrosion protection essential parts of the repair.

when.summary: When damage calls for partial replacement of the outer rocker panel only.
notes: Damage extending beyond the outer panel requires a repair assessment beyond this section-replacement operation.

prepare.title: Provide body-repair capability
prepare.detail: The job requires an air body saw, spot weld drill bit, resistance spotwelding equipment and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment, with the skills to use them.

prepare.title: Prepare the replacement and finishes
prepare.detail: Select the service part for the body style. Have the specified seam sealer, a Ford-approved paint system and the materials required by the corrosion-prevention procedure.

prepare.title: Plan restraint and interior access
prepare.detail: The front seatbelt retractor and pretensioner must be removed through their dedicated procedure. The carpet and wiring also need to be moved away from the repair area.

steps.title: Clear the repair area
steps.body: Remove the front door, rocker moulding, and front seatbelt retractor and pretensioner using their linked procedures. Position the carpet and wiring harness aside. This provides access to the panel and separates the repair area from the displaced interior components.

steps.title: Remove only the damaged outer section
steps.body: Follow the section boundaries illustrated in the [rocker panel procedure](#/document/G1687544). Carefully cut through the outer panel only with the air body saw, drill out the spot welds and remove the section. The highlighted illustration identifies the removable area; it does not supply cut dimensions.

steps.title: Prepare and weld the replacement section
steps.body: Cut the corresponding section from the replacement service part. Install it and seam weld it with the specified MIG/MAG equipment, then resistance spot weld the panel. These are separate joining operations in the installation sequence.

steps.title: Finish, prime and seal
steps.body: Complete the metal finishing, then prime the repair area with a Ford-approved paint system. Seal all affected areas back to production level with one of the seam sealers specified in the procedure. Sealing must address the repaired joints, not just their visible surfaces.

steps.title: Restore coatings and removed components
steps.body: Refinish with a Ford-approved paint system and carry out [corrosion prevention](#/document/G1687508). Return the harness and carpet to their original positions. Reinstall the door, rocker moulding and seatbelt retractor/pretensioner through their individual installation procedures.

watchFor.title: Cutting into underlying material
watchFor.body: The repair is explicitly limited to the outer panel; do not extend the saw cut into the structure behind it.

watchFor.title: Stopping after paint
watchFor.body: Refinishing does not replace seam sealing or the separate corrosion-protection operation.

notes: Use the correct coupe or convertible service part even though the working method is similar.
No welding settings or section dimensions are specified here; follow the complete repair illustrations and joining procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Damage involves more than the outer rocker skin.
diagnostics.meaning: The stated partial outer-panel repair does not cover the full damage.
diagnostics.next: Establish the appropriate repair scope before cutting a replacement section.

verification.title: Confirm the complete repair sequence
verification.body: Confirm completion of seam welding, resistance spot welding, metal finishing, priming, production-level sealing, refinishing and corrosion protection.

verification.title: Check restoration and record protection
verification.body: Verify that the wiring and carpet are back in their original positions and the removed components are reinstalled. Record the sealing and corrosion-protection work.

procedures.purpose: Coupe and convertible outer rocker section removal, welding and finishing sequence.
Front door removal and installation for repair access.
Rocker panel moulding removal and installation.
Front seatbelt retractor and pretensioner removal and installation.
Restore corrosion protection after the welded panel repair.

guides.title: Replace the SYNC USB cable at the APIM or media hub
guides.summary: Install a replacement USB cable alongside the existing harness using the correct SYNC routing, then remove both ends of the original cable.
guides.introduction: The Universal Serial Bus (USB) cables connect the vehicle's ports with the SYNC interface hardware. The Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) is part of that system, but the cable path changes with the fitted display: non-touchscreen SYNC uses direct APIM connections, while touchscreen systems also use a media hub. This job replaces an internal cable while leaving its taped-in original body within the wiring harness.
guides.why: The original USB cables cannot be removed separately from the harness. The prescribed repair therefore overlays a new cable, secures it to prevent noise and vibration, and cuts both ends off the old cable. Correct endpoint identification prevents confusing the direct-to-APIM and media-hub arrangements.

when.summary: When replacement of an identified internal USB cable is required.
notes: This is a cable-replacement operation, not a procedure for removing the original cable intact.
Identify the fitted display and affected cable route before selecting the access procedure.

prepare.title: Identify the connection layout
prepare.detail: Establish whether the vehicle has AM/FM/CD/SYNC or a touchscreen display, and identify the front or rear cable being replaced.

prepare.title: Prepare access and fastening materials
prepare.detail: Have the replacement cable and tape or zip ties ready. The work requires floor-console and APIM removal using the procedures for the fitted system.

steps.title: Remove the console and matching APIM
steps.body: Remove the [floor console](#/document/G1693973). For AM/FM/CD/SYNC, follow the [SYNC APIM procedure](#/document/G1704004); for a touchscreen display, use the [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 APIM procedure](#/document/G1704012). These are equipment-specific access paths even though both expose the cable connections.

steps.title: Select the correct cable endpoints
steps.body: On AM/FM/CD/SYNC vehicles, both the front USB port cable and the rear port cable in the floor console route directly to the APIM. On touchscreen vehicles, the front USB port cable routes to the media hub; the rear cable at the console media hub routes directly to the APIM. Trace the intended branch before installing the replacement.

steps.title: Overlay and secure the replacement
steps.body: Follow the routing illustration for the applicable branch in the [SYNC cable procedure](#/document/G1694056) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 cable procedure](#/document/G1693905). Lay the new cable along the harness and make the corresponding connections. Secure it with tape or zip ties as necessary so it cannot move around and create noise, vibration and harshness concerns.

steps.title: Disable the original cable and restore access parts
steps.body: After confirming which cable is the original, cut both ends off it as directed. Leave its taped-in length within the harness; do not try to extract it. Reinstall the APIM and floor console through their matching installation procedures.

watchFor.title: Applying the wrong equipment branch
watchFor.body: The touchscreen front cable terminates at the media hub. The non-touchscreen front cable runs directly to the APIM.

watchFor.title: Loose replacement routing
watchFor.body: An unsecured overlay can move against surrounding parts. Retain it along the illustrated harness route before closing the console.

watchFor.title: Cutting the wrong cable
watchFor.body: Positively identify the disconnected original USB cable before removing its ends.

notes: APIM removal provides access; it does not by itself mean the APIM needs replacement.
The routing illustration must be read with its equipment branch, rather than treated as a universal port layout.

verification.title: Check the replacement path
verification.body: Confirm the new cable follows the applicable route, reaches the correct endpoints and is retained with tape or zip ties.

verification.title: Confirm completion before closing
verification.body: Check that both original cable ends have been removed and the APIM and console have been reinstalled. Record the equipment branch and cable replaced.

procedures.purpose: USB cable replacement and equipment-dependent routing in the SYNC section.
USB cable replacement and equipment-dependent routing in the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 section.
Floor console removal and installation for cable access.
AM/FM/CD/SYNC APIM removal and installation.
Touchscreen SYNC 2/SYNC 3 APIM removal and installation.

guides.title: Replace a convertible top front striker
guides.summary: Remove and refit the front roof striker using its alignment marks, while preserving the left-side latch-switch connection.
guides.introduction: The front striker provides the engagement point for the convertible roof latch at the windshield header. Its installed position matters to how the roof latches. A magnet-operated latch switch also tells the roof controller when the top is secured. This repair opens the header trim, removes the striker and returns it to the recorded position during installation.
guides.why: The striker and its upper retainers need separate reference marks before removal. Those marks preserve the required alignment. On the left side, the latch-switch harness must also be disconnected and restored; mechanical attachment and electrical confirmation of latching are related parts of the completed job.

when.summary: When an established repair requires removal or replacement of a convertible top front striker.
notes: A roof-status message or failure to move does not, by itself, identify a faulty striker.

prepare.title: Prepare for header trim access
prepare.detail: The work requires careful release of trim clips, handling of any visor wiring, a means of making alignment marks and torque-controlled fastening.

prepare.title: Use the normal roof operating conditions
prepare.detail: Opening requires active accessory-delay power, a released latch and vehicle speed below 5 km/h (3 mph). Carry out the repair with the vehicle stationary.

steps.title: Position the roof and remove the side trim
steps.body: Open the convertible top approximately halfway. Remove both [convertible A-pillar trim panels](#/document/G1692609), providing access to the ends of the windshield header trim.

steps.title: Remove the visors and upper header trim
steps.body: On both sides, remove the sun visor cap, release the clip and remove the visor, disconnecting its electrical connector if fitted. Remove the visor latch clips. Release the upper header panel clips from the lower panel first, then from the windshield header, and remove the upper panel.

steps.title: Lower the lower header trim for access
steps.body: Release the lower panel's clips from the header, followed by the clips at the sun visor locations, and lower the panel. Disconnect wiring as necessary for clearance. The illustrations omit some components for clarity; follow the [striker procedure](#/document/G1708673) for the actual access sequence.

steps.title: Mark and release the lower attachment
steps.body: On the left side, disconnect the convertible top latch-switch harness connector. Mark the striker's position against the header before removing its lower bolt. Preserve this reference for installation rather than relying on memory of the striker position.

steps.title: Mark the upper retainers and remove the striker
steps.body: Mark the header around the upper retainers before removing them. Remove the retainers and striker, keeping both sets of alignment references visible. The left and right striker removal methods are similar, with the electrical disconnection applying to the left side.

steps.title: Install to the recorded position
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence using the striker and retainer reference marks. Tighten the upper retainers to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm) and the lower bolt to 133 lb.in (15 Nm). Reconnect the left-side latch-switch harness, restore any other disconnected wiring and reinstall the header trim, visors and A-pillar panels.

watchFor.title: Missing alignment marks
watchFor.body: Both the striker-to-header and upper-retainer marks are required installation references.

watchFor.title: Forgotten left-side connector
watchFor.body: A disconnected latch switch interrupts the controller's information about whether the roof is secured.

notes: Brief audio muting when the roof is latched or unlatched is normal system behavior.

diagnostics.finding: TOP NOT SECURE is displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: With the top raised and speed above 5 km/h (3 mph), this message indicates that the latch is not fully engaged.
diagnostics.next: Check the actual latching condition and the disturbed alignment and switch connection; do not replace a striker solely because of the message.

diagnostics.finding: The roof does not move.
diagnostics.meaning: Operation also depends on latch status, operating prerequisites and confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully lowered.
diagnostics.next: Check those conditions before attributing the complaint to the striker or roof motors.

verification.title: Confirm alignment and reassembly
verification.body: Verify that the striker and retainers match their saved references, their tightening is complete and all disturbed wiring and trim are restored.

verification.title: Record the completed work
verification.body: Record the side serviced, restoration to the alignment marks and reconnection of the latch switch when working on the left side.

procedures.purpose: Convertible top front striker removal and installation, alignment references and fastener torques.
Convertible A-pillar trim removal and installation for header access.
Explain latch-switch feedback, roof operating prerequisites and roof-status messages.

guides.title: Replace the coolant pump on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Replace the coolant pump with the correct engine-specific seals, tightening sequence, belt protection and cooling-system filling procedure.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven coolant pump circulates coolant through the engine so heat can be carried away. On the V8 systems described here, coolant also feeds a separate heater circuit. Pump replacement opens the cooling system and disturbs the accessory drive, so the repair includes resealing the pump, restoring the drive and removing air during filling. Access and fastening differ by engine.
guides.why: Coolant must be kept off the drive belts. Removed pump seals must be renewed, and the V8 pump must enter its cavity straight: rotating it after insertion can damage the O-ring and cause leakage. Engine-specific tightening and bleeding are essential to completing the repair correctly.

when.summary: When diagnosis or inspection establishes that the coolant pump or its sealing joint requires repair.
notes: Overheating alone does not establish pump failure.
Select the engine procedure before ordering seals or applying tightening values.

prepare.title: Provide cooling-system service capability
prepare.detail: Have the engine-specific draining, vacuum-filling and bleeding procedure and its required equipment available before opening the cooling system.

prepare.title: Prepare seals and coolant
prepare.detail: All engines require a new pump O-ring; the 3.7L also requires a new gasket. V8 heater outlet tube transfer requires a new tube O-ring. Lubricate seals with the specified clean Motorcraft Orange coolant, VC-3-B, WSS-M97B44-D.

prepare.title: Prepare drive and hose tools
prepare.detail: Have waterproof plastic for belt protection, suitable torque tools and angle-tightening capability where required. The V8 procedures specify a hose clamp remover/installer.

steps.title: Select the engine branch and drain
steps.body: Use the complete pump procedure for the [2.3L](#/document/G1673128), [3.7L](#/document/G1694559), [5.0L](#/document/G1694591) or [5.2L](#/document/G1807373). Drain through that engine's cooling-system procedure before removing pump connections.

steps.title: Clear the intake and loosen the pulley bolts
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the engine appearance cover and retainers first. Remove the air cleaner outlet pipe on every engine using its matching cross-reference. Loosen the coolant pump pulley bolts before moving or removing the accessory belt.

steps.title: Release the drive and protect the belts
steps.body: On the 2.3L, turn the tensioner counter clockwise and position the accessory belt aside, then completely cover both the accessory and air-conditioning belts with waterproof plastic. On the other engines, remove the accessory belt through its dedicated procedure and completely cover the air-conditioning compressor belt.

steps.title: Remove the remaining access components
steps.body: On the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L, remove the thermostat housing before removing the pump pulley. Remove the pulley on every engine. On the V8s, disconnect the heater outlet hose and release the clamp to disconnect the lower degas-bottle hose from the heater outlet tube.

steps.title: Remove the pump and renew the seals
steps.body: Remove the pump bolts and pump. Discard its O-ring; on the 3.7L, discard the gasket as well. For V8 new-component installation, remove the heater outlet tube and discard its O-ring. Refit the tube with a new coolant-lubricated O-ring and tighten its bolt to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). Clean and inspect the V8 pump sealing surface for debris or damage.

steps.title: Install using the correct engine method
steps.body: Fit a new pump O-ring lubricated with clean specified coolant, plus the new gasket on the 3.7L. The 2.3L pump bolts tighten to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). The 3.7L's seven bolts require the illustrated sequence, first 89 lb.in (10 Nm), then 45°. For either V8, align the bolt holes before inserting the pump straight into its cavity; do not rotate it once inserted. Tighten V8 pump bolts first to 177 lb.in (20 Nm), then 60°.

steps.title: Restore hoses, pulley and accessory drive
steps.body: Reconnect the V8 heater and degas-bottle hoses and position the clamp. Install the pulley bolts finger tight. Refit the thermostat housing where removed, remove the belt protection and reinstall the accessory belt. On the 2.3L, turn the tensioner counter clockwise to return the belt. Finally tighten pulley bolts to 20 Nm on the 2.3L, 24 Nm on the 3.7L or 25 Nm on either V8.

steps.title: Refill and complete the engine branch
steps.body: Reinstall the air cleaner outlet pipe. On the 2.3L, refit the appearance cover and retainers using their separate specified fastener torques. Fill and bleed through the matching engine procedure. The 5.2L procedure additionally requires a road test.

watchFor.title: Twisting a V8 pump into place
watchFor.body: Rotation after insertion can damage the new O-ring and create a leak.

watchFor.title: Coolant reaching a belt
watchFor.body: Position and fully protect the specified belts before exposing the pump area to remaining coolant.

watchFor.title: Rising temperature after repair
watchFor.body: On the V8s, overheating warnings can progress to restricted operation and engine shutdown. Do not continue operating an overheating engine.

notes: The lead illustration shows the 5.0L pump arrangement; use the selected engine's procedure for its actual layout.
The V8 heater outlet tube transfer is conditional on new-component installation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0125 or P0128 on a 5.0L or 5.2L.
diagnostics.meaning: These codes relate to thermostat monitoring; they do not prove coolant pump failure.
diagnostics.next: Investigate thermostat and cooling-system operation before deciding on pump replacement.

diagnostics.finding: P1285 or P1299 on a 5.0L or 5.2L.
diagnostics.meaning: These indicate overheating and escalation of fail-safe cooling, rather than identification of a failed pump.
diagnostics.next: Establish and rectify the overheating cause. Use a scan tool to clear the applicable fault after repair as required to extinguish the malfunction indicator.

verification.title: Confirm engine-specific assembly
verification.body: Confirm the required new seals, correct pump and pulley tightening, restored hoses and clamps, and removal of belt protection.

verification.title: Record completion of filling and testing
verification.body: Record the engine variant and completion of its filling and bleeding procedure. For the 5.2L, also record the required road-test result.

guides.title: Replace the thermostat on the 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine
guides.summary: Replace the thermostat and its sealing ring, protect the accessory belts from coolant, and restore the cooling system using the engine-specific filling and bleeding procedure.
guides.introduction: The thermostat is a temperature-operated valve that controls coolant flow through the radiator. Replacing it changes the valve that regulates this flow, while a new O-ring seals its housing connection. The three engines follow a similar repair sequence, but intake access and cooling-system servicing must follow the matching engine procedure.
guides.why: A correctly installed thermostat still depends on a sealed connection and properly filled cooling system. Trapped air can interfere with circulation, and coolant spilled onto the accessory belts causes contamination. On the 5.0L and 5.2L, the thermostat sits on the cold side of the circuit, where coolant returns from the radiator; repeated opening and closing during initial warm-up can be normal.

when.summary: When cooling-system diagnosis establishes that the thermostat requires replacement.
notes: A temperature complaint or thermostat-monitor code does not establish the failed component by itself.
The cold-side operating description applies to the supplied 5.0L and 5.2L information.

prepare.title: Arrange cooling-system service
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and capability required by the matching draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure. Complete its safety prerequisites before opening the system.

prepare.title: Prepare the seal, coolant and protection
prepare.detail: Have the correct replacement thermostat and new O-ring, waterproof plastic for the belts, and a torque wrench suitable for the connector bolts. The specified coolant is Motorcraft Orange Concentrated Antifreeze/Coolant VC-3-B, WSS-M97B44-D.

steps.title: Drain the cooling system
steps.body: Follow the draining procedure for the installed engine before disturbing the thermostat connection. This controls coolant loss when the housing is opened and establishes the correct route for refilling afterward.

steps.title: Create the correct intake access
steps.body: On the 3.7L and 5.0L, remove the air cleaner outlet pipe. On the 5.2L, remove the air cleaner. Use the corresponding intake procedure rather than assuming these access operations are interchangeable.

steps.title: Cover the accessory belts
steps.body: Completely cover the accessory drive belts with waterproof plastic before opening the coolant connection. Leave no exposed belt surface in the spill area.

steps.title: Remove the thermostat and old seal
steps.body: Remove the connector bolts, detach the coolant inlet connector and remove the thermostat. Discard the O-ring; the installation requires a new seal.

steps.title: Install and seat the replacement
steps.body: Lubricate the new O-ring with clean specified coolant and install it with the thermostat. Fully seat the coolant connection on the thermostat housing before tightening its bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). The bolts should secure an already seated connection.

steps.title: Restore access parts and coolant
steps.body: Reverse the remaining removal operations, removing the belt protection once coolant-spill work is finished. Reinstall the engine-specific intake components, then fill and bleed the cooling system through the matching procedure.

watchFor.title: Connection not fully seated
watchFor.body: An unevenly seated connection can compromise the seal. Correct its seating before applying the specified bolt torque.

watchFor.title: Overheating during assessment
watchFor.body: The 5.0L and 5.2L cooling descriptions identify a red temperature gauge and powertrain warning as reasons to stop the engine. Do not continue running it to wait for the thermostat to open.

notes: Normal cold-side thermostat cycling during warm-up must not be confused with a sticking valve.

diagnostics.finding: P0125 or P0128 on the 5.0L or 5.2L
diagnostics.meaning: The powertrain control module has detected a thermostat-monitor malfunction; the code alone does not isolate the cause.
diagnostics.next: Complete cooling-system diagnosis before selecting replacement as the repair.

verification.title: Confirm the mechanical installation
verification.body: Confirm that a new coolant-lubricated O-ring was installed, the connection is fully seated and the connector bolts received the specified torque.

verification.title: Complete filling and bleeding
verification.body: Finish the engine-specific cooling-system procedure before evaluating warm-up behavior.

guides.title: Replace the dashboard headlamp switch
guides.summary: Remove the left-hand dashboard trim, disconnect and release the headlamp switch, then reinstall the switch and finish panels.
guides.introduction: The headlamp switch provides the driver's lighting selections to a system that also includes the body control module, lamp assemblies and other controls. It incorporates the front fog-lamp switch and participates in automatic lighting control. This job replaces the dashboard switch assembly through the left-hand finish panel; it does not involve removing the headlamps themselves.
guides.why: The switch is retained by tabs behind the panel, so gaining access before releasing it protects the surrounding trim. Lighting behavior also depends on operating conditions and other components. A lamp that stays off, or remains on after shutdown, does not by itself establish that the dashboard switch is faulty.
searchTerms: front fog lamps will not turn on
autolamps stay on after ignition off

when.summary: When the headlamp switch requires replacement after the lighting complaint has been assessed.
notes: Check the operating conditions for the affected lighting function before condemning the switch.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim access
prepare.detail: Use a non-marring trim tool and a suitable tool for the finish-panel screw. Be able to support the panel while accessing the switch connector and retaining tabs.

steps.title: Remove the access trim
steps.body: Use the non-marring tool to remove the trim panel. This exposes the finish-panel attachment without relying on a metal edge against the visible trim.

steps.title: Move the finish panel aside
steps.body: Remove its screw and position the left-hand dash finish panel aside. Create enough access to handle the connector and switch retainers directly.

steps.title: Disconnect and release the switch
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector first. Release the retaining tabs shown in the illustration, then remove the switch from the panel. Follow this order so the wiring does not restrain the switch during removal.

steps.title: Install the switch and restore the panel
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: seat and retain the switch, reconnect its electrical connector, restore the finish panel and screw, and reinstall the trim. Confirm that the tabs have secured the switch before closing access.

watchFor.title: Switch still caught in its opening
