watchFor.body: Check the retaining tabs rather than forcing the switch against the panel.

notes: China-market rear fog-lamp controls are a separate equipment branch; their operation should not be assumed for every switch.

diagnostics.finding: Front fog lamps do not illuminate
diagnostics.meaning: Their stated operating conditions require ignition in RUN, parking lamps on and high beams off.
diagnostics.next: Establish those conditions before interpreting the result as a fault.

diagnostics.finding: Exterior lamps remain on after ignition shutdown in autolamp operation
diagnostics.meaning: The system includes an adjustable delayed switch-off function.
diagnostics.next: Check the selected delay before treating continued illumination as a failed switch.

verification.title: Confirm installation
verification.body: Check that the switch is retained, its connector is connected and both panels are restored.

verification.title: Assess the affected lighting function
verification.body: Operate the relevant control under its stated conditions, accounting for fog-lamp restrictions and the autolamp delay.

procedures.purpose: Headlamp switch removal and installation through the left-hand dash finish panel.

guides.title: Replace a rear seatbelt buckle
guides.summary: Remove the rear cushion, replace the affected buckle at its mounting bolt, and verify restraint operation after restoring untwisted, accessible belts.
guides.introduction: The rear buckle receives the belt tongue and connects that side of the restraint to its body mounting. The retractor performs a different job: it manages webbing movement and locking. Buckle replacement requires access beneath the rear cushion, correct tightening of the mounting bolt and careful positioning when the cushion goes back.
guides.why: The mounting bolt is part of the restraint attachment, so its specified torque matters. Correct installation also means occupants can reach the buckle and wear the belt without twisted webbing. The required final restraint check confirms more than the appearance of the newly fitted part.

when.summary: When inspection or seatbelt diagnosis establishes that a rear buckle requires replacement.
notes: The illustrated procedure shows the right-hand buckle; the left-hand operation is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange cushion access and torque control
prepare.detail: Have the rear cushion removal procedure, suitable bolt tools and a torque wrench for the buckle attachment.

prepare.title: Prepare for the restraint check
prepare.detail: Be able to carry out the active-restraint operational checks in the linked Seatbelt Systems diagnosis and testing procedure.

steps.title: Expose the buckle mounting
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion using its dedicated procedure. Identify the affected buckle and its mounting before disturbing the attachment.

steps.title: Remove the buckle
steps.body: Remove the mounting bolt and withdraw the buckle assembly. The attached illustration identifies the right-hand mounting; use the corresponding location for a left-hand repair.

steps.title: Install and position the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal operation and tighten the buckle bolt to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm). Restore the cushion while keeping the belt webbing untwisted and ensuring the belts and buckles remain accessible to their occupants.

steps.title: Check the restraint system
steps.body: Carry out the active-restraint operational check in [Seatbelt Systems](#/document/G1883856). Use that procedure to assess any remaining buckle or retractor complaint before considering the job finished.

watchFor.title: Buckle trapped beneath the cushion
watchFor.body: Restore its accessibility during installation; a correctly attached buckle still needs to be reachable by its occupant.

watchFor.title: Child seat used during a collision
watchFor.body: The child-seat mounting areas require inspection and restoration to the original production configuration. Replacing a buckle alone does not address that requirement.

notes: The described Belt-Minder warning functions concern the driver and front passenger; they are not confirmation of rear-buckle operation.

diagnostics.finding: Passenger belt cannot be pulled out after being fully extended and allowed to retract
diagnostics.meaning: Automatic Locking Retractor mode may be active for child-seat restraint; this is distinct from buckle operation.
diagnostics.next: Allow full retraction to disengage that mode and use the specified retractor test if the complaint remains.

verification.title: Confirm attachment and accessibility
verification.body: Confirm the buckle mounting torque, untwisted webbing and accessible belt and buckle positions with the cushion installed.

verification.title: Record the operational result
verification.body: Record the repaired seating position and the result of the required active-restraint check.

procedures.purpose: Rear buckle removal and installation, including mounting torque and belt positioning.
Rear seat cushion removal and installation for buckle access.
Required seatbelt and active-restraint operational diagnosis and testing.

guides.title: Replace the convertible luggage-compartment lock cylinder
guides.summary: Remove the convertible rear backrest, disconnect the latch cable and replace the retained lock cylinder before restoring the seat.
guides.introduction: The convertible luggage-compartment lock cylinder provides a mechanical input to the lid latch through a cable. This repair separates that cable connection and removes the cylinder from its mounting. Access comes through the rear seating area, making correct seat reinstallation an essential part of the job.
guides.why: The cable connection uses retaining tabs, while a separate retaining clip secures the cylinder. Releasing those attachments in sequence avoids pulling against a part that is still retained. The rear backrest also has critical mounting requirements: nothing may be trapped between seat components and the body or within a seat-structure joint.

when.summary: When the convertible luggage-compartment lock cylinder requires removal or replacement.
notes: A luggage-lid release complaint can involve the cylinder, cable or latch; this procedure covers cylinder replacement.

prepare.title: Prepare seat access
prepare.detail: Follow the convertible backrest procedure, including its preliminary rear cushion removal. Have suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench for restoring the backrest attachments.

prepare.title: Plan the attachment sequence
prepare.detail: Identify the cable retaining tabs and the separate cylinder retaining clip before removal. Keep the seat mounting joints clear throughout the work.

steps.title: Remove the rear backrest
steps.body: Follow [Rear Seat Backrest – Convertible](#/document/G1709034): remove the rear cushion, release the backrest-to-floor fasteners, then release the backrest locking clips and remove the backrest. The attached illustration shows the seat-access fasteners, not the lock cylinder.

steps.title: Detach the latch cable
steps.body: Release the lock-cylinder retaining tabs and detach the luggage-compartment lid latch cable. Complete this connection release before attempting to withdraw the cylinder.

steps.title: Exchange the cylinder
steps.body: Remove the separate cylinder retaining clip, then remove the lock cylinder. Reverse these operations to install the replacement: secure the cylinder with its clip and restore the cable connection and retaining tabs.

steps.title: Restore the rear seating
steps.body: Reverse the backrest removal sequence and tighten its floor attachments to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm). Restore the cushion as directed. Keep objects out of all seat mounting joints, and leave the belt webbing untwisted with belts and buckles accessible.

watchFor.title: Cable or cylinder still retained
watchFor.body: The cable tabs and cylinder clip are separate attachments. Confirm the appropriate attachment is released before moving either component.

watchFor.title: Obstructed seat joints
watchFor.body: Objects between the seat structure and body can prevent correct installation and operation. Clear the joints before securing the backrest.

notes: Mechanical cylinder and cable attachment should be checked separately from any passive-entry release complaint.

verification.title: Confirm cylinder and cable attachment
verification.body: Before closing access, confirm the cylinder retaining clip is installed and the cable connection and tabs are restored.

verification.title: Confirm seating restoration
verification.body: Check the backrest locking clips, specified floor-fastener torque and clear seat joints. Confirm that belts and buckles remain accessible without twisted webbing.

procedures.purpose: Convertible luggage-compartment lock cylinder and latch-cable removal and installation.
Convertible rear backrest removal and installation for cylinder access.

guides.title: Remove and refit the rear seat cushion
guides.summary: Release the rear cushion’s floor locking tabs, lift out the cushion, and refit it with the seatbelts correctly positioned.
guides.introduction: The rear seat cushion supports the occupants and is secured to the floor by locking tabs at its front edge. Removing it provides access beneath the seating area or allows the cushion itself to be replaced. This is a straightforward interior job, but understanding how the tabs release matters more than applying force. The seatbelts and buckles also need attention when the cushion goes back in.
guides.why: The locking tabs must be pressed inward before the cushion is lifted. Pulling against engaged tabs can damage them. During installation, trapped buckles or twisted belt webbing can leave the rear seating positions improperly arranged even when the cushion appears to be in place.
searchTerms: rear seat cushion will not release

when.summary: When the rear cushion needs replacement or access is required beneath it.
notes: Move both front seats fully forward before working at the cushion’s front edge.

prepare.title: Create working room
prepare.detail: Provide access from both sides of the rear seating area. You need room to reach the front locking tabs and lift the released cushion clear.

prepare.title: Identify the release points
prepare.detail: Locate the floor locking tabs at the front of the cushion before lifting. Note where the belt webbing and buckles emerge so they can be arranged correctly during refitting.

steps.title: Move the front seats forward
steps.body: Move the front seat on each side to its full forward position. This exposes the working area along the front of the rear cushion.

steps.title: Release the floor locking tabs
steps.body: Press inward on the locking tabs at the front of the cushion to release it from the floor. Keep the release action separate from lifting so the tabs are not forced while still engaged.

steps.title: Lift out the cushion
steps.body: Once the tabs have released, lift and release the cushion, then remove it from the vehicle. The illustration in the linked procedure shows the cushion being lifted away.

steps.title: Refit with the belts accessible
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to install the cushion. Arrange the seatbelt webbing without twists and keep every belt and buckle accessible to its occupant as the cushion is secured.

watchFor.title: Resistance at the front edge
watchFor.body: Check that the locking tabs have been pressed inward before applying more lifting force; engaged tabs can be damaged.

verification.title: Cushion retention and belt routing
verification.body: Confirm that the cushion is secured at its floor locking points, the belt webbing is untwisted, and the belts and buckles remain accessible above the installed cushion.

procedures.purpose: Complete rear seat cushion removal and installation, including floor-tab release and seatbelt positioning.

guides.title: Replace the rear brake pads with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Remove the retained rear pads, retract the caliper pistons, and install the pads with the specified hardware and lubrication.
guides.introduction: The rear brake pads provide the friction surfaces that act against the brake disc. On the SVT Performance Package arrangement covered here, pins and a spring retain the pads in the caliper. The job involves removing those retainers, retracting the pistons with a suitable tool, and preparing the pad contact surfaces before reassembly. These instructions apply to the package-specific rear brakes on the 5.2L application.
guides.why: Piston retraction creates clearance for pad removal and installation. Clean pad-to-caliper contact surfaces and correctly applied kit lubricant matter because the pads must sit and move as intended. Depressing the brake pedal after assembly brings the pistons and pads back into their working relationship; the reservoir level must then be checked.
searchTerms: SVT Performance Package rear brake pads

when.summary: When the SVT Performance Package rear pads require replacement or removal for related work.
notes: This removal and installation procedure does not establish a pad wear limit or diagnose a braking complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange wheel access
prepare.detail: Have suitable vehicle lifting and support capability and follow the linked Wheel and Tire procedure for wheel removal and refitting.

prepare.title: Prepare the retraction tool and pad kit
prepare.detail: Have a brake caliper piston retractor or brake pad spreader suitable for the operation shown. When fitting new pads, retain all new hardware, lubricant, and application instructions supplied with the kit.

prepare.title: Identify the correct brake fluid
prepare.detail: Use the linked Brake System Specifications to select fluid if topping up is necessary. Do not choose a fluid specification from another vehicle system.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and tire
steps.body: Follow the Wheel and Tire removal procedure to expose the rear caliper and its pad retainers.

steps.title: Release the pad retainers
steps.body: Remove the brake pad pins, followed by the brake pad spring. These parts must be released before the pads can be removed.

steps.title: Retract the pistons and remove the pads
steps.body: Use the brake caliper piston retractor or pad spreader to compress the caliper pistons, then remove the brake pads. Follow the illustrated tool placement in the pad procedure.

steps.title: Prepare the contact surfaces
steps.body: Clean the pad-to-caliper contact surfaces. For new pads, apply the lubricant supplied with the kit according to its instruction sheet and use all supplied new hardware.

steps.title: Reassemble the brakes
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to install the pads, spring, and retaining pins, then refit the wheel and tire using its linked procedure.

steps.title: Apply the pedal and check fluid
steps.body: Depress the brake pedal after assembly. Check the brake fluid reservoir level and top up as necessary using the fluid identified in Brake System Specifications.

watchFor.title: Unspecified lubricant placement
watchFor.body: Use the pad kit’s application instructions; the requirement to lubricate contact surfaces is not permission to coat the friction faces.

watchFor.title: Old hardware carried into a new-pad installation
watchFor.body: New pads must be installed with all new hardware supplied in their kit.

verification.title: Complete the installation checks
verification.body: Confirm the pads, spring, pins, and wheel have been reinstalled and that the brake pedal has been depressed after assembly.

verification.title: Record the fluid-level result
verification.body: Record the reservoir level after pedal application and any top-up performed with the specified brake fluid.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the rear brake pads for the 5.2L SVT Performance Package, including piston retraction and pad-kit requirements.
Remove and reinstall the wheel and tire for brake access.
Identify the specified brake fluid for the final reservoir-level correction.

guides.title: Section-repair the rear outer wheelhouse
guides.summary: Replace a damaged section of rear outer wheelhouse sheet metal, then restore its welded seams, sealing, and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The rear outer wheelhouse is the sheet metal surrounding the rear wheel opening behind the quarter panel. This repair removes the damaged portion and joins a matching section cut from a replacement panel. Access requires the quarter panel procedure appropriate to the body style. Successful work includes restoring body dimensions where necessary, joining the replacement section, and rebuilding the protective finish around the repair.
guides.why: A replacement section must fit a correctly shaped body. Cutting before necessary dimensional restoration can make the new piece fit distorted surrounding metal. The illustrated cutline is only a general guide: damage extent determines the repair boundary. Welding also disturbs protective coatings, so sealing and refinishing are essential parts of completing the repair.
searchTerms: rear wheel arch sheet metal replacement

when.summary: When rear outer wheelhouse damage requires removal and replacement of a sheet-metal section.
notes: The illustration shows the left side of a coupe; the right side and convertible use similar repair principles.
Use the quarter panel removal and installation procedure for the actual body style.

prepare.title: Arrange body-repair capability
prepare.detail: This work requires dimensional assessment and correction where needed, controlled panel sectioning, welding, metal finishing, and corrosion-protection restoration.

prepare.title: Gather the specified equipment
prepare.detail: Provide an air body saw, locking pliers, resistance spotwelding equipment, and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment.

prepare.title: Prepare access and finishing materials
prepare.detail: Have the replacement panel, a seam sealer listed in the wheelhouse procedure, and a Ford-approved paint system. Plan to move the carpet and wiring harness away from the work.

steps.title: Restore dimensions if required
steps.body: Assess the body against the applicable Body and Frame information. Where accident damage has changed its shape, restore the vehicle to its pre-accident dimensions before proceeding.

steps.title: Expose the wheelhouse
steps.body: Remove the quarter panel using either the coupe or convertible procedure. Reposition the carpeting and wiring harness away from the working area before cutting or welding.

steps.title: Mark and remove the damaged section
steps.body: Choose and mark the cutline according to the extent of the damage. Use the illustration as a general guide, then cut out the damaged wheelhouse portion with the air body saw.

steps.title: Prepare and weld the replacement
steps.body: Cut the required section from the replacement panel. Position it with locking pliers and install it using resistance spotwelding as directed in the wheelhouse procedure. Weld the panel seams using MIG/MAG equipment.

steps.title: Finish the repaired metal
steps.body: Metal-finish the repaired area as required using normal body-repair techniques. This prepares the joined sheet metal for the subsequent sealing and finishing work.

steps.title: Restore sealing and corrosion protection
steps.body: Seal all areas to production level with a listed seam sealer. Refinish with a Ford-approved paint system and follow the linked Corrosion Prevention procedure.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding components
steps.body: Return the carpet and wiring harness to position. Install the quarter panel using the correct body-style procedure to complete the access work.

watchFor.title: Treating the drawing as a fixed cut boundary
watchFor.body: The cutline must suit the damage; copying the illustrated line without assessing the panel can leave unsuitable metal in the repair.

watchFor.title: An unfinished protective repair
watchFor.body: Weld completion alone does not finish this job. All repair areas require production-level sealing and the specified refinishing and corrosion-protection work.

notes: The body uses several steel types. General body construction information does not identify the wheelhouse material or supply substitute welding instructions.

diagnostics.finding: The vehicle requires dimensional restoration after the accident.
diagnostics.meaning: The surrounding body geometry must be corrected before fitting the replacement wheelhouse section.
diagnostics.next: Use Body and Frame information to guide restoration before panel sectioning.

verification.title: Check repair completion
verification.body: Confirm the replacement section is welded and metal-finished, all repair areas are sealed and refinished, and the carpet, harness, and correct quarter panel are reinstalled.

verification.title: Record dimensional work where required
verification.body: Where dimensional restoration was necessary, record the applicable body measurements used to establish the restored condition.

procedures.purpose: Section, replace, weld, seal, and refinish the rear outer wheelhouse.
Provide body construction and dimensional information for required pre-accident geometry restoration.
Remove and install the coupe quarter panel for wheelhouse access.
Remove and install the convertible quarter panel for wheelhouse access.
Restore corrosion protection following sheet-metal repair and refinishing.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger coolant supply tube
guides.summary: Renew the turbocharger coolant supply tube and its seal while preserving clean sealing surfaces and restoring the cooling and exhaust connections.
guides.introduction: The turbocharger uses exhaust energy to compress incoming air. Engine coolant circulates through its center housing, helping manage heat between the hot turbine and the compressor. The supply tube carries coolant into that housing. Replacement involves draining the cooling system, opening the nearby exhaust connections, removing the paired coolant tubes, and separating the supply tube from the return tube.
guides.why: Reliable sealing depends on clean, undamaged ports and correctly aligned tube brackets. Old O-ring residue, scratches, or a bent retaining bracket can cause repeat leaks. Any opened intake ports also need protection: even small debris can damage the compressor vanes. Initial finger-tight assembly allows the tube connections to be positioned before final tightening.

when.summary: When inspection establishes that the 2.3L turbocharger coolant supply tube requires replacement.
notes: Coolant near the turbocharger does not by itself distinguish a tube fault from a seal or sealing-surface problem.

prepare.title: Arrange cooling-system service
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment required by the linked 2.3L draining, vacuum filling, and bleeding procedure. Complete its draining phase before disconnecting the tubes.

prepare.title: Gather replacement parts and cleaning materials
prepare.detail: Provide a new supply tube, coolant-tube O-ring seal, and turbocharger flange gasket. Have a hose clamp remover/installer, nylon brush, specified Motorcraft brake cleaner, and clean specified engine coolant.

prepare.title: Protect openings and sealing areas
prepare.detail: Keep debris out of the turbocharger and intake system, covering any opened intake ports. Preserve the sealing surfaces of coolant and oil connections throughout the work.

steps.title: Drain the cooling system
steps.body: Follow the 2.3L Engine Cooling System Draining, Vacuum Filling and Bleeding procedure before opening the coolant connections.

steps.title: Release the exhaust-side access
steps.body: Disconnect the heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) electrical connector. Remove the catalytic converter flange nuts and bracket bolts, then remove and discard the turbocharger flange gasket. Remove the turbocharger exhaust studs only if needed.

steps.title: Remove and separate the coolant tubes
steps.body: Remove the coolant-tube bolts and disconnect the hose using the clamp tool, then remove the tubes. Remove their clamp bolt and clamp. Separate the supply tube from the return tube and discard the supply tube.

steps.title: Inspect and clean the sealing components
steps.body: Check the tube and sealing surfaces, including whether the retaining bracket is bent or out of square with the O-ring area. Remove and discard the coolant-tube O-ring. Clean with the specified brake cleaner and a nylon brush; never use a metal brush.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement assembly
steps.body: Install the new O-ring and lubricate it with clean engine coolant. Assemble the supply and return tubes, fitting their clamp and clamp bolt finger tight. Lubricate the tube O-ring seals. Remove old O-ring residue from the turbocharger bore with a nylon brush, rinse with brake cleaner, and inspect for deep scratches or gouges.

steps.title: Seat and secure the tubes
steps.body: Keep the coolant-tube bolts finger tight during positioning. Fit the O-ring ends to the turbocharger with the lower coolant inlet tube entering first, then connect the hose end to the water outlet adapter. Tighten the tube bolts in the procedure’s stated sequence, followed by the clamp bolt. The tube bolts have different tightening specifications.

steps.title: Restore the exhaust connections
steps.body: If removed, reinstall and tighten the exhaust studs. Fit a new turbocharger flange gasket, then install and tighten the catalytic converter flange nuts and bracket bolts to their respective specifications. Reconnect the HO2S connector.

steps.title: Refill and bleed
steps.body: Complete the linked cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure. The tube procedure specifies Motorcraft Orange Concentrated Antifreeze/Coolant; follow the cooling procedure for its preparation and filling method.

watchFor.title: Abrasive cleaning damage
watchFor.body: A metal brush can damage the sealing area and create leaks. Use nylon and the specified cleaner.

watchFor.title: Premature tightening
watchFor.body: Preserve the finger-tight assembly stages and lower-inlet-first insertion sequence rather than tightening each connection as soon as it is encountered.

diagnostics.finding: A retaining bracket is bent, or a sealing area has deep scratches, gouges, or remaining O-ring residue.
diagnostics.meaning: The connection may not align or seal reliably.
diagnostics.next: Remove residue as specified and resolve damaged or misaligned components before reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm the required renewals and reconnections
verification.body: Confirm the new supply tube, O-ring, and flange gasket are installed, the hose and fasteners are secured, and the HO2S connector is reconnected.

verification.title: Record inspection and cooling completion
verification.body: Record the sealing-surface and bracket inspection results and completion of the specified cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure.

procedures.purpose: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger coolant supply tube, including sealing preparation, assembly sequence, and individual fastener specifications.
Drain, vacuum fill, and bleed the 2.3L EcoBoost cooling system before and after tube replacement.

guides.title: Replace the right rear outer constant velocity joint boot
guides.summary: Renew the serviceable right-hand outer joint boot, distribute its grease, vent the boot during assembly, and secure it with new clamps.
guides.introduction: A constant velocity (CV) joint transmits drive through the halfshaft while accommodating changes in angle. Its flexible boot holds grease around the joint and helps keep contamination out. This repair restores that enclosure around the outer joint. Only the right-hand rear halfshaft outer boot is serviceable by this procedure, and the work includes removing and reinstalling the inner CV joint boot.
guides.why: The boot and its clamps work together to contain the joint’s lubricant. Removed clamps must be discarded and replaced. Grease must be distributed through both the boot and housing, and air must be allowed to escape while the housing is installed. Cleaning and inspecting the cage before closure helps establish whether the joint is suitable for reassembly.
searchTerms: right rear outer CV joint boot

when.summary: When the right-hand rear outer CV joint boot needs replacement and the joint is suitable for reassembly.
notes: Do not apply this outer-boot service procedure to the left-hand halfshaft.
Allow for the linked inner-boot procedure at both the beginning and end of the job.

prepare.title: Plan the complete access sequence
prepare.detail: Be equipped and capable of carrying out the Inner Constant Velocity Joint Boot removal and installation procedure, including its prerequisites. That work is required to complete this outer-boot repair.

prepare.title: Prepare the assembly tools and materials
prepare.detail: Have a small flat-blade screwdriver, boot clamp pliers, the replacement boot, new boot clamps, and the grease sachet used for the joint assembly.

prepare.title: Provide a clean working area
prepare.detail: The joint cage must be cleaned and inspected before fresh grease and the boot enclose it. Keep the prepared parts and grease free of contamination.

steps.title: Remove the inner joint boot
steps.body: Complete the removal phase of the linked inner CV joint boot procedure first. Preserve its sequence and requirements rather than starting with the outer boot in isolation.

steps.title: Remove the outer boot and discard its clamps
steps.body: Remove and discard the outer CV joint boot clamps, then remove the boot. The illustration identifies both clamps as discarded parts.

steps.title: Inspect the cage and distribute the grease
steps.body: Clean and inspect the CV joint cage before assembly. Distribute the grease sachet evenly between the CV joint boot and housing so lubricant is placed in both parts of the enclosure.

steps.title: Install the housing while venting the boot
steps.body: Install the CV joint housing with a small flat-blade screwdriver inserted beneath the boot seat to let air escape. Use the screwdriver for this specified venting action while the housing is being fitted.

steps.title: Clamp the boot and restore the inner end
steps.body: Use boot clamp pliers to install new outer-boot clamps. Then complete the installation phase of the linked inner CV joint boot procedure.

watchFor.title: Air trapped during housing installation
watchFor.body: Retain the specified venting step before securing the boot with its new clamps.

watchFor.title: An unsuitable joint hidden by a new boot
watchFor.body: Complete the cage inspection before closing the assembly; replacing the enclosure does not establish that the joint itself is serviceable.

diagnostics.finding: Cleaning reveals a concern with the CV joint cage.
diagnostics.meaning: The joint’s condition needs resolution before boot installation can be considered a complete repair.
diagnostics.next: Assess the joint before reassembly; this boot procedure does not provide cage wear limits.

verification.title: Confirm the assembly sequence
verification.body: Confirm grease was distributed in the boot and housing, air was vented during housing installation, new clamps were installed with boot clamp pliers, and inner-boot installation is complete.

verification.title: Record the cage inspection
verification.body: Record the cage’s inspected condition before the boot is closed around the joint.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the serviceable right-hand rear outer CV joint boot, including grease distribution, venting, and new clamps.
Carry out the required inner CV joint boot removal before outer-boot work and its installation afterward.

guides.title: Remove and refit the convertible A-pillar trim panel
guides.summary: Remove the sun visor, release the pillar trim in stages, and reconnect any fitted visor and speaker wiring during refitting.
guides.introduction: The A-pillar borders the windshield, and its interior trim covers the body member beside the front occupants. On this convertible arrangement, removing the sun visor is the first access step. The panel then releases from retainers and clips. A fitted pillar speaker and an electrically connected sun visor introduce separate connectors that must be dealt with during removal and installation.
guides.why: The removal sequence creates access while allowing any attached wiring to be disconnected before the component is carried away. The panel’s retainers are released before the optional speaker connector, followed by the remaining clips. Recognizing these stages helps prevent pulling on a panel that is still mechanically attached or tethered by wiring.
searchTerms: sun visor removal for pillar trim

when.summary: When the convertible A-pillar trim needs replacement or removal for access behind it.
notes: The illustrated arrangement is left-hand drive with the right-side panel shown; right-hand drive and the opposite side are similar.
Visor and speaker electrical disconnections apply only where those connections are fitted.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted connections
prepare.detail: Check whether the sun visor has an electrical connection and whether the pillar panel carries a speaker. Plan to support each component while disconnecting its wiring.

prepare.title: Understand the attachment sequence
prepare.detail: Use the procedure and illustration to identify the visor cap and clip, followed by the pillar retainers and remaining clips. The speaker connection is released between the panel’s two mechanical release stages.

steps.title: Remove the sun visor
steps.body: Remove the sun visor cap, release its clip, and remove the visor. If equipped, disconnect its electrical connector while keeping the visor supported.

steps.title: Release the pillar retainers
steps.body: Release the A-pillar panel retainers as shown. This is the initial panel-release stage; the remaining clips still need to be released before removal is complete.

steps.title: Disconnect the speaker and remove the panel
steps.body: If a speaker is fitted, disconnect its electrical connector. Then release the remaining clips and remove the A-pillar trim panel.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the panel clips, any speaker connection, and the retainers. Reconnect the visor wiring if fitted, reinstall the visor, and restore its clip and cap.

watchFor.title: A component still attached by wiring
watchFor.body: A released visor or panel may remain connected electrically. Disconnect the applicable connector before moving it away.

verification.title: Confirm attachments and connections
verification.body: Confirm the pillar panel’s retainers and clips are engaged, any speaker and visor connectors are reconnected, and the sun visor clip and cap are restored.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the convertible A-pillar trim, including sun visor access and equipment-dependent electrical connections.

guides.title: Replace individual solenoids in the 6R80 automatic transmission
guides.summary: Replace the required solenoid while preserving its factory calibration match, valve-body location and leadframe alignment.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 selects gears by directing transmission fluid to internal clutches. Electrical solenoids in its main control valve body regulate that flow, influencing engagement, shifting and torque converter clutch operation. This job replaces individual solenoids after the valve body has been removed. It requires careful identification because physically similar variable force solenoids can have different factory calibrations.
guides.why: The replacement solenoid must match both the original nozzle color and calibration band number. A mismatch can cause harsh or erratic shifts, abnormal engagement or transmission damage. Correct leadframe alignment also matters: its transmission range sensor pin must engage the manual control valve correctly.
searchTerms: solenoid nozzle color and band number

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that an individual 6R80 solenoid requires replacement.
notes: Shift quality complaints alone do not establish which solenoid, if any, needs replacement.

prepare.title: Plan the valve-body work
prepare.detail: This requires automatic-transmission valve-body handling capability. Follow the linked main control valve body procedure for vehicle access, removal and final installation.

prepare.title: Gather matching parts and assembly supplies
prepare.detail: Have a way to identify solenoids and ports, a suitable torque wrench, a new leadframe foam strip seal and Motorcraft MERCON LV fluid, XT-10-QLVC, meeting WSS-M2C938-A.

steps.title: Remove the valve body and separate the leadframe
steps.body: Remove the main control valve body using its complete procedure. Remove the long leadframe bolts and carefully separate the molded leadframe. If a foam strip seal is present, remove and discard it.

steps.title: Expose and identify the solenoids
steps.body: Remove the solenoid bracket bolts and bracket. Before removing multiple solenoids, number each solenoid and its corresponding valve-body port so their locations remain unambiguous.

steps.title: Select the correct replacement
steps.body: Identify whether the unit is normally high, normally low or ON/OFF. For every variable force solenoid, record its nozzle color and band number and obtain a replacement matching both. Pull the required solenoid from its port.

steps.title: Lubricate and install the solenoids
steps.body: Lubricate the solenoid O-rings with the specified transmission fluid, then position each solenoid in its identified port. Refit the bracket and tighten its bolts to 53 lb.in (6 Nm).

steps.title: Reassemble the leadframe
steps.body: Install a new foam strip seal even if none was originally fitted. Position the leadframe while aligning the transmission range sensor pin with the manual control valve. Tighten the long bolts in the illustrated sequence to 53 lb.in (6 Nm).

steps.title: Return the assembly to the transmission
steps.body: Install the main control valve body using the linked procedure and complete its installation requirements. Keep the solenoid identification record with the repair details.

watchFor.title: Color alone is insufficient
watchFor.body: The calibration band must also match. Similar appearance does not establish interchangeability.

watchFor.title: Leadframe positioning
watchFor.body: Confirm sensor-pin alignment before tightening; bolt installation does not establish that the pin is correctly engaged.

notes: Brown-nozzle, normally low units serve the forward clutch (shift solenoid A), intermediate clutch (shift solenoid C) and torque converter clutch. Black-nozzle, normally high units serve the direct clutch (shift solenoid B), line-pressure control and low/reverse/overdrive clutch (shift solenoid D). Shift solenoid E is normally off and operates ON/OFF.
Replacing a complete solenoid body requires its strategy to match the powertrain control module. That separate requirement should not be confused with matching an individual replacement solenoid.

diagnostics.finding: Replacement nozzle color or band number differs from the original.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement does not meet the required calibration match.
diagnostics.next: Obtain the matching solenoid before assembly.

verification.title: Assembly check
verification.body: Confirm the new foam seal, sensor-pin alignment, bracket tightening and sequenced leadframe tightening before completing valve-body installation.

verification.title: Recorded identification
verification.body: Record the original and replacement nozzle colors, band numbers and installed ports.

procedures.purpose: Individual 6R80 solenoid removal, identification and installation for the listed engines.
Required main control valve body removal and installation surrounding solenoid work.
6R80 hydraulic operation, calibration bands and complete solenoid-body strategy requirements.

guides.title: Remove and replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger
guides.summary: Replace the turbocharger with new specified oil components, seals and mounting hardware, then check lubrication and leaks.
guides.introduction: The turbocharger uses exhaust energy to compress the air entering the engine, allowing it to produce more power. Engine oil lubricates its bearings, while oil and coolant circulate through its center housing. Removing the turbocharger therefore involves its air connections, oil circuit, coolant connection and mounting hardware, with the air-conditioning compressor moved aside for access.
guides.why: Even tiny particles can damage the compressor vanes. Oil and coolant sealing ports must also be completely clean and undamaged: trapped seal residue or a tube tightened before it is seated can leave a leak. The specified discarded parts must be replaced during reassembly.

when.summary: When the turbocharger requires removal for an established repair or replacement.
notes: This procedure provides the replacement path; it does not establish the cause of a performance complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the specified lifting points, with the vehicle in NEUTRAL. Provide support for the displaced air-conditioning compressor. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare parts and clean handling
prepare.detail: Have port covers, a torque wrench, specified engine oil, new oil supply and drain tubes, a new turbocharger oil filter, gasket and mounting nuts. Replace mounting studs if removed. Arrange the belt and coolant-tube procedures before starting.

steps.title: Open the access path
steps.body: Raise the vehicle and remove the air-conditioning compressor belt. Disconnect the turbocharger bypass-valve connector and harness retainers, then loosen the outlet-pipe clamps and remove the pipe. Cover exposed air openings immediately.

steps.title: Move the compressor and disconnect the coolant supply
steps.body: Disconnect the compressor electrical connectors and harness retainers. Remove its bolts, then position and support it aside. Remove the turbocharger coolant supply tube using its dedicated procedure, then disconnect the turbocharger control hoses.

steps.title: Remove the oil connections and turbocharger
steps.body: Remove and discard the oil supply tube assembly, oil filter and oil drain tube. Discard the upper mounting nuts, remove the lower heat-shield bolt and remove the shield. Discard the lower mounting nuts, remove the turbocharger and discard its gasket. If studs need removal, discard those too.

steps.title: Install the turbocharger and heat shield
steps.body: Clean the mating faces and inspect the sealing ports and lines for damage or O-ring residue. Install new studs if removed, then the new gasket, turbocharger and new lower nuts. Fit the heat shield, new upper nuts and lower shield bolt finger tight; tighten the upper nuts before the lower shield bolt as directed.

steps.title: Rebuild the oil connections
steps.body: Lubricate the new drain-tube O-ring with clean specified engine oil and fully seat the tube before tightening its bolts. Install a new oil filter. Lubricate the supply-tube O-ring, fully seat the new supply assembly and initially fit its retaining bolts finger tight. Follow the illustrated procedure for their different tightening values.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding components
steps.body: Reconnect the control hoses and install the coolant supply tube through its linked procedure. Refit the compressor, its electrical connectors and harness retainers. Install and clamp the outlet pipe, reconnect the bypass valve and retainers, and install the compressor belt.

steps.title: Check oil and complete the running checks
steps.body: Check and top off engine oil to the engine specification. Start the engine and inspect for leaks. If a new turbocharger was installed, road test the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Contamination at open connections
watchFor.body: Inspect and clean components before reassembly; compressor protection depends on keeping foreign material out throughout the job.

watchFor.title: Unseated oil tubes
watchFor.body: Both oil tubes must be fully seated before fastener rundown. The fasteners must not substitute for correct seating.

notes: Use the 2.3L engine oil specification and the individual fastening values in the linked procedure.

verification.title: Leak and fluid check
verification.body: Confirm the engine oil check is complete and inspect the installed connections with the engine running.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record the leak-check result and, when a new turbocharger was fitted, the required road-test result.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger removal, mandatory replacement parts, installation and final checks.
Correct vehicle lifting points and support precautions.
2.3L air-conditioning compressor belt removal and installation for access.
2.3L turbocharger coolant supply tube removal and installation.
2.3L engine oil specification for seal lubrication and oil-level restoration.

guides.title: Inspect the dual-mass flywheel on 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Assess surface condition, bearing condition and flywheel movement using the correct engine-specific acceptance limits.
guides.introduction: A dual-mass flywheel has a primary mass attached to the crankshaft and a secondary mass carrying the clutch contact surface. Internal springs allow controlled movement between them to cushion changes in transmitted torque. Some movement and heat marking are normal. This inspection separates acceptable wear from damage requiring replacement, using visual checks, rotational tests and a supported bench measurement.
guides.why: Cleaning methods, applied force and measurement location affect this inspection. The 5.2L uses different rotational and axial criteria from the 2.3L and 3.7L. These flywheels cannot be machined, so an unacceptable result requires replacement rather than resurfacing.

when.summary: When an exposed dual-mass flywheel needs a reuse-or-replace decision during repair.
notes: Select the inspection procedure by engine before measuring or tightening anything.

prepare.title: Arrange access and measurement capability
prepare.detail: The inspection begins with the flywheel exposed and includes removal for bench testing. Have flywheel holding tool 303-103, dial-indicator holding fixture 100-002, a suitable long screwdriver or bar, stable support blocks and torque-controlled installation capability.

prepare.title: Prepare for the engine-specific test
prepare.detail: The 5.2L requires controlled application of the specified load. Obtain new flywheel bolts for every variant. Use a dry cloth only: no cleaning fluid, compressed air or cleaning between the masses.

steps.title: Inspect the clutch face and applicable pilot bearing
steps.body: Clean only the bolt connection and clutch surfaces. Replace a flywheel with large cracks or clutch scoring; minor heat cracks, discoloration and the minor heat scoring described in the procedure are acceptable. On the 2.3L and 5.2L, also inspect the pilot bearing for excessive wear, heat damage and smooth operation. An unacceptable bearing requires a new flywheel.

steps.title: Check the internal support components
steps.body: Inspect the hub bushing for wear on all variants. On the 2.3L and 3.7L, inspect the plastic friction control plate between the masses for damage or melting. Replace as required; a damaged friction control plate prevents a valid rotational-freeplay inspection.

steps.title: Measure rotational freeplay with light pressure
steps.body: Turn the secondary mass counterclockwise and mark both masses. Turn it clockwise using light hand pressure to the end of freeplay, then mark the primary mass opposite the secondary mark. Measure between the primary marks. Replace above 14 degrees (6.5 ring gear teeth) for the 2.3L or 3.7L, or above 16 degrees (7 ring gear teeth) for the 5.2L.

steps.title: Test spring engagement in both directions
steps.body: Install the flywheel holding tool. Using the suitable bar or screwdriver, firmly rotate the secondary mass clockwise and then counterclockwise. Beyond freeplay, the internal springs should engage with increasing resistance. If the secondary mass does not rotate, replace the flywheel.

steps.title: Remove and support the flywheel
steps.body: Remove the flywheel and discard its bolts. Inspect its crankshaft mounting flange for rust or residual thread locking compound and clean as necessary. Place the flywheel on blocks on a firm, level surface so it is stable and level, then remove the holding tool.

steps.title: Measure axial movement on the 2.3L or 3.7L
steps.body: Place the dial indicator on the outer upper surface of the secondary mass. Press lightly downward at the opposite point and record deflection. Repeat at 45 degree intervals. Replace if any reading exceeds 1.1 mm (0.043 in).

steps.title: Use the alternative axial test on the 5.2L
steps.body: Position the indicator on the clutch mounting surface 130 mm (5.12 in) from center. Apply 50 N (11.24 lb) at the opposite point on the secondary mass and zero the indicator. Move that load to the opposite side. Replace if peak-to-peak displacement exceeds 2.8 mm (0.11 in).

steps.title: Inspect the engine and transmission mounting features
steps.body: On the 5.2L, remove the crankshaft position sensor ring first. Check engine dowel installation and condition, the rear spacer plate for damage or warping, the crankshaft flange for rust or compound, and transmission dowel holes for damage or elongation. Renew damaged dowels or the spacer plate as necessary and clean the flange. Reinstall the sensor ring on the 5.2L.

steps.title: Refit using the correct bolt procedure
steps.body: Fit the serviceable or replacement flywheel with new bolts finger tight and install the holding tool. Follow the engine-specific illustrated tightening order: the 2.3L and 5.2L have different staged torque schedules, while the 3.7L has a single specified torque. Remove the holding tool afterward.

watchFor.title: Mixing measurement methods
watchFor.body: The light-pressure axial test and the 5.2L loaded peak-to-peak test have different limits and cannot be substituted for each other.

watchFor.title: Unnecessary replacement or resurfacing
watchFor.body: Minor acceptable heat marks alone do not justify replacement. Machining is prohibited on all three variants.

notes: Use the 2.3L inspection article for its own measurements and reinstallation details; the linked 3.7L flywheel removal procedure applies only to the 3.7L.

diagnostics.finding: Rotational or axial movement exceeds the applicable limit.
diagnostics.meaning: The flywheel fails its engine-specific movement criterion.
diagnostics.next: Install a new dual-mass flywheel.

diagnostics.finding: Only minor acceptable heat cracks or discoloration are present.
diagnostics.meaning: These marks alone do not impair flywheel function.
diagnostics.next: Continue the remaining checks before deciding on reuse.

verification.title: Record the inspection decision
verification.body: Record engine variant, surface and bearing findings, rotational freeplay and axial readings, then state the reuse-or-replace decision.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Verify new bolts, completion of the correct tightening sequence, removal of the holding tool and, on the 5.2L, restoration of the sensor ring.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost flywheel inspection, pilot-bearing checks, movement limits and staged reinstallation.
3.7L Duratec flywheel inspection, movement limits and single-torque reinstallation.
5.2L flywheel inspection, loaded axial measurement, sensor-ring handling and staged reinstallation.
3.7L flywheel removal and installation when replacement is required.
5.2L flywheel removal and installation when replacement is required.

guides.title: Remove and refit the instrument panel center finish panel
guides.summary: Release the right-hand trim and center fascia clips, disconnect the optional panel module and refit both panels in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel center finish panel is the visible fascia across the center and passenger side of the dashboard. Retaining clips secure it to the instrument panel. Some versions also carry an electrical module, so the panel may remain connected to wiring after its clips have released. This job removes the fascia for replacement or access and returns it to its fitted position.
guides.why: The right-hand trim panel comes off first to establish the removal sequence. Using an interior trim remover helps release the retaining clips without concentrating force on the decorative face. Supporting the center panel while releasing any electrical connection prevents its weight from pulling on the wiring.
searchTerms: instrument panel center finish panel removal

when.summary: When the center finish panel needs replacement or removal to reach components behind it.

prepare.title: Use the specified trim tool
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and identify the right-hand trim panel and center finish panel in the complete procedure.

prepare.title: Allow for an electrical connection
prepare.detail: Be ready to support the released fascia while checking whether the optional panel-mounted module is fitted.

steps.title: Remove the right-hand trim panel
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release its clips, then remove the panel. Complete this first operation before attempting to withdraw the larger center fascia.

steps.title: Release the center fascia
steps.body: Use the trim remover to release the center finish panel clips shown in the illustration. Support the panel as it separates, keeping its movement controlled while checking behind it.

steps.title: Disconnect the optional module
steps.body: If the panel-mounted module is fitted, disconnect its electrical connector before carrying the fascia away. A panel without that module has no corresponding connector-disconnection step.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Reconnect the optional module if fitted, position the center fascia and engage its retaining clips. Reinstall the right-hand trim panel after the center panel is back in place.

watchFor.title: Panel remains tethered
watchFor.body: Released clips do not mean the optional electrical connector has been disconnected.

watchFor.title: Localized resistance
watchFor.body: Check for a clip that remains engaged before continuing to pull the fascia.

notes: The illustration shows the optional module; its presence is not required for this procedure.

verification.title: Confirm restored fit
verification.body: Check that both panels are retained by their clips and that any connector disconnected during removal has been restored.

procedures.purpose: Center finish panel removal and installation, including initial right-hand trim removal and the optional electrical connection.

guides.title: Replace the driver-side dashboard air register
guides.summary: Remove the surrounding dashboard trim in sequence, release the driver-side register and restore the panels and electrical connections.
guides.introduction: The driver-side register is the dashboard outlet through which conditioned air reaches the driver. The climate-control system determines air temperature, distribution and blower operation; the register provides the final outlet into the cabin. Replacing it involves several surrounding trim panels because its retaining clips are reached after the instrument-cluster trim is removed.
guides.why: This is a layered trim-removal job. Some panels use bolts as well as clips, and the lighting-switch and left-hand finish panels have electrical connections to release. Following the sequence keeps attached wiring and the steering-column gap hider from being pulled as the panels are separated.

when.summary: When the driver-side register requires replacement or removal during dashboard repair.
notes: A broader heating or cooling complaint needs climate-system diagnosis before selecting a register repair.

prepare.title: Prepare trim and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover and tools for the illustrated bolts. Have a torque tool suitable for the specified 27 lb.in (3 Nm) trim-fastener tightening.

prepare.title: Plan the center-panel prerequisite
prepare.detail: Begin with the linked instrument panel center finish panel procedure. Be ready to support removed panels while releasing their electrical connectors.

steps.title: Remove the center finish panel
steps.body: Complete the linked center finish panel removal procedure before working through the driver-side trim. Follow its fitted-equipment instructions for any panel electrical connection.

steps.title: Release the left-hand instrument panel trim
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release the clips and remove the left-hand trim panel. This is the next access layer in the specified sequence.

steps.title: Remove the lighting-switch trim
steps.body: Remove its bolt, release its clips and separate the panel. Disconnect the electrical connector before removing the panel fully. Keep track of this fastener for the specified installation torque.

steps.title: Remove the left-hand finish panel
steps.body: Remove its bolts and release its clips with the trim remover. Disconnect its electrical connector, then remove the finish panel so the remaining lower and cluster trim can be reached.

steps.title: Clear the lower cover and cluster trim
steps.body: Release the lower instrument panel cover clips and position the cover aside. Remove the instrument panel cluster trim bolts and release its clips. Detach the gap hider from the upper steering-column trim cover as the cluster trim is removed.

steps.title: Separate the register assembly
steps.body: Release the register's retaining clips and remove the driver-side register assembly. The illustration identifies the clips holding the register to its surrounding trim; release these before separating the parts.

steps.title: Reassemble the dashboard
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, starting with the register. Restore the cluster trim and gap hider, lower cover, left-hand finish panel, lighting-switch trim and remaining panels. Reconnect the disconnected electrical connectors. Tighten the cluster-trim, left-hand finish-panel and lighting-switch trim bolts to 27 lb.in (3 Nm). Finish by reinstalling the center finish panel through its linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Bolts still holding a panel
watchFor.body: The lighting-switch, left-hand finish and cluster trim panels have bolts in addition to clips; release both forms of attachment.

watchFor.title: Gap hider still attached
watchFor.body: Detach it from the upper steering-column cover before taking the cluster trim away, and restore it during installation.

notes: The lower instrument panel cover is positioned aside during access; the procedure does not call for its complete removal.
The register removal procedure is not restricted to either manual or dual automatic temperature control.

verification.title: Confirm the completed trim assembly
verification.body: Check register and panel clip engagement, restoration of the gap hider and electrical connectors, and tightening of the specified trim bolts.

procedures.purpose: Driver-side register removal and installation through the left-hand dashboard and cluster trim.
Required center finish panel removal before register access and reinstallation afterward.

guides.title: Replace an outer tie rod end
guides.summary: Replace the outer tie rod end with a proper separator, renew its retaining nut and check front toe after reassembly.
guides.introduction: The outer tie rod end connects the steering linkage to the wheel spindle. It carries the steering rack’s push and pull to the wheel while its joint accommodates movement. Although this vehicle uses electric power-assisted steering, this connection remains mechanical. The outer end is separately serviceable, so replacing it does not require replacing the complete steering gear.
guides.why: Disconnecting the battery protects the steering gear during linkage work. A separator releases the joint without hammering the spindle, and recording the removal turns preserves a useful installation reference. That reference does not establish correct wheel alignment: front toe still needs checking.
searchTerms: front toe after tie rod replacement

when.summary: When the outer tie rod end has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Heavy steering alone does not establish that the outer tie rod end is faulty.

prepare.title: Arrange separation and alignment equipment
prepare.detail: Have a tie rod end remover, suitable torque equipment, safe wheel-removal capability and access to front-toe measurement and adjustment.

prepare.title: Identify the fastening specification
prepare.detail: Obtain a new outer tie rod end nut. The stud-nut torque has separate SVT and non-SVT build-date branches; select the applicable branch before reassembly.

steps.title: Isolate the steering system and remove the wheel
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground cable using [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Then remove the wheel and tire using [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Battery disconnection is required whenever this steering linkage is serviced.

steps.title: Release the fasteners
steps.body: Follow the [tie rod end procedure](#/document/G1686682). Loosen the jam nut, which locks the threaded adjustment, then remove and discard the outer tie rod end nut.

steps.title: Separate the joint from the spindle
steps.body: Use the tie rod end remover to release the outer end from the wheel spindle. Position the tool carefully around the protective boot. Do not strike the spindle with a hammer.

steps.title: Record the threaded position
steps.body: Unscrew the outer tie rod end while counting and recording the turns required to remove it. Keep that record available for fitting the replacement.

steps.title: Install and secure the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, using the recorded turns as the installation reference. Reconnect the joint with a new retaining nut, applying the correct vehicle-specific torque, and tighten the jam nut to its specified torque.

steps.title: Restore access parts and check toe
steps.body: Refit the wheel and reconnect the battery through their procedures. Check front toe and adjust it if necessary using the Front Toe Adjustment procedure referenced from the tie rod article.

watchFor.title: Separator damage
watchFor.body: Poor tool placement can damage the outer joint’s boot. Hammering the spindle can damage the spindle itself.

watchFor.title: An apparently unchanged adjustment
watchFor.body: Matching the removal turns is only a starting reference; it does not replace the required toe measurement.

notes: Where selectable steering is fitted, battery disconnection returns its setting to Standard.

diagnostics.finding: Steering feels unusually heavy.
diagnostics.meaning: The electric assistance system can reduce or remove assistance in response to faults; heavy effort does not identify a failed outer joint.
diagnostics.next: Establish whether the concern involves the linkage or steering assistance before choosing this repair.

verification.title: Fasteners completed
verification.body: Confirm the discarded stud nut was replaced and both the stud nut and jam nut were tightened to their applicable specifications.

verification.title: Alignment result recorded
verification.body: Record the front-toe check and any adjustment made. Keep this result distinct from the recorded removal-turn count.

procedures.purpose: Outer tie rod end removal and installation, including fastener branches and the required front-toe follow-up.
Required battery ground disconnection and reconnection.
Wheel and tire removal and installation for access.

guides.title: Disconnect and reconnect a washer hose coupling
guides.summary: Separate and reconnect C-lock or pinch-type washer hose couplings while protecting their seals and locking features.
guides.introduction: Washer hoses carry fluid from the washer pump toward the windshield. Their couplings let a hose separate from a fitting for service while maintaining a sealed connection during use. This job covers two connector designs: a C-lock with a rotating lock ring and a pinch-type connector released at raised points.
guides.why: The lock holds the connection together; the O-ring seals the fluid passage. Both need care. Tools can damage either coupling design, and leaving a C-lock ring unlocked weakens it, potentially causing poor retention and a leak after assembly.

when.summary: When a washer hose connection must be separated for service or its coupling needs attention.
notes: Choose the branch matching the connector fitted to the hose.

prepare.title: Provide hand access
prepare.detail: Arrange enough access to support and release the connector by hand. Do not use hand tools to disconnect or connect either design.

prepare.title: Identify the locking feature
prepare.detail: Use the rotating-ring instructions for a C-lock and the raised squeeze-point instructions for a pinch-type coupling.

steps.title: C-lock: release without disturbing the seal
steps.body: Following [Washer Hose Coupling](#/document/G1694647), hold the female side at its hose connection to prevent internal rotation. Gently rotate the ring approximately 90 degrees, then slide the coupling off the fitting without losing its O-ring. Leave the ring attached and immediately return it to its original locked position.

steps.title: C-lock: reconnect with the ring locked
steps.body: Verify the ring is locked before inserting the male fitting. The ring flexes slightly to admit the fitting and snaps into engagement. Gently pull on the coupling to confirm that it is seated.

steps.title: Pinch type: release and inspect
steps.body: Squeeze the connector at its two raised points and gently pull the connection apart. Inspect the O-ring and replace it if necessary before reconnecting.

steps.title: Pinch type: engage and check retention
steps.body: Insert the male fitting until the connector locks with an audible click. Gently pull on the coupling to verify correct seating.

watchFor.title: C-lock ring left open
watchFor.body: The ring must return to its locked position while the connection is apart; reconnecting starts with the ring locked.

watchFor.title: A click without a retention check
watchFor.body: The audible snap or click does not replace the specified gentle pull check.

notes: The C-lock ring stays on the coupling throughout disconnection and reconnection.

diagnostics.finding: The pinch-type coupling’s O-ring needs replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing element requires attention before the connector is reassembled.
diagnostics.next: Replace the O-ring as necessary, reconnect and perform the retention check.

verification.title: Connection retained
verification.body: Confirm the applicable lock engages and the assembled coupling remains seated during a gentle pull.

verification.title: Seal and ring accounted for
verification.body: Confirm the C-lock O-ring was retained, or the pinch-type O-ring was inspected, and that the C-lock ring is locked.

procedures.purpose: Separate disconnection and reconnection methods for C-lock and pinch-type washer hose couplings.

guides.title: Replace a rear parking aid sensor and check its alignment
guides.summary: Remove the rear bumper cover to replace the selected parking aid sensor, then check horizontal and vertical detection alignment.
guides.introduction: Rear parking aid sensors use reflected ultrasonic sound to detect suitable objects behind the vehicle. With reverse selected, the parking aid module (PAM) calculates distance and requests warning tones through the rear speakers. Replacing a sensor involves the wiring and retaining clips behind the bumper cover, followed by checks that establish whether the sensors are correctly aligned.
guides.why: A sensor can be electrically connected yet aimed incorrectly. Its orientation affects what it detects, so secure clip engagement alone does not complete this job. Equally, a disabled system does not identify a particular sensor: sensor, network and module faults can all disable parking assistance.
searchTerms: rear parking sensors not detecting objects

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a rear parking aid sensor for replacement, or it must be removed during bumper work.
notes: Check installation, contamination and operating conditions before treating missed detections as proof of sensor failure.

prepare.title: Plan bumper-cover access
prepare.detail: Be prepared to remove and reinstall the rear bumper cover and release its harness guides, clips and retainers using the linked procedures.

prepare.title: Arrange alignment checks
prepare.detail: Have the Azimuth System Check and Elevation System Check available. Their specified setups are needed to complete the repair.

steps.title: Remove the rear bumper cover
steps.body: Use [Rear Bumper Cover](#/document/G1694215) to obtain access to the sensor mountings and wiring behind the cover.

steps.title: Clear the harness and reinforcement
steps.body: Following [Rear Parking Aid Sensor](#/document/G1693924), separate the wiring harness guides and move the harness aside. Remove the pin-type retainers, release the clips and remove the bumper-cover reinforcement.

steps.title: Release the selected sensor
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector belonging to the sensor being serviced. Release its retaining clips and remove the sensor from its mounting.

steps.title: Reassemble the bumper components
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to install the sensor, reconnect it, refit the reinforcement and return the harness to its guides. Reinstall the bumper cover through its procedure.

steps.title: Check both directions of alignment
steps.body: Perform the [Azimuth System Check](#/document/G1672936) for horizontal alignment and the [Elevation System Check](#/document/G1672937) for vertical alignment. Use their findings to establish whether the installation is satisfactory.

watchFor.title: Obscured or misaligned sensors
watchFor.body: Dirt, ice and incorrect installation can prevent detection. Heavy rain, snow and an object’s reflective properties also affect performance.

watchFor.title: Blocked detection area
watchFor.body: Add-on devices can intrude into the detection zone and cause false audible alerts.

notes: The system assists with detecting certain objects and may not detect moving objects.
The sensors share voltage and ground circuits, so system-wide symptoms do not automatically justify replacing every sensor.

diagnostics.finding: The message center reports parking aid disabled.
diagnostics.meaning: A sensor, communications-network or PAM fault can disable the system.
diagnostics.next: Identify the fault before selecting a sensor for replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Objects are missed or unexpected tones occur.
diagnostics.meaning: Alignment, contamination, weather, object characteristics or obstructions can affect detection.
diagnostics.next: Assess those conditions and complete the specified alignment checks after installation.

verification.title: Installation restored
verification.body: Confirm the sensor clips, connector, harness guides, reinforcement and bumper-cover attachments have been restored.

verification.title: Alignment results recorded
verification.body: Record the outcomes of both the azimuth and elevation checks, including any correction required.

procedures.purpose: Rear parking aid sensor removal and installation behind the bumper cover.
Rear bumper cover removal and installation for sensor access.
Required horizontal, or azimuth, parking aid alignment check.
Required vertical, or elevation, parking aid alignment check.

guides.title: Replace Gateway Module A and transfer its configuration
guides.summary: Capture the existing gateway configuration before removal, install the replacement and complete programmable module installation.
guides.introduction: Gateway Module A (GWM) translates and forwards messages between vehicle communications networks. Two networks reach the diagnostic scan tool through this gateway rather than connecting directly to it. The module therefore forms part of the diagnostic communication route as well as the vehicle’s shared-message system. Replacement includes transferring its configuration, not just exchanging the mounted unit.
guides.why: The configuration must be uploaded while the original module is still installed, then downloaded into the new module. Starting that process before disconnection preserves the required sequence. The mechanical work is brief, but installation remains incomplete until the scan-tool programming instructions have been followed.

when.summary: When Gateway Module A is to be replaced, with its configuration captured before removal.
notes: These replacement steps do not provide a test that condemns the gateway for a communication complaint.

prepare.title: Provide programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of performing programmable module installation (PMI) for the GWM, including configuration upload and download.

prepare.title: Arrange module access and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Identify the module, mounting nuts and electrical connector from the procedure illustration. Have suitable tools and torque equipment for the mounting nuts.

steps.title: Begin PMI with the original module installed
steps.body: Follow [Gateway Module A](#/document/G1693123) and the scan tool’s on-screen instructions to begin PMI. When installing a new module, upload the existing configuration before removing the original unit.

steps.title: Remove the gateway
steps.body: Remove the mounting nuts and withdraw the GWM, then disconnect its electrical connector. Keep this mechanical sequence after the required configuration capture.

steps.title: Connect and mount the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure to reconnect and position the replacement module. Tighten the mounting nuts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm).

steps.title: Complete the configuration transfer
steps.body: Use the diagnostic scan tool to complete GWM PMI, following the on-screen instructions. Download the captured configuration into the replacement module as part of this process.

watchFor.title: Premature disconnection
watchFor.body: Removing the original module before uploading its configuration interrupts the required replacement sequence.

watchFor.title: Incomplete scan-tool procedure
watchFor.body: A physically installed gateway is not a completed replacement. Resolve an interrupted or unavailable PMI process before treating the job as finished.

notes: The vehicle’s diagnostic connector is under the instrument panel; the linked illustration identifies the gateway mounting and connector arrangement.

verification.title: Mechanical installation completed
verification.body: Confirm the electrical connector is reconnected and the module is secured with its mounting nuts tightened to specification.

verification.title: Programming result recorded
verification.body: Record that the original configuration was uploaded and that the replacement module’s PMI process, including configuration download, was completed.

procedures.purpose: Gateway Module A removal and installation, including configuration capture before removal and PMI completion afterward.

guides.title: Replace the fuel pump driver module, including the 5.2L twin-module assembly
guides.summary: Access the fuel pump driver module beneath the rear seat and follow the engine-specific mounting procedure for a single module or the 5.2L pair.
guides.introduction: The fuel pump driver module (FPDM) is part of the pump’s electrical control system. It sits beneath the rear seat cushion on the left-hand side. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L procedures service a single mounted module. The 5.2L uses two modules on a bracket, adding an assembly-removal and bracket-disassembly phase.
guides.why: Engine identification matters because the bracket arrangement and tightening specifications differ. The seat cushion also needs deliberate release: pulling it up without pressing its locking tabs can damage them. Restoring the seat includes keeping the seatbelt webbing straight and the belts and buckles available to occupants.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies an FPDM for replacement or its assembly must be removed for service.
notes: Choose the engine-specific procedure before disconnecting or unfastening the module.

prepare.title: Select the correct installation branch
prepare.detail: Use the [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1673144), [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1691951), [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1692000) or [5.2L procedure](#/document/G1805342). The 5.2L bracket work is a separate branch.

prepare.title: Provide seat access and torque equipment
prepare.detail: Arrange access to the rear cushion’s front locking tabs and have suitable tools for the module retainers and their specified tightening torques.

steps.title: Release and remove the rear seat cushion
steps.body: Follow [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168). Move both front seats fully forward. Press in the locking tabs at the front of the rear cushion to release it from the floor, then lift, release and remove the cushion.

steps.title: Remove the single module on 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L
steps.body: For these engines, disconnect the FPDM electrical connector. Remove its retaining nuts and lift out the module. Continue with the single-module installation branch.

steps.title: Remove and separate the 5.2L assembly
steps.body: For the 5.2L, disconnect the FPDM electrical connectors and remove the assembly retainers. Swing the assembly out from beneath the trim panel and remove it. Then remove the module retainers and separate both FPDMs from their bracket.

steps.title: Install the correct module arrangement
steps.body: On 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines, install the FPDM and tighten its retaining nuts to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). On the 5.2L, install the modules onto their bracket and tighten those retainers to 71 lb.in (8 Nm); install the assembly and tighten its retainers to 71 lb.in (8 Nm).

steps.title: Reconnect the electrical connections
steps.body: After securing the module or assembly, reconnect the single FPDM connector on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, or the FPDM connectors on the 5.2L.

steps.title: Restore the rear seat
steps.body: Install the cushion by reversing its removal procedure. Make sure the seatbelt webbing is not twisted and that the seatbelts and buckles remain accessible to the occupants.

watchFor.title: Seat tabs resisting release
watchFor.body: Press the locking tabs inward before lifting the cushion; forcing it upward risks breaking the tabs.

watchFor.title: Torque transferred between layouts
watchFor.body: Use the specification for the actual engine and mounting location. The single-module specification differs from the 5.2L bracket and assembly specification.

notes: Removing both 5.2L modules from the bracket is part of the assembly procedure; it does not itself establish that both modules are faulty.

verification.title: Mounting branch completed
