verification.body: Record the engine branch used and confirm its mounting fasteners were tightened. On the 5.2L, check both the module-to-bracket and assembly-to-vehicle retainers.

verification.title: Connections restored
verification.body: Confirm the electrical connector or connectors have been reconnected before completing seat installation.

verification.title: Occupant access restored
verification.body: Confirm the cushion is reinstalled with untwisted webbing and accessible seatbelts and buckles.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost single FPDM removal and installation.
3.7L Duratec single FPDM removal and installation.
5.0L single FPDM removal and installation.
5.2L twin-FPDM assembly removal, separation from the bracket and installation.
Rear seat cushion access, locking-tab release and correct seatbelt positioning during installation.

guides.title: Replace an inner tie rod and reseal the steering rack
guides.summary: Replace the inner tie rod while protecting the steering rack, fitting a new steering stop and restoring the airtight bellows seal.
guides.introduction: The inner tie rod connects the steering rack to the outer tie rod end, transmitting rack movement to the wheel while allowing the linkage to articulate. It is separately serviceable on the electric power-assisted steering system. This repair also renews the steering stop and protective bellows boot; those parts are essential to a successful replacement.
guides.why: Loosening or tightening the joint without holding the rack can damage the steering gear. The bellows seal matters just as much: steering movement can draw water and dirt through a poorly sealed boot, and water damages both the gear and the inner joint's grease.

when.summary: When an inner tie rod has been identified for replacement.
notes: For right-hand inner tie rod work, the left-hand outer tie rod end and bellows boot must also be removed to reach the rack-holding location.

prepare.title: Arrange rack-holding capability
prepare.detail: Use rack holding tool 204-816, a suitable crow's-foot or open-end wrench, and boot clamp pliers. Plan for the two-person operation shown in the illustration and access to the fitted underbody shields.

prepare.title: Have the replacement sealing parts ready
prepare.detail: Provide a new inner tie rod, steering stop, bellows boot and inner and outer clamps. Use Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-E1, specification ESA-M1C75-B, at the specified boot mating surfaces.

steps.title: Remove the outer tie rod end
steps.body: Follow the [Tie Rod End procedure](#/document/G1686682). For right-hand work, also arrange the left-side access described above; the holding tool cannot be used on the right side of the gear.

steps.title: Open the underbody access
steps.body: Remove the shields applicable to the vehicle using the [inner tie rod procedure](#/document/G1686681). Where a V-brace is fitted, the brace and shield can come off together without separating them.

steps.title: Expose the joint and position the rack
steps.body: Remove and discard both bellows clamps. Move the boot aside far enough to reach the inner joint, move the steering stop aside, and position the rack completely to the left.

steps.title: Hold the rack and remove the tie rod
steps.body: Secure the rack with tool 204-816 before applying loosening force. Reverse the tool for right-hand tie rod removal. Remove and discard the inner tie rod, then remove and discard the steering stop.

steps.title: Install the joint and seat the new stop
steps.body: Position the new steering stop and install the new inner tie rod with the rack securely held, again reversing the tool for right-hand work. Tighten to the specified torque. Press the stop into place by hand until it clicks and cannot be separated by hand.

steps.title: Restore the airtight boot seal
steps.body: Apply the specified grease to the steering gear's boot mating surface and the boot groove on the tie rod. Seat the new boot over the housing bead and rod groove. Install the new inner clamp with boot clamp pliers, then install the new outer clamp.

steps.title: Reassemble the linkage and access parts
steps.body: Thread the jam nut onto the inner tie rod. Refit the applicable V-brace and shields, observing their specified fastener tightening. Reinstall the outer tie rod end through its separate procedure.

watchFor.title: An apparently secure but leaking boot
watchFor.body: Zip ties do not provide the required airtight seal. Keep water out of the joint grease and use the specified new clamps.

watchFor.title: A stop that needs force
watchFor.body: Do not strike the steering stop. Hand pressure, an audible click and resistance to hand removal are the specified seating criteria.

notes: The rack holding tool always acts on the left-hand side, including when servicing the right-hand tie rod.

verification.title: Confirm stop seating
verification.body: After assembly, turn the steering wheel lock-to-lock to ensure the steering stops are fully seated.

verification.title: Confirm boot positioning
verification.body: Check that the new boot is correctly seated over both the steering gear housing bead and the inner tie rod groove, with both new clamps installed.

procedures.purpose: Complete inner tie rod removal and installation, including rack holding, steering stop replacement, bellows sealing and fitted shield branches.
Outer tie rod end removal and installation required for access and final reassembly.

guides.title: Replace a rear wheel knuckle
guides.summary: Replace the rear wheel knuckle with new attachment fasteners, tighten the suspension at its loaded position and check rear toe.
guides.introduction: The rear wheel knuckle carries the wheel bearing and hub and connects them to the upper arm, lower arm and toe link. These connections locate the wheel while the independent rear suspension moves over the road. Replacing the knuckle requires separating those attachments, supporting the halfshaft and restoring the wheel's alignment afterward.
guides.why: Suspension fasteners carry loads that directly affect wheel control, so their quality and tightening matter. The bushing attachments must be tightened with the suspension loaded: tightening them while the suspension hangs can create incorrect clamp load and damage the bushings. A rear toe check confirms the wheel's direction after the connections have been disturbed.

when.summary: When an identified rear suspension repair requires wheel knuckle removal or replacement.
notes: Plan the job with the separate wheel bearing and hub, lower arm vertical link, and rear toe procedures available.

prepare.title: Provide controlled suspension support
prepare.detail: Arrange access and support that holds the suspension at curb height, plus separate support for the halfshaft. You must be able to maintain the loaded suspension position during bushing-fastener tightening.

prepare.title: Prepare new attachment hardware
prepare.detail: Have new knuckle-to-upper-arm and knuckle-to-toe-link bolts and nuts, and a new knuckle-to-lower-arm bolt. Use the same or equivalent quality and design, with torque equipment suitable for the specified values.

prepare.title: Arrange alignment capability
prepare.detail: Rear toe must be checked and adjusted if necessary after reassembly. Include that capability in the repair plan.

steps.title: Remove the hub and clear attached components
steps.body: Remove the [wheel bearing and hub](#/document/G1686657). Remove the wheel speed sensor bolt and position the sensor aside, then remove the parking brake cable bracket bolt and move the bracket aside.

steps.title: Support the suspension and halfshaft
steps.body: Support the suspension at curb height. Remove the [lower arm vertical link](#/document/G1686649), and support the halfshaft before releasing the knuckle attachments.

steps.title: Release the knuckle
steps.body: Following the [Wheel Knuckle procedure](#/document/G1686658), remove and discard the upper-arm bolt and nut, then the toe-link bolt and nut. Remove and discard the lower-arm bolt and remove the knuckle.

steps.title: Install and tighten the new attachments
steps.body: Position the knuckle and install the new lower-arm bolt, followed by the new toe-link bolt and nut and the new upper-arm bolt and nut. Tighten each to its own specification with the suspension loaded or the vehicle's weight on its wheels.

steps.title: Restore the sensor, cable bracket and hub
steps.body: Refit the parking brake cable bracket and wheel speed sensor, using their individual tightening specifications. Reinstall the lower arm vertical link, then the wheel bearing and hub through their linked procedures.

steps.title: Check rear toe
steps.body: Check rear toe and adjust it if necessary using the Rear Toe Adjustment procedure referenced by the knuckle article. Completing the mechanical assembly alone does not complete this repair.

watchFor.title: Fastener substitution or reuse
watchFor.body: The specified discarded knuckle attachment hardware must be replaced. Lesser-quality or substitute-design suspension fasteners are unsuitable.

watchFor.title: Tightening at full suspension droop
watchFor.body: Keep the required loaded position during bushing-fastener tightening to avoid incorrect clamp load and bushing damage.

notes: Keep the halfshaft supported while the knuckle is disconnected.

verification.title: Confirm the restored attachments
verification.body: Confirm that the specified new knuckle fasteners were used and tightened in the loaded position, and that the sensor and parking brake cable bracket are restored.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record the rear toe check and any adjustment made, using the applicable alignment specifications.

procedures.purpose: Rear wheel knuckle removal and installation, replacement fasteners, loaded-position tightening and final rear toe check.
Rear wheel bearing and hub removal before knuckle work and installation afterward.
Lower arm vertical link removal and installation during knuckle access.

guides.title: Find a parked battery drain on the 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Measure settled battery current without resetting the modules, then isolate an excessive draw to its circuit and underlying cause.
guides.introduction: The battery supplies the vehicle's electrical system even when the engine is stopped. Some modules continue drawing current normally; a drain check establishes whether consumption remains excessive after the vehicle has had time to sleep. It then separates a circuit problem, an awake module, an external input or an unfused load from a battery complaint.
guides.why: Interrupting battery continuity can reset the modules and erase the condition being investigated. Opening doors normally, keeping keys nearby or testing before shutdown has finished can also change the result. A thermal camera helps locate active circuits, but the in-line ammeter provides the current measurement needed to confirm the finding.
searchTerms: module will not go to sleep

when.summary: When the battery loses charge while parked and excessive key-off current is suspected.
notes: Charge and test the battery first using the referenced Battery Charging procedure. Do not begin while deep-sleep or battery-saver warnings are present.

prepare.title: Use suitable electrical test equipment
prepare.detail: Provide a meter that reads milliamps and has 10 amp capability, a 30A fused jumper, wiring diagrams and, preferably, a thermal camera. A test lamp or voltmeter is not an accurate substitute for the in-line ammeter.

prepare.title: Resolve equipment-dependent wake conditions
prepare.detail: If over-the-air updates are fitted and enabled, check the specified Over The Air Update Dashboard and let active updates finish. If an automatic-transmission gear-position display is fitted, verify Park indication and operation.

steps.title: Activate the systems and prepare the parked vehicle
steps.body: Drive for at least 5 minutes over 48 km/h (30 mph). Disable approach detection and the perimeter alarm if fitted, then park and switch off. Open the hood and doors and manually close their latch mechanisms with a suitable tool so access can remain open during testing.

steps.title: Make every test location accessible
steps.body: Use Wiring Diagrams Cell 13 to identify fuse boxes and arrange access without switching on lights. If auxiliary batteries are actually fitted, disconnect them through the referenced Battery Disconnect procedure so the primary-battery measurement includes all draws.

steps.title: Insert the meter without breaking continuity
steps.body: Connect the fused jumper between the negative battery cable and post, then disconnect the cable while preserving that bridge. Lock with the key fob and move all keys/fobs at least 50 feet away. Connect the meter between the negative cable terminal and post, then remove the jumper.

steps.title: Let the vehicle sleep and measure
steps.body: Wait at least 90 minutes, allowing for region and vehicle options. Note the current and compare with a similarly equipped vehicle. Use the thermal camera, if available, to inspect the fuse panel and battery junction box for a suspect heat signature.

steps.title: Identify the fused circuit
steps.body: For excessive current, remove main-box fuses one at a time and note the drop. When a fuse brings current to an acceptable level, reinstall it and allow another shutdown period of at least 90 minutes before continuing.

steps.title: Separate the circuit's loads
steps.body: Continue with subsystem fuses and component disconnections, leaving them disconnected until isolation is finished. If necessary, remove all relevant fuses and test each individually by installing, measuring and removing it. Isolate aftermarket electrical connections from factory wiring; disconnect suspected modules individually and check their hardwired and network inputs before condemning a module.

steps.title: Investigate feeds outside the fuse boxes
steps.body: If the draw remains unexplained, use the wiring diagrams to find battery feeds that bypass the fuse boxes and isolate them. Disconnect the generator electrical connections and retest if necessary; an internal generator short can cause a drain.

steps.title: Restore connections and initialization
steps.body: After testing, restore the disconnected circuits and battery connections. Perform Power Door Window Initialization if one-touch-up windows are fitted. Use the complete [Battery Drain Check](#/document/G1692357) for the isolation sequence and referenced supporting procedures.

watchFor.title: Resetting the test
watchFor.body: Refit the fused jumper before changing meter settings or lead sockets. If continuity is broken, repeat the shutdown waiting procedure.

watchFor.title: Mistaking an awake module for a failed module
watchFor.body: A module may be responding correctly to an incorrect input. Establish what keeps it awake before choosing a repair.

notes: Apply optional-equipment branches only to verified fitment. The shared power roller shutter initialization branch is outside this Mustang job.

diagnostics.finding: Settled current exceeds the applicable factory-equipment allowance in the 25–50 mA range.
diagnostics.meaning: The parked draw is excessive for the vehicle's equipment; continuous module consumption alone is not necessarily abnormal.
diagnostics.next: Isolate fuses and loads while preserving valid shutdown conditions.

diagnostics.finding: The drain is approximately 1 amp.
diagnostics.meaning: A continuously illuminated engine-compartment, glove-compartment or interior lamp is a typical possibility, not a confirmed diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Check those loads and confirm the responsible circuit by its measured current drop.

verification.title: Confirm an acceptable settled draw
verification.body: After correcting the cause, repeat the settled-current measurement under the same shutdown conditions.

verification.title: Record the electrical result
verification.body: Record the initial and final current, shutdown waiting period, isolating fuse or component, and any input found to be keeping a module awake.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L battery drain measurement, uninterrupted meter connection, sleep timing, fused and unfused circuit isolation, and applicable initialization.

guides.title: Replace the left exhaust manifold: 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Follow the engine-specific route to remove and reseal the left exhaust manifold, including engine support and steering-shaft work where required.
guides.introduction: The left-hand exhaust manifold collects exhaust from that cylinder bank and routes it toward the catalytic converter. Its joints must seal correctly after removal. Access differs substantially between these engines: the 5.0L manifold and catalytic converter are serviced as an assembly, while the 5.2L procedure removes the converter separately and also disconnects oil cooler hoses.
guides.why: The V8 procedures create clearance by supporting and raising the engine. Incorrect support can damage the body, while forcing the steering shaft or reusing its discarded bolt can compromise steering control. Correct engine identification also prevents mixing manifold hardware, tightening sequences and reassembly requirements.

when.summary: When an identified left-side exhaust repair requires manifold removal or replacement.
notes: Choose the complete procedure for the installed engine before starting; the three access routes are not interchangeable.

prepare.title: Provide safe lifting and engine support
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the designated lifting points identified by stamped triangles. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Check hoist adapters for interference with suspension, steering and exhaust parts.

prepare.title: Prepare the V8 support equipment
prepare.detail: Both V8 routes specify lifting bracket 303-050 and support bar 303-F072. The 5.0L also specifies 303-290B and adapters 303-290-01 and 303-290A-03A. Place support legs on the body structure, never the fenders.

prepare.title: Obtain the correct renewal parts
prepare.detail: Provide new manifold gaskets, studs and nuts. Also provide the branch-specific discarded parts: 3.7L converter flange nuts, steering-shaft bolts where removed, and 5.2L cross-brace nuts. The 5.2L materials include Motorcraft Silicone Gasket Remover ZC-30-A and Castrol EDGE Supercar 5W-50, specification WSS-M2C931-C.

steps.title: Identify the engine and establish access
steps.body: Position the vehicle in NEUTRAL on the hoist using the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Follow only the matching engine branch below. Both V8 branches require disconnecting the negative/ground and positive battery cables through [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356).

steps.title: 3.7L: remove the manifold
steps.body: Remove the [air cleaner](#/document/G1675694). Disconnect the left heated oxygen sensor and catalyst monitor sensor connectors. Remove and discard the converter flange nuts, remove the heat shield, then remove the manifold and discard its nuts, gasket and studs. Clean the converter mating surfaces and perform [manifold cleaning and inspection](#/document/G1661749).

steps.title: 3.7L: install and reseal
steps.body: Follow [G1681520](#/document/G1681520) to install new studs, gasket and manifold nuts, using its two-stage tightening. Refit the heat shield and converter with new flange nuts, reconnect both sensors and install the air cleaner. Start the engine and check the exhaust for leaks.

steps.title: 5.0L: prepare the engine-support installation
steps.body: For left-hand-drive, rear-wheel-drive vehicles, loosen the dash seal carefully, hand-start its nuts and position the steering straight ahead. Remove the intake outlet pipe and air cleaner, both engine-mount nuts, radiator sight shield and cross brace after moving the positive cable aside. Remove the battery tray, cowl grille, cowl extension and battery heat shield. Install the specified support arrangement and raise the engine 45 mm.

steps.title: 5.0L: clear the shaft and remove the assembly
steps.body: In the left-hand-drive, rear-wheel-drive branch, discard the lower steering-shaft bolt, separate the coupling without force and secure the shaft to the frame rail. Remove the muffler inlet pipe, move the air deflector aside and remove the engine-mount bracket. Disconnect both exhaust sensor connectors and release the harness retainers. Remove the manifold/converter assembly and discard the manifold nuts, gasket and studs.

steps.title: 5.0L: rebuild in the prescribed sequence
steps.body: Reverse [G2262730](#/document/G2262730), renewing discarded parts and cleaning all exhaust connections. Finger-tighten the manifold nuts, then use the illustrated sequence and both tightening stages. Restore the support, mount, steering, intake, body-access and battery connections as directed. Inspect the lower steering shaft after reassembly where disconnected, and check the exhaust for leaks.

steps.title: 5.2L: clear the steering and raise the engine
steps.body: Loosen the dash seal, hand-start its nuts and hold the steering wheel straight ahead with a holding device. Remove the underbody shields and [left catalytic converter](#/document/G1805802), then disconnect the oil cooler hoses. Discard the steering-shaft bolt, separate the lower coupling without force and secure the shaft to the frame rail. Remove the intake assembly, release the harness retainer, remove the cross brace and discard its nuts. Remove both engine-mount nuts, install the support tools and raise the engine 50 mm.

steps.title: 5.2L: renew the manifold joint
steps.body: Disconnect the heated oxygen sensor connector and harness retainer, then remove the left mount bracket and manifold, discarding the manifold nuts. Clean and inspect the manifold, then discard the gasket and studs. Install new studs, gasket and nuts using [G1800276](#/document/G1800276), including its illustrated tightening sequence. Restore the mount bracket, sensor connection and retainer, lower the engine, remove the tools and install the mount nuts.

steps.title: 5.2L: restore steering, oil and access parts
steps.body: Reconnect the steering shaft with a new bolt and perform the [Steering Column Collapsed Check](#/document/G1721912). Reconnect the oil cooler hoses; install the converter, shields and cross brace with new nuts. Restore the harness retainer and intake assembly, remove the steering holding device, seat and tighten the dash seal, then reconnect the battery. Inspect and adjust the engine oil level with the specified oil.

watchFor.title: Steering shaft resistance
watchFor.body: Never hammer, pry or force the shaft. On the 5.2L, the dash seal and fasteners must be loosened before removing or installing the lower joint at the steering gear.

watchFor.title: Damaged dash sealing
watchFor.body: Protect the sealer foam and retain the dash-seal brackets on their pins. Damage can admit noise, fumes, air or water.

notes: On the 5.0L, sensors can remain in a manifold assembly being reused, but their electrical connectors must still be disconnected.
If both 5.0L manifolds are being removed, use the engine-support setup specified by the right-hand manifold procedure.

verification.title: Complete the applicable exhaust check
verification.body: The 3.7L procedure requires starting the engine and checking for exhaust leaks; the 5.0L procedure also requires an exhaust leak check.

verification.title: Complete steering and oil checks
verification.body: Perform the lower steering-shaft inspection after the applicable 5.0L shaft work and after 5.2L reassembly. On the 5.2L, confirm the engine oil level has been inspected and adjusted.

procedures.purpose: 3.7L left exhaust manifold removal and installation, renewed hardware, staged tightening and running leak check.
5.0L left manifold/converter assembly removal and installation, engine support, conditional steering-shaft access and staged tightening.
5.2L left manifold removal and installation, engine support, steering and oil cooler disconnection, and final oil-level inspection.
Correct vehicle lifting points and hoist positioning precautions.

Battery cable disconnection and reconnection for the V8 procedures.
Battery tray removal and installation in the 5.0L access route.
Cowl panel grille removal and installation in the 5.0L access route.
Lower steering-shaft inspection after the applicable V8 steering-shaft work.

guides.title: Remove and refit an exterior front door handle
guides.summary: Release the exterior handle through its internal screw mechanism, protect its electrical connection and complete the full engagement sequence on installation.
guides.introduction: The exterior handle operates the door from outside, beside the lock-cylinder and cover assembly. It also has an electrical connector reached from inside the door. Removal therefore begins with interior access, even though the part being changed is outside. This guide covers removing and refitting the handle and its adjoining cover assembly.
guides.why: The handle releases before the release screw has completed the travel required for installation. Stopping at the first movement leaves the mechanism short of its specified position. The wiring presents a separate risk: pulling the handle too far outward before disconnecting it can damage the harness.

when.summary: When the exterior front door handle needs replacement or removal for a door repair.
notes: The illustrated left-hand-drive, left-side procedure is similar for right-hand-drive vehicles and the right side.

prepare.title: Plan access from inside the door
prepare.detail: Have the Front Door Trim Panel procedure available. The trim panel and lower watershield must be removed so the handle connector can be reached from inside.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled screw travel
prepare.detail: Use a suitable driver for the release screw and torque equipment capable of its specified 62 lb.in (7 Nm) final tightening.

steps.title: Expose the release mechanism and connector
steps.body: Remove the [front door trim panel](#/document/G1692600), then the lower watershield and grommet. This establishes the internal access needed to release the assembly and disconnect its wiring.

steps.title: Release the lock-cylinder and cover assembly
steps.body: Hold the front door handle open and turn the release screw 8 turns. Although the handle releases around 6 to 6.5 turns, continue through all 8. Remove the lock-cylinder and door handle cover assembly.

steps.title: Disconnect and exchange the handle
steps.body: Disconnect the handle connector from inside the door before pulling the handle out too far, then remove the handle. For installation, connect the wiring from inside the door and partially insert the handle into the opening.

steps.title: Engage the mechanism and restore the door
steps.body: Install the lock-cylinder and cover assembly and release the handle. Apply light pressure while turning the screw 8 turns: engagement occurs around 6 to 6.5 turns, but complete all 8 before tightening to 62 lb.in (7 Nm). Refit the grommet, lower watershield and trim panel using the [complete handle procedure](#/document/G1695902).

watchFor.title: Early release or engagement
watchFor.body: Movement before the eighth turn is expected; it is not the stopping point.

watchFor.title: Harness tension
watchFor.body: Keep outward handle movement limited until the connector has been disconnected from inside the door.

notes: The release screw's final torque follows the full installation travel; torque alone does not replace the turn-count requirement.

verification.title: Confirm completed retention
verification.body: Confirm the full installation turn count, handle engagement and final release-screw torque.

verification.title: Confirm restored access parts
verification.body: Confirm the handle connector is attached and the grommet, lower watershield and trim panel have been reinstalled.

procedures.purpose: Exterior front door handle removal and installation, connector protection and release-screw travel and torque.
Front door trim panel removal and installation for internal handle access.

guides.title: Prepare a body repair for welding
guides.summary: Establish the permitted repair method, protect vehicle electronics and prepare the work area before welding body steel.
guides.introduction: A body weld joins metal at a repair location, but its heat, electrical current and radiation also affect the surrounding vehicle and work area. This job establishes the precautions needed before welding begins: deciding whether the component can be repaired, protecting nearby systems and selecting a replacement weld pattern that preserves the original attachment.
guides.why: A sound-looking weld does not by itself establish a suitable repair. Heating certain structural steels to straighten them is prohibited, and some components must be replaced rather than welded. Electronics can be damaged by heat or welding current, while exposed wiring and nearby components need protection from spatter. These decisions belong before the first test weld.

when.summary: Before any body welding, after identifying the material and the permitted repair method.
notes: Vehicle subframes, steering components and suspension components are replacement-only items; do not weld them.

prepare.title: Provide welding and grinding protection
prepare.detail: Use protective clothing and a welding helmet with suitable dark filter lenses. For electric welding, use the deepest shade that still provides adequate visibility. People in the weld area should wear flash safety goggles. Sanding and grinding require eye protection with side shields and a dust mask.

prepare.title: Prepare the equipment and workspace
prepare.detail: Provide ventilation against noxious and oxygen-displacing gases, protective covers, a test sample, and grinding discs and wire brushes dedicated to the material being welded. Follow the welding equipment manufacturer's procedures and settings.

steps.title: Confirm that welding is an appropriate repair
steps.body: Identify the component and steel type using the complete welding precautions. Do not heat boron, martensitic, high-strength steel (HSS) or ultra-high-strength steel (UHSS) components to straighten or repair them. Replace severely bent or kinked components.

steps.title: Depower and protect electrical systems
steps.body: Depower and disconnect supplemental restraint system (SRS) components before welding. Disconnect and isolate the battery ground cable. Disconnect on-vehicle electronic modules and remove or reposition modules and related wiring away from heat-affected areas, protecting them from welding heat and current.

steps.title: Protect the surrounding area
steps.body: Place covers around nearby components and wiring harnesses to intercept spatter. Establish ventilation and protective equipment before welding or surface preparation starts; welding radiation can injure unprotected eyes and skin even though ultraviolet and infrared rays are invisible.

steps.title: Plan the replacement weld pattern
steps.body: Factory welds may be replaced with squeeze-type resistance welding (STRW) spot welds or metal active gas (MAG) plug welds. MAG plug welds must match the original locations and quantity, using 8 mm (0.31 in) holes. Resistance spot welds must match the original quantity and sit adjacent to the original weld locations.

steps.title: Prepare and prove the welding setup
steps.body: Use material-dedicated abrasives and brushes, and weld-through primer where applicable. Set the equipment for the selected weld type and make a test weld on a test sample. ER70S-3 or ER70S-6 wire is typically used for MAG welding on steel.

steps.title: Position the welding ground connection
steps.body: Place the welder ground clamp as close as possible to the weld area. Never attach it to the vehicle subframe. Confirm the component protections and planned weld locations before proceeding with the body repair.

watchFor.title: Heat-straightening a restricted steel
watchFor.body: Heating a damaged structural component is not an acceptable substitute for replacement when the material or damage falls under the stated restrictions.

watchFor.title: An exposed module or harness
watchFor.body: A nearby electronic component needs protection from both heat and current; spatter covers alone do not satisfy those precautions.

diagnostics.finding: The proposed repair involves a vehicle subframe, steering component or suspension component.
diagnostics.meaning: Welding is prohibited for that component.
diagnostics.next: Use replacement service.

verification.title: Confirm readiness before welding
verification.body: Verify electrical isolation, SRS depowering and disconnection, component protection, ventilation, personal protection and completion of the test weld.

verification.title: Check the planned attachment
verification.body: Confirm that weld quantity and placement match the selected replacement method, and that the ground clamp is near the work rather than on the subframe.

procedures.purpose: Complete body-welding precautions, material restrictions, electrical protection and replacement weld requirements.

guides.title: Adjust vertical headlamp aim using the VOL or VOR cutoff
guides.summary: Set each low-beam cutoff against a measured screen reference using the aiming rule marked on its headlamp lens.
guides.introduction: The low-beam pattern has a boundary between its bright and dark areas called the cutoff. Vertical adjustment positions that boundary relative to the road. The headlamp system uses a dual-beam high-intensity discharge arrangement, but this aiming procedure works from the low-beam pattern and the lens identification. It adjusts aim; it does not diagnose a lamp that fails to illuminate.
guides.why: Vehicle height, loading and tire inflation all affect where the beam lands. The reference line also changes with headlamp optical-center height. Finally, Visually Optically Aligned Left (VOL) and Visually Optically Aligned Right (VOR) headlamps use different portions of the cutoff and different target positions. Ignoring any of these distinctions can produce an incorrect adjustment.

when.summary: When functioning low beams need their vertical aim checked or corrected.
notes: Horizontal aim is not adjustable.
Use the applicable vehicle-inspection guidance for visual-aim tolerance ranges.

prepare.title: Arrange a suitable aiming area
prepare.detail: Use level ground facing a vertical wall or screen at least 2.4 m wide, with space to park approximately 7.6 m away. Work in darkness so the cutoff is clearly visible.

prepare.title: Gather measuring and adjustment equipment
prepare.detail: Have a measuring tool, a 2.4 m length of masking tape, a way to cover one headlamp, and the appropriate adjuster tool. Locate the adjustment screw using the owner's literature.

steps.title: Identify the lens marking
steps.body: Look for VOL and SAE or VOR and SAE molded into each lens. These markings determine which cutoff edge to use; they do not simply identify the left or right side of the vehicle.

steps.title: Establish the vehicle conditions
steps.body: Correct the tire pressures, use the vehicle's normal loading, clean the headlamps and confirm that they operate correctly. Park on level ground approximately 7.6 m from the wall directly ahead. If air suspension is fitted, its switch must be on.

steps.title: Measure and mark the reference height
steps.body: Identify the low-beam optical center, using its lens marking where provided or the applicable reflector, bulb, LED shield or projector inner-lens center. Measure its height above the ground and record it. Below 95 cm, place the tape reference at that height. From 95–105 cm, place it 1.3 cm lower. Above 105 cm, place it 2.5 cm lower.

steps.title: Find the actual cutoff
steps.body: Switch on the low beams and open the hood. Locate the horizontal boundary with the greatest change between light and dark. Use this cutoff rather than the center of the brightest patch; beam-pattern appearance can vary.

steps.title: Adjust the first headlamp
steps.body: Cover the other headlamp. For VOR, align the distinct cutoff on the right portion of the pattern with the horizontal reference line. For VOL, position the distinct left-side cutoff edge 5 cm below that line. Turn the adjustment screw as needed, preserving the applicable height correction already built into the reference line.

steps.title: Adjust the remaining headlamp
steps.body: Swap the cover and repeat the appropriate VOL or VOR adjustment for the other lamp. Each marking's rule applies to either side of the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Two overlapping patterns
watchFor.body: Covering the opposite lamp is necessary to identify the cutoff of the lamp being adjusted.

watchFor.title: Applying the VOR target to a VOL lamp
watchFor.body: A VOL cutoff belongs below the reference line; placing it directly on the line loses its required offset.

notes: The air-suspension condition applies only where that equipment is actually fitted.

diagnostics.finding: A headlamp does not operate correctly.
diagnostics.meaning: The entry conditions for visual aiming have not been met.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the operating concern before adjusting aim.

verification.title: Confirm both cutoff positions
verification.body: Check each lamp separately against its correct target with the vehicle still under the original setup conditions.

verification.title: Retain the measured result
verification.body: Record the optical-center measurement, resulting reference height and VOL or VOR marking so the completed adjustment has a clear measured basis.

procedures.purpose: Complete vertical headlamp aiming procedure, including setup, height corrections and separate VOL/VOR targets.

guides.title: Replace the output shaft speed sensor on the 2.3L MT82
guides.summary: Drain the MT82, replace its output shaft speed sensor and restore the electrical connection and specified transmission fill.
guides.introduction: The output shaft speed (OSS) sensor monitors rotation at the transmission's output. On the 2.3L EcoBoost MT82 manual transmission, it is an externally mounted component retained by a bolt and connected to the vehicle wiring. Replacement leaves the internal gears assembled, but the procedure requires draining and refilling the transmission.
guides.why: This repair combines a small electrical component with transmission-fluid service. The vehicle must be safely supported and level for the work, and the sensor fastener has a different tightening requirement from the fluid plugs. Completing the sensor installation without restoring the transmission fill would leave an essential part of the job unfinished.

when.summary: When diagnosis or an established repair calls for OSS sensor removal or replacement on the 2.3L MT82.
notes: The removal procedure does not establish which symptoms or electrical faults justify sensor replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange safe, level access
prepare.detail: Use a vehicle hoist and the linked jacking and lifting procedure. The vehicle must be in neutral and level for the fluid service.

prepare.title: Prepare for draining and filling
prepare.detail: Have fluid collection equipment, a fluid suction gun, suitable hand tools and torque tools. Establish the applicable MT82 fluid specification and filling requirements before draining.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in neutral, position the vehicle on the hoist using the lifting procedure. Maintain a level attitude for the subsequent draining and filling operations.

steps.title: Drain and remove the sensor
steps.body: Remove the transmission drain plug and drain the fluid. Disconnect the OSS electrical connector, then remove the retaining bolt and sensor. The illustration identifies the sensor and its bolt on the transmission housing.

steps.title: Install and reconnect the sensor
steps.body: Install the sensor and its retaining bolt, tightening the bolt to 10 Nm. Reconnect the OSS electrical connector. Follow the dedicated 2.3L sensor procedure for this removal and installation phase.

steps.title: Restore the transmission fill
steps.body: Refit the drain plug and tighten it to 35 Nm. Following Transmission Draining and Filling, remove the fill plug and use a fluid suction gun to fill with the specified transmission fluid. Install the fill plug and tighten it to 35 Nm. Use the applicable specifications for the fill rather than assuming a quantity.

watchFor.title: Confusing the tightening values
watchFor.body: The sensor bolt uses 10 Nm; the drain and fill plugs use 35 Nm. These are separate fastener requirements.

watchFor.title: An unfinished fluid service
watchFor.body: Draining is part of sensor removal here. Refilling and installing the fill plug are required before the repair is complete.

notes: The MT82 overview describes its fluid as lasting the transmission's service life without a routine service change; draining here is required by the sensor repair.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Check that the sensor bolt is tightened, the electrical connector is connected, both plugs are installed at their specified torque and the prescribed fill is complete.

procedures.purpose: OSS sensor removal and installation specifically for the 2.3L EcoBoost MT82.
Required vehicle jacking and hoist-positioning guidance before underbody access.
MT82 draining and filling sequence, level-vehicle requirement, suction-gun use and fluid-plug tightening.

guides.title: Replace a 6-piston front brake caliper on the 5.0L
guides.summary: Remove and refit the 6-piston front caliper with new mounting bolts and hose washers, then pressure-bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The front brake caliper uses hydraulic pressure to press the pads against the brake disc. Removing it separates both its mechanical mounting and its brake-hose connection. This procedure covers the 5.0L application equipped with 6-piston front calipers, including the required pad-removal prerequisite, replacement hardware and final bleeding operation.
guides.why: The mounting bolts secure the caliper, while the washers seal the hydraulic hose connection. Both have explicit discard instructions, so they must be replaced during installation. Opening the hose connection also makes brake-system bleeding a required finishing phase. Clean, sealed openings help protect the hydraulic circuit while it is disconnected.

when.summary: When an established repair requires removal or replacement of a 6-piston front brake caliper.
notes: This procedure gives the replacement path; it does not diagnose the cause of a braking complaint.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct hardware and tools
prepare.detail: Have new caliper mounting bolts, new brake-hose sealing washers, suitable tools and torque equipment. The removed mounting bolts and washers must not return to service.

prepare.title: Arrange hydraulic protection and bleeding
prepare.detail: Provide suitable means to seal every opened connection and the equipment and capability for Brake System Pressure Bleeding in section 206-00. Have the linked 6-piston brake-pad procedure available for removal and installation.

steps.title: Remove the brake pads
steps.body: Follow Brake Pads — Vehicles With: 6-Piston Brake Caliper before removing the caliper. This is the first required phase and provides the equipment-specific pad handling and installation details.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the caliper
steps.body: Remove the brake-hose flow bolt, disconnect the hose and discard the sealing washers. Seal all openings. Remove the two caliper mounting bolts, discard them and remove the caliper. If brake fluid reaches paintwork, immediately wash the affected area with cold water.

steps.title: Refit with replacement hardware
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Install the caliper with new mounting bolts and tighten them to 115 Nm. Reconnect the hose with new sealing washers and tighten the flow bolt to 40 Nm. Reinstall the pads using the dedicated 6-piston procedure.

steps.title: Complete pressure bleeding
steps.body: Perform Brake System Pressure Bleeding after reassembly. Follow that complete procedure for the hydraulic finishing phase; bolting the caliper back into place does not complete a repair that opened the brake circuit.

watchFor.title: Old hardware mixed with new parts
watchFor.body: The caliper mounting bolts and hose washers are specifically discarded. Keep that requirement distinct from the flow bolt, which has no discard instruction here.

watchFor.title: Fluid on paint or exposed openings
watchFor.body: Wash paint contamination immediately with cold water and keep disconnected hydraulic openings sealed.

notes: The illustrated pair of mounting bolts is the pair that must be discarded.

verification.title: Confirm the completed assembly
verification.body: Verify installation of new mounting bolts and sealing washers, the specified fastener tightening and completion of the pad installation.

verification.title: Confirm hydraulic completion
verification.body: Confirm that the required brake-system pressure-bleeding procedure has been completed before closing the repair.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L 6-piston front caliper removal and installation, including discarded hardware, tightening and the pressure-bleeding requirement.
Equipment-specific brake-pad removal before caliper service and pad installation during reassembly.

guides.title: Deactivate factory mode and complete the transition through transport mode
guides.summary: Use the ignition-type-specific sequence to move the vehicle out of factory mode, then perform transport-mode deactivation.
guides.introduction: During vehicle build, modules including the instrument panel cluster (IPC) and body control module (BCM) can be placed in factory mode. This reduces battery drain during extended periods without use and can alter or disable various functions. Deactivation is a staged process: the ignition sequence changes factory mode to transport mode, and a separate procedure then restores normal operation.
guides.why: The cluster message identifies the current operating mode. Altered electrical functions while a storage mode is active do not, by themselves, establish a defective module. Recognizing the change to transport mode also prevents stopping too early: transport mode still limits functions to conserve battery charge.
searchTerms: electrical functions disabled in factory mode

when.summary: When the message center displays FACTORY MODE CONTACT DEALER.
notes: If TRANSPORT MODE CONTACT DEALER is already displayed, go directly to Transport Mode Deactivation.

prepare.title: Establish battery readiness
prepare.detail: Begin with the ignition off and verify that the battery is fully charged using the Battery guidance in section 414-01.

prepare.title: Identify the ignition arrangement
prepare.detail: Choose the keyed-ignition or push-button branch before starting. For push-button operation, keep one integrated keyhead transmitter (IKT) inside the vehicle as specified by the procedure.

steps.title: Read the displayed mode
steps.body: Confirm the message center shows factory mode. If it already shows transport mode, the factory-to-transport transition has occurred and the separate transport procedure is the appropriate next step.

steps.title: Start from ignition off
steps.body: Place the ignition in the OFF position and verify full battery charge. This is the required starting condition before carrying out the repeated ignition operations.

steps.title: Perform the applicable transition sequence
steps.body: Without push-button start, cycle the ignition from off to on 60 times. With push-button start and the required transmitter inside the vehicle, press the Engine Start/Stop button 120 times. These are alternative branches for different ignition arrangements.

steps.title: Finish with transport-mode deactivation
steps.body: After the factory-mode transition, follow the linked Transport Mode Deactivation procedure. The vehicle automatically moves from factory mode to transport mode after 60 ignition cycles; reaching transport mode is an intermediate result, not normal operation.

watchFor.title: Stopping when the message changes
watchFor.body: A transport-mode message means another deactivation phase remains.

watchFor.title: Mixing cycles and button presses
watchFor.body: Keep the two counts separate: keyed ignition uses off-to-on cycles, while the push-button branch specifies button presses.

notes: Use this process for the displayed factory or transport state; it is not a general reset for unrelated electrical faults.

diagnostics.finding: FACTORY MODE CONTACT DEALER is displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: Factory mode remains active and can alter or disable vehicle functions.
diagnostics.next: Perform the applicable factory-mode transition sequence.

diagnostics.finding: TRANSPORT MODE CONTACT DEALER is displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: The vehicle is in the battery-conserving transport state.
diagnostics.next: Perform Transport Mode Deactivation.

verification.title: Record the state transition
verification.body: Record the starting message and the message reached after the applicable ignition sequence.

verification.title: Confirm the final phase
verification.body: Complete the transport-mode procedure and its confirmation of return to normal operation before treating deactivation as finished.

procedures.purpose: Factory-mode deactivation with separate keyed-ignition and push-button sequences.
Required follow-on deactivation of transport mode to restore normal operation.

guides.title: Replace the front seatbelt retractor and pretensioner on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Depower the restraints, remove the front belt assembly through the correct body-style access path, then restore routing and verify operation.
guides.introduction: The seatbelt retractor stores the webbing and locks it when restraint is needed. The pretensioner forms part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). Replacement therefore involves more than removing a belt spool: electrical isolation, anchor handling and belt routing are essential. Coupe and convertible access differs, and the coupe has a specific lower-anchor rotation during installation.
guides.why: The rear anchor-pretensioner bolt must stay attached and flush with its anchor plate throughout removal and installation. Losing that relationship prevents correct installation and requires a new belt assembly. Routing also matters: the coupe's prescribed lower-anchor twist must not become a twist between the upper D-ring guide and the retractor.

when.summary: When seatbelt-system diagnosis calls for front retractor and pretensioner removal or replacement.
notes: The procedure illustrates left-hand-drive and right-side work; the corresponding opposite arrangements are similar.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Use personnel able to follow the complete SRS depowering, repowering and seatbelt testing procedures. These are required phases, not substitutes for one another.

prepare.title: Prepare body-style access
prepare.detail: Have the appropriate coupe or convertible loadspace-trim procedure, trim and fastener tools, and torque equipment. Convertible work also involves speaker-bracket access and an additional module on the right side.

steps.title: Depower and expose the anchors
steps.body: Follow SRS Depowering before disconnecting restraint components. Remove the loadspace trim using the correct body-style procedure, then move the carpet aside.

steps.title: Release the anchor pretensioner
steps.body: Disconnect its electrical connector and remove the first anchor bolt. While pulling outward on the pretensioner, release the rear bolt from its mounting, keeping it attached and flush with the anchor plate. Both anchor-bolt installation torques are 40 Nm.

steps.title: Clear convertible-only obstructions
steps.body: For right-side convertible work, remove the specified module by detaching its wiring retainers, removing its nut and bolt, and disconnecting its connector. Remove the speaker and bracket assembly by releasing its harness retainer, connector, screw, stud bolt and nuts. Use the individual tightening values in the complete procedure during reassembly.

steps.title: Remove the upper guide and retractor
steps.body: On a convertible, remove the D-ring bolt and move the belt aside, then disconnect the retractor connector and remove its retainer and assembly. On a coupe, follow the illustrated D-ring-cover and bolt removal, then remove the retractor retainer, disconnect the connector and withdraw the assembly.

steps.title: Install the retractor and D-ring
steps.body: Reverse the convertible removal sequence. On a coupe, connect and position the retractor, install its retainer at 40 Nm, then position the belt and install the D-ring bolt at 40 Nm before fitting its cover.

steps.title: Restore the correct lower-belt routing
steps.body: On a coupe, keep the webbing untwisted between D-ring and retractor. Rotate the anchor pretensioner 180 degrees clockwise on the left side or counterclockwise on the right side. On a convertible, ensure the webbing is untwisted and belts and buckles remain accessible. Complete reverse assembly, preserving the rear anchor bolt's attached, flush position.

steps.title: Repower and test
steps.body: Follow SRS Repowering after reassembly, then check the active restraint system using Seatbelt Systems diagnosis and testing.

watchFor.title: Rear anchor bolt displaced from its plate
watchFor.body: Failure to keep it attached and flush requires installation of a new safety belt assembly.

watchFor.title: Applying coupe routing to a convertible
watchFor.body: The specified lower-anchor rotation belongs to the coupe installation branch.

diagnostics.finding: A passenger belt clicks and cannot extend after being fully pulled out and allowed to retract.
diagnostics.meaning: This can be normal automatic locking retractor operation for securing a child seat.
diagnostics.next: Allow full retraction to disengage that mode; use the prescribed functional tests if operation remains in question.

verification.title: Check routing and access
verification.body: Confirm the applicable webbing arrangement, secure anchors and accessible belts and buckles before completing the restraint checks.

verification.title: Record functional completion
verification.body: Record completion of SRS repowering and the results of the required active-restraint operational check.

procedures.purpose: Front retractor and pretensioner removal and installation, including distinct coupe and convertible access and routing.
Required SRS depowering before restraint-component disconnection.
Coupe loadspace-trim removal and installation for belt access.
Convertible loadspace-trim removal and installation for belt access.
Required SRS repowering after reassembly.
Seatbelt diagnosis and functional testing, including the required final active-restraint operation check.

applicability.equipment: The cranking test branches here cover the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines.

guides.title: Compression testing: find a cylinder that cannot hold its share
guides.summary: Compare how well the cylinders build pressure, then use the result to choose the next test instead of guessing at an engine repair.
guides.introduction: Each cylinder has to squeeze its air charge before combustion can do useful work. A compression gauge checks that squeezing ability while the engine cranks. Think of it as comparing the cylinders on the same test bench: consistency matters, and the test only means something when the conditions stay the same.
guides.why: A weak cylinder can make the engine run unevenly even when its ignition and fuel systems are working. Compression testing helps separate a sealing problem from an electrical or fuel problem. A low reading identifies a direction to investigate; it does not by itself tell you to replace the engine.

when.summary: Use after a persistent running problem points toward a mechanical cylinder fault.
notes: This is a diagnostic test, not a scheduled tune-up item.
Use the engine-specific preparation in the linked engine-testing article. The 3.7L is not included in these cranking-test instructions.

prepare.title: Gauge and a repeatable test setup
prepare.detail: Use a suitable compression gauge and the equipment required by the engine-specific cranking procedure. The battery must be properly charged so later cylinders are not tested at a slower cranking speed.

prepare.title: Spark-plug access and clean working conditions
prepare.detail: Identify the correct plug procedure below. Dirt around an open plug hole can fall into the cylinder; organize removed plugs by cylinder so their condition remains useful evidence.

prepare.title: A technician-controlled cranking arrangement
prepare.detail: The test calls for a defined ignition-off auxiliary cranking setup. If you cannot establish that arrangement correctly, have a workshop carry out the pressure test; do not improvise a starter bypass.

steps.title: Confirm the engine and the complaint
steps.body: Record which engine is fitted and what happens when it runs poorly. Check the oil level and correct viscosity and confirm the battery is charged. These checks remove avoidable differences before you compare cylinders.

steps.title: Prepare the warm engine using its own test branch
steps.body: The test specifies normal engine operating temperature, ignition off, removal of all spark plugs and preparation of the intake and throttle. Follow the matching branch: the EcoBoost intake connection differs from the V8 arrangement.

steps.title: Measure the first cylinder
steps.body: Install the gauge in the first cylinder. Using the specified ignition-off cranking setup, allow at least five compression strokes and record the highest pressure. Also note how many strokes were needed to reach it.

steps.title: Repeat without changing the conditions
steps.body: Test the remaining cylinders with approximately the same number of compression strokes. Record the readings by cylinder rather than relying on memory. A slowing battery or a changed throttle opening can distort the comparison.

steps.title: Compare the low reading with the high one
steps.body: The cited engine test uses a lowest-cylinder reading of at least 75% of the highest as its comparison criterion. For example, a highest reading of 200 psi gives a 150 psi comparison point. This is a relationship between readings, not a universal target pressure.

steps.title: Investigate a repeatable low result
steps.body: Recheck the setup before blaming the engine. A follow-up cylinder leak-down test can help locate the escaping pressure. The engine-testing article also explains controlled follow-up checks; do not add oil or disassemble components without following that procedure.

steps.title: Restore the intake and ignition components
steps.body: Refit the plugs, intake parts and electrical connections using the matching procedures and tightening specifications. Confirm connector locks are engaged and that the engine runs normally after reassembly.

diagnostics.finding: One cylinder stays noticeably below the others
diagnostics.meaning: A local sealing problem is possible, but the test setup can also create a low reading.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the reading under the same conditions, then locate leakage before deciding on a repair.

diagnostics.finding: Two neighboring cylinders read low
diagnostics.meaning: Leakage between adjacent cylinders is one possibility.
diagnostics.next: Use the follow-up tests to distinguish a head-gasket path from valve or ring concerns.

diagnostics.finding: Every reading is low
diagnostics.meaning: A shared test-condition problem or broader mechanical issue may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Check battery speed, gauge connection and throttle preparation before interpreting the numbers.

watchFor.title: An unsafe engine should not be warmed for a test
watchFor.body: Do not run an engine with a serious oil-pressure problem, severe mechanical noise or overheating just to reach test temperature. Resolve whether running it is appropriate first.

verification.title: A usable cylinder record
verification.body: Keep engine identification, test conditions, stroke counts and pressures together. The record should explain why the next test is needed.

verification.title: Reassembly complete
verification.body: Verify every disturbed connection and plug is restored before returning the vehicle to use.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L spark-plug access and refitting.
5.0L spark-plug access and refitting.
5.2L spark-plug access and refitting.
Open the matching compression-test branch and its result interpretation.

guides.title: Cylinder leak-down: listen for where compression escapes
guides.summary: Use controlled air pressure to distinguish leakage through the intake, exhaust, crankcase or cooling system.
guides.introduction: A compression test asks how much pressure a cylinder can build. A leak-down test asks where pressure escapes when the cylinder should be sealed. With the piston correctly positioned and the valves closed, a tester feeds controlled air into the cylinder and measures the loss.
guides.why: Different escape routes point toward different parts of the engine. Listening at the intake, exhaust and crankcase helps narrow the investigation before a large repair. The result is most useful alongside the earlier compression readings and the original symptoms.

when.summary: Use to investigate a repeatable low-compression result or suspected cylinder sealing fault.
notes: There is no routine mileage interval for this test.
Positioning the crankshaft and managing compressed air require workshop competence.

prepare.title: Cylinder leakage tester and regulated air
prepare.detail: Use a tester with the correct spark-plug-hole adapter and follow its setup instructions. The scale and air supply must be set correctly before comparing cylinders.

prepare.title: Correct cylinder position
prepare.detail: Identify top dead center on the compression stroke, when both valves should be closed. The piston reaches the top on another stroke too, so position alone is not enough.

prepare.title: Safe control of engine movement
prepare.detail: Compressed air can turn the engine if the piston is not held in the correct position. Keep hands and tools clear and establish a safe crankshaft-control arrangement before admitting air.

steps.title: Choose the cylinder from the evidence
steps.body: Start with the cylinder implicated by compression readings, plug condition or other mechanical checks. Label your measurements so you can compare that cylinder with the rest.

steps.title: Prepare spark-plug access
steps.body: Follow the correct engine-specific plug procedure. Fit the tester adapter without damaging the threads and keep debris out of the open cylinder.

steps.title: Set the piston at compression top dead center
steps.body: Confirm the cylinder is on its compression stroke. A valve held open by the wrong crank position can make a healthy cylinder appear to leak badly.

steps.title: Apply air in a controlled way
steps.body: Set up and connect the tester as its instructions require, while maintaining control of the crankshaft. Record the leakage reading once the test is stable. The linked engine test treats leakage above 20% as excessive; a result still needs a location and a cause.

steps.title: Listen at the possible escape routes
steps.body: Air heard at the intake suggests an intake-valve path; air at the tailpipe suggests an exhaust-valve path. Air at the crankcase ventilation connection points toward leakage past the pistons and rings. These observations guide further inspection rather than prove a particular part has failed.

steps.title: Check for a path into another cylinder or the cooling system
steps.body: Air at an adjacent open plug hole can indicate a path between cylinders. Bubbles in the cooling system can indicate a combustion-to-coolant path. Never open a hot or pressurized cooling system to make this observation.

steps.title: Release pressure before moving to the next cylinder
steps.body: Remove test pressure before changing connections or crank position. Refit the plugs and disturbed components with their matching procedure once testing is complete.

diagnostics.finding: Air is strongest at the intake
diagnostics.meaning: An intake valve may not be sealing, or the crank position may be wrong.
diagnostics.next: Reconfirm compression top dead center before investigating the valve.

diagnostics.finding: Air is strongest at the tailpipe
diagnostics.meaning: An exhaust-valve sealing path is possible.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the setup and compare with other cylinder evidence.

diagnostics.finding: Air reaches a neighboring plug hole or coolant
diagnostics.meaning: A head-gasket, head or block path is possible.
diagnostics.next: Document the route and carry out the relevant mechanical inspection before choosing parts.

watchFor.title: A percentage is only part of the result
watchFor.body: Test setup, crank position and the location of the air loss all matter. Avoid turning one gauge number into an unsupported engine-replacement decision.

verification.title: Record the route, not just the reading
verification.body: Keep the percentage, cylinder, piston position and where air was heard together. That makes the next inspection much more focused.

3.7L spark-plug access.
5.0L spark-plug access.
5.2L spark-plug access.
Cylinder Leakage Detection explains the test and escape routes.

guides.title: EcoBoost oil pressure: measure the pressure behind the warning
guides.summary: Use a mechanical gauge to check actual hot oil pressure before deciding whether the switch, oil supply or engine needs attention.
guides.introduction: The oil pump sends oil through passages that feed the engine bearings and other moving parts. The warning switch reports a pressure condition; it is not a complete measurement of how the lubrication system behaves. A mechanical gauge lets you compare real pressure with the engine specification.
guides.why: Replacing the warning switch will not fix a genuine pressure loss. Measuring first helps distinguish an indication problem from low oil supply, pump trouble or excessive internal clearance. This guide is specific to the 2.3L test arrangement.

when.summary: Investigate an oil-pressure warning or a lubrication concern before continued driving.
notes: This is a diagnostic job, not a routine pressure check at every oil change.
Stop the engine when an oil-pressure warning or severe lubrication noise appears. Do not keep it running simply to see whether the warning clears.

prepare.title: Mechanical gauge and matching adapter
prepare.detail: Use a gauge and fitting suitable for the oil-gallery test connection. Keep the gauge, adapter and port scrupulously clean.

prepare.title: Safe access and replacement switch
prepare.detail: The linked switch procedure specifies discarding the removed switch. Have the correct replacement available and follow its installation requirements.

prepare.title: Hot-pressure specification
prepare.detail: The 2.3L specification is 29–60 psi (200–414 kPa) with the engine hot at 2,000 rpm. Cold or idle readings are not directly interchangeable with this test point.

steps.title: Check the basics with the engine stopped
steps.body: Confirm the oil level and look for leakage or contamination. An empty or seriously contaminated lubrication system needs attention before the engine is run for a gauge test.

steps.title: Access the switch safely
steps.body: Use the proper lifting procedure where underside access is needed. Disconnect the switch connector and follow the 2.3L removal procedure, protecting the connector and the oil-gallery opening.

steps.title: Connect the mechanical gauge
steps.body: Fit the correct clean adapter and gauge at the test port. Route the test equipment clear of exhaust heat and moving components. A leaking connection can affect both the reading and the engine oil level.

steps.title: Measure only when it is appropriate to run the engine
steps.body: A technician should decide whether the engine can safely be operated. The specified measurement is made at normal operating temperature and the stated engine speed; shut down if the test reveals a serious pressure loss or distress.

steps.title: Compare the actual test conditions and result
steps.body: Record temperature condition, engine speed and pressure together. Compare the hot 2,000 rpm measurement with 29–60 psi (200–414 kPa), rather than comparing an unrelated dashboard indication or cold reading.

steps.title: Follow the cause of a low result
steps.body: The diagnostic paths include insufficient oil, leakage, the pump, pickup restriction and excessive internal clearances. A failed reading warrants that investigation; it is not proof that the pump alone is faulty.

steps.title: Remove the gauge and restore the switch connection
steps.body: With the engine stopped, remove the test equipment and install the replacement switch using its specified sealing and tightening instructions. Restore the connector, confirm oil level and check the repaired connection for leakage when a safe verification run is possible.

diagnostics.finding: Gauge pressure is low at the specified test point
diagnostics.meaning: There may be a genuine lubrication-system fault.
diagnostics.next: Stop further running as needed and investigate oil supply, pickup, pump and internal leakage.

diagnostics.finding: Gauge pressure meets specification but the warning remains
diagnostics.meaning: The indication circuit or switch may need testing.
diagnostics.next: Use the appropriate electrical diagnosis; normal pressure does not identify which electrical component is wrong.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure reading changes with a leaking gauge connection
diagnostics.meaning: The test setup is unreliable and oil is being lost.
diagnostics.next: Stop, correct the connection and restore the proper oil level before repeating the test.

watchFor.title: Keep dirt out of the gallery
watchFor.body: Material introduced through the gauge connection can travel directly into lubricated engine parts.

watchFor.title: Avoid mixing engine specifications
watchFor.body: These pressure values and this access arrangement apply to the 2.3L engine. Other engines have separate test conditions and hardware.

verification.title: A documented pressure result
verification.body: Record the gauge reading with the required temperature and rpm. Keep the result with the diagnosis rather than recording only “oil pressure checked.”

verification.title: A sealed, restored connection
verification.body: Confirm the switch connector, oil level and leak check after the gauge is removed.

procedures.purpose: Use the Oil Pressure Test 2.3L EcoBoost branch.
2.3L oil-pressure switch removal and installation.
2.3L hot oil-pressure specification.

guides.title: Where is the oil going? Build an oil-consumption diagnosis
guides.summary: Separate an external leak from oil entering the cylinders, then measure usage consistently before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: Oil can leave an engine in more than one way. It may leak onto the outside, travel through the crankcase ventilation system, or enter a cylinder through worn or damaged sealing surfaces. Topping up keeps the level safe, but a useful diagnosis starts by finding which route the oil takes.
guides.why: Uneven dipstick checks can look like oil consumption, and an external leak can be mistaken for oil burning. A repeatable record helps separate those situations. It also gives a workshop better evidence than a vague report that the car “needs oil sometimes.”

when.summary: Start when repeated top-ups, oil fouling or smoke suggest unusual oil use.
notes: There is no single oil-use threshold here for every engine, driving style and operating condition.
Formal consumption testing is a controlled diagnostic exercise, not a new maintenance interval.

prepare.title: A consistent record
prepare.detail: Record mileage, the amount and specification of oil added, how the car was driven and any smoke or leaks. Keep the measurement conditions consistent.

prepare.title: The correct level-check method
prepare.detail: Use level ground and allow oil to drain back before reading the dipstick. The diagnostic procedure calls for at least ten minutes after a hot engine is stopped.

prepare.title: Access to the ventilation and filter systems
prepare.detail: Identify the fitted PCV arrangement and air filter. The EcoBoost oil separator and the V6/V8 valve arrangements are different components.

steps.title: Make sure the readings are comparable
steps.body: Check that the dipstick is fully seated and repeat the reading under consistent conditions. Adding oil immediately after shutdown can lead to overfilling because some oil has not yet returned to the pan.

steps.title: Look for external leakage first
steps.body: Inspect the engine for the origin of fresh oil rather than replacing the lowest wet seal. Oil can travel down the engine or along surfaces before it drips. Resolve an external leak before trying to measure internal consumption.

steps.title: Check the crankcase breathing path
steps.body: Inspect the relevant PCV hoses, connections, filler cap and dipstick seating. A disconnected or restricted ventilation path can change where oil mist goes. Use the matching component procedure instead of assuming every engine has the same serviceable PCV valve.

steps.title: Inspect the air-filter condition
steps.body: Look for a damaged or poorly seated filter as well as dirt. The filter must keep abrasive debris out of the engine; replacement is about restoring that barrier, not simply hiding a dirty element.

steps.title: Measure usage with a controlled test
steps.body: The engine-testing article provides a workshop method for establishing a known fill and measuring oil use against distance. Keep the car at the correct operating oil level throughout. Record top-ups accurately and retain the driving-condition information.

steps.title: Use cylinder evidence when internal loss remains likely
steps.body: Oil-fouled plugs, compression testing and cylinder leak-down results can help guide the next investigation. Normal compression does not eliminate every valve-guide or valve-seal cause of oil use.

steps.title: Repeat the measurement after the repair
steps.body: Use comparable conditions to check whether the confirmed repair changed oil consumption. A successful part replacement should produce a result you can verify.

diagnostics.finding: The level differs mainly when checking immediately after shutdown
diagnostics.meaning: Drain-back time may be changing the reading.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the check with the same waiting period and level surface.

diagnostics.finding: Fresh oil is visible outside the engine
diagnostics.meaning: An external path may account for some or all of the loss.
diagnostics.next: Find the highest fresh source and repair the confirmed leak before an internal consumption test.

diagnostics.finding: Oil-fouled plugs remain after external and ventilation checks
diagnostics.meaning: Oil may be entering particular cylinders.
diagnostics.next: Use the plug locations with compression and leakage evidence to focus the inspection.

watchFor.title: Do not overfill to compensate
watchFor.body: Maintain the correct level. Extra oil is not a repair and can create its own problems.

watchFor.title: Driving conditions matter
watchFor.body: High load and engine speed can change oil use. Keep that context in the test record instead of comparing unlike driving periods.

verification.title: An actual rate, with context
verification.body: The final record should show distance, oil added, measurement conditions and whether visible leaks were present.

verification.title: A result after corrective work
verification.body: Repeat the same measurement approach so the before-and-after comparison is meaningful.
